faculty.name: Nancy Reid
faculty.title: University Professor
faculty.summary: Reid is a foundational researcher in statistical theory and inference. Her recent work advances higher-order asymptotics and likelihood-based inference, composite and pseudo-likelihood for complex and intractable models, and the interface between Bayesian and frequentist approaches. She studies accurate approximations for p-values and confidence limits, inference under nuisance parameters, and principled design and analysis of studies, contributing both deep theory and practical guidance that shape how uncertainty is quantified across the statistical sciences.

faculty.name: Radu Craiu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Craiu works on Bayesian computation and applied statistics. His recent research develops Markov chain Monte Carlo methodology, including adaptive, parallel, and divide-and-conquer schemes for large and complex models, together with copula-based approaches for modeling dependence. He studies data augmentation, mixture and latent-variable models, and inference for correlated and high-dimensional data, with applications in health, genetics, and environmental science, aiming to make flexible Bayesian modeling computationally practical for challenging real-world datasets.

faculty.name: Jeffrey Rosenthal
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Rosenthal specializes in the theory and methodology of Markov chain Monte Carlo and applied probability. His recent work establishes quantitative convergence-rate bounds for Markov chains, analyzes adaptive MCMC algorithms and optimal scaling of proposal distributions, and studies the reliability of simulation-based inference. He contributes broadly to probability theory and its applications, and is also known for communicating probability and statistics to wide audiences, connecting rigorous theory with practical guidance for computational Bayesian methods.

faculty.name: Daniel Roy
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Roy studies the theoretical foundations of machine learning and probabilistic modeling. His recent work develops generalization theory, including PAC-Bayes and information-theoretic bounds, analyses of stochastic optimization and deep learning, and nonparametric Bayesian models grounded in exchangeability and computability. He studies probabilistic programming, the limits of learning and inference, and principled uncertainty quantification, combining probability, statistics, and computer science to understand when and why modern learning algorithms generalize and how to make them more reliable.

faculty.name: Linbo Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Wang works on causal inference and causal machine learning, and holds a Canada Research Chair in Causal Machine Learning. His recent research develops estimators robust to unmeasured confounding, methods using instrumental variables, negative controls, and proximal inference, and high-dimensional and nonparametric approaches to estimating causal effects. He studies mediation, semiparametric efficiency, and the integration of causal reasoning with machine learning, with applications in biomedicine and genetics, aiming to draw reliable causal conclusions from complex observational data.

faculty.name: Stanislav Volgushev
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Volgushev works on time series, nonparametric statistics, and large-scale inference. His recent research develops methods for high-dimensional and dependent data, including quantile and copula-based approaches, extreme value analysis, and distributed inference that aggregates estimates across many machines. He studies asymptotic theory for weakly dependent processes, change-point and structural analysis, and resampling methods, providing rigorous guarantees for statistical procedures applied to complex temporal and spatial data arising in modern applications.

faculty.name: Lei Sun
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Sun develops statistical methods for genetics and genomics, working at the interface of biostatistics and statistical theory. Her recent research addresses genome-wide association analysis, multiple hypothesis testing, and robust and rank-based methods for detecting genetic associations. She studies quality control, pleiotropy, gene-environment interaction, and analysis of the X chromosome, along with methods for combining evidence across studies, translating rigorous statistical ideas into practical tools for reliable discovery in large-scale human genetic data.

faculty.name: Dehan Kong
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Kong develops statistical methods for complex, high-dimensional biomedical data, with emphasis on neuroimaging. His recent work builds tensor and functional data methods, dimension-reduction and regression techniques for imaging and genetics, and approaches integrating causal inference and machine learning in health applications. He studies scalable estimation for structured high-dimensional objects and methods for brain-imaging biomarkers, aiming to extract interpretable signals from massive, richly structured datasets relevant to neuroscience and precision medicine.

faculty.name: Jessica Gronsbell
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Gronsbell develops statistical machine learning methods for large-scale biomedical data, particularly electronic health records. Her recent research advances semi-supervised and weakly-supervised learning that exploits abundant unlabeled data alongside scarce expert labels, robust evaluation of risk-prediction models, and phenotyping using clinical text and natural language processing. She studies efficient inference when gold-standard labels are limited, and methods for digital and data-driven health, bridging biostatistics and machine learning to make real-world clinical data usable for reliable prediction.

faculty.name: Murat Erdogdu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Erdogdu works on the theoretical foundations of machine learning at the intersection of optimization, statistics, and probability. His recent research analyzes sampling algorithms and Langevin-type dynamics, high-dimensional asymptotics of estimators, and the optimization and generalization behavior of neural networks, including feature learning. He studies stochastic gradient methods, non-convex optimization, and the statistical limits of learning, developing rigorous analyses that explain when and why modern learning and sampling algorithms succeed in high dimensions.

faculty.name: Usman Khan
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: IEEE Fellow. Research in optimization, control theory, machine learning, multi-agent robotics, and foundation model scalability and interpretability.

faculty.name: Jose Bento
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in distributed optimization, graphical models, graph matching, network theory, and bioinformatics (antibiotic resistance, genetic networks). Amazon Scholar with Amazon Robotics.

faculty.name: Emily Prud'hommeaux
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in NLP and automatic speech recognition for low-resource and endangered languages, and language in autism and communication disorders. Giannino Family Sesquicentennial Assistant Professor 2020-2024, promoted 2024.

faculty.name: Howard Straubing
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in theory of computation, focusing on connections among logic, automata, and computational complexity. Algebraic and model-theoretic approaches to circuit complexity.

faculty.name: Aaron Stump
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science; John R. and Pamela Egan Chair
faculty.summary: John R. and Pamela Egan Chair (joined Summer 2024). Research in computational logic, programming languages theory, formal verification, and type theory.

faculty.name: Ilya Volkovich
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in computational complexity theory, algebraic complexity, derandomization and randomness in computation, cryptography, and computational learning theory.

faculty.name: Hsin-Hao Su
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in distributed graph algorithms, parallel and massively parallel computation (MPC), combinatorial optimization (matching, clustering, routing), and biologically inspired algorithms.

faculty.name: Donglai Wei
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: NSF CAREER awardee (2023). Research in computer vision and ML for connectomics -- reconstructing brain wiring diagrams from 3D microscopy images. Leads the BC Computer Vision Lab.

faculty.name: Nam Wook Kim
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in data visualization and HCI, focusing on accessible visualization, LLM-based design feedback, narrative visualization, and visualization literacy. PhD from Harvard.

faculty.name: Yuan Yuan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in multisensory and generative AI (vision, AIoT, language/LLMs, medical data), AI for medicine and health (digital biomarker discovery, Parkinson's detection), and trustworthy/safe AI.

faculty.name: Jessica Finocchiaro
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in theoretical machine learning, algorithmic economics, property elicitation, fairness and algorithmic discrimination, and objective function design. Joined September 2024.

faculty.name: Francisco Marmolejo
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in applied modeling, algorithms, and AI for societally-facing challenges including public health and access to financial services. Faculty Associate at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center. DPhil from Oxford. Joined January 2025.

faculty.name: Ethan Baxter
faculty.title: Professor

His work integrates isotope geochemistry, field geology, petrology, and numerical modeling across global field sites.

faculty.name: Mark D. Behn
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates active tectonic and magmatic processes using geophysical techniques to understand rock and ice deformation, melt generation, and volcanic activity in glacial, marine, and terrestrial environments. His group develops geodynamic models addressing faulting, mantle convection, ice-sheet response to climate change, and earthquake and volcanic hazards.

faculty.name: Seth C. Kruckenberg
faculty.title: Associate Professor and Associate Chair
faculty.summary: Investigates how rock properties and pressure-temperature conditions affect petrofabric development and lithospheric deformation, using a multi-disciplinary approach combining field mapping, electron backscatter diffraction, geochronology, and magnetic fabric studies across diverse orogenic systems.

faculty.name: Yi Ming
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Physical climate scientist who investigates how Earth's climate system operates, with particular focus on aerosol-monsoon interactions and regional precipitation patterns under climate change, using climate models and observations across scales.

faculty.name: Hilary Palevsky
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how the ocean absorbs atmospheric carbon dioxide through biological, chemical, and physical processes, combining field measurements, autonomous sensor data, satellite observations, and climate models to improve understanding of ocean carbon cycling.

faculty.name: Juliet Ryan-Davis
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates igneous and ore-forming processes with emphasis on subduction zones, integrating geological field observations with geochemistry, geochronology, and petrologic modeling to understand crustal-scale interactions and mineral formation over time.

faculty.name: Jeremy Shakun
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Director of Undergraduate Studies
faculty.summary: Paleoclimatologist who uses the geologic record to decipher the patterns and mechanisms of past changes in climate and ice sheets on decade to million-year time scales, analyzing geochemical records and developing paleoclimate datasets to understand climate sensitivity and ice-sheet dynamics.

faculty.name: Noah P. Snyder
faculty.title: Professor and Department Chair
faculty.summary: Studies how rivers respond to environmental changes by connecting high-resolution elevation data with field measurements, focusing on river management challenges that balance human needs such as water supply and flood control with ecological functions like fish migration.

faculty.name: Laura J. Steinberg
faculty.title: Professor; Executive Director, Schiller Institute for Integrated Science and Society
faculty.summary: Focuses on infrastructure management, disaster preparedness and response, and environmental modeling, drawing on a background in environmental and civil engineering and prior service as an engineering dean and EPA advisor.

faculty.name: Hanqin Tian
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Global Change Ecology & Earth System Modeling
faculty.summary: Earth system scientist studying the Earth as a complex, interconnected system, focusing on how the terrestrial biosphere interacts with atmospheric and climate systems. Employs modeling, satellite data, and ground observations to examine biogeochemical cycles and their responses to climate change and human activities.

faculty.name: Xingchen (Tony) Wang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: His lab investigates biogeochemical cycles in modern and ancient oceans using stable isotope analysis, with applications toward understanding Earth's habitability and the evolution of life.

faculty.name: Kat Wilson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how sedimentary processes in modern and ancient coastal systems respond to climate-driven changes, with particular focus on storm impacts and sea-level fluctuations, integrating morphodynamic analysis with coastal hazard assessment and community resilience strategies.

faculty.name: Elizabeth Blanton

faculty.name: Michael Mendillo

faculty.name: Toshi Nishimura

faculty.name: Dillon Brout

faculty.name: Emily Cunningham
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Dark matter in the Milky Way. Using stellar kinematics and galactic archaeology to constrain the Milky Way's dark matter distribution.

faculty.name: Chuanfei Dong
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Computational space plasma physics. Solar wind interaction with planets, Mars atmospheric escape, magnetospheric physics, and exoplanetary space environments.

faculty.name: Scarlett Bellamy
faculty.title: Professor and Chair
faculty.summary: Research focuses on evaluating intervention efficacy in longitudinal behavioral modification trials, particularly interested in applying this methodology to address health disparities for outcomes including HIV/AIDS, cardiovascular disease, and health-promoting behaviors.

faculty.name: Alexa S. Beiser
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Howard J. Cabral

faculty.name: Anita L. DeStefano

faculty.name: Michael P. LaValley
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Ching-Ti Liu
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Chunyu Liu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on assessing risk factors for cardiovascular disease and Alzheimer's disease, with leadership roles on multiple NIH grants and a specialization in statistical genetics for omics data analysis.

faculty.name: Kathryn L. Lunetta
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Yorghos Tripodis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Applied statistician who collaborates with researchers in medicine and public health to address scientific questions with appropriate statistical methods, with expertise in longitudinal data analysis and health disparities research. Serves as Director of Statistics and Data Management for the Framingham Heart Study and the BU Alzheimer's Disease and CTE Center.

faculty.name: Janice M. Weinberg
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the Master of Science in Clinical Research (MSCR) program, has served as lead statistical editor for the Journal of the American Heart Association, and regularly serves on Data Safety Monitoring Committees for clinical trials.

faculty.name: Helen E. Jenkins
faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Sara Lodi
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Work centers on causal inference methods for observational studies using big data and improving statistical analysis of clinical trials, applied primarily to infectious diseases (HIV, hepatitis C, tuberculosis) and substance use disorder.

faculty.name: Gina Marie Peloso
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Work focuses on statistical genetics, identification of common genetic variants through GWAS with complex cardiovascular traits, and studying rare genetic variation's role in blood lipid levels, Alzheimer's disease, and clinically meaningful applications like risk prediction and therapeutic targets.

faculty.name: Qiong Yang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for genetic studies, including modeling multivariate phenotypes, rare variants analysis, family-based association tests, and multiple testing problems. Creator of the GWAF R package for family-based genome-wide analyses and collaborator on Framingham Heart Study projects.

faculty.name: Huimin Cheng
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans LLMs, machine learning, statistical network analysis, deep learning, and causal inference, with applied collaborations across biophysics, political science, smart grids, public health/bioinformatics, and smart cities.

faculty.name: Wei Jin
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Jungwun Lee
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Haolin Li
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops and applies advanced statistical methods for clinical trials, survival analysis, machine learning, and epidemiologic studies, bridging statistical methodology and real-world healthcare applications.

faculty.name: Shariq Mohammed
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Prasad Patil
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on machine learning in public health and statistical methods for reproducibility, including techniques for combining data from and/or models trained in multiple studies to improve generalizability of predictive models.

faculty.name: Fatema Shafie Khorassani
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Work centers on data integration methods for time-to-event outcomes and on statistical methods for surrogate endpoints, with collaborative projects examining health disparities in cancer, substance abuse, and stroke.

faculty.name: Lukas M. Weber
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on statistical genomics and biomedical data science, focusing on developing statistical and computational methods for high-throughput genomic data — particularly spatial transcriptomics and single-cell platforms — applied to neuroscience and cancer biology.

faculty.name: Kate Saenko
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Director of the Computer Vision and Learning Group. Research focuses on adaptive machine learning, vision and language understanding, and deep learning.

faculty.name: Adam Smith

faculty.name: Leonid Reyzin

faculty.name: Marco Gaboardi
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Sharon Goldberg
faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Vasiliki Kalavri
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Boqing Gong
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Deepti Ghadiyaram
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Renato Mancuso
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Directs BU's Cyber-Physical Systems Lab, focusing on controllable timeliness in safety-critical applications within complex accelerator-enabled embedded systems, with work spanning hybrid CPU+FPGA platforms for robotics and autonomous vehicles.

faculty.name: Hongwei Xi
faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Ankush Das
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Rich West
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Specializes in principled system design for embedded and real-time computing. Current work focuses on Quest, a real-time OS for multicore processors, and Quest-V, a secure separation kernel for predictable execution of sandboxed systems.

faculty.name: John Byers
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Emily Whiting
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the Shape Design & Computation Lab, conducting research in computer graphics with emphasis on computational fabrication and architectural geometry. Serves as Director of Ph.D. Admissions.

faculty.name: Assaf Kfoury
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on applications of mathematical logic within computer science, including programming languages and formal methods. Teaches principles of programming languages and formal methods.

faculty.name: Leonid Levin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works in theoretical computer science, particularly complexity theory and the nature of randomness in computation, addressing fundamental questions including the P vs. NP problem. Joined BU in 1980.

faculty.name: Stan Sclaroff
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Jonathan Appavoo
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on operating system design and cloud computing architectures, including projects such as EbbRT and MultiLibOS. Joined BU in 2009 after working as a Research Staff Member at IBM Research.

faculty.name: Gary Benson
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biology and Computer Science
faculty.summary: Develops algorithms and software tools for the detection and analysis of novel patterns and repeats in DNA and RNA sequences, emphasizing effective, efficient, and user-friendly tools for biological sequence analysis.

faculty.name: Ed Chien
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Kyle Deeds
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Nathan Klein
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops fast, approximately optimal algorithms for computationally hard tasks including the traveling salesperson problem, using combinatorial and probabilistic techniques along with rounding methods.

faculty.name: John Liagouris
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Andrea Lincoln
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Aaron Mueller

faculty.name: Sabrina Neuman

faculty.name: Alexander Poremba

faculty.name: Alyssa Novak
faculty.title: Research Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Solesne Bourguin
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Director of Graduate Admissions for Statistics
faculty.summary: Works on stochastic analysis and probability theory, including Malliavin calculus, Stein's method for limit theorems, free probability on Wigner space, and quantitative fluctuation analysis for interacting particle systems. Studies Gaussian approximations on Hilbert-Poisson spaces and regularity of laws via PDE methods. Co-author of 'Four Moments Theorems on Markov Chaos' (Annals of Probability, 2019). Organizes the BU Statistics and Probability Seminar Series.

faculty.name: Michael Salins
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Stochastic Partial Differential Equations and Large Deviations
faculty.summary: Studies qualitative behavior of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations, including explosion/non-explosion criteria, metastability theory for stochastic reaction-diffusion equations, and rare event simulation via importance sampling. Proved non-explosion for the stochastic heat equation at the critical growth regime, resolving an open problem. Member of both Applied Mathematics and Probability & Statistics research groups.

faculty.name: Guangqu Zheng
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on stochastic analysis, particularly Malliavin calculus, Stein's method, and stochastic partial differential equations. Develops probabilistic tools such as Gaussian Poincare inequalities and central limit theorems for random fields driven by Gaussian, Levy, and fractional noise. Applications to Anderson model, nonlinear Schrodinger equations, and wave equations. Joined BU in Summer 2024. 28+ publications in top probability journals.

faculty.name: Samuel Isaacson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops particle-based stochastic reaction-diffusion models for cellular processes, including the Convergent Reaction-Diffusion Master Equation (CRDME) framework that overcomes mesh-refinement issues of standard RDME. Studies mean-field limits connecting stochastic particle models to reaction-diffusion PDEs. Applications to T cell receptor signaling, antibody-antigen binding, and immune cell processes. Collaborates frequently with Konstantinos Spiliopoulos.

faculty.name: Konstantinos Spiliopoulos
faculty.title: Professor; Director of Statistics
faculty.summary: Works on probability theory and stochastic processes, including multiscale diffusions, large deviations principles, metastability analysis, and interacting particle systems. Also develops mathematical foundations for deep learning models and algorithms. Research spans rigorous probability theory alongside computational methods. Author of 2025 AMS textbook on mathematical foundations of deep learning. NSF CAREER award, Simons Fellow in Mathematics (2020).

faculty.name: Yves Atchade
faculty.title: Professor; Duan Family Faculty Fellow of Data Science
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical foundations for Markov chain Monte Carlo methods in high-dimensional settings, studying convergence properties, scalability, and statistical optimality of sampling algorithms. Research on asynchronous MCMC and quasi-Bayesian inference bridges computational statistics and probability theory. Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics. Editorial board service for Bernoulli and JASA Theory & Methods.

faculty.name: Mark Kon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Quantum Probability and Statistical Learning Theory
faculty.summary: Research includes quantum probability and quantum information, statistical learning theory for neural networks, and complexity theory. Also works on stochastic process anomaly detection via Karhunen-Loeve expansions. Leads the Stochastic Machine Learning Group at BU. Editorial board of Neural Networks. PhD from MIT.

faculty.name: Yves Atchade
faculty.title: Professor; Duan Family Faculty Fellow of Data Science
faculty.summary: Develops fast, scalable Markov chain Monte Carlo methods for high-dimensional Bayesian inference, including asynchronous MCMC samplers and quasi-Bayesian approaches with spike-and-slab priors. Applies these methods to large discrete graphical models and environmental remote sensing problems. Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.

faculty.name: Luis Carvalho
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on Bayesian inference for structured, high-dimensional discrete spaces, including centroid estimation, objective Bayes variable selection, and MCMC methods in constrained discrete structures. Applications include network community detection via degree-corrected stochastic blockmodels, computational biology (GWAS, glyco-proteomics), and urban crime modeling.

faculty.name: Amiremad Ghassami
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for causal inference and causal discovery under real-world data challenges including unobserved confounders, measurement error, and missing/censored values. Draws on tools from semiparametric and nonparametric statistics, machine learning, and information theory. PhD from UIUC (Information Theory), postdoc at Johns Hopkins.

faculty.name: Jonathan Huggins
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Scalable Bayesian Methods and Machine Learning
faculty.summary: Develops statistically principled and scalable machine learning methods with a focus on reliable uncertainty quantification under model misspecification and approximate inference. Applied work targets ecological/Earth science forecasting and genomic data analysis. NSF CAREER award (2024), Blackwell-Rosenbluth Award (2023). Joint appointment with Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences.

faculty.name: Judith Lok
faculty.title: Professor; Associate Director of Statistics
faculty.summary: Develops causal inference methods for survival analysis and mediation, including organic direct/indirect effects and structural nested models for continuous and discrete time. Applied work focuses on HIV/AIDS treatment effects, CD4 trajectories, and clinical trial designs (LAGO). Radcliffe Institute Fellow (2023-2024), writing textbook 'Causal Inference: A Statistics Playground.' Previously 13 years on Harvard Biostatistics faculty.

faculty.name: Debarghya Mukherjee
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: High-Dimensional Statistics and Machine Learning Theory
faculty.summary: Studies complex statistical models including deep neural networks in high dimensions, with work on algorithmic fairness, domain adaptation, and domain generalization under constrained classification/regression settings. Also works on deconvolution under vanishing noise. Joint appointment with Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences. Recent papers at NeurIPS 2025.

faculty.name: Konstantinos Spiliopoulos
faculty.title: Professor; Director of Statistics
faculty.sub_field: Probability, Stochastic Processes, and Deep Learning Theory
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of probability, statistics, and machine learning, developing mathematical foundations for deep learning models and algorithms. Research includes multiscale stochastic systems, Monte Carlo methods for rare events, interacting particle systems, and uncertainty quantification in scientific machine learning. Author of 2025 AMS textbook on mathematical foundations of deep learning. NSF CAREER award, Simons Fellow in Mathematics (2020).

faculty.name: Emily Stephen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Statistical Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Develops statistical models for neural signals across spatial scales from spikes to EEG/MEG. Builds models incorporating prior knowledge about brain-state features to bridge micro-scale neural dynamics with macro-scale biomarkers of disease. Advises PhD students in Statistics and Graduate Program for Neuroscience.

faculty.name: Uri Eden
faculty.title: Professor; Associate Chair
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for analyzing neural spiking activity using point process models and state-space estimation algorithms. Builds Bayesian adaptive filters to dynamically model neural representations and reconstruct biological signals in real time. Applications include hippocampal navigation, motor cortex decoding, and seizure dynamics. PhD from Harvard, NSF CAREER award.

faculty.name: Mark Kon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Machine Learning and Statistical Learning Theory
faculty.summary: Leads the Stochastic Machine Learning Group at BU. Research spans statistical learning theory, neural networks, quantum probability and information, bioinformatics (gene regulatory networks, cancer classification), and wavelet signal processing. Recent work on multilevel stochastic optimization for medical data imputation. PhD from MIT. ~100 publications.

faculty.name: Brian Cleary
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computing & Data Sciences
faculty.summary: Develops algorithms at the interface of ML and experimental biology for scalable genetic screening and modeling gene expression.

faculty.name: Ignaty Leshchiner
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Medicine
faculty.summary: Research in computational methods for studying cancer evolution, tumor heterogeneity, and clonal dynamics from genomic data.

faculty.name: Chao Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computational Biomedicine
faculty.summary: Research in computational methods integrating statistical ML with genomics for biomedical discovery.

faculty.name: Xiaoling Zhang
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Medicine and Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Research integrating statistical genetics, systems biology, and machine learning for studying complex traits.

faculty.name: Adriana Tomic
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Engineering and Virology, Immunology & Microbiology
faculty.summary: Research applying computational approaches and ML to systems immunology and multi-omics data integration.

faculty.name: Douglas Densmore
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Research in computational approaches to synthetic biology, including design automation and databases for DNA assembly (CIDAR Lab).

faculty.name: Charles DeLisi
faculty.title: Metcalf Professor of Biomedical Engineering and Physics
faculty.summary: Pioneer of the Human Genome Project. Research in computational biology, systems biology, protein-protein interactions, and genomics.

faculty.name: Pankaj Mehta
faculty.title: Professor of Physics
faculty.summary: Uses statistical physics and ML including transformer models for single-cell data to understand emergent collective behaviors in biological systems.

faculty.name: Yannis Paschalidis
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor of Engineering
faculty.sub_field: Optimization, machine learning, healthcare systems, computational biology
faculty.summary: Director of the Hariri Institute for Computing. Develops AI, machine learning, and optimization methods for healthcare delivery, precision medicine, and pandemic preparedness. NSF, NIH, and ARO-funded research.

faculty.name: Eric Kolaczyk
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Statistical methodology, network science, data science
faculty.summary: Research in statistical methodology for complex networks and high-dimensional data, with applications in neuroscience, genomics, and social systems.

requirements.admission_model: Umbrella admission with 3 lab rotations first year

faculty.name: Michael Blower
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies mitosis, transcription, and chromatin structure, investigating how chromosomes and the cell-division machinery are regulated. Serves as the department's Graduate Program Director.

faculty.name: Mikel Garcia-Marcos
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates G protein signaling circuits and how their dysregulation contributes to the molecular basis of disease.

faculty.name: Alla Grishok
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies gene regulation by RNA and chromatin, including small RNA pathways and their role in controlling genome expression.

faculty.name: David A. Harris
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Department Chair whose lab studies the molecular basis of Alzheimer's disease and prion diseases, focusing on protein misfolding and neurodegeneration.

faculty.name: Xaralabos Varelas
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates Hippo-YAP/TAZ signaling in lung epithelial biology and cancer, studying how these pathways control tissue growth and tumorigenesis.

faculty.name: Mohsan Saeed
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: NEIDL investigator studying the role of viral proteases in shaping virus-host interactions during RNA virus infection.

faculty.name: Nelson C. Lau
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies transposable elements and regulatory RNAs, investigating how small RNA pathways silence transposons and shape genome regulation.

faculty.name: Valentina Perissi
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the genomic regulation of metabolism and nuclear-mitochondrial communication in metabolic homeostasis.

faculty.name: Venetia Zachariou
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Department Chair investigating signal transduction and epigenetic mechanisms underlying CNS disorders, using genetic mouse models to study chronic pain, addiction, and depression and identify therapeutic targets.

faculty.name: Neil J. Ganem
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the molecular mechanisms of genome instability in cancer, using microscopy and genetic screens to identify tumor-suppression pathways and how cancer cells bypass them.

faculty.name: Rachel Litman Flynn
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the mechanisms regulating mammalian telomere maintenance and how cancer cells exploit telomere elongation pathways such as telomerase and ALT, aiming to identify novel therapeutic targets.

faculty.name: Olga Gursky
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses biophysical methods to study the stability and remodeling of plasma lipoproteins in cardiovascular health, and protein misfolding and amyloid aggregation of apolipoproteins.

faculty.name: William J. Lehman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structural mechanisms of actin-containing thin filaments and thin-filament-linked regulation of muscle contraction, using electron microscopy and computational simulation.

faculty.name: Valentina Sabino
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the neurobiology of addiction and stress-related disorders, with emphasis on neurochemical systems driving excessive alcohol consumption, anxiety, and depression.

faculty.name: Rachel Fearns
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Department Chair studying how non-segmented negative-strand RNA viruses (RSV, measles, Ebola, Nipah) control transcription and genome replication, aiming to develop broad-spectrum antiviral targets.

faculty.name: John H. Connor
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how viruses hijack host cellular machinery and evade immune defenses, applying that knowledge to develop improved antiviral molecules and vaccines.

faculty.name: Elke Mühlberger
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies highly pathogenic RNA viruses, particularly filoviruses like Ebola and Marburg, focusing on genome replication/transcription mechanisms and host immune responses using primary and iPSC-derived human cells.

faculty.name: Rahm Gummuluru
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates interactions of HIV with myeloid cells such as dendritic cells and macrophages, including innate immune detection, chronic inflammation, and nanoparticle-based therapeutics.

faculty.name: Florian Douam
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses advanced human cell systems and humanized mouse models to study protective and pathological immune responses to RNA viruses, developing vaccines and immunotherapies for respiratory viruses and arboviruses like dengue and Zika.

faculty.name: Robert Davey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: NEIDL Director developing small-molecule and antibody-based treatments for hemorrhagic fever viruses such as Ebola and Marburg by targeting viral and host proteins required for infection.

faculty.name: Venetia Zachariou
faculty.title: Professor and Chair
faculty.summary: Edward Avedisian Professor and Chair who studies the signal transduction and epigenetic mechanisms of neurological disorders and their treatment, using genetic mouse models, genomic assays, and brain biochemistry, with a focus on novel therapeutic targets for chronic pain.

faculty.name: David H. Farb
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates pharmacological treatments for cognitive disorders by studying how drugs affect hippocampal function, integrating electrophysiology, behavior, and molecular techniques to examine neuroactive steroids and cognitive enhancers for memory deficits in aging, Alzheimer's, schizophrenia, and autism.

faculty.name: Shelley J. Russek
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how the dynamic regulation of neurotransmitter receptors in the brain shapes nervous system development and contributes to neurological disease, developing therapeutic approaches for epilepsy and molecular tools to monitor neural network activity.

faculty.name: Valentina Sabino
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the neurobiological mechanisms underlying addiction and stress-related disorders, with emphasis on alcohol abuse, using behavioral neuroscience, neuropharmacology, neuroanatomy, biochemistry, and molecular biology to develop therapeutic interventions.

faculty.name: Pietro Cottone
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the neurobiological mechanisms of motivated behaviors, focusing on how stress contributes to compulsive eating and food dependence, to identify biological bases and potential treatments for eating disorders, obesity, and related anxiety and depression.

faculty.name: Nikolaos P. Daskalakis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the molecular, cellular, and genomic pathways linking stress to brain function and dysfunction, combining functional genomics with machine learning to study epigenetic mechanisms of stress-related disorders such as PTSD and identify therapeutic targets.

faculty.name: Philipp Mews
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the intersection of neuroepigenetics, metabolism, and neural plasticity in the adult brain, with emphasis on substance use disorders, examining how diet and drugs of abuse alter chromatin dynamics and gene expression.

faculty.name: Vidhya Kumaresan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates neuronal activity-dependent plasticity and its relevance to brain disorders, focusing on how psychostimulant addiction alters neural circuits and the lasting changes that drive drug relapse, with applications to PTSD and traumatic memory.

faculty.name: Weiming Xia
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on Alzheimer's disease research including target identification, characterization, validation, and early-stage drug development, quantifying pathological proteins such as amyloid-beta and Tau and developing mass spectrometry approaches for disease biomarkers.

faculty.name: Julia TCW
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates Alzheimer's disease mechanisms using induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models, examining how genetic risk factors like APOE4 affect human brain cells, and developing CNS cell culture systems and 3D brain models for drug screening.

faculty.name: Clint L. Makino
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the molecular mechanisms of visual signal transduction in retinal rods, focusing on how cGMP links photon capture by rhodopsin to cellular responses and the role of guanylyl cyclase activating proteins (GCAPs) in regulating vision.

faculty.name: Christopher V. Gabel
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies neurophotonics in simple systems, using optical techniques in the nervous system of C. elegans, including laser-based neuronal surgery and regeneration, calcium imaging of brain activity, and the effects of volatile anesthetics on nervous system function.

faculty.name: Neil J. Ganem
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the mechanisms underlying genome instability in cancer, examining how tumor suppressor pathways (such as Hippo) limit abnormal cells and identifying genetic adaptations that allow cancer cells to proliferate despite chromosomal abnormalities.

faculty.name: Rachel Litman Flynn
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the mechanisms regulating mammalian telomere maintenance and how defects contribute to premature aging and cancer, investigating how cancer cells achieve immortality through telomere elongation pathways to develop novel therapeutic strategies.

faculty.name: Hui Feng
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies cancer development and progression, focusing on identifying novel genes and pathways essential for MYC/MYCN-driven tumor initiation and progression using zebrafish models and human genomics, targeting T-lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia, breast cancer, and neuroblastoma.

faculty.name: Christopher W. Akey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structural and functional mechanisms of large cellular protein complexes, including the nuclear pore complex, ribosome-channel complexes, apoptosomes, and secretion systems, using cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, and computational modeling.

faculty.name: Esther Bullitt
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses electron microscopy and image analysis to understand how protein structures enable biological function, studying how adhesion pili aid pathogenic bacterial survival, viral impacts on cells, and type III secretion systems in bacteria.

faculty.name: Olga Gursky
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: A leading expert in lipoprotein biophysics and structural thermodynamics of proteins, focusing on the molecular mechanisms of function of plasma lipoproteins (Good and Bad Cholesterol) and their protein constituents in health and disease.

faculty.name: William J. Lehman
faculty.title: Professor and Vice Chair
faculty.summary: Studies the assembly and function of actin-containing thin filaments in striated and smooth muscles, examining how tropomyosin regulates protein interactions and abnormal filament behavior in muscle disease using electron microscopy and molecular dynamics simulations.

faculty.name: C. James McKnight
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the folding, function, and dynamics of proteins with emphasis on protein stability and molecular motion, using the villin headpiece domain (HP35) as a model system studied by NMR spectroscopy.

faculty.name: Assen Marintchev
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the molecular mechanisms of eukaryotic translation initiation and its regulation, focusing on how cells control protein synthesis through translation initiation complexes and the integrated stress response, with applications to cancer and neurodegenerative diseases.

faculty.name: Morgan Gilman
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how bacteria regulate the multi-protein complexes involved in cell wall synthesis, using structural biology, biochemistry, and bacterial genetics to identify vulnerabilities in peptidoglycan production for developing treatments against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

faculty.name: Zhen Y. Jiang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how neutrophils and metabolic processes contribute to obesity-related inflammation and vascular dysfunction, focusing on obesity-related systemic inflammation, vascular aging, and lipid metabolism regulation through molecular signaling pathways.

faculty.name: Shannon Fisher
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates craniofacial defects affecting formation of the face and skull using zebrafish as a model organism, studying skeletal development and birth defects through genetic analysis, enhancer identification, and advanced imaging.

faculty.name: Stavroula Chrysanthopoulou
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics, Director of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Dr. Chrysanthopoulou's research centers on microsimulation modeling, with a focus on complex predictive models applied in medical decision making, calibration and predictive accuracy methods, causal inference, missing data, and high performance computing techniques. She developed the MILC model for lung cancer and published an accompanying R package.

faculty.name: Fenghai Duan
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: His research interests include high-throughput data analysis, bioinformatics, diagnostic test and biomarker evaluation, and radio(geno)mics. He works on methodological and multidisciplinary research in cancer clinical trials, medical imaging, and radiogenomics.

faculty.name: Ani Eloyan
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics, Vice Chair of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Statistical Imaging, Dimension Reduction, Machine Learning
faculty.summary: Dr. Eloyan works on semi-parametric likelihood based methods for matrix decompositions, statistical analyses of brain images, and integrating complex data structures for health care data. Her applied work spans MS lesion modeling, Alzheimer's disease, fMRI, epilepsy, and autism.

faculty.name: Constantine Gatsonis
faculty.title: Henry Ledyard Goddard University Professor of Statistical Sciences, Director of the Center for Biostatistics and Health Data Science
faculty.sub_field: Diagnostic Test Evaluation, Comparative Effectiveness Research, Bayesian Methods
faculty.summary: Dr. Gatsonis is a leading authority on the evaluation of diagnostic and screening tests, focusing on methods for applying and synthesizing evidence on diagnostic tests in medicine and developing methods for Comparative Effectiveness Research in diagnosis, prediction, and radiomics. He is the founding Chair of Biostatistics and Network Statistician for ECOG-ACRIN, having served as lead statistician for landmark trials including DMIST, NLST, and TMIST.

faculty.name: Roee Gutman
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Bayesian Methods, Causal Inference, Data Linkage
faculty.summary: Dr. Gutman's research focuses on Bayesian data analysis, missing data, matching, file linkage, causal inference, and bioinformatics. His work develops techniques for valid causal inferences from observational studies and handles challenges of linking administrative and clinical data without unique identifiers.

faculty.name: Larry Han
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics and Data Science
faculty.sub_field: Causal Inference, Machine Learning, Real-World Data
faculty.summary: His research centers on creating innovative statistical and machine learning methods to utilize real-world data to improve public health and clinical medicine, focusing on developing robust and targeted estimators for learning causal effects from large-scale observational studies and randomized trials.

faculty.name: Joseph W. Hogan
faculty.title: Carole and Lawrence Sirovich Professor of Public Health, Professor of Biostatistics, Chair of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: His research concerns the development of statistical methods for missing data, causal inference, and sensitivity analysis, with focus on applications in HIV/AIDS. He co-directs the Biostatistics Program for AMPATH in Kenya and supervises 2-3 PhD and masters students at any given time.

faculty.name: Rebecca Hubbard
faculty.title: Carl Kawaja and Wendy Holcombe Professor of Public Health, Professor of Biostatistics and Data Science
faculty.sub_field: Real-World Data, EHR Methods, Measurement Error
faculty.summary: Dr. Hubbard's research focuses on the development and application of methods to improve analyses using real world data sources including electronic health records (EHR) and medical claims data, addressing the messiness and complexity of real world data including informative observation schemes, phenotyping error, and error and missingness in confounders.

faculty.name: Youjin Lee
faculty.title: Manning Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Causal Inference, Social Networks, Evidence Synthesis
faculty.summary: Dr. Lee develops statistical and causal inference methods with applications to public health and social science, focusing on settings where standard assumptions like independence or no unmeasured confounding are violated. She works on causal methods for complex and dependent data and causal evidence synthesis.

faculty.name: Tao Liu
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Health Data Science, Clinical Decision-Making, Causal Inference
faculty.summary: His research interests are in the area of health data science and include clinical decision-making, incomplete data problems, causal inference, diagnostic testing, and design of clinical trials. He serves as Director of the Online Master's Program in Biostatistics.

faculty.name: Ying Ma
faculty.title: Edens Family Assistant Professor of Healthcare Communications and Technology, Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Statistical Genomics, Single-Cell Analysis, AI for Biology
faculty.summary: Her lab focuses on developing rigorous statistical learning and AI methods for high-dimensional genomics and genetics, with emphasis on single-cell RNA-seq, spatial omics, and clinical informatics. Highly motivated students with interests in statistics, machine learning, AI, or computational biology are warmly encouraged to reach out.

faculty.name: Anarina Murillo
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Her research sits at the intersection of statistics education and applied work in nutrition, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. She focuses on analyzing complex real-world data, particularly longitudinal data, and addressing issues like measurement error, while integrating community-engaged scholarship.

faculty.name: Arman Oganisian
faculty.title: Thomas J. and Alice M. Tisch Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Bayesian Nonparametrics, Causal Inference, Sequential Treatments
faculty.summary: His work centers on developing Bayesian nonparametric methods for causal estimation, focusing on sequential treatment decisions for chronic diseases like cancer, HIV, and osteoporosis. He provides an advising page for ScM or PhD students at Brown considering working with him.

faculty.name: George Papandonatos
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Hierarchical Modeling, Behavioral Medicine, Population Genetics
faculty.summary: Dr. Papandonatos is a Professor of Biostatistics with research interests in hierarchical modeling of continuous and discrete data and population genetics related to smoking and nicotine dependence. He has extensive collaborations in Behavioral Medicine and Epidemiology around lifestyle interventions and environmental exposures.

faculty.name: Alice Paul
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics, Director of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Optimization Algorithms, Machine Learning, Data Science
faculty.summary: Dr. Paul is interested in algorithms, optimization, data science, and education, with research focusing on the design and analysis of optimization algorithms underlying machine learning, with applications including clustering, variable selection, risk models, and bike-share or other shared mobility systems.

faculty.name: Christopher Schmid
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: His research focuses on methods and applications for meta-analysis, particularly Bayesian methods and software, on predictive models derived from combining data from different sources, and on clinical trials, particularly N-of-1 trials.

faculty.name: Jon Steingrimsson
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Machine Learning, Survival Analysis, Causal Inference
faculty.summary: Dr. Steingrimsson focuses on generalizing or transporting treatment effects or risk prediction models to different populations and has developed machine learning algorithms for risk prediction with censored data and for identifying treatment effect heterogeneity. He works with the ECOG-ACRIN cancer research group.

faculty.name: Zhijin (Jean) Wu
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Dr. Wu's research focuses on developing statistical methods and software for high throughput technologies such as DNA microarrays, second generation sequencing, and high throughput screening assays.

faculty.name: Corwin Zigler
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics, Director of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Environmental Health, Spatial Causal Inference, Bayesian Methods
faculty.summary: Dr. Zigler's research centers on quantitative methodology for assessing health impacts of environmental and climate exposures, with statistical emphasis on causal inference, particularly spatially-indexed data, spatial confounding, interference networks, physical process modeling, and Bayesian methodology.

faculty.name: Alyssa Bilinski
faculty.title: Peterson Family Assistant Professor of Health Policy, Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Health Policy Modeling, Infectious Disease, Maternal Health
faculty.summary: Her research lies at the intersection of policy modeling and evaluation, focusing on developing novel methods to support decision-making to improve population health, with applications in infectious disease and maternal health. She has collaborated with state, local, and federal public health officials to translate research into practice.

faculty.name: Lorin Crawford
faculty.title: Distinguished Senior Fellow in Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Interpretable Machine Learning, Statistical Genetics, Genomics
faculty.summary: The central aim of his research program is to build interpretable machine learning algorithms to study how genetic effects and gene-by-environmental interactions contribute to the architecture of complex traits and disease progression. He is also a Principal Researcher at Microsoft Research and has received a Sloan Fellowship, Packard Fellowship, and COPSS Emerging Leader Award.

faculty.name: Sana Raoof
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics, Assistant Professor of Radiation Oncology
faculty.summary: Dr. Raoof holds dual appointments as Assistant Professor of Biostatistics and Assistant Professor of Radiation Oncology at Brown. She holds an MD from Harvard Medical School and a BA from Harvard College. Her VIVO profile is minimal with no detailed research statement listed.

faculty.name: Argie Veroniki
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics, Associate Professor of Health Services, Policy and Practice
faculty.sub_field: Evidence Synthesis, Network Meta-Analysis, Evidence-Based Medicine
faculty.summary: Dr. Veroniki is an Associate Professor at the Center for Evidence Synthesis in Health at Brown's School of Public Health. Her work focuses on optimizing the processes of evidence-based medicine and statistical modeling for evidence synthesis, including network meta-analysis. She holds a Cochrane Methods Group role.

faculty.name: Jeremy Warner
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Clinical Informatics, Cancer Data Science, EHR Analysis
faculty.summary: Dr. Warner's research focuses on making sense of structured and unstructured EHR data and biomedical knowledge bases to improve cancer care. He works at the interface of data and healthcare and has contributed to clinical genomics standards, knowledge curation initiatives including HemOnc.org, and the COVID-19 and Cancer Consortium.

funding.note: Fully funded 5 yrs; first-year fellowship, no teaching required in year 1

requirements.admission_model: Faculty-match emphasized (applicants must name at least two faculty of interest)

faculty.name: Amy Greenwald
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Greenwald designs AI agents that interact effectively in multi-agent environments, drawing on AI, decision theory, game theory, and economics to enable agents to cooperate, compete, and trade with human and artificial counterparts.

faculty.name: Michael L. Littman
faculty.title: University Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Littman is a University Professor of Computer Science (and Associate Provost for AI) studying machine learning and decision making under uncertainty, with primary research in reinforcement learning.

faculty.name: Ellie Pavlick
faculty.title: Briger Family Distinguished Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Pavlick leads the LUNAR Lab, which aims to understand how language works and to build computational models that comprehend language similarly to humans, studying conceptual representations, reasoning, learning, and generalization, often collaborating with cognitive science, neuroscience, and philosophy.

faculty.name: Stephen Bach
faculty.title: Eliot Horowitz Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Bach researches machine learning that improves how humans teach and instruct computers, measuring success by the reduced effort non-specialists need to train effective models, with applications in information extraction and scientific discovery.

faculty.name: George D. Konidaris
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Konidaris aims to build generally intelligent robots that learn abstraction hierarchies enabling fast, goal-oriented planning, integrating machine learning, reinforcement learning, optimal control, and planning. He directs the Intelligent Robot Lab.

faculty.name: Chen Sun
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Sun studies computer vision, machine learning, and AI; his current work focuses on learning temporal dynamics from unlabeled videos and applying video-centric world models in robotics. He directs the PALM research lab.

faculty.name: Srinath Sridhar
faculty.title: John E. Savage Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Sridhar leads the Interactive 3D Vision & Learning Lab (IVL), building foundational methods for 3D and 4D visual understanding of objects, humans in motion, and human-object interactions.

faculty.name: Daniel C. Ritchie
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Ritchie works at the intersection of computer graphics and AI, developing data-driven methods for designing, synthesizing, and manipulating visual content, including neurosymbolic and procedural models for 3D shapes; he co-leads the Brown Visual Computing group.

faculty.name: Nora Ayanian
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Ayanian's work is in robotics with a focus on multi-robot systems, multi-agent coordination, and artificial intelligence. Her lab is the Autonomy, Control, and Teams (ACT) group.

faculty.name: Serena Booth
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Booth's research is in artificial intelligence, spanning reinforcement learning, human-computer interaction, and robotics.

faculty.name: Stefanie A. Tellex
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Tellex's research focuses on constructing robots that seamlessly use natural language to communicate with humans, using probabilistic methods and corpus-based training so robots can understand commands, ask clarifying questions, and request assistance.

faculty.name: Ugur Cetintemel
faculty.title: Khosrowshahi University Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Cetintemel works on data science and database/distributed systems, facilitating data management and analysis in resource-constrained environments, with recent focus on high-rate data streams and big-data, self-managing systems.

faculty.name: Malte Schwarzkopf
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Schwarzkopf studies computer systems with a focus on distributed systems, operating systems, and privacy-preserving systems; he leads the ETOS (Efficient and Trustworthy Operating Systems) group at Brown.

faculty.name: Nikos Vasilakis
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Vasilakis's research spans parallel and distributed systems, programming languages, and computer security, with recent focus on program analysis, transformation, and synthesis to automatically accelerate, secure, and correct modern systems with strong (often formal) guarantees.

faculty.name: Maurice P. Herlihy
faculty.title: An Wang Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Herlihy works on the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of concurrent and distributed systems, spanning multiprocessor synchronization, combinatorial topology, and blockchain/cryptocurrency technology.

faculty.name: Anna A. Lysyanskaya
faculty.title: James A. and Julie N. Brown Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Lysyanskaya studies cryptographic methods that protect individual privacy in digital contexts, with notable contributions in anonymous credentials and electronic cash systems.

faculty.name: Vasileios Kemerlis
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Kemerlis works on software, hardware, and systems security, developing defensive mechanisms across system layers from kernel-level protections against code-reuse attacks to user-space hardening, memory protection, and dynamic exploit detection.

faculty.name: Peihan Miao
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Miao's research spans cryptography, security, and theoretical computer science, with a focus on secure multi-party computation and bridging theory and practice in cryptography.

faculty.name: Roberto Tamassia
faculty.title: James A. and Julie N. Brown Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Tamassia's work focuses on algorithmic approaches to graph drawing/visualization and the design of efficient data structures, reflected in his authored textbooks on algorithms and data structures.

faculty.name: Shriram Krishnamurthi
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Krishnamurthi works at the intersection of programming languages, computing education, and cognitive engineering, incorporating human-factors and cognitive-science ideas to help people effectively learn abstractions. He leads the PL/Formal Methods, Computing Education, and Cognitive Engineering labs.

faculty.name: Sorin Istrail
faculty.title: James A. & Julie N. Brown Professor of Computational and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Istrail's lab conducts computational biology research focused on large-scale genomic analysis, including whole-genome shotgun assembly, sequencing, and understanding the logic of genomic regulatory elements.

faculty.name: Eli Upfal
faculty.title: Rush C. Hawkins Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Upfal's research focuses on the design and analysis of algorithms, particularly randomized algorithms and probabilistic analysis, with applications spanning optimization, networking, computational biology, and computational finance.

faculty.name: Philip Klein
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Klein develops efficient algorithms for fundamental graph and network problems, with particular emphasis on approximation algorithms for computationally difficult combinatorial optimization challenges.

faculty.name: Ellis Hershkowitz
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Hershkowitz is a theoretical computer scientist interested in the mathematical aspects of computation, especially graph-theoretic questions in approximation, online, and distributed algorithms and metric embeddings, focused on efficiently solving and approximating computationally challenging problems.

faculty.name: Suresh Venkatasubramanian
faculty.title: Professor of Data Science and Computer Science
faculty.summary: Venkatasubramanian directs the Center for Technological Responsibility (CNTR); his current research is in algorithmic fairness and the societal impact of automated decision-making systems, building on a background in algorithms, computational geometry, and machine learning.

faculty.name: Randall Balestriero
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Balestriero develops theoretical foundations of world models, self-supervised learning, and learnable signal processing for time-series, aiming for systems that are provably safe, sample-efficient, and real-world ready.

faculty.name: Yu Cheng
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Cheng focuses on the design and analysis of scalable and provably robust algorithms for machine learning, especially high-dimensional robust statistics, non-convex optimization, and learning with strategic agents.

faculty.name: Will Crichton
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Crichton works at the intersection of programming languages and human-computer interaction, building systems that help programmers use advanced languages effectively while grounding programming in human cognition and usability.

faculty.name: Diana Freed
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Data Science
faculty.summary: Freed directs the Sociotechnical Systems and Wellbeing Research lab, working at the intersection of HCI, security/privacy, and policy to improve online safety and wellbeing for vulnerable and marginalized populations (e.g., intimate partner violence, caregiving, digital health).

faculty.name: Kathi Fisler
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science (Research)
faculty.summary: Fisler investigates human learning and the effective organization of information and people; her work spans formal methods and verification through to computing education.

faculty.name: Jeff Huang
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Huang's research spans human-computer interaction and information retrieval; he is broadly interested in decoding user interactions to build novel applications.

faculty.name: David H. Laidlaw
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Laidlaw applies visualization, computational modeling, and computer graphics to scientific disciplines, focusing on visualizing complex multivalued multidimensional imaging data and comparing virtual versus non-virtual environments for research tasks.

faculty.name: Akshay Narayan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Narayan's research areas are networking and computer systems.

faculty.name: Deepti Raghavan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Raghavan works in systems and networking, designing and building systems with efficient communication abstractions to improve the performance of networked applications, including recent work on systems support for compound AI applications.

faculty.name: Adriana Schulz
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Schulz is a member of the Brown Visual Computing group whose research group creates design tools and systems for building physical artifacts, grounded in geometry processing and combining machine learning and programming languages.

faculty.name: Ritambhara Singh
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Data Science
faculty.summary: Singh is a member of the Center for Computational Molecular Biology whose lab develops machine learning methods for data integration and model interpretation in biological and biomedical (genomics) applications.

faculty.name: Harini Suresh
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Suresh's interdisciplinary research explores equity, accountability, agency, and participation in machine learning and AI systems. She leads the Data in Society Collective (DISCO Lab) and helps lead the cross-institutional Counterdata Network project.

faculty.name: James H. Tompkin
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Tompkin's research sits at the intersection of computer vision, computer graphics, and HCI to develop new visual computing tools and experiences; his lab creates techniques for 3D scene reconstruction from multi-camera systems and for dynamic scenes.

faculty.name: Andries van Dam
faculty.title: Thomas J. Watson Jr. University Professor of Technology and Education
faculty.summary: Van Dam's research focuses on computer graphics, hypermedia systems, and post-WIMP user interfaces, and he has worked for over four decades on systems for creating and reading electronic books with interactive illustrations.
