faculty.name: Dan Abramovich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works in algebraic geometry and arithmetic geometry, focusing on birational geometry, resolution of singularities, moduli spaces, toric Artin stacks, and virtual intersection theory. Invited speaker at the 2018 ICM on resolution of singularities of complex algebraic varieties and their families.

faculty.name: Melody Chan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Bridges combinatorics and algebraic geometry, studying moduli spaces of curves, tropical geometry, graph theory, and Brill-Noether theory. Major contributions on tropical curves, graph complexes, and top weight cohomology of moduli spaces. Sloan Research Fellow (2018) and AWM-Microsoft Research Prize winner (2020).

faculty.name: Georgios Daskalopoulos
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on differential geometry, gauge theory, and geometric analysis. Major contributions to harmonic maps into singular/CAT(0) spaces (with Chikako Mese), Teichmuller theory and the Weil-Petersson metric, and best Lipschitz maps between surfaces (with Karen Uhlenbeck).

faculty.name: Javier Gomez Serrano
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of analysis, PDEs, fluid mechanics, spectral geometry, numerical computation, and machine learning. Pioneered ML methods to discover finite-time singularities in fluid equations. Awarded the 2025 R.E. Moore Prize for constructing smooth imploding solutions to 3D Euler and Navier-Stokes equations.

faculty.name: Thomas Goodwillie
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Invented the calculus of functors (Goodwillie calculus), a foundational framework in algebraic topology that approximates general functors by those taking homotopy pushouts to homotopy pullbacks. Also works on algebraic K-theory, manifold topology, and abstract homotopy theory. Fellow of the AMS.

faculty.name: Brendan Hassett
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leading figure in algebraic geometry focusing on cubic fourfolds and rationality questions, K3 surfaces and their derived categories, moduli spaces, and equivariant birational geometry. Director of ICERM. Fellow of the AMS and AAAS.

faculty.name: Jeffrey Hoffstein
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses analytic and algebraic methods to investigate L-functions of automorphic forms over GL(n). Pioneer in multiple Dirichlet series with applications to non-vanishing theorems. Co-founder of NTRU Cryptosystems. Fellow of the AMS.

faculty.name: Justin Holmer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on nonlinear dispersive PDEs, particularly nonlinear Schrodinger equations including blow-up phenomena, soliton dynamics, and scattering. Also works on rigorous derivation of NLS from quantum many-body dynamics, published in Inventiones Mathematicae.

faculty.name: Jeremy Kahn
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on hyperbolic geometry, Teichmuller theory, 3-manifolds, and complex dynamics. With Markovic, proved the Surface Subgroup Theorem (every closed hyperbolic 3-manifold contains a surface subgroup) and the Ehrenpreis conjecture. Invited speaker at 2014 ICM.

faculty.name: Nicolaos Kapouleas
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leading expert in PDE gluing methods for constructing minimal surfaces. Developed the Linearized Doubling methodology for constructing minimal surfaces resembling parallel copies joined by catenoidal bridges. Verified Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue for large classes of minimal surfaces in the 3-sphere.

faculty.name: Benoit Pausader
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches asymptotic behavior of solutions to PDEs from physics including nonlinear Schrodinger equation, Euler-Maxwell system, water wave systems, and Vlasov-Poisson system. Major contributions to scattering theory for dispersive equations and global existence for fluid and plasma models. Chair of Mathematics.

faculty.name: Jill Pipher
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on harmonic analysis including dyadic and multiparameter harmonic analysis, weighted norm inequalities, and regularity theory for elliptic/parabolic PDEs with non-smooth coefficients. Co-founder of NTRU Cryptosystems. Served as AMS President (2019-2021) and founding director of ICERM. Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

faculty.name: Richard Schwartz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on billiards, discrete dynamical systems, hyperbolic geometry, and topology. Introduced the influential Pentagram Map (proved completely integrable). Solved the Moser-Neumann problem on outer billiards and Thomson's 5-electron problem. Recent proof of the optimal shape of a paper Mobius band published in Annals of Mathematics (2025).

faculty.name: Joseph Silverman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: World-renowned expert on elliptic curves, arithmetic geometry, and arithmetic dynamics. Author of the standard graduate text The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves. Research spans number theory, Diophantine geometry, and mathematical cryptography. AMS Steele Prize winner (1998) and Guggenheim Fellow.

faculty.name: Sergei Treil
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of operator theory, complex analysis, and harmonic analysis. Major contributions to weighted norm inequalities for singular integral operators, spectral theory of Hankel and Toeplitz operators, the Corona problem, and the Bellman function method (co-developed with Nazarov and Volberg).

faculty.name: Christine Breiner
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works on minimal and constant mean curvature surfaces, harmonic maps into singular spaces, and geometric variational problems. Recent research on harmonic maps into Euclidean buildings with applications to rigidity in geometric group theory. NSF CAREER award recipient.

faculty.name: Junehyuk Jung
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Number Theory / Automorphic Forms / Spectral Geometry
faculty.summary: Works on analytic number theory, automorphic forms and L-functions, and spectral geometry/quantum chaos. Studies nodal domains of eigenfunctions on hyperbolic surfaces, non-vanishing of symmetric cube L-functions, and intersecting geodesics on the modular surface. Former member at IAS.

faculty.name: Eric Larson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works on Brill-Noether theory, interpolation problems, and moduli spaces of curves. Solved the Maximal Rank Conjecture, a landmark result about the behavior of general curves in projective space. Major contributions with Isabel Vogt on interpolation for Brill-Noether curves. Morgan Prize winner (2014).

faculty.name: Nicole Looper
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of arithmetic dynamics and arithmetic geometry, with emphasis on uniformity problems including the Uniform Boundedness Conjecture of Morton and Silverman. Research on canonical heights, Galois representations in dynamics, and equidistribution. Sloan Research Fellow (2023).

faculty.name: Bena Tshishiku
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works on geometry and topology focusing on manifolds, fiber bundles, mapping class groups, diffeomorphism groups, and arithmetic groups. Major contributions to the Nielsen realization problem and mapping class groups of circle bundles. NSF CAREER award recipient.

faculty.name: Isabel Vogt
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works on algebraic geometry, arithmetic geometry, and Brill-Noether theory. With Eric Larson, solved a folklore conjecture on interpolation for Brill-Noether curves. Proved analogs of main theorems of Brill-Noether theory for curves with fixed gonality. NSF CAREER award recipient.

faculty.name: Stephon Alexander
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical physicist working at the interface between cosmology, particle physics, and quantum gravity.

faculty.name: Ian Dell'Antonio
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Observational cosmologist studying the distribution of dark matter and the growth of cosmic structure through gravitational lensing and cluster surveys.

faculty.name: Dmitri Feldman
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Richard Gaitskell

faculty.name: Ulrich Heintz

faculty.name: Antal Jevicki

faculty.name: Savvas Koushiappas

faculty.name: Greg Landsberg

faculty.name: Xinsheng Sean Ling

faculty.name: David Lowe

faculty.name: Brad Marston

faculty.name: Robert Pelcovits

faculty.name: Marcus Spradlin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical high-energy physicist working on string theory, quantum field theory, and scattering amplitudes.

faculty.name: Jay Tang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Physics & Engineering; experimental biological physicist studying cell mechanics and the cytoskeleton.

faculty.name: Gregory Tucker
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental astrophysicist studying the cosmic microwave background and exoplanets, and building associated instrumentation.

faculty.name: James Valles, Jr.
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental condensed matter physicist studying superconductivity and the effects of magnetic fields in thin films and biological systems.

faculty.name: Anastasia Volovich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical physicist working on quantum field theory, string theory, and scattering amplitudes.

faculty.name: Gang Xiao
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Ford Foundation Professor of Physics & Engineering; experimental condensed matter physicist focusing on nanoscale physics and spin-based systems.

faculty.name: JiJi Fan
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Particle theorist working on physics beyond the Standard Model, including Higgs phenomenology and dark matter.

faculty.name: Loukas Gouskos

faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist focusing on Higgs boson properties at the CMS experiment at the LHC.

faculty.name: Kemp Plumb

faculty.summary: Director of the Master's Program; experimental condensed matter physicist using scattering and spectroscopy to study quantum materials.

faculty.name: Jonathan Pober

faculty.summary: Experimental astrophysicist developing radio telescopes to observe neutral hydrogen and probe the early universe.

faculty.name: Aaron Hui

faculty.summary: Theoretical condensed matter physicist studying strongly correlated electron systems.

faculty.name: Matthias Kuehne

faculty.name: Leenoy Meshulam

faculty.summary: June and Howard Zimmerman Assistant Professor of Physics, Neuroscience and Brain Science; theoretical biological physicist studying neural dynamics using statistical physics methods.

faculty.name: Jennifer Roloff
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist working on the CMS experiment and tests of QCD.

requirements.admission_model_note: Admission is decided by a graduate admissions committee. 'Applications are reviewed and evaluated for admission starting on December 1st, after all credentials have been received, and the Graduate Admission Committee usually decides on admissions by the end of March.' No advisor pre-match is required at admission; a thesis supervisor is chosen after passing the preliminary examination (per Caltech Catalog ACM regulations).

funding.note: 'In general, students offered admission to graduate study at Caltech are simultaneously offered a package of financial support that pays all tuition charges and provides them with a stipend' via fellowships, research/teaching assistantships (cms.caltech.edu/academics/grad). Note: 'admission and financial aid are considered separately; on rare occasions, some students may be admitted without financial aid.' Number of guaranteed years not published - Unknown/Verify.

requirements.contact_note: No official statement requiring pre-application contact with faculty. Admission is committee-based and a thesis supervisor is selected after the preliminary examination, not at application. Unknown/Verify for any informal recommendation.
requirements.duration: 5 years (typical) ('The PhD program requires a minimum of three academic years of residence, and most students complete the PhD program in four to six years.')

faculty.name: Anima Anandkumar
faculty.title: Bren Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.sub_field: Machine Learning and AI for Science
faculty.summary: Invented Neural Operators for learning multiscale phenomena in fluid dynamics, material modeling, and wave propagation. Created the first AI-based high-resolution weather model, tens of thousands of times faster than physics-based forecasting. Research spans AI for nuclear fusion plasma modeling, autonomous drones, drug design, and enzyme engineering.

faculty.name: Katherine L. (Katie) Bouman
faculty.title: Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences, Electrical Engineering and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Designs systems that tightly integrate algorithm and sensor design to observe phenomena impossible to measure with conventional sensors. Led imaging work for the Event Horizon Telescope that produced the first images of a black hole, building an earth-sized computational telescope to study general relativity in the strong-field regime.

faculty.name: Oscar P. Bruno
faculty.title: Professor of Applied and Computational Mathematics
faculty.summary: Creates accurate, high-performance numerical PDE solvers for realistic scientific and engineering problems involving intricate geometries and solution singularities. Developed Fourier Continuation (FC) and integral-equation techniques enabling solutions to previously intractable PDE problems in computational electromagnetics, CFD, and solid mechanics.

faculty.name: Venkat Chandrasekaran
faculty.title: Kiyo and Eiko Tomiyasu Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences and Electrical Engineering
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of applied mathematics and electrical engineering, studying mathematical foundations of optimization and information sciences. Focuses on convex optimization, statistical inference, inverse problems, graphs and combinatorial optimization, and applied algebra and geometry. Develops principled methods for applications in science and engineering.

faculty.name: Georgia Gkioxari
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences and Electrical Engineering
faculty.summary: Focuses on teaching machines to see and understand the world from visual data. Co-creator of PyTorch3D and key contributor to Mask R-CNN (46,000+ citations, Marr Prize at ICCV 2017). Current work on self-improving machine perception, spatial reasoning with multimodal verifiers, and 3D data engines for scaling 3D annotations. 2025 Packard Fellow.

faculty.name: Babak Hassibi
faculty.title: Mose and Lillian S. Bohn Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.sub_field: Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
faculty.summary: Works across information theory, signal processing, control theory, and machine learning. Contributions include wireless communications, robust control, adaptive filtering, neural networks, network information theory, phase retrieval, structured signal recovery, and high-dimensional statistics. Mathematical focus on linear algebra, fast algorithms, random matrices, and group representation theory.

faculty.name: Franca Hoffmann
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of model-driven and data-driven approaches, building rigorous mathematical foundations for modeling tools used in applications. Bridges traditionally separate approaches — model-based methods and data-driven techniques — applying mathematical rigor to improve how these tools function in real-world applications.

faculty.name: Thomas Y. Hou
faculty.title: Charles Lee Powell Professor of Applied and Computational Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works on computational methods for multi-scale problems in fluid dynamics. Known for analysis of singularity formation in the 3D Euler equations and development of multiscale finite element methods. Research spans numerical analysis, scientific computing, and mathematical theory of incompressible flows.

faculty.name: Victoria Kostina
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Works in information theory, coding, and wireless communications, with focus on the nonasymptotic regime. Employs tools from random processes and concentration of measure to gain fundamental insight into modern delay-constrained communication systems, bridging theory and practical system design.

faculty.name: Steven Low
faculty.title: Frank J. Gilloon Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences and Electrical Engineering
faculty.summary: Works on power systems, cyber-physical systems, and network architecture. His NetLab group produced technology that was commercialized as PowerFlex for smart grid applications. Develops mathematical foundations for networked infrastructure including the electricity grid and internet architecture.

faculty.name: Urmila Mahadev
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Investigates cryptographic possibilities of quantum information, developing new protocols by adapting classical cryptographic techniques for quantum settings. Known for breakthroughs in quantum homomorphic encryption (computation on encrypted quantum data) and verifiable delegation of quantum computation (allowing clients to verify quantum computations by untrusted servers).

faculty.name: Matilde Marcolli
faculty.title: Robert F. Christy Professor of Mathematics and Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of mathematics, theoretical physics, and information theory. Co-authored landmark monograph with Alain Connes on noncommutative geometry and quantum fields. Research spans Feynman integrals and motives, quantum statistical mechanics, noncommutative cosmology, and mathematical models of syntactic structures in linguistics.

faculty.name: Eric V. Mazumdar
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences and Economics
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical foundations for deploying machine learning in societal-scale systems. Examines how learning algorithms perform in uncertain, dynamic environments where they interact with strategic agents, humans, and other algorithms. Applications span intelligent infrastructure, online markets, healthcare delivery, and distributionally robust learning.

faculty.name: Dan Meiron
faculty.title: Fletcher Jones Professor of Aeronautics and Applied and Computational Mathematics
faculty.summary: Focuses on computation and modeling of basic fluid mechanical phenomena including shock-driven flow instabilities, turbulence, and simulation approaches for high strain rate solid mechanics. Develops adaptive numerical methods for complex flows suitable for high-performance computation.

faculty.name: Houman Owhadi
faculty.title: IBM Professor of Applied and Computational Mathematics and Control and Dynamical Systems
faculty.summary: Investigates connections between numerical approximation, statistical inference, and learning through a game-theoretic lens. Develops operator-adapted wavelets, numerical homogenization, fast solvers, and Gaussian process regression methods. Research focuses on automating and facilitating discovery processes at the interface of computation and statistics.

faculty.name: Lior Pachter
faculty.title: Bren Professor of Computational Biology and Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Works on computational methods for genomics and systems biology, with key contributions to single-cell RNA-seq analysis, transcript quantification, and computational tools for high-throughput biological data. Develops open-source software and mathematical frameworks for interpreting genomic data.

faculty.name: Niles A. Pierce
faculty.title: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Professor of Applied and Computational Mathematics and Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Engineers small conditional DNAs and RNAs for signal transduction in vitro, in situ, and in vivo. Develops computational algorithms for designing nucleic acid structures and systems, and programmable molecular technologies for readout and regulation of endogenous biological circuitry. Bridges applied mathematics with molecular biology.

faculty.name: Peter Schroeder
faculty.title: Shaler Arthur Hanisch Professor of Computer Science and Applied and Computational Mathematics
faculty.sub_field: Computer Graphics and Discrete Differential Geometry
faculty.summary: Focuses on efficient, reliable algorithms for computer graphics covering geometric modeling and physical simulation (e.g., cloth deformation). A core emphasis is Discrete Differential Geometry — rebuilding the foundations of classical differential geometry in a discrete setting suited for practical computation and numerical algorithms.

faculty.name: Andrew Stuart
faculty.title: Bren Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Creates mathematical and algorithmic frameworks that integrate models with data through the Bayesian formulation of inverse problems and data assimilation for dynamical systems. Major focus on quantification of uncertainty. Applied interests span problems in the geophysical sciences and graph-based learning.

faculty.name: Joel A. Tropp
faculty.title: Steele Family Professor of Applied and Computational Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of applied mathematics, electrical engineering, computer science, and statistics. Focuses on theoretical and computational dimensions of data analysis, sparse modeling, randomized linear algebra, and random matrix theory. Develops mathematical foundations for modern data science algorithms.

faculty.name: Adam Wierman
faculty.title: Carl F Braun Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Develops mathematical tools in machine learning, optimization, control, and economics to make networked systems sustainable and resilient. Designs algorithms and markets with provable guarantees for deployment in data centers, the electricity grid, transportation systems, and beyond. Focuses on sustainable computing and network economics.

faculty.name: Yisong Yue
faculty.title: Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Focuses on theory and application of statistical machine learning, developing new approaches for interactive and structured machine learning. Methods applied across information retrieval, recommender systems, robotics, clinical therapy, sports analytics, experiment design for science, and policy learning in robotics.

faculty.name: Lin Lin
faculty.title: Judge Shirley Hufstedler Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Judge Shirley Hufstedler Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences on the CMS faculty directory, with research spanning numerical analysis and scientific computing.

faculty.name: Animashree (Anima) Anandkumar
faculty.title: Bren Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Bren Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences on the CMS faculty directory, working in machine learning and computational mathematics.

faculty.name: Katherine L. (Katie) Bouman
faculty.title: Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences, Electrical Engineering and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences, Electrical Engineering and Astronomy on the CMS directory, working in computational imaging and inverse problems.

faculty.name: Konstantin Zuev
faculty.title: Teaching Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Teaching Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences on the CMS faculty directory, with interests in statistics and applied probability.

faculty.name: Harry A. Atwater
faculty.title: Otis Booth Leadership Chair; Professor of Applied Physics and Materials Science
faculty.summary: Interdisciplinary materials and device research spanning photonics and electronics. Si-based photonics, plasmonics, artificial photosynthesis, and mechanically active thin-film devices.

faculty.name: Paul M. Bellan
faculty.title: Professor of Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Laboratory plasma physics. Magnetohydrodynamics, solar coronal loop simulations in the laboratory, and astrophysical plasma jet experiments.

faculty.name: Marco Bernardi
faculty.title: Professor of Applied Physics, Physics and Materials Science
faculty.summary: Theory and ab initio computation of light-matter interaction, carrier dynamics, and transport in materials.

faculty.name: Kaushik Bhattacharya
faculty.title: Howell N. Tyson, Sr., Professor of Mechanics and Materials Science; Vice Provost
faculty.summary: Mechanics and physics of materials. Multifunctional materials, microstructure evolution, soft active materials, and deformation mechanisms.

faculty.name: Chiara Daraio
faculty.title: G. Bradford Jones Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Design and characterization of architected materials with unusual mechanical and thermal properties. Acoustic metamaterials, soft robotics.

faculty.name: Michael B. Elowitz
faculty.title: Professor of Biology and Biological Engineering; Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Synthetic biology and biophysics. Design and study of gene circuits in living cells. Cellular information processing and noise in biological systems.

faculty.name: Brent Fultz
faculty.title: Barbara and Stanley R. Rawn, Jr., Professor of Materials Science and Applied Physics

faculty.name: William A. Goddard
faculty.title: Charles and Mary Ferkel Professor of Chemistry, Materials Science, and Applied Physics

faculty.name: Julia R. Greer
faculty.title: Ruben F. and Donna Mettler Professor of Materials Science, Mechanics, and Medical Engineering

faculty.name: Alireza Marandi
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Nonlinear photonic devices and systems for quantum optics, optical computing, and information processing.

faculty.name: Austin J. Minnich
faculty.title: Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Fundamental understanding of heat transport at the nanoscale. Ballistic phonon transport, thermal management, and thermoelectric energy conversion.

faculty.name: Mohammad Mirhosseini
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Superconducting qubits and chip-based quantum devices. Quantum optics at microwave frequencies, quantum transduction.

faculty.name: Stevan Nadj-Perge
faculty.title: Professor of Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Low-temperature STM/STS studies of topological and correlated quantum materials. Majorana zero modes in topological superconductors and 2D moire materials.

faculty.name: Rob Phillips
faculty.title: Fred and Nancy Morris Professor of Biophysics, Biology, and Physics
faculty.summary: Physical biology of the cell. Quantitative models of gene regulation, allostery, membrane biophysics, and viral infection biophysics.

faculty.name: Michael L. Roukes
faculty.title: Frank J. Roshek Professor of Physics, Applied Physics, and Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Nanoscale electromechanical systems (NEMS). Nanofluidic devices for single-molecule analysis and NEMS-based biosensing.

faculty.name: Axel Scherer
faculty.title: Bernard Neches Professor of Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, and Medical Engineering

faculty.name: Keith C. Schwab
faculty.title: Professor of Applied Physics

faculty.name: Sandra Troian
faculty.title: Professor of Applied Physics, Aeronautics, and Mechanical Engineering

faculty.name: Kerry J. Vahala
faculty.title: Ted and Ginger Jenkins Professor of Information Science and Technology, and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Ultra-high-Q optical microcavities. Soliton microcombs, nonlinear optics in microresonators, and precision optical metrology.

faculty.name: Amnon Yariv
faculty.title: Martin and Eileen Summerfield Professor of Applied Physics and Electrical Engineering
faculty.summary: Pioneer of nonlinear optics and quantum electronics. Semiconductor lasers, photonic integrated circuits, and slow light. National Medal of Science (2010).

faculty.name: Lynne Hillenbrand

faculty.name: Jonas Zmuidzinas

faculty.name: David Conlon
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in Hungarian-style combinatorics, finding conditions for the appearance of substructures inside larger structures. Proved the first superpolynomial improvement on the Erdos-Szekeres bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers and made significant progress on Sidorenko's conjecture. Recipient of the European Prize in Combinatorics (2011) and Whitehead Prize (2019).

faculty.name: Vesselin Dimitrov
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in number theory and Diophantine geometry. Proved the Schinzel-Zassenhaus conjecture (2019) and jointly resolved the 50-year-old Unbounded Denominators conjecture. Published in Annals of Mathematics on uniform Mordell-Lang for curves. Recipient of the 2026 New Horizons in Mathematics Prize, 2026 Cole Prize, 2025 Salem Prize, and 2025 Fermat Prize.

faculty.name: Matthias Flach
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in arithmetic algebraic geometry, focusing on special values of L-functions and the conjectures of Bloch, Beilinson, Deligne, and Bloch-Kato. Proved the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for Dirichlet L-functions. Develops Weil-etale cohomology as a framework for zeta functions of arithmetic schemes, with connections to the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.

faculty.name: Thomas B. Graber
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in algebraic geometry with a focus on moduli spaces, numerical invariants of algebraic varieties, and birational geometry. Known for relative virtual localization techniques (with Ravi Vakil) and recent work on log Gromov-Witten invariants. Presented at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians. Serves as Executive Officer for Mathematics.

faculty.name: Sergei Gukov
faculty.title: John D. MacArthur Professor of Theoretical Physics and Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of theoretical physics, mathematics, and machine learning. Known for the Gukov-Vafa-Witten superpotential, Gukov-Witten surface operators in geometric Langlands, and Z-hat invariants of 3-manifolds. Recent research applies machine learning to low-dimensional topology including the smooth 4D Poincare conjecture.

faculty.name: Thomas M. Hutchcroft
faculty.title: Gordon and Betty Moore Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in probability theory and mathematical physics, specializing in Bernoulli percolation on Cayley graphs, random walks, and uniform spanning forests. Solved fundamental conjectures in percolation theory and proved that every countably infinite group with Kazhdan's property (T) has cost 1. Recipient of the 2024 EMS Prize and 2025 Whitehead Prize.

faculty.name: Philip Isett
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in nonlinear PDEs with focus on fluid dynamics, particularly the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations of incompressible flow. Best known for solving Onsager's conjecture (1949) on anomalous energy dissipation in turbulent flows, published in Annals of Mathematics (2018). Currently investigates endpoint regularity and local energy dissipation in turbulence. 2019 Clay Research Award.

faculty.name: Anton Kapustin
faculty.title: Earle C. Anthony Professor of Theoretical Physics and Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of theoretical physics and mathematics. With Edward Witten, reinterpreted the geometric Langlands correspondence in terms of dualities in N=4 supersymmetric gauge theories. Current research includes classification of topological phases of matter, SPT phases, higher-form symmetries, and many-body quantum chaos.

faculty.name: Alexei Kitaev
faculty.title: Ronald and Maxine Linde Professor of Theoretical Physics and Mathematics
faculty.summary: Pioneering researcher in quantum information theory and condensed matter physics. Known for the Kitaev model of topological quantum computation using anyons, the toric code, and fundamental insights into fault-tolerant quantum computation. Bridges theoretical physics and mathematics with deep implications for quantum computing architectures.

faculty.name: Nikolai G. Makarov
faculty.title: Richard Merkin Distinguished Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in complex analysis and its deep connections to probability and mathematical physics. Famous for Makarov's theorem proving harmonic measure on simply connected planar domains has Hausdorff dimension 1. Recent work on mathematical foundations of conformal field theory, Schramm-Loewner evolution, and random normal matrix ensembles. 2020 Rolf Schock Prize laureate.

faculty.name: Elena Mantovan
faculty.title: Taussky-Todd-Lonergan Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in arithmetic geometry focusing on Shimura varieties, p-adic automorphic forms, and the Langlands program. Studies moduli of abelian varieties and p-divisible groups. Constructed p-adic analogues of Maass-Shimura differential operators on unitary Shimura varieties (with Ellen Eischen). Ph.D. from Harvard under Richard Taylor. Serves as Executive Officer for Mathematics.

faculty.name: Matilde Marcolli
faculty.title: Robert F. Christy Professor of Mathematics and Computing and Mathematical Sciences
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of mathematics, theoretical physics, and information theory. Co-authored 'Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives' with Alain Connes. Research spans Feynman integrals and motives, quantum statistical mechanics, noncommutative cosmology, the spectral action model, and mathematical models of syntactic structures (book with Noam Chomsky, 2025).

faculty.name: Yi Ni
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in low-dimensional topology with focus on 3-manifolds, knot theory, and Heegaard Floer homology. Studies cosmetic surgeries on knots, finite Dehn surgeries, and characterization of right-veering monodromy via knot Floer homology. Coorganizes the Geometry and Topology Seminar and the LA Topology Seminar (LaToP).

faculty.name: Hiroshi Ooguri
faculty.title: Fred Kavli Professor of Theoretical Physics and Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in superstring theory, quantum gravity, and quantum field theory. Co-recipient of the inaugural AMS Eisenbud Prize for Mathematics and Physics (with Strominger and Vafa) for connecting black hole entropy to topological string theory. Founding Director of the Walter Burke Institute for Theoretical Physics. Now serves as PMA Division Chair.

faculty.name: Houman Owhadi
faculty.title: IBM Professor of Applied and Computational Mathematics and Control and Dynamical Systems
faculty.summary: Investigates connections between numerical approximation, statistical inference, and learning through a game-theoretic lens. Develops operator-adapted wavelets, numerical homogenization methods, and fast solvers. Research focuses on automating discovery processes at the interface of computation, statistics, and machine learning.

faculty.name: Huy Tuan Pham
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in probabilistic and extremal combinatorics, additive combinatorics, and probability theory. Jointly proved the Kahn-Kalai conjecture (2022), a fundamental result predicting thresholds for properties of random networks. Also proved Talagrand's conjectures on suprema of selector processes. 2026 Sloan Fellow.

faculty.name: Antoine Song
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in differential geometry and geometric analysis, focusing on optimal shapes and minimal surfaces. Proved Yau's conjecture (2018) showing any closed 3-manifold contains infinitely many smooth immersed minimal surfaces, published in Annals of Mathematics. Recently proved the Huisken-Ilmanen conjecture on stability of Euclidean space for the positive mass theorem. Clay Research Fellow (2019-2024).

faculty.name: Omer Tamuz
faculty.title: Professor of Economics and Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of probability theory, dynamical systems, and microeconomic theory. Studies decision-making under uncertainty, information costs, and social learning. Recently proved that the Boltzmann distribution is the only law accurately describing unrelated (uncoupled) systems, linking economic theory to fundamental physics. 2020 Sloan Fellow and NSF CAREER awardee.

faculty.name: Yunqing Tang
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in arithmetic geometry and number theory. Jointly resolved the 50-year-old Unbounded Denominators conjecture and proved Ogus' conjecture for a large class of abelian varieties. Made progress on the Grothendieck-Katz p-curvature conjecture. Recipient of the 2026 Cole Prize, 2026 New Horizons Prize, and 2022 SASTRA Ramanujan Prize.

faculty.name: Tony Yue Yu
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of enumerative geometry, non-Archimedean geometry, and mirror symmetry. Pioneered counting curves using non-Archimedean methods. Published landmark Frobenius structure theorem in Annals of Mathematics (2023, with Sean Keel). Established fundamental comparisons between non-Archimedean and logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants.

faculty.name: Lingfu Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Works in probability theory centered on the KPZ universality class — random growth models describing phenomena from bacterial colonies to traffic jams. Studies the directed landscape, Tracy-Widom fluctuations, and first passage percolation. Proved the directed landscape is uniquely characterized by the KPZ fixed point, advancing the strong KPZ universality conjecture.

faculty.name: Amit Acharya
faculty.title: Paul P. Christiano Professor
faculty.sub_field: Continuum mechanics and theoretical materials science
faculty.summary: Acharya specializes in continuum mechanics and theoretical materials science, spanning fundamental theory to computational modeling. His work has contributed to finite element methods, including widely used nonlinear material models in commercial FE software.

faculty.name: Peter Adams
faculty.title: Thomas Lord Professor
faculty.summary: Adams develops chemical transport models focusing on aerosol microphysical processes, ultrafine particles, and cloud condensation nuclei formation in global climate models. He also studies climate change impacts on air quality and particulate matter formation.

faculty.name: Burcu Akinci
faculty.title: Hamerschlag University Professor; Dean, College of Engineering
faculty.sub_field: Advanced infrastructure systems and building information modeling
faculty.summary: Akinci develops approaches to model and reason about information-rich histories of facilities to streamline construction and facility management processes, integrating building information models with data capture technologies such as 3D imaging and embedded sensors.

faculty.name: Mario Bergés
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Smart infrastructure and building energy analytics
faculty.summary: Bergés works on making the built environment more operationally efficient and robust through information and communication technologies. His current research develops approximate inference techniques to extract actionable insights from infrastructure sensor data, particularly for building energy efficiency.

faculty.name: Kaushik Dayal
faculty.title: Walter J. Blenko, Sr. Professor
faculty.summary: Dayal develops theoretical and computational multiscale methods for problems in materials science, focusing on bridging atomic to continuum scales in the context of functional behavior, non-equilibrium response, and electromagnetic effects.

faculty.name: Sarah Fakhreddine
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Fakhreddine develops water management solutions addressing both quantity and quality by investigating the hydrologic and biogeochemical processes controlling contaminant and nutrient fate in complex watersheds, with focus on how climate-driven changes and water management alter water quality outcomes.

faculty.name: Katherine Flanigan
faculty.title: Henry Posner, Anne Molloy, and Robert and Christine Pietrandrea Career Development Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Flanigan transforms traditional infrastructure into intelligent cyber-physical systems by integrating sensing, computing, and actuation technologies. Her work extends to cyber-physical-social systems that account for human-infrastructure interactions and community-driven data collection.

faculty.name: James Garrett
faculty.title: Thomas Lord Professor; Provost and Chief Academic Officer
faculty.sub_field: Sensing and data analytics for infrastructure
faculty.summary: Garrett applies sensing technologies and data analytics to improve infrastructure condition assessment and management, bridging sensor systems, machine learning, and intelligent decision support for civil engineering applications.

faculty.name: Kelvin Gregory
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Gregory investigates the microbiology, ecology, and fundamental interactions between bacteria and their physical and chemical environment. His work encompasses produced water management, environmental nanotechnology, and geologic carbon sequestration.

faculty.name: Corey Harper
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Harper directs the Future Mobility Systems Lab and applies modeling, simulation, and data analytics to assess how emerging technologies impact transportation equity, environment, and congestion, including work on climate resilience and vehicle automation.

faculty.name: Su Jiang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Jiang combines artificial intelligence with domain expertise to model subsurface flow processes, with applications to geological carbon storage, hydrocarbon production, enhanced geothermal systems, and seawater intrusion.

faculty.name: Gregory Lowry
faculty.title: Interim Department Head, Hamerschlag University Professor
faculty.summary: Lowry's environmental nanotechnology and chemistry research aims to enhance agricultural efficiency, environmental cleanup processes, and water purification systems, exploring how nanoparticles can be engineered for practical environmental applications.

faculty.name: Destenie Nock
faculty.title: Alex Hills Career Development Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Nock uses mathematical modeling to address sustainability planning and energy policy challenges, focusing on energy systems modeling and multi-criteria decision analysis to help policymakers understand energy planning options with attention to equity and vulnerable populations.

faculty.name: Matteo Pozzi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pozzi focuses on risk analysis for civil infrastructure systems using engineering models and sensor data, with emphasis on probabilistic approaches to seismic vulnerability, infrastructure deterioration, and maintenance optimization.

faculty.name: Sean Qian
faculty.title: H.J. Heinz III Professor
faculty.sub_field: Transportation network modeling and data analytics
faculty.summary: Qian specializes in large-scale dynamic network modeling and large-scale data analytics for multi-modal transportation systems, developing intelligent transportation systems and studying infrastructure interdependencies.

faculty.name: David Rounce
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Director of CERCA
faculty.summary: Rounce's research seeks to quantify the response of glaciers, water resources, and hazards to climate change to inform adaptation and mitigation efforts, using computational models integrated with remote sensing and fieldwork.

faculty.name: Costa Samaras
faculty.title: Trustee Professor; Director, Wilton E. Scott Institute for Energy Innovation
faculty.summary: Samaras examines pathways to clean, climate-safe, equitable, and secure energy and infrastructure systems, analyzing how technologies and policies affect energy use, climate resilience, and environmental outcomes across electric vehicles, renewable electricity, and climate adaptation.

faculty.name: Pingbo Tang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Remote sensing and human-cyber-physical systems for infrastructure
faculty.summary: Tang explores remote sensing, human systems engineering, data analytics, and information modeling to support spatiotemporal analyses for predictive management of constructed facilities, examining sensing methods for human-cyber-physical systems in construction and infrastructure operations.

faculty.name: Gerald Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Nanoscale transport phenomena and the energy-water nexus
faculty.summary: Wang applies mechanics, statistical physics, and high-performance computing to understand nanoscale structural and transport phenomena, developing innovations for challenges at the intersection of water and energy systems.

faculty.name: Lue Pan

faculty.name: Semon Rezchikov

faculty.name: Giulia Sacca

faculty.name: Ovidiu Savin

faculty.name: Mehtaab Sawhney

faculty.name: Michael Thaddeus

faculty.name: Mu-Tao Wang

faculty.name: Daniel Bienstock

faculty.name: Chris H. Wiggins

faculty.name: Jay Sethuraman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches market design, optimization, and matching theory with applications in decentralized finance and allocation mechanisms.

faculty.name: Clifford Stein
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches algorithms design and analysis, combinatorial optimization, and scheduling. Co-author of 'Introduction to Algorithms'; ACM Fellow and Wei T. Chang Professor.

faculty.name: David D. Yao
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches stochastic systems and applied probability, with emphasis on queueing networks, inventory systems, and their applications in operations research.

faculty.name: Xunyu Zhou
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches stochastic control theory and its applications in quantitative finance, mean-field games, and behavioral portfolio management.

faculty.name: Shipra Agrawal
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches online optimization, multi-armed bandits, reinforcement learning, and learning in games, with applications in revenue management and decision making under uncertainty. Affiliated with CS and Data Science Institute.

faculty.name: Eric Balkanski
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches algorithms and optimization, with a focus on discrete optimization problems and their applications in data-driven decision making. Director of Undergraduate Programs.

faculty.name: Christian Kroer
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches game theory, online optimization, equilibrium computation, and market design, developing efficient algorithms for large-scale competitive environments.

faculty.name: Daniel Lacker
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches probability theory and stochastic processes, with emphasis on mean-field games and large-scale interacting systems.

faculty.name: Henry Lam
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches simulation methodology, risk analysis, and stochastic optimization. Serves as Director of Doctoral Programs.

faculty.name: Yuri Faenza
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches discrete optimization, polyhedral combinatorics, and matching theory with applications in market design. Recipient of NSF CAREER Award.

faculty.name: Cédric Josz
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Researches optimization theory and algorithms, with focus on polynomial optimization and semidefinite programming methods.

faculty.name: Tianyi Lin
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Researches optimization and machine learning, developing algorithms for non-convex optimization problems arising in modern AI applications.

faculty.name: Bento Natura
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Researches optimization algorithms and theory, with applications in convex programming and large-scale computational optimization.

faculty.name: Wenpin Tang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Researches dynamic pricing, statistical learning, and applied probability with applications in financial technology and online platforms.

faculty.name: Noémie Elhadad
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Department Chair
faculty.summary: Research at the intersection of AI, human-centered computing, and medicine. Develops ML methods and AI tools for patients and clinicians. Leads eve_n initiative on data-powered women's health.

faculty.name: George Hripcsak
faculty.title: Vivian Beaumont Allen Professor of Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Pioneer in biomedical informatics, former DBMI chair for 15 years. Research on observational health research, causal inference in healthcare AI, and clinical data science.

faculty.name: Chunhua Weng
faculty.title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics (in Medicine)
faculty.summary: Research on clinical research informatics, NLP for clinical trial eligibility criteria, and translational informatics for patient-centered care.

faculty.name: Andrea Califano
faculty.title: Clyde '56 and Helen Wu Professor of Chemical Biology (in Systems Biology); Professor of Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on systems biology and cancer genomics. Leads the Califano Lab at the Institute for Cancer Genomics.

faculty.name: Raul Rabadan
faculty.title: Professor of Systems Biology and Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on systems biology and biomedical informatics, with focus on cancer genomics and computational methods.

faculty.name: Lena Mamykina
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Graduate Program Director
faculty.summary: Research on human-computer interaction and health informatics, with focus on self-management and patient-centered design for chronic disease. Serves as Graduate Program Director.

faculty.name: Shalmali Joshi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (DBMI and CS)
faculty.summary: Research on algorithmic safety of machine learning for healthcare. Develops causal inference, probabilistic modeling, and deep learning methods. Leads the reAIM Lab. Affiliated with CS.

faculty.name: Matthew McDermott
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on machine learning and clinical AI for healthcare applications.

faculty.name: Xuhai Orson Xu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (DBMI, CS, Data Science Institute)
faculty.summary: Research on HCI and AI for health. Leads the SEA Lab. Joint appointment with CS and Data Science Institute. Recruiting PhD students for Fall 2026.

faculty.name: Despina Kontos
faculty.title: Herbert and Florence Irving Professor of Radiological Sciences; Professor of Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on AI in medical imaging, radiomics, and machine learning for cancer imaging and precision medicine.

faculty.name: Suzanne Bakken
faculty.title: Alumni Professor of Nursing; Professor of Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on nursing informatics, health equity, precision health, and community health informatics.

faculty.name: Yufeng Shen
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology and Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on systems biology and biomedical informatics, with focus on genomics and statistical genetics.

faculty.name: Dennis Vitkup
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology and Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on systems biology and computational biology, with focus on metabolic networks and genomics.

faculty.name: Aristidis Floratos
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology and Biomedical Informatics
faculty.summary: Research on systems biology and biomedical informatics with focus on computational genomics.

faculty.name: Sarah Rossetti
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics and Nursing
faculty.summary: Research on clinical informatics, patient safety, and health IT.

faculty.name: Kiros Berhane
faculty.title: Chair and Cynthia and Robert Citrone-Roslyn and Leslie Goldstein Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Berhane develops biostatistical methods with applications to environmental health, chronic disease, and child, adolescent, and urban health.

faculty.name: Melissa Begg
faculty.title: Professor of Social Work and Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: Biostatistical methods and public health education
faculty.summary: Begg's work spans biostatistical methods and public health education; she also serves as Dean of the Columbia School of Social Work.

faculty.name: Xiaoyu Che
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics (in the Center for Infection and Immunity)
faculty.summary: Che develops biostatistical methods for OMICs and applies them to infectious diseases, chronic disease, and autism spectrum disorder within the Center for Infection and Immunity.

faculty.name: Qixuan Chen
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Chen's methodological research focuses on causal inference, data integration, measurement error, and missing data.

faculty.name: Bin Cheng
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Cheng develops biostatistical methods with applications in aging and global health.

faculty.name: Ying Kuen Cheung
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Cheung's research focuses on biostatistical methodology, including the design and analysis of clinical trials.

faculty.name: Codruta Chiuzan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Chiuzan works on biostatistical methods for clinical and chronic-disease research and serves as a biostatistician at the Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center.

faculty.name: Hanga Galfalvy
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics (in Psychiatry)
faculty.summary: Galfalvy's research addresses statistical genetics and statistical methods in psychiatry, with a focus on suicidal behavior.

faculty.name: Jeff Goldsmith
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics and Associate Dean for Data Science
faculty.summary: Goldsmith advances functional data analysis methods for complex datasets from neuroscience and physical-activity monitoring, including stroke patients' reaching movements and wearable-device accelerometer data.

faculty.name: Prakash Gorroochurn
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Gorroochurn works on statistical genetics, structural equation modeling, and missing data, and has written extensively on the history of probability and statistics.

faculty.name: R. Todd Ogden
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics (in Psychiatry)
faculty.summary: Ogden develops statistical methodology in functional data analysis, nonparametric regression, and wavelet methods, collaborating extensively on brain imaging studies.

faculty.name: Iuliana Ionita-Laza
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Ionita-Laza develops statistical and machine learning approaches for high-dimensional genetic data, applying them to the genetic basis of autism, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease.

faculty.name: Yuanjia Wang
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Wang develops machine learning and AI methods for precision medicine in psychiatry and neurodegenerative diseases, integrating large-scale multimodal data including EHRs and digital phenotypes.

faculty.name: Zhezhen Jin
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Jin's methodological research covers resampling methods, survival analysis, nonparametric and semiparametric methods, and smoothing, with collaborations across neurology, cardiology, and oncology.

faculty.name: Shuang Wang
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Wang develops statistical methods for detecting gene-gene interactions and for quantitative trait locus mapping in genetic linkage and association studies.

faculty.name: Ian McKeague
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: McKeague develops statistical methodology including post-selection inference, empirical likelihood, and functional data analysis, with applications to wearable-device data and survival outcomes in precision medicine.

faculty.name: Min Qian
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Qian develops statistical methods for individualized treatment policies and medical decision-making, with applications in mental health, cardiology, and clinical trial design.

faculty.name: Seonjoo Lee
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics (in Psychiatry)
faculty.summary: Lee develops statistical and AI/ML methods that integrate neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical data to study psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders such as schizophrenia and Alzheimer's disease.

faculty.name: Chris Xu
faculty.title: IBM Professor of Engineering; Director of the School of AEP
faculty.summary: Director of Cornell AEP and pioneer in multiphoton microscopy for deep-tissue imaging, developing optical methods for neuroscience and neurotechnology.

faculty.name: Joel Donald Brock
faculty.title: Given Foundation Professor of Engineering
faculty.summary: Director of the Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source (CHESS), advancing synchrotron X-ray science for materials research and thin-film characterization.

faculty.name: David Anthony Muller
faculty.title: Samuel B. Eckert Professor of Engineering
faculty.summary: Applied physicist and co-director of CCMR, pushing atomic-resolution electron microscopy and spectroscopy to understand materials at the atomic scale.

faculty.name: Gennady Shvets
faculty.title: J. Preston Levis Professor of Engineering
faculty.summary: Director of the Laboratory of Plasma Studies, working on plasma-based accelerators, metamaterials, and laser-plasma interactions.

faculty.name: Gregory David Fuchs
faculty.title: James R. Meehl Professor
faculty.summary: Applied physicist studying spin defects in solids for quantum sensing and information, including NV centers in diamond and related quantum materials.

faculty.name: Kin Fai Mak
faculty.title: Josephson Family Professor (A&S/AEP)
faculty.summary: Discovering and probing emergent quantum phenomena in atomically thin 2D materials, moiré superlattices, and van der Waals heterostructures.

faculty.name: Jie Shan
faculty.title: Walter S. Carpenter, Jr. Professor of Engineering
faculty.summary: Studying optical and electronic properties of 2D quantum materials and van der Waals heterostructures for emergent quantum phenomena.

faculty.name: Peter McMahon
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Developing optical and quantum information processing systems including photonic neural networks and quantum computing architectures.

faculty.name: Jeffrey Moses
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Director of Graduate Studies
faculty.summary: Developing ultrafast nonlinear optical sources and techniques for studying dynamics in materials and molecules at femtosecond timescales.

faculty.name: Lois Pollack
faculty.title: John Edson Sweet Memorial Professor of Engineering; Associate Dean
faculty.summary: Biophysicist using X-ray scattering and complementary techniques to study biomolecular structure and dynamics including RNA and protein folding.

faculty.name: Craig J. Fennie
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical materials physicist using first-principles methods to design and understand functional materials including ferroelectrics and multiferroics.

faculty.name: Ankit Disa
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studying emergent phenomena in complex oxide heterostructures and quantum materials using ultrafast optical and THz spectroscopy.

faculty.name: Valla Fatemi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor; Aref and Manon Lahham Faculty Fellow
faculty.summary: Studying quantum transport in superconducting and topological materials, exploring exotic quasiparticles and non-reciprocal transport phenomena.

faculty.name: Berit Goodge
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Developing advanced electron microscopy techniques to probe the structure and properties of quantum materials at atomic resolution.

faculty.name: Or Katz
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Developing trapped-ion quantum systems for quantum information processing and quantum simulation of many-body physics.

faculty.name: Nicholas Rivera
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Theorist studying quantum light-matter interactions in nanophotonic structures and 2D materials for quantum optical technologies.

faculty.name: Kenji Yasuda
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studying emergent ferroelectric and electronic phenomena in 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures.

faculty.name: Beth A. Ahner
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Ahner investigates how organisms adapt to trace metal stress and influence metal forms in the environment. Her lab studies plant metal solubilization, uptake, detoxification, and sequestration, with applications in phytoremediation of contaminated soils.

faculty.name: C. Lindsay Anderson
faculty.title: Department Chair, Professor
faculty.summary: Anderson works on energy system decarbonization at the interface of environmental and systems engineering, electric power systems, applied optimization, and decision science. Projects include renewable energy integration, wind generation uncertainty mitigation, and biofuels production optimization.

faculty.name: Buz M. Barstow
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Barstow is a physicist using synthetic biology to build sustainable energy technologies. His work spans systems and synthetic biology for sustainable energy and molecular/cellular bioengineering.

faculty.name: Natalie Cápiro
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Cápiro examines the biotransformation of emerging (e.g., PFAS) and legacy (e.g., chlorinated solvents) organic contaminants in the environment. Her research explores degradation pathways, microbial community dynamics, and biological-chemical interactions relevant to groundwater remediation and water quality protection.

faculty.name: Michael Charles
faculty.title: Cornell Provost's New Faculty Fellow and Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computational sustainability and Indigenous knowledge systems
faculty.summary: Charles develops computational sustainability frameworks combining dynamic ecological models with community-centered relationships. His work focuses on the role landscapes can play in addressing sustainability challenges and on interfaces between institutionalized science and Indigenous knowledge systems.

faculty.name: Ashim K. Datta
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Datta develops mechanistic understanding of food processes under various heating modes to enhance food safety and quality. His group uses a fundamentals-based approach applying multiphase and multicomponent porous media analysis across scales and physics domains.

faculty.name: Jacqueline Gerson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Gerson investigates how human activities alter nutrient and contaminant cycling through watersheds, focusing on the fate and transport of these elements in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. She studies biogeochemical cycles in socioenvironmental systems and their implications for people and animals.

faculty.name: Peter Hess
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Hess focuses on understanding atmospheric chemistry within the context of the Earth's climate system. He examines how atmospheric composition may shift during the 21st century and investigates coupled interactions between climate change and air quality.

faculty.name: Sunghwan (Sunny) Jung
faculty.title: Professor and Director of Graduate Studies
faculty.summary: Jung studies physics and biology problems arising from biological systems interacting with their environments, using mathematical modeling, fluid dynamics, and experiments. Topics include animal drinking mechanics, bird diving, plant spore dispersal, and raindrop impacts on biological surfaces.

faculty.name: Manoj Karkee
faculty.title: The Norman R. and Sharon R. Scott Professor of Agriculture and Life Sciences
faculty.summary: Karkee focuses on sensing, machine vision, AI, and robotics in agriculture. His program develops AI, machine learning, and robotics solutions to reduce resource consumption and address farming challenges.

faculty.name: Dan Luo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: DNA materials and nucleic acid engineering
faculty.summary: Luo's work focuses on DNA and RNA as both generic and genetic materials. His lab develops novel DNA materials such as tree-shaped DNA, DNA gels, and DNA-nanoparticle hybrids, with applications in diagnostics, pharmaceutics, protein production, drug delivery, cell culture, and optoelectronics.

faculty.name: Minglin Ma
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Biomaterials for biomedical and agricultural applications
faculty.summary: Ma's group develops advanced biomaterials for agricultural and biomedical applications, with emphasis on cell replacement therapies for type 1 diabetes. The work spans polymers, hydrogels, inorganics, and composites that interact with biological systems.

faculty.name: John March
faculty.title: Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies
faculty.summary: March focuses on reconfiguring biological systems for improved performance in biomedicine and sustainability. His lab concentrates on signal transduction, metabolism, and eukaryotic-prokaryotic interactions, with emphasis on subcellular-level events.

faculty.name: Chris Roh
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Roh studies insect adaptations in fluid environments and applies biomechanics findings to agricultural, biomedical, and aeronautical engineering. Research areas include fluid mechanics, entomology, comparative biomechanics, bio-inspired engineering, and in vivo engineering.

faculty.name: Rosa Santomartino
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Santomartino investigates microbial behavior in space conditions to advance sustainable space exploration and address environmental challenges on Earth. Her work covers biotechnologies for in situ resource utilization, bioregenerative life support systems, and waste upcycling, including plastic-degrading and bioleaching microorganisms.

faculty.name: Vivek Srikrishnan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Srikrishnan focuses on quantifying impacts from climate change and identifying and evaluating strategies for climate risk management. His research uses systems engineering, data science, decision science, and economics to enhance societal resilience, spanning flood management to energy investments.

faculty.name: Tammo Steenhuis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Steenhuis investigates landscape processes and water movement across the northeastern US, Ethiopia, and China, with focus on sustainable agricultural practices, distributed hydrological processes, pesticide transport, and gully formation prevention.

faculty.name: Scott Steinschneider
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Steinschneider specializes in statistical hydroclimatology, examining how climate and hydrologic systems affect water resources planning. His work addresses hydroclimate variability, risks to water infrastructure from climate processes, and adaptation strategies for sustainable water management.

faculty.name: M. Todd Walter
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Walter focuses on interactions between hydrology, ecology, and biogeochemistry. Current research encompasses linkages between hydrology and biogeochemical hotspots, plus nano-biotechnology applications to ecohydrological systems.

faculty.name: Mingming Wu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Wu's lab develops micro-scale devices and computational tools for measuring cell-generated forces and exploring cellular growth dynamics in relation to environmental factors. Current work focuses on tumor mechanics and invasion, motivated by health and environmental challenges.

faculty.name: Lirong Xiang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Xiang develops smart cyber-physical systems integrating robotics, computer vision, and machine learning for agriculture. Focus areas include AI and robotic sensing for controlled environment agriculture, bio-inspired robotic systems, high-throughput phenotyping, and digital twins for agricultural automation.

faculty.name: John D. Albertson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Albertson studies the exchange rates of mass (water, CO2, pollutants), energy, and momentum between the land and atmosphere, using integrated measurement and modeling with applications in hydrometeorology and air quality.

faculty.name: Edwin (Todd) Cowen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Cowen studies environmental fluid mechanics with a focus on sustainability, renewable energy, and water systems, pairing laboratory experiments with field studies of natural and anthropogenic flows including surface turbulence, wave energy, and environmental DNA tracking.

faculty.name: Ricardo Daziano
faculty.title: Director of Graduate Studies, Professor
faculty.summary: Daziano works on engineering decision making, specifically theoretical and applied econometrics of consumer behavior and discrete choice models applied to technological innovation in transportation and energy.

faculty.name: Fani Derveni
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Derveni develops multiscale smart metastructures for sustainable and resilient infrastructure, integrating experimental and computational mechanics with work on renewable materials and lightweight metamaterials with high energy dissipation.

faculty.name: Pete J. Diamessis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Diamessis develops high-accuracy spectral computational methods and parallel simulations to study stratified turbulence, internal waves, and mixing in oceanographic and environmental fluid systems.

faculty.name: Christopher J. Earls
faculty.title: J. Preston Levis Professor of Engineering
faculty.summary: Earls develops mathematical and computational approaches for complex systems, focusing on Scientific Artificial Intelligence and inverse problems, including uncertainty quantification and sparse sensing in engineering and applied science.

faculty.name: Stefano Galelli
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Galelli studies interactions between critical infrastructure systems and the natural environment, focusing on how hydro-climatic variability affects interconnected water-energy infrastructures and developing adaptive management for reliability, resilience, and sustainability.

faculty.name: H. Oliver Gao
faculty.title: Howard Simpson 1942 Professor of Engineering; Director, Systems Engineering Program
faculty.summary: Gao works at the intersection of environmental health, sustainability, and systems engineering, developing computational and systems solutions integrating engineering, data science, and policy for climate-smart mobility, low-emission infrastructure, and data-enabled health systems.

faculty.name: Andrea Giometto
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Giometto investigates the spatial growth dynamics of microbial communities, examining how ecological and evolutionary processes play out in spatially extended populations through statistical physics, experiments, and genetic engineering.

faculty.name: Mircea Dan Grigoriu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Grigoriu specializes in random vibration, stochastic calculus, numerical methods for stochastic problems, probabilistic microstructure models, and wind and earthquake engineering, spanning computational solid mechanics and structural engineering.

faculty.name: April Gu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Gu applies microorganisms and biotechnology to address environmental pollutants in water systems, with work on sustainable wastewater treatment, nutrient recovery, climate change impacts on phosphorus cycling, and toxicogenomics-based water quality assessment.

faculty.name: Damian E. Helbling
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Helbling studies organic chemicals in water systems using high-resolution mass spectrometry, examining fate and transformation processes and remediation technologies to understand how chemical contaminants impact freshwater resources and global health.

faculty.name: Andreas Malikopoulos
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Control and learning for autonomous systems
faculty.summary: Malikopoulos works at the intersection of learning and control to enable autonomous systems—vehicles, robots, and infrastructure—to operate optimally while safely adapting to dynamic environments, with applications in connected and automated mobility.

faculty.name: Jacob Mays
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Mays applies optimization and statistical learning to energy systems, with a focus on electricity market design and analysis, drawing on prior experience at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

faculty.name: Gregory McLaskey
faculty.title: Director of Undergraduate Studies, Associate Professor
faculty.summary: McLaskey studies earthquake mechanics, fracture, and friction using seismic waves and piezoelectric sensors, applying these techniques to structural health monitoring and damage detection in buildings, bridges, and civil infrastructure.

faculty.name: Sriramya Duddukuri Nair
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Nair advances cementitious materials for infrastructure, energy, and automated construction, studying how composition and processing affect cement-based materials, with emphasis on alternative formulations, subsurface well cementing, and 3D concrete printing.

faculty.name: Linda K. Nozick
faculty.title: Associate Dean for Professional Programs, Professor
faculty.summary: Nozick focuses on quantitative modeling of risk, resilience, and complex infrastructure systems through optimization, game theory, and stochastic methods, with applications to transportation networks, hazardous materials, disaster recovery, and insurance mechanisms.

faculty.name: Patrick Michael Reed
faculty.title: Director of the School; Joseph C. Ford Professor of Engineering
faculty.summary: Reed advances multiobjective systems engineering and decision analytics for complex water systems facing climate change risks, bridging sustainability science, economics, operations research, and high-performance computing to design and manage engineered systems.

faculty.name: Matthew Charles Reid
faculty.title: Director of Undergraduate Studies for Environmental Engineering Major, Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Reid combines molecular-level experimental studies with modeling to understand aquatic contaminant dynamics for sustainable ecosystem management, focusing on nutrients in agricultural watersheds and geogenic metal(loid)s affected by climate change.

faculty.name: Ruth E. Richardson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Richardson applies molecular biological tools—genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics—to study microbial communities involved in bioremediation, sustainable wastewater treatment, and bioenergy, including organisms that remediate chlorinated contaminants and uranium.

faculty.name: Samitha Samaranayake
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Samaranayake focuses on the analysis and control of networked cyber-physical systems with applications to transportation and urban infrastructure, using optimization, algorithms, and real-time data to enable sustainable mobility including mobility-on-demand platforms.

faculty.name: Chloé Arson
faculty.title: Professor and M.Eng. Director
faculty.summary: Arson specializes in damage and healing rock mechanics, poromechanical modeling of porous media, and computational geomechanics, developing numerical tools to evaluate underground storage, simulate rock fracturing, and design bio-inspired geotechnical systems.

faculty.name: Nikolaos Bouklas
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Bouklas develops theoretical frameworks and computational methods to study soft, active, and biomaterials with applications to fracture, instabilities, and multiscale coupled systems, integrating machine learning with physics for constitutive modeling and PDE solutions.

faculty.title: Professor of Astronomy
faculty.summary: Theoretical astrophysicist working on neutron star physics, cosmology, dark energy models, cosmic strings, and general relativistic astrophysics.
