faculty.name: Aaron Young
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the EPIC (Exoskeleton and Prosthetic Intelligent Controls) Lab, researching wearable robotic systems for human augmentation and rehabilitation. Develops intent recognition, control strategies, and mechatronic design for powered prostheses and exoskeletons.

faculty.name: Ye Zhao
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the Laboratory for Intelligent Decision and Autonomous Robots (LIDAR), researching planning and control for legged robots. Develops whole-body motion planning and model predictive control algorithms for bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion in challenging environments.

faculty.name: Jonathan Rogers
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches nonlinear control theory and its application to robotic systems, including autonomous ground and aerial vehicles. Works on dynamics, estimation, and mechatronic design for high-performance robotic platforms.

faculty.name: Jaydev Desai
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the Robotics and Mechatronics Lab (RoboMed), researching surgical and interventional robotics. Develops MRI-compatible robotic systems, haptic feedback for robot-assisted surgery, and micro-robotic platforms for minimally invasive medical procedures.

faculty.name: Jun Ueda
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches novel actuation and mechatronic systems for robotics, including cellular actuators inspired by biological muscle. Develops precision motion systems and robotic devices for human-robot interaction and rehabilitation applications.

faculty.name: Lena Ting
faculty.title: McCamish Foundation Distinguished Chair Professor
faculty.summary: Researches neuromechanics of posture and locomotion, studying how the nervous system controls movement and balance. Work informs the design of bio-inspired robotic control, rehabilitation robotics, and wearable assistive devices.

funding.note: Fully funded (SEAS PhD guarantee: tuition + stipend)

faculty.name: Petros Koumoutsakos
faculty.title: Herbert S. Winokur, Jr. Professor of Computing in Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Research in computational science and engineering, fluid mechanics, machine learning, and active matter. Primary teaching area: Applied Mathematics.

faculty.name: Boris Kozinsky
faculty.title: Gordon McKay Professor of Materials Science and Mechanical Engineering and Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Biology
faculty.summary: Research in computational materials science. Affiliated with Applied Mathematics.

faculty.name: Zhiming Kuang
faculty.title: Gordon McKay Professor of Atmospheric and Environmental Science and of Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: Research in atmospheric and environmental science. Joint appointment in Applied Mathematics.

faculty.name: L. Mahadevan
faculty.title: Lola England de Valpine Professor of Applied Mathematics, of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, and of Physics
faculty.summary: Research in applied mathematics spanning biological and physical systems, soft matter, and mechanics. MacArthur Fellow.

faculty.name: Michael D. Mitzenmacher
faculty.title: Thomas J. Watson, Sr. Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in randomized algorithms, networking, and information theory. Affiliated with Applied Mathematics.

faculty.name: Cengiz Pehlevan
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: Research in computational neuroscience, machine learning, and theoretical neuroscience.

faculty.name: Anna Seigal
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: Research in applied algebra and geometry, machine learning, and numerical analysis.

faculty.name: Nick Trefethen
faculty.title: Professor of Applied Mathematics in Residence
faculty.summary: Research in numerical analysis, scientific computing, and approximation theory. Fellow of the Royal Society.

faculty.name: Eli Tziperman
faculty.title: Pamela and Vasco McCoy, Jr. Professor of Oceanography and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Research in oceanography, climate dynamics, and applied physics. Affiliated with Applied Mathematics.

faculty.name: Leslie G. Valiant
faculty.title: T. Jefferson Coolidge Professor of Computer Science and Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: Research in theory of computation, machine learning, and computational neuroscience. Turing Award (2010).

faculty.name: Melanie Weber
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Applied Mathematics and of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Research in applied algebra and geometry, machine learning, and numerical analysis.

funding.note: Fully funded (SEAS PhD guarantee: tuition + stipend)

faculty.name: Federico Capasso
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneer of flat optics and metasurfaces and co-inventor of the quantum cascade laser.

faculty.name: David A. Weitz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental soft-matter physicist working on colloids, emulsions, and microfluidic technologies.

faculty.name: Eric Mazur
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies ultrafast optics, laser-matter interactions, and nanophotonic materials.

faculty.name: Conor J. Walsh
faculty.title: Paul A. Maeder Professor of Engineering and Applied Sciences
faculty.summary: Global leader in soft wearable robotics for human augmentation and rehabilitation. His soft exosuits use textiles and soft actuation to assist mobility-impaired individuals. Work has direct clinical impact for stroke and ALS patients.

faculty.name: Lene Vestergaard Hau
faculty.title: Mallinckrodt Professor of Physics and of Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Famous for experimentally stopping light in a Bose-Einstein condensate — a landmark demonstration of quantum optical control. Research has profound implications for quantum information storage and quantum networks. MacArthur Fellow.

faculty.name: Philip Kim
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies electronic transport in graphene, two-dimensional materials, and van der Waals heterostructures.

faculty.name: Evelyn Hu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on nanoscale photonic and quantum devices and the fabrication of engineered semiconductor materials.

faculty.name: Vinothan N. Manoharan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies self-assembly of colloidal particles and soft-matter physics using optical methods.

faculty.name: Zhigang Suo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the mechanics of materials, including soft materials, tough hydrogels, and electromechanical systems.

faculty.name: Donhee Ham
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on electronic devices and circuits, including brain-inspired chips and nanoelectronic bio-interfaces.

faculty.name: Frans A. Spaepen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure and properties of materials, including metallic glasses and colloidal crystals; serves as a director of graduate studies for Applied Physics.

faculty.name: Joanna Aizenberg
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on biologically inspired materials, self-assembly, wettability, and adaptive surfaces.

faculty.name: Jennifer Lewis
faculty.title: Hansjorg Wyss Professor of Biologically Inspired Engineering
faculty.summary: World leader in 3D printing of functional, structural, and biological materials. Pioneered multimaterial 3D printing for soft robotics, printed electronics, vascularized tissues, and structural materials. Her innovations are commercialized through multiple startups. Member of the National Academy of Engineering.

faculty.name: Kit Parker
faculty.title: Tarr Family Professor of Bioengineering and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Army veteran and Harvard professor who builds human heart tissue on chips to study cardiac disease and drug responses. His group bridges fundamental biophysics with tissue engineering, creating models of neuromuscular and cardiac diseases. Multiple startup companies spun out.

faculty.name: Efthimios Kaxiras
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops computational methods for electronic structure and quantum materials, including twisted graphene.

faculty.name: Julia A. Mundy
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Synthesizes atomically precise complex-oxide thin films to engineer new quantum materials.

faculty.name: David J. Mooney
faculty.title: Robert P. Pinkas Family Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Leader in biomaterials for immunoengineering and tissue regeneration. His group developed implantable biomaterial scaffolds that program immune cells in situ for cancer immunotherapy — a transformational approach now in clinical trials. Member of the National Academy of Engineering.

faculty.name: Katia Bertoldi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies mechanical metamaterials and how instabilities and geometry produce novel material behaviors.

faculty.name: Boris Kozinsky
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops machine-learning and first-principles methods for materials discovery, including energy and battery materials.

faculty.name: Michael J. Aziz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on materials for energy storage and conversion, including organic flow batteries.

faculty.name: Daniel Needleman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the biophysics of cell division, the cytoskeleton, and self-organization in living matter.

faculty.name: Joost J. Vlassak
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies mechanical behavior of thin films and materials, and develops microfabricated characterization tools.

faculty.name: Philippe Cluzel
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Quantitative biologist studying gene regulation and behavior in single cells and microbial systems.

faculty.name: Zachary Schiffer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on electrochemical reaction engineering for decarbonization and sustainable chemical manufacturing.

faculty.name: Maxim Prigozhin
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Biology developing optical and single-molecule imaging methods to study biomolecular dynamics.

faculty.name: David Mooney
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops biomaterials and hydrogels for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and cancer immunotherapy.

faculty.name: Samir Mitragotri
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on drug delivery technologies, including transdermal and targeted delivery systems.

faculty.name: Kevin Kit Parker
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies cardiac tissue biophysics and builds engineered tissues and organs-on-chips.

faculty.name: Jia Liu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops soft, tissue-integrated bioelectronics and cyborg-engineering tools for neuroscience, cardiac disease, and developmental biology.

faculty.name: Sharad Ramanathan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies decision-making in cells and developmental systems using theory and quantitative experiments.

faculty.name: Doeke Romke Hekstra
faculty.title: Unknown/Verify
faculty.summary: Studies protein conformational dynamics and molecular biophysics using structural and quantitative methods; exact professorial rank should be verified.

faculty.name: Ahmad S. Khalil
faculty.title: Unknown/Verify
faculty.summary: Synthetic biologist (listed among Applied Physics affiliated faculty) working on engineered gene circuits and cellular systems; primary appointment and rank should be verified.

faculty.name: Markus Basan
faculty.title: Unknown/Verify
faculty.summary: Studies quantitative microbial physiology and metabolism; exact professorial rank should be verified.

faculty.name: Martin Bechthold
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on materials, digital fabrication, and design robotics; appointment is at the Graduate School of Design with Applied Physics affiliation.

faculty.name: David Clarke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies structural and functional materials, including ceramics, coatings, and electromechanical materials.

faculty.name: Roy G. Gordon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on thin-film materials chemistry, atomic layer deposition, and materials for energy applications.

faculty.name: Jenny Hoffman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses scanning probe microscopy to study superconductors, topological materials, and engineered thin films.

faculty.name: Jennifer A. Lewis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneers 3D printing of functional and biological materials through engineered inks and additive manufacturing.

faculty.name: Conor Walsh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops soft wearable robotic devices and exosuits for augmentation and rehabilitation.

faculty.name: Gage Hills
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops emerging nanoelectronic technologies, including carbon-nanotube-based computing systems.

faculty.name: Marko Loncar
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on integrated and quantum nanophotonics, including thin-film lithium niobate and diamond photonic devices.

faculty.name: Kiyoul Yang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops integrated photonic devices and systems, including chip-scale frequency combs and quantum photonics.

faculty.name: Anurag Anshu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of Computer Science working on quantum information theory, Hamiltonian complexity, and quantum algorithms.

faculty.name: Sitan Chen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of Computer Science working on the theory of machine learning and quantum learning algorithms.

faculty.name: Giulia Semeghini
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental AMO physicist using neutral-atom arrays for quantum simulation and quantum information.

faculty.name: Amir Yacoby
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies quantum electronic systems, spin qubits, and nanoscale magnetic sensing.

faculty.name: Michael P. Brenner
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Applied mathematician working on fluid dynamics, machine learning for science, and problems in climate technology.

faculty.name: David Brooks
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on energy-efficient computer architecture and hardware systems for machine learning.

faculty.name: Frank N. Keutsch
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies atmospheric chemistry, aerosols, and climate, including field and laboratory spectroscopy.

faculty.name: Petros Koumoutsakos
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on computational science and engineering, combining simulation, fluid dynamics, and machine learning.

faculty.name: Na Li
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on control, optimization, and learning for networked and energy systems.

faculty.name: John H. Shaw
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies structural geology and geophysics, including earthquake hazards and subsurface energy resources.

faculty.name: Le Xie
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on electric power systems, grid data analytics, and the integration of renewable energy.

faculty.name: David R. Nelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical physicist working on soft matter, biophysics, and statistical mechanics of ordered and living systems.

faculty.name: L. Mahadevan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on the physics and mathematics of living and non-living matter, including morphogenesis and biomechanics.

faculty.name: Robert J. Wood
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops insect-scale and soft robots and the microfabrication and actuation technologies behind them.

faculty.name: Lene V. Hau
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on quantum optics, ultracold atoms, and light-matter interactions, including slowing and stopping light.

faculty.name: Robert M. Westervelt
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental physicist working on nanoscale electronic systems, imaging of electron flow, and quantum devices.

funding.note: Fully funded (SEAS PhD guarantee: tuition + stipend)

faculty.name: Isaac S. Kohane
faculty.title: Professor and Chair of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Founding Chair of DBMI at Harvard Medical School. Pioneer in biomedical informatics and clinical data science. Creator of the i2b2 platform. Leads the Undiagnosed Diseases Network Coordinating Center. Work on neuropsychiatric disease genomics and research data-sharing infrastructure.

faculty.name: Peter J. Park
faculty.title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in cancer genomics and mutational processes. Work on computational methods for genome and epigenome analysis, somatic mutations in cancer and normal cells. Director of the Park Lab for computational biology.

faculty.name: Tianxi Cai
faculty.title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; John Rock Professor of Population and Translational Data Sciences, Harvard Chan School
faculty.summary: Leading biostatistician developing statistical and machine learning methods for electronic health record data mining. Work on predictive modeling, real-world evidence generation, and personalized medicine. Co-director of CELEHS (Cai Lab).

faculty.name: Shamil R. Sunyaev
faculty.title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in population genetic variation and evolutionary genomics. Work on analyzing patterns of sequence divergence to understand disease risk, human evolution, and the functional impact of genetic variants.

faculty.name: Heng Li
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Associate Professor of Data Science, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
faculty.summary: Creator of widely-used bioinformatics tools including BWA, SAMtools, minimap2, and hifiasm, collectively cited over 100,000 times. Leading researcher in sequence alignment algorithms, genome assembly, and computational methods for biological problems.

faculty.name: Nils Gehlenborg
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in computational visualization techniques for biomedical data. Director of the HIDIVE Lab. Co-founder of BioVis and VIZBI. Work on visualizing heterogeneous data from large-scale cancer genomics studies (TCGA), 3D genome conformation, and EHR data.

faculty.name: Chirag Patel
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in computational and bioinformatics methods for studying gene-environment interactions. Work on the exposome, integrating EHR data to understand complex disease etiology, and machine learning approaches to environmental health.

faculty.name: Maha Farhat
faculty.title: Gilbert S. Omenn Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leader in translational genomics and informatics for drug-resistant tuberculosis and other infectious diseases. Work on bacterial genome-wide association studies, phenotype prediction from genomic data, and clinical applications of microbial genomics.

faculty.name: Michael Baym
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in microbial evolutionary genomics. Work on visualizing and understanding the evolution of antibiotic resistance. Combines experimental microbiology with computational approaches to study genetic arms races between bacteria and drugs.

faculty.name: Paul Avillach
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Researcher in translational bioinformatics focused on integrating multiple heterogeneous data sources (clinical, genomic, environmental) for clinical applications. Work on federated data query systems and clinical decision support.

faculty.name: Pranav Rajpurkar
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher building reliable AI technologies for biomedical decision-making. Work on medical AI benchmarks, foundation models for medical imaging, and AI systems that match or exceed physician performance on diagnostic tasks. High-impact across medicine and AI.

faculty.name: Marinka Zitnik
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Rising star in AI/ML for biomedical networked systems. Work on infusing structure and domain knowledge into machine learning for drug discovery, therapeutic recommendation, and scientific discovery. Pioneer in biomedical knowledge graph methods.

faculty.name: Arjun K. Manrai
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Researcher in machine learning for medical decision-making. Work on quantitative approaches to support physicians, addressing bias and health disparities in clinical algorithms, and translating biomedical data science into clinical practice.

faculty.name: Kun-Hsing Yu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in cancer multi-omics integration spanning genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics. Work on computational pathology and AI-driven cancer diagnostics. Bridges machine learning, molecular biology, and clinical oncology.

faculty.name: Luke O'Connor
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
faculty.summary: Researcher in statistical genetics and complex trait analysis. Work on understanding how genetic variation influences gene regulation and complex disease risk. Developing computational methods for integrative genetic analysis.

faculty.name: Adam E. Cohen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops optical and molecular tools, including fluorescent reporters of membrane voltage, to probe electrical signaling in cells and map neural and cardiac activity across scales from single molecules to whole organisms.

faculty.name: Xiaowei Zhuang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: HHMI Investigator who develops advanced imaging methods with single-molecule sensitivity and molecular-scale resolution, including super-resolution microscopy and MERFISH spatial genomics, to visualize cellular structures from chromatin organization to neuronal connectivity.

faculty.name: Andrew W. Murray
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses budding yeast, experimental evolution, and synthetic biology to uncover the 'rules of the game' that explain how cells function, evolve, and generate biological novelty in response to environmental pressures.

faculty.name: Rachelle Gaudet
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the mechanisms of signaling and transport across cellular membranes, using structural biology, biochemistry, and computation to study Nramp transporters, non-classical cadherins, ABC transporters, and TRP channels.

faculty.name: Nicholas Bellono
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how organisms adapt to their ecological and behavioral niches by dissecting signal transduction and ion-channel biophysics in specialized biological systems, connecting molecular mechanisms to organismal physiology and behavior.

faculty.name: Vinothan N. Manoharan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Wagner Family Professor of Chemical Engineering and Professor of Physics whose research spans soft matter and biophysics, studying self-assembly and developing optical methods such as engineered structural color and tools to manipulate microscale particles.

faculty.name: Sean R. Eddy
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: HHMI Investigator who uses computational and probabilistic modeling of genome sequences to reconstruct evolutionary history, emphasizing RNA structure and function and improved methods for remote protein homology detection.

faculty.name: Michael P. Brenner
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Catalyst Professor of Applied Mathematics and Applied Physics who uses mathematics and computation to study fluid mechanics, soft matter, and biological self-organization, including AI-assisted approaches to biomolecule design.

faculty.name: L. Mahadevan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Lola England de Valpine Professor whose work applies mathematics and physics to soft matter, active systems, and biomechanics, modeling collective behavior and the mechanics of living systems.

faculty.name: Sharad Ramanathan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how multipotent cells receive and process signals to build correctly patterned tissues during early human development, and how neural circuits (e.g., in C. elegans) process signals to drive decision-making and behavior.

faculty.name: Ethan Garner
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the self-organizing mechanisms that create and read out long-range shape in bacteria and archaea, using genetics, biochemistry, and biophysical imaging to examine cytoskeletal dynamics and cell-wall synthesis.

faculty.name: Philippe Cluzel
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Molecular and Cellular Biology and Gordon McKay Professor of Applied Physics whose lab performs real-time systems analysis of signal transduction and genetic networks at the single-cell level, combining experiment and computation.

faculty.name: Maofu Liao
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor of Cell Biology who uses single-particle cryo-electron microscopy and biochemistry to determine structures and mechanisms of membrane proteins and protein-DNA/RNA complexes, including transporters, CRISPR, and lipid-interacting proteins.

faculty.name: Eugene I. Shakhnovich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Roy G. Gordon Professor of Chemistry whose group integrates theory, computation, and experiment to understand the physical principles of protein folding, functional dynamics, molecular evolution, drug resistance, and the origins of life.

faculty.name: Andrew C. Kruse
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology who uses protein engineering, structural biology, and pharmacology to elucidate the molecular basis of membrane-protein signaling, focusing on G protein-coupled receptors and other targets in neurotransmission and metabolism.

faculty.name: Stephen C. Harrison
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: HHMI Investigator and Professor of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology who leads the Laboratory of Structural Cell Biology, using crystallography and cryo-EM to study viral architecture and cell entry, protein-DNA recognition, and signaling mechanisms.

faculty.name: David R. Nelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Arthur K. Solomon Professor of Biophysics and Professor of Physics whose research spans collective effects in condensed matter and physical biology, including single-molecule biophysics, spatial population genetics, and the buckling of viral shells.

faculty.name: Vamsi K. Mootha
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: HHMI Investigator and Professor of Systems Biology and of Medicine (based at Massachusetts General Hospital) who combines genomics, systems biology, and classical biochemistry to study mitochondrial bioenergetics, evolution, and disease, including membrane biophysics of ion and metabolite transport.

faculty.name: Johan Paulsson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Systems Biology who studies how molecular randomness affects cellular processes in single cells, using theory and experiment to understand noise in gene networks and how cells exploit or suppress fluctuations.

faculty.name: Debora S. Marks
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Systems Biology who directs a computational biology lab building methods, drawing on statistical physics and machine learning, to model protein conformational plasticity, predict the effects of mutations on disease and drug response, and design synthetic proteins.

faculty.name: Timothy A. Springer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Latham Family Professor of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology (Boston Children's Hospital) who studies how protein conformational change and tensile force activate integrins, von Willebrand factor, TGF-beta family members, and malaria-sporozoite adhesins.

faculty.name: Wesley P. Wong
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology and of Pediatrics (Boston Children's Hospital / Wyss Institute) who develops and applies single-molecule manipulation and detection methods, including DNA nanoswitch technology, to understand the physical basis of biological systems at the nanoscale.

faculty.name: John Quackenbush
faculty.title: Professor of Computational Biology and Bioinformatics; Chair, Department of Biostatistics
faculty.sub_field: computational biology and gene regulatory networks
faculty.summary: Quackenbush, who chairs the Department of Biostatistics, uses massive genomic and regulatory data to probe how many small effects combine to influence human health and disease, developing network-based methods to understand disease mechanisms.

faculty.name: Xihong Lin
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Lin develops scalable statistical and machine learning/AI methods for the analysis of massive and complex genetic, genomic, epidemiological, and health data, with applications including whole genome sequencing studies and polygenic risk prediction. She holds a joint appointment as Professor and Chair of the Department of Statistics at Harvard University.

faculty.name: Francesca Dominici
faculty.title: Clarence James Gamble Professor of Biostatistics, Population, and Data Science
faculty.summary: Dominici's research applies machine learning, artificial intelligence, and causal inference to environmental and climate policy, in particular using large-scale air pollution studies to inform and strengthen environmental regulations.

faculty.name: Tianxi Cai
faculty.title: John Rock Professor of Population and Translational Data Sciences
faculty.sub_field: machine learning, EHR, and biomedical informatics
faculty.summary: Cai develops statistical and machine learning methods for biomarker evaluation, risk prediction, model selection, and personalized medicine, with emphasis on integrating high-dimensional data and electronic health records for translational research.

faculty.name: Rafael A. Irizarry
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Irizarry focuses on the analysis and signal processing of microarray, next-generation sequencing, and genomic data, and is a founder of the Bioconductor project; current work leverages this expertise for developing diagnostic tools and discovering biomarkers. He also chairs the Department of Data Sciences at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

faculty.name: Curtis Huttenhower
faculty.title: Professor of Computational Biology and Bioinformatics
faculty.summary: Huttenhower works at the intersection of microbial community function and human health, developing computational methods to understand how microbial communities in the human body influence health outcomes.

faculty.name: Giovanni Parmigiani
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Parmigiani develops models and software for predicting who is at risk of carrying genetic variants that confer cancer susceptibility, along with Bayesian statistical methods for analyzing genomic data and comparative effectiveness research.

faculty.name: Brent Coull
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Coull's methodological research covers categorical data analysis and semiparametric regression modeling, applied to environmental health questions such as air pollution effects and complex exposure mixtures.

faculty.name: Rui Duan
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Duan develops statistical and computational methods for integrating evidence across different data sources and identifying signals from high-dimensional data, while accounting for the suboptimality of real-world data such as missing values and measurement error.

faculty.name: Junwei Lu
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Lu develops machine learning and high-dimensional statistical methods, including large-scale knowledge graphs and medical embedding vectors derived from electronic health records.

faculty.name: Lorenzo Trippa
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Trippa develops adaptive clinical trial designs and studies algorithms and methodologies for analyzing data generated by adaptive trials, including applications of Bayesian nonparametrics in biomedical research.

faculty.name: Jeffrey W. Miller
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Miller develops statistical methods, using high-throughput genomic data to build mathematical models of the key biological processes and molecular mechanisms that underlie age-related decline in general, and cancer in particular.

faculty.name: Nima Hejazi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Hejazi explores how advances in causal inference, statistical machine learning, and computational statistics catalyze discovery in the biomedical and public health sciences, developing inference methods that incorporate flexible machine learning while providing strong uncertainty quantification.

faculty.name: Rajarshi Mukherjee
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Mukherjee develops biostatistical methods for high-dimensional inference and epidemiological studies, addressing problems such as selection bias in emulated target trials as well as environmental health questions like lead exposure and cognition.

faculty.name: Martin Aryee
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Aryee develops computational methods for analyzing complex biological data, with applications spanning cancer genomics, hematologic malignancies, epigenomics, and single-cell transcriptomics.

faculty.name: Christoph Lange
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Lange works at the intersection of biostatistical methodology, numerical analysis, and computer science, addressing statistical and computational challenges in genome-wide association and whole-genome sequencing studies, with collaborative research in asthma, COPD, and Alzheimer's genetics.

faculty.name: Georg Hahn
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Hahn develops statistical methodology in the Biostatistics Department, with emphasis on computational and statistical methods including real-world evidence analysis and applications in statistical genetics.

faculty.name: Rachel Nethery
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Nethery develops statistical methods for environmental and population health questions, focusing on estimating the health impacts of environmental contaminant exposures and policies, and studying the effects of extreme weather exposures and natural disasters on health.

faculty.name: Jukka-Pekka (JP) Onnela
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Onnela's research spans statistical network science and digital phenotyping, defined as the moment-by-moment quantification of individual-level human phenotypes using data from smartphones and other personal digital devices.

faculty.name: Briana Joy K. Stephenson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Stephenson uses Bayesian methods to create innovative model-based clustering techniques that address data complexities in large, heterogeneous populations, with collaborative applications in maternal health, nutritional epidemiology, cardiovascular disease, and cancer disparities.

faculty.name: L. J. Wei
faculty.title: Professor of Biostatistics
faculty.summary: Wei develops statistical methods for the design and analysis of clinical trials, having introduced the urn design for sequential studies, response-adaptive designs, and multivariate methods for analyzing data with multiple outcomes.

faculty.name: Adam E. Cohen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops new physical tools to study molecules and cells, including the first fluorescent voltage-indicating proteins that enable all-optical mapping of neural activity. Holds joint appointments in Chemistry & Chemical Biology and Physics.

faculty.name: Eric J. Heller
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneers time-dependent wavepacket methods for molecular spectroscopy and reaction dynamics. Known for discovering quantum scarring of wavefunctions by unstable periodic orbits, and extending wave mechanics to electron flow in 2D materials and graphene quantum dots. Earned his PhD in Chemical Physics from Harvard.

faculty.name: Hongkun Park
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of quantum materials, nanophotonics, and bio-nano interfaces. Pioneered single-molecule transistors and developed diamond NV-center quantum sensors for room-temperature NMR detection of single proteins. Currently on leave as Corporate President of Samsung Electronics.

faculty.name: Kang-Kuen Ni
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Creates ultracold molecules at temperatures near absolute zero to study quantum-controlled chemical reactions. Recently demonstrated a two-qubit entangling quantum gate using individually controlled molecules, advancing molecular quantum information science.

faculty.name: Joonho Lee
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical and computational methods for electron-electron and electron-vibration correlation problems. Applies quantum chemistry and quantum computing methods to energy-relevant materials including perovskites, moire materials, and electrocatalysis. Also a visiting researcher at Google Quantum AI.

faculty.name: Eugene I. Shakhnovich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses statistical mechanics, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to understand protein folding principles, the relationship between amino acid sequence and structure, and how protein stability mutations affect organismal fitness.

faculty.name: Boris Kozinsky
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads the Materials Intelligence Research group developing ML-accelerated atomistic and electronic structure methods for functional materials. Creator of the NequIP and Allegro neural network interatomic potentials, applied to catalysts, batteries, and 2D materials. Joint appointment with SEAS.

faculty.name: Jarad A. Mason
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Designs new classes of porous materials including liquids with intrinsic microporosity, microporous nanocrystals for gas transport in aqueous environments, and barocaloric materials for sustainable solid-state heating and cooling. Applies synthetic chemistry and nanoscience to challenges in energy, sustainability, and medicine.

faculty.name: Frank N. Keutsch
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies photochemical oxidation of volatile organic compounds that produce tropospheric ozone and secondary organic aerosol, combining field observations aboard NASA aircraft, laboratory kinetics studies, and laser-induced fluorescence instrument development. Also leads the SCoPEx solar geoengineering research project.

faculty.name: Daniel G. Nocera
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneered the artificial leaf — a silicon solar cell coated with self-healing catalysts that splits water into hydrogen and oxygen at high efficiency. Extended this to the bionic leaf, integrating engineered bacteria to produce liquid fuels and renewable ammonia fertilizer from sunlight, air, and water.

faculty.name: James G. Anderson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneered measurements of chlorine radical chain reactions that directly linked CFCs to stratospheric ozone depletion, informing the Montreal Protocol. Develops advanced laser, lidar, and high-altitude aircraft instrumentation to study climate-radiation-dynamics coupling in the atmosphere.

faculty.name: Joanna Aizenberg
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneers biomimetic materials chemistry, studying biological architectures such as biominerals and using those principles to design bio-inspired synthetic materials. Inventor of SLIPS (Slippery Liquid-Infused Porous Surfaces), omniphobic self-healing coatings inspired by pitcher plants. Holds joint appointments with SEAS and the Wyss Institute.

faculty.name: George M. Whitesides
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Developed foundational technologies including self-assembled monolayers on gold, soft lithography for nanofabrication, and paper-based microfluidic diagnostics. Currently investigates the origin of life through prebiotic chemistry, with over 1,200 publications and the highest Hirsch index of any living chemist.

faculty.name: Xiaowei Zhuang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Invented STORM super-resolution microscopy that overcomes the diffraction limit, and MERFISH for genome-scale single-cell imaging of thousands of RNA species simultaneously. Created a comprehensive cell atlas of the entire adult mouse brain. Joint appointment in Chemistry & Chemical Biology and Physics.

faculty.name: Efthimios Kaxiras
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Holds the John Hasbrouck Van Vleck Professorship in Physics with an affiliate appointment in Chemistry and Chemical Biology. Works on electronic properties of solids, graphene and 2D materials, and machine learning for materials modeling. Founding Director of the Institute for Applied Computational Science.

faculty.name: Roy G. Gordon
faculty.title: Professor Emeritus
faculty.summary: Studied chemical physics at Harvard under Nobel laureate J.H. Van Vleck. Research spans quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, chemical vapor deposition of thin films for solar cells and energy-efficient windows, and flow batteries for grid-scale energy storage. Elected to National Academy of Sciences in 1975.

faculty.name: Dudley R. Herschbach
faculty.title: Professor Emeritus
faculty.summary: Nobel Laureate (1986) who pioneered crossed molecular beam experiments that revealed detailed molecular-level mechanisms of elementary chemical reactions in single collisions. His work uncovered both rebound and stripping reaction dynamics, fundamentally transforming the field of chemical reaction dynamics.

faculty.name: Cynthia M. Friend
faculty.title: Professor Emerita
faculty.summary: First female full professor of chemistry at Harvard (1989). Research focused on heterogeneous catalysis on coinage metals and their alloys, developing selective catalytic syntheses. Directed the DOE Energy Frontier Research Center IMASC on mesoscale architectures for sustainable catalysis. Now President of the Kavli Foundation.

faculty.summary: Researches large-scale distributed systems, web systems, and security and privacy.

faculty.name: Daniel Jacob
faculty.title: Vasco McCoy Family Professor of Atmospheric Chemistry and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Jacob's group uses atmospheric observations from satellites and other platforms combined with advanced models to understand the chemical composition of the atmosphere, its perturbation by human activity, and the implications for climate and life on Earth.

faculty.name: James G. Anderson
faculty.title: Philip S. Weld Professor of Atmospheric Chemistry
faculty.summary: The Anderson Group develops lasers, lidars, radars, hyperspectral imaging, and in-situ instruments deployed on airborne stratospheric platforms to study free-radical kinetics, catalytic processes controlling ozone, and global climate change.

faculty.name: Frank N Keutsch
faculty.title: Stonington Professor of Engineering and Atmospheric Science and Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Biology
faculty.summary: Research in the Keutsch group aims to improve understanding of the photochemical oxidation of volatile organic compounds that produce tropospheric ozone and secondary organic aerosol, which affect human health and comprise the largest uncertainties in estimates of anthropogenic climate forcing.

faculty.name: Scot T. Martin
faculty.title: Gordon McKay Professor of Environmental Science and Engineering and Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Martin studies the chemistry of the atmosphere and environmental systems, including aerosol particles, atmosphere-biosphere interactions, and biogeochemical processes, with field and laboratory work spanning tropical forest and urban environments.

faculty.name: Steven C. Wofsy
faculty.title: Abbott Lawrence Rotch Professor of Atmospheric and Environmental Science
faculty.summary: Wofsy studies the chemistry of the atmosphere on global and regional scales, including stratospheric and tropospheric chemistry, and leads forest and atmospheric measurement programs tracking greenhouse gases and the carbon cycle.

faculty.name: Zhiming Kuang
faculty.title: Gordon McKay Professor of Atmospheric and Environmental Science and of Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: Kuang's research seeks to understand and simulate how tropical convection interacts with the large-scale flow, a key control on tropical circulation, rainfall distribution, and its variability, with implications for monsoon droughts and floods.

faculty.name: Peter John Huybers
faculty.title: Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences and of Environmental Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Huybers studies how and why climate changes and the implications for human wellbeing, spanning paleoclimate, ice dynamics and sea level, ocean processes, and climate impacts on agriculture and society.

faculty.name: Eli Tziperman
faculty.title: Pamela and Vasco McCoy, Jr. Professor of Oceanography and Applied Physics
faculty.summary: Tziperman's research addresses ocean, atmosphere, and climate dynamics, seeking to understand physical processes that affect Earth's climate on time scales from a few years to millions of years, in the past, present, and future.

faculty.name: Kaighin A McColl
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences and of Environmental Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: McColl's work focuses on understanding the terrestrial water cycle and its changes in a warming world, using theory, numerical models, and observations of land-atmosphere interactions.

faculty.name: Fiamma Straneo
faculty.title: Gordon McKay Professor of Environmental Science and Engineering and Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Straneo's research focuses on the climate of the polar regions, including the interactions of the ocean, ice sheets, and sea ice, and their role in climate change and sea-level rise.

faculty.name: Robin Wordsworth
faculty.title: Gordon McKay Professor of Environmental Science and Engineering and Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Wordsworth's research focuses on planetary climate, atmospheric evolution, and habitability, both in the solar system and around other stars, using fluid dynamics and radiative modeling.

faculty.name: Elsie M Sunderland
faculty.title: Fred Kavli Professor of Environmental Chemistry and Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Research in the Sunderland Lab examines how biogeochemical processes affect the fate, transport, and food-web bioaccumulation of trace metals and organic chemicals, developing models across scales to characterize how changes in climate and emissions affect human and ecological health.

faculty.name: Ann Pearson
faculty.title: Murray and Martha Ross Professor of Environmental Sciences; Affiliate in Environmental Science & Engineering
faculty.summary: Pearson's research applies analytical chemistry, isotope geochemistry, and molecular biology to biogeochemical oceanography and Earth history, reconstructing carbon and nitrogen cycling in modern and ancient environments.

faculty.name: Daniel P. Schrag
faculty.title: Sturgis Hooper Professor of Geology and Professor of Environmental Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Schrag studies climate and climate change over Earth history and works on technological and policy approaches to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, including energy systems and carbon capture and storage; he co-directs the Science, Technology and Public Policy Program.

faculty.name: John H. Shaw
faculty.title: Harry C. Dudley Professor of Structural and Economic Geology and Professor of Environmental Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Shaw's research integrates structural geology, geophysics, and subsurface imaging to study earthquake hazards, fault systems, and energy resources, including carbon sequestration and subsurface energy systems.

faculty.name: Jerry X. Mitrovica
faculty.title: Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science; Affiliate in Environmental Science & Engineering
faculty.summary: Mitrovica studies the Earth's response to external and internal forcings across time scales from seconds to billions of years, including ice-age geodynamics, the rotational stability of planets, and the geophysical signatures of ice-sheet mass change and sea-level rise.

faculty.name: Paul R Moorcroft
faculty.title: Professor of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology; Affiliate in Environmental Science & Engineering
faculty.summary: Moorcroft's research focuses on the ecological dynamics of terrestrial plant communities and ecosystems and their interactions with the atmosphere, developing mathematical and statistical models of vegetation dynamics and biosphere-atmosphere exchange.

faculty.name: Noel Michele Holbrook
faculty.title: Charles Bullard Professor of Forestry; Affiliate in Environmental Science & Engineering
faculty.summary: Holbrook studies the physics and physiology of vascular transport in plants to understand how constraints on the movement of water and solutes between soil and leaves influence ecological and evolutionary processes, including stomatal regulation and xylem embolism during drought.

faculty.name: Hannah Greenwald Healy
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Environmental Health and Exposure Science
faculty.summary: Healy's research studies pathogens and microbiomes of engineered water systems to inform water management and treatment, infectious disease surveillance, and healthcare infection prevention; she leads the Healy Health 'Omics (H2O) Lab.

faculty.name: Daniel Jafferis

faculty.name: Matthew Schwartz

faculty.name: Douglas Finkbeiner

faculty.name: John Kovac

faculty.name: Xing Fan

faculty.name: Lene V. Hau
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Mikhail D. Lukin
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Hongkun Park
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Norman Y. Yao
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Eric J. Heller
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Susanne F. Yelin
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Michael P. Brenner

faculty.name: SueYeon Chung

faculty.name: Adam E. Cohen

faculty.name: Michael M. Desai
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: L. Mahadevan
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Mara Prentiss
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Sunghan Ro
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Aravinthan D. T. Samuel

faculty.name: Jennifer E. Hoffman

faculty.name: Matteo Mitrano
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Julia A. Mundy
faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Su-Yang Xu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Eslam Khalaf
faculty.title: Assistant Professor

faculty.name: Carlos Argüelles-Delgado
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Physics

faculty.name: Stefan Knirck
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimentalist searching for axion dark matter using novel detectors at the intersection of particle physics, quantum sensing, and photonics.

faculty.name: Masahiro Morii
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Arthur M. Jaffe

faculty.name: Sonia Paban

faculty.name: Matthew D. Schwartz
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Xi Yin
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Peter Galison
faculty.title: University Professor

programs.program_name: Speech and Hearing Bioscience and Technology

faculty.name: Xihong Lin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops scalable statistical and machine learning methods for massive genomic and health data, including whole genome sequencing studies, polygenic risk prediction, causal inference, and federated learning for multi-ethnic biobanks. Also works on COVID-19 epidemic modeling and single-cell multi-omics analysis.

faculty.name: Samuel Kou
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops stochastic models for single-molecule biophysics and statistical methods for Bayesian inference, including the equi-energy sampler and catalytic prior distributions. Also works on big data analytics, digital disease tracking, and Monte Carlo methods.

faculty.name: Susan Murphy
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Reinforcement Learning, Causal Inference, Mobile Health
faculty.summary: Leads the Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab, developing adaptive interventions and just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs) using reinforcement learning for real-time mobile health treatment delivery. Focuses on causal inference for adaptively sampled clinical trial data in substance use, physical activity, and oral health.

faculty.name: Xiao-Li Meng
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Theoretical Statistics, Bayesian Inference, Data Science
faculty.summary: Works on the theoretical foundations of statistical inference from Bayesian, Fiducial, and Frequentist perspectives, with contributions to the EM algorithm, MCMC methods, and bridge/path sampling. Founding editor-in-chief of the Harvard Data Science Review.

faculty.name: Neil Shephard
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Financial Econometrics, Bayesian Nonparametrics, Causal Inference
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methodology for financial econometrics including high-frequency data analysis and simulation-based inference. Also works on defining causality for time series experiments and Bayesian nonparametric methods.

faculty.name: Kosuke Imai
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Causal Inference, Computational Social Science, Political Methodology
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods and machine learning algorithms for social science research, including causal inference with experimental and observational data, algorithmic redistricting analysis, data-driven policy evaluation, and fairness in algorithmic decision-making.

faculty.name: Lucas Janson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops methods for high-dimensional inference including model-X knockoffs for controlled variable selection, and works on reinforcement learning, uncertainty quantification for adaptively collected data, and interpretable AI. Applies these methods in genetics, political science, and microbiome research.

faculty.name: Natesh S. Pillai
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on computational statistics with a focus on Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithms, reinforcement learning, and applied probability, with applications in climate science and responsible AI. Also serves as a Distinguished Engineer at LinkedIn.

faculty.name: Sham Kakade
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Machine Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Foundation Models
faculty.summary: Works on the mathematical and scientific principles of large-scale machine learning, including scaling laws for foundation models, autonomous agent architectures, and full-stack training pipelines. Co-director of the Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence.

faculty.name: Tracy Ke
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Network Analysis, Text Analysis, High-Dimensional Statistics
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for network data analysis, text analysis and natural language processing, high-dimensional statistics, and machine learning, with applications in bioinformatics and statistical genetics.

faculty.name: Morgane Austern
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Probability, Machine Learning Theory, High-Dimensional Statistics
faculty.summary: Develops probability tools for modern machine learning, including limit theorems for dependent and structured data, cross-validation theory, debiased machine learning, generalization bounds, and random matrix theory, with applications to stable matching problems.

faculty.name: Mark Sellke
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Probability Theory, Mathematical Physics, Theoretical Computer Science
faculty.summary: Studies computational barriers and algorithmic thresholds in random complex systems including spin glasses, high-dimensional optimization, and machine learning theory. Explores the intersection of probability, statistical physics, and theoretical computer science.

faculty.name: Pragya Sur
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: High-Dimensional Statistics, Machine Learning Theory, Causal Inference
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical frameworks for high-dimensional statistics and machine learning, including overparametrized learning, distribution shifts, high-dimensional logistic regression, and uncertainty quantification. Also works on causal inference in high dimensions.

faculty.name: Subhabrata Sen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Probability, Spin Glasses, High-Dimensional Statistics
faculty.summary: Works on applied probability and its connections to statistics and machine learning, including sparse graph limit theory, large deviations for random graphs, spin glass theory, variational inference, and community detection on networks.

faculty.name: Joseph Blitzstein
faculty.title: Professor of the Practice
faculty.sub_field: Network Inference, Graphical Models, Statistics Education
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for network data analysis including respondent-driven sampling, link-tracing designs, and graphical models, combining probability theory and combinatorics with Monte Carlo algorithms such as sequential importance sampling and Markov chains.

faculty.name: Fadil Santosa
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops methods for inverse problems, wave propagation in complex media, and optimal design. Pioneered sparse L1-norm optimization for signal recovery and level-set methods for structural optimization. Recent work includes modeling direct air capture of CO2 and electromagnetics on graphene.

faculty.name: Amitabh Basu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on integer programming and mixed-integer optimization using techniques from convex geometry, geometry of numbers, and algebraic topology. Author of a forthcoming textbook on convexity in discrete and continuous optimization. NSF CAREER Award and INFORMS Egon Balas Prize recipient.

faculty.name: Carey E. Priebe
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for high-dimensional and graph-structured data, including spectral graph embedding, vertex nomination, and graph matching. Applies these methods to brain connectomics, human trafficking detection, and national security. Fellow of ASA and IMS.

faculty.name: Daniel Q. Naiman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of geometry, computing, and applied statistics. Developed the theory of abstract tubes using differential geometry for improved statistical inference and computational methods. Also directs the Financial Mathematics MSE program. IMS Fellow.

faculty.name: Edward R. Scheinerman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on discrete mathematics, graph theory, and combinatorics. Invented random dot product graphs, a widely used model for analyzing social and biological networks. Author of multiple textbooks including 'Mathematics: A Discrete Introduction.' Fellow of AMS.

faculty.name: Mauro Maggioni
faculty.title: Bloomberg Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Develops algorithms exploiting hidden geometric structures in high-dimensional data for machine learning. Created Geometric Multi-Resolution Analysis (GMRA) for data-supported manifold approximation. Also works on learning interaction laws from particle/agent-based systems. Fellow of AMS.

faculty.name: Gregory Eyink
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads theoretical research on fluid turbulence and nonequilibrium statistical physics. Provided the first published proof of Onsager's conjecture on turbulent energy dissipation and discovered spontaneous stochasticity in turbulent flows. Fellow of American Physical Society.

faculty.name: James C. Spall
faculty.title: Research Professor
faculty.summary: Invented the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) algorithm for efficient gradient approximation in high-dimensional optimization. Author of the most-cited textbook in stochastic optimization. Works on control, estimation, and reliability analysis. IEEE Fellow.

faculty.name: Mark Kramer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Bridges mathematical modeling, statistics, and machine learning with systems neuroscience. Develops quantitative methods to characterize neural dynamics from human brain voltage recordings, with applications to epilepsy, sleep, and memory. NSF CAREER Award recipient. Joining JHU July 2026.

faculty.name: Donniell E. Fishkind
faculty.title: Associate Research Professor
faculty.summary: Works on graph theory, matrix analysis, and graph matching algorithms. Applies graph methods to topological correction in medical imaging, probabilistic path planning, and scheduling problems. Also serves as Director of Undergraduate Studies in AMS.

faculty.name: Avanti Athreya
faculty.title: Associate Research Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical inference methods for random graphs, particularly random dot product graphs and latent structure models. Works on multi-sample graph inference via omnibus embeddings, community detection, and applications to brain connectomics.

faculty.name: Nicolas Loizou
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops large-scale optimization algorithms for modern machine learning, with a focus on adaptive (no-tuning-needed) learning rates, Polyak-type step sizes, and stochastic gradient methods. Also works on federated learning and algorithmic game theory. Received Johns Hopkins Catalyst Award.

faculty.name: Soledad Villar
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Designs machine learning models that respect symmetries from physical laws using group theory and invariant theory. Also studies expressive power of graph neural networks and applies GNNs to combinatorial optimization. Sloan Research Fellow and NSF CAREER Award recipient.

faculty.name: Dmitriy (Tim) Kunisky
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Explores the intersection of probability theory, mathematical statistics, and computational complexity. Studies information-computation gaps where datasets contain enough statistical signal but no efficient algorithm can detect it. Uses sum-of-squares relaxations and random matrix theory.

faculty.name: Daniel Grimmer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on extending the reach of first-order optimization theory, developing theoretical guarantees and improved algorithms for convex and structured optimization problems. PhD in Operations Research from Cornell University.

faculty.name: James Guest
faculty.title: Professor and Department Head
faculty.summary: Researches topology optimization for structural design, developing algorithms for design under uncertainty, design for manufacturability, and multifunctional materials, with applications in aerospace, biomedical, energy, and infrastructure. Holds MS in civil engineering and operations research from Princeton.

faculty.name: Benjamin Schafer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches structural engineering of steel structures, particularly cold-formed steel. Developed the internationally approved Direct Strength Method and led first full-scale seismic tests on cold-formed steel buildings. Director of ROSEI and the Cold-Formed Steel Research Consortium.

faculty.name: Somnath Ghosh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches computational mechanics and multiscale/multiphysics modeling of materials, co-directing NASA's IMQCAM institute for digital twin development in additive manufacturing. Recipient of 2025 Theodore von Karman Medal and elected to European Academy of Sciences and Arts.

faculty.name: Lori Graham-Brady
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches mechanical behavior of materials with random microstructure applied to composites, metal alloys, and advanced ceramics, specializing in stochastic mechanics and structural reliability. HEMI Fellow.

faculty.name: Michael Shields
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Researches uncertainty quantification, ML, and stochastic methods for understanding the effects of uncertainties on materials and structures under extreme events. Recipient of DOE Early Career Award, NSF CAREER Award, and ONR Young Investigator Award. Leads the Center on High-Throughput Materials Discovery for Extremes.

faculty.name: Yury Dvorkin
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches AI and optimization for power grid management, including renewable energy integration, grid capacity optimization, and electricity market design. U.S. Director of the EPICS Center with joint appointment in Electrical & Computer Engineering.

faculty.name: Thomas Gernay
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Researches fire safety engineering and structural resilience to fire, developing computational models for structures under extreme thermal environments. Co-author of SAFIR software used by 300+ institutions worldwide. Recipient of NSF CAREER Award and ASCE Maryland Outstanding Educator of the Year.

faculty.name: Jan Drgona
faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Gonzalo Pita
faculty.title: Associate Research Professor

faculty.name: Susu Xu

faculty.name: Magdalena Klemun

faculty.name: Venkataraman "Venkat" Lakshmi
faculty.title: B. Howell Griswold, Jr. Professor in Geography and International Affairs
faculty.summary: Studies how water, land, and climate interact across landscapes using Earth observations, physical models, and AI/ML methods to better understand water resources and environmental impacts on human health.

faculty.name: Scot Miller
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Combines satellite data and statistics to understand greenhouse gas emissions across the globe.

faculty.name: Carsten Prasse
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on the occurrence and fate of organic contaminants in the urban water cycle and their impact on environmental and human health.

faculty.name: Sarah Preheim
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the microorganisms and environmental drivers of impairments to inland and coastal water bodies, such as oxygen depletion and algal blooms.

faculty.name: Ruggero Rossi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of electrochemistry, microbiology, and material science to achieve sustainable energy-water infrastructure and environmentally sustainable production of chemicals.

faculty.name: Shilva Shrestha
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on innovative biotechnologies to produce bioenergy and biochemicals that substitute for fossil-fuel-based products, address environmental problems, and strengthen the bioeconomy.

faculty.name: Alan Stone
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Applies chemistry fundamentals to biogeochemical processes to address issues of anthropogenic chemicals in the environment and engineered systems.

faculty.name: Steven Hanke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: An expert in financial statecraft, including water resource economics.

programs.program_name: Biology (Cellular, Molecular, Developmental Biology and Biophysics), PhD

faculty.name: Xin Chen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the epigenetic regulation of stem cell lineages, studying how chromatin and inherited histone marks control self-renewal versus differentiation decisions. HHMI Investigator in the Department of Biology.

faculty.name: Rejji Kuruvilla
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the sympathetic nervous system, focusing on its connectivity, development, and physiological functions and the neurotrophic signaling that shapes neuronal circuits.

faculty.name: Mark Van Doren
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates germ cell development and gonad formation, using Drosophila to study how sexual identity and the reproductive system are established.

faculty.name: Carl Wu
faculty.title: Bloomberg Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies eukaryotic chromatin structure and function, including the biochemistry of nucleosome remodeling and gene transcription and live-cell single-molecule imaging of histone and nuclear protein dynamics.

faculty.name: Vincent Hilser
faculty.title: Professor and Chair, Department of Biology
faculty.summary: Studies protein conformational fluctuations and their role in function, adaptation, and disease, developing statistical-thermodynamic frameworks for allostery and protein ensembles. Chair of the Department of Biology.

faculty.name: Steven A. Farber
faculty.title: Professor; Director, CMDB Graduate Program
faculty.summary: Uses real-time imaging in live zebrafish to study the cell and molecular biology of lipids, identifying genes that regulate digestive-organ lipid metabolism through biochemical and genetic strategies. Director of the CMDB Graduate Program.

faculty.name: Robert Johnston
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies development and gene regulation controlling cell-fate specification in human retinal organoids and fly eyes, including stochastic and deterministic mechanisms of photoreceptor patterning.

faculty.name: Yumi Kim
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates chromosome dynamics during meiosis, studying how chromosomes pair, recombine, and segregate to ensure genome integrity across generations.

faculty.name: John Kim
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works to decipher the biological function of microRNAs and other small RNAs encoded in the genome and how they regulate gene expression.

faculty.name: Tatjana Trcek
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the spatial organization of mRNAs and the regulation of post-transcriptional gene expression, using imaging to investigate RNA granules and germ-granule assembly.

faculty.name: Haiqing Zhao
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the function and development of olfactory sensory neurons and the molecular mechanisms of odor detection and signal transduction.

faculty.name: Andrew Gordus
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how innate behaviors are encoded at the cellular and genetic level in invertebrate systems, combining behavior, imaging, and genetics.

faculty.name: Nichole Broderick
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which the microbiome affects animal development, physiology, and immunity, using Drosophila as a model.

faculty.name: Erik Andersen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the genetics and genomics of complex traits, host-pathogen genomics and drug resistance, and evolutionary genetics, largely using natural variation in Caenorhabditis nematodes.

faculty.name: Damian Ekiert
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Combines microbiology, parasitology, structural biology, cell biology, and molecular biology to study host-pathogen interactions and the machinery bacteria use to build and maintain their cell envelopes.

faculty.name: Gira Bhabha
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies structural mechanisms and the cell biology of microbes using cryo-electron microscopy and cryo-electron tomography to understand molecular machines and host-pathogen systems.

faculty.name: Jocelyne DiRuggiero
faculty.title: Associate Research Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the molecular microbial ecology of extremophiles and the molecular mechanisms of stress response and ribosome rescue, with a focus on archaea living in extreme environments.

faculty.name: Douglas Barrick
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works toward an atomic-level description of structure and function in proteins, using repeat proteins as model systems to dissect folding, stability, and cooperativity. Department of Biophysics.

faculty.name: Karen Fleming
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure, energetics, and folding of membrane proteins, elucidating the biophysical principles that govern how membrane proteins fold and assemble. Department of Biophysics.

faculty.name: Gregory Bowman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies chromatin structure and nucleosome remodeling, investigating the mechanisms by which remodeling enzymes reposition nucleosomes to regulate access to DNA. Department of Biophysics.

faculty.name: Yuan He
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure and mechanism of how cells read, write, and repair the genome, using structural biology and biophysics to visualize large protein-DNA assemblies. Department of Biophysics.

faculty.name: Margaret Johnson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the control and dynamics of self-assembly in living systems using theory, modeling, and computation to understand how molecular components organize in space and time. Department of Biophysics.

faculty.name: Doug Barrick
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Statistical Thermodynamics, Protein Folding and Design
faculty.summary: Studies protein folding thermodynamics and design using repeat proteins as model systems, and investigates conformational transitions in the Notch signaling pathway that control cell fate determination. Authored the textbook Biothermodynamics: from Theory to Application.

faculty.name: Gregory Bowman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the structure and mechanisms of ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers such as Chd1 that reposition nucleosomes along DNA, using cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography to understand the twist-defect mechanism of nucleosome sliding.

faculty.name: Brian Camley
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses theory, computation, and simulation to study the physics of cell biology — how cells crawl, sense chemical gradients and electric fields, and migrate collectively through complex environments. Joint appointment with Physics and Astronomy.

faculty.name: Karen Fleming
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the physical principles of membrane protein folding and biogenesis in lipid bilayers, including chaperone functions and the BAM complex in Gram-negative bacteria. Elected AAAS Fellow in 2024 and received the Biophysical Society Avanti Award in Lipids.

faculty.name: Bertrand Garcia-Moreno
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies electrostatic effects in proteins using experimental and computational methods, focusing on buried ionizable groups in hydrophobic environments and engineering pH-sensitive switches for therapeutic applications. Serves as Executive Vice Dean of the Krieger School.

faculty.name: Thomas Graham
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops proximity-assisted photoactivation (PAPA) and single-molecule tracking methods to visualize individual endogenous molecular complexes regulating transcription in live cells. Joined the department in July 2025.

faculty.name: Yuan He
faculty.title: Bloomberg Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Uses cryo-electron microscopy and biochemical approaches to study how cells read, write, and repair their genomes, with focus on transcription initiation complexes and DNA double-strand break repair. Joined Johns Hopkins in January 2025 as a Bloomberg Distinguished Professor with appointments in Biophysics and Biology.

faculty.name: William Huang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates biochemical reactions at the cell membrane using reconstitution and single-molecule approaches, focusing on kinetic proofreading mechanisms in Ras GTPase activation and membrane localization effects on signaling.

faculty.name: Margaret Johnson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops computational and theoretical models of protein self-assembly on membranes, focusing on clathrin-mediated endocytosis and HIV-1 Gag lattice assembly. Creator of the NERDSS reaction-diffusion simulation package.

faculty.name: Albert Lau
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses molecular dynamics simulations and free energy calculations on supercomputers to study atomic mechanisms of ionotropic glutamate receptors that mediate excitatory synaptic transmission, informing drug discovery for neurological disorders.

faculty.name: Juliette Lecomte
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses NMR spectroscopy and other biophysical methods to investigate the structure, dynamics, and function of heme proteins, particularly truncated hemoglobins from bacteria, cyanobacteria, algae, and deep-sea extremophiles. Elected AAAS Fellow in 2023.

faculty.name: Evgenia Nikolova
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure and dynamics of nucleic acids and their protein complexes, focusing on how pioneer transcription factors such as Sox2 and Oct4 engage nucleosomes to remodel chromatin and activate gene expression. Joined the department in 2017.

faculty.name: Sarah Woodson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how RNA molecules fold into three-dimensional structures and how RNA-protein complexes such as the ribosome assemble, using single-molecule fluorescence, X-ray footprinting, and SAXS. Also investigates small non-coding RNAs and the Hfq chaperone in bacteria.

faculty.name: Yaojun Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical and computational models of biomolecular phase separation using statistical mechanics and polymer theory, studying how condensates form, the interface resistance that controls material exchange, and how phase separation organizes intracellular space. Named a 2025 Sloan Research Fellow.

faculty.name: Jacob Bernstein
faculty.title: Professor and Vice Chair
faculty.summary: Vice Chair. Research in geometric analysis, minimal surfaces, and mean curvature flow.
