faculty.name: Ludmilla Aristilde
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering (by courtesy); Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences (by
faculty.summary: Aristilde combines experimental and computational tools in chemistry and biochemistry to gain molecular insights into natural mineral and biological catalysts in environmental organic processes, with work on cellular carbon metabolism in environmental bacteria, extracellular enzyme dynamics, and the physical chemistry of organic contaminants.

faculty.name: Oluwaseyi Balogun
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and Mechanical Engineering
faculty.summary: Balogun's group studies the propagation of elastic vibrations in materials using optical and scanning probe techniques to characterize thermal conductivity, vibrational properties, and elastic properties of thin films, interfaces, and biological tissues, and to understand coupling of optical and acoustic oscillations in nanostructures.

faculty.name: Zdeněk Bažant
faculty.title: McCormick Institute Professor and Walter P. Murphy Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and (by courtesy) Mechanical Engineering and Materials Scien
faculty.summary: Bažant works on interdisciplinary problems in the mechanics of solids and structures, including nonlinear fracture mechanics, size effects and scaling of failure, damage micromechanics, creep in nanoporous materials, hydraulic fracturing of shale, and probabilistic mechanics of quasibrittle structures.

faculty.name: Neal Blair
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Blair studies the behavior of carbon on the Earth's surface, focusing on pathways of organic carbon decomposition and sequestration mediated by biological and physical processes in soils and sediments, integrated into conceptual models of carbon transformation across landscapes and the seafloor.

faculty.name: Giuseppe Buscarnera
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Director of Graduate Studies
faculty.summary: Buscarnera works on constitutive modeling of geomaterials, mechanics of unsaturated soils, chemo-mechanics of porous rocks, material stability theory, fracture and crushing in granular materials, and applications to natural hazards, slope stability, and landslide forecasting.

faculty.name: Giorgia Chinazzo
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Director of the Architectural Engineering and Design Program
faculty.summary: Chinazzo's work focuses on intelligent buildings that sense, adapt, and improve occupant quality of life while reducing environmental impact, blending engineering, architecture, data science, and health and social sciences to study how buildings influence people's health, well-being, and behavior.

faculty.name: Federico Ciardo
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Ciardo's research interests span geomechanics and applied mechanics for geophysical, geomechanical, and engineering problems, with an emphasis on computational mechanics.

faculty.name: Gianluca Cusatis
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and (by courtesy) Mechanical Engineering
faculty.summary: Cusatis works on the mechanics of infrastructure materials and constitutive modeling of concrete and cementitious composites, developing multiscale computational models for their deformation and failure.

faculty.name: Pablo Durango-Cohen
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Durango-Cohen develops and analyzes optimization and econometric models to support monitoring, management, and operation of transportation infrastructure systems, and has published in transportation economics and policy and life-cycle assessment, including work on decarbonization of freight transportation.

faculty.name: Jean-François Gaillard
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and (by courtesy) Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Gaillard's group works to understand the molecular and biogeochemical processes affecting the fate of metals in aquatic systems, emphasizing how chemical speciation controls bioavailability, using field studies, laboratory experiments, and spectroscopic modeling of metals such as As, Ni, and Hg.

faculty.name: Kimberly Gray
faculty.title: Stanley F. Pepper Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering (by courtesy)
faculty.summary: Gray's expertise is in environmental chemistry and applied ecology in natural and engineered systems, studying TiO2-based nanocomposites for resource recovery and water/air treatment, nature-based stormwater strategies, ecotoxicology of nanomaterials, and resilient design of urban systems in response to climate change.

faculty.name: Erica Hartmann
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and (by courtesy) Medicine (Pulmonary Division)
faculty.summary: Hartmann's research investigates at the molecular level how microbial communities respond to anthropogenic chemicals, using field sampling, shotgun DNA sequencing, and laboratory model systems to control the spread of undesirable traits such as antibiotic resistance in the built environment.

faculty.name: Jackson Jewett
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Jewett's work focuses on computational design for the built environment, exploring how optimization methods improve material utilization in building-scale structures under construction constraints, complemented by physical experiments and novel digital fabrication methods for civil engineering applications.

faculty.name: Sinan Keten
faculty.title: Jan and Marcia Achenbach Professor; Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Civil and Environmental Engineering and (by courtesy) Biomedical Engineering
faculty.summary: Keten's group establishes theory, multiscale simulation, and machine learning approaches to understand the mechanical behavior of soft materials, focusing on nanostructured polymers, biomolecular building blocks such as proteins, and bioinspired systems, to accelerate design of materials for infrastructure, manufacturing, and therapeutics.

faculty.name: Yu (Marco) Nie
faculty.title: Roxelyn and Richard Pepper Family Chair in Civil and Environmental Engineering; Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Nie studies how to understand, predict, and improve the behavior of transportation networks, formulating design and control strategies for mobility, reliability, and sustainability using tools from optimization, network science, traffic flow theory, and economics, including routing algorithms and Pareto-improving congestion pricing.

faculty.name: Aaron Packman
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and (by courtesy) Mechanical Engineering and Chemical and Biological Engineering
faculty.summary: Packman's research focuses on water, sediments, and microorganisms, particularly the intersection of physical transport with biological and biogeochemical processes, studying environmental interfaces, surface-groundwater interactions, and biofilms with applications to water sustainability, urban flooding, and contaminant transport.

faculty.name: Alessandro Rotta Loria
faculty.title: Louis Berger Associate Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Rotta Loria's work lies at the intersection of mechanics, energy, and electrochemistry focused on the subsurface, using theoretical, computational, and experimental studies to understand the impacts of energy transfers on geological and granular materials, addressing subsurface urban heat islands, geological energy storage, and sustainable construction.

faculty.name: John Rudnicki
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and Mechanical Engineering
faculty.summary: Rudnicki studies inelastic behavior and failure of geomaterials, particularly deformation instabilities in brittle rocks and granular media and their interactions with pore fluids, with applications to fault instability, earthquake energy radiation, and resource-related geomechanics.

faculty.name: Amanda Stathopoulos
faculty.title: William Patterson Junior Professor; Associate Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Stathopoulos's research examines human-centered sustainable mobility, studying how lifestyles, values, and priorities of travelers and decision-makers shape adoption of sustainable transportation practices, using discrete choice modeling, statistical analysis, qualitative fieldwork, and large-scale surveys.

faculty.name: Lucia Stein-Montalvo
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Stein-Montalvo's research focuses on the mechanics of shape-shifting, compelling structures to change configuration on demand or in response to environmental stimuli, bridging fundamental studies of nonlinear deformations and instabilities with adaptive architectural solutions for the built environment.

faculty.name: George Wells
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Wells works on environmental biotechnology and microbial ecology of engineered and impacted natural systems, including microbial nitrogen and phosphorus cycling, shortcut biological nutrient removal, sustainable wastewater treatment, resource and energy recovery from waste, and mathematical modeling of biofilms and bioprocesses.

faculty.name: Samir Khuller
faculty.title: Peter and Adrienne Barris Chair of Computer Science, Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Khuller leads the Computer Science department and works on the design and analysis of combinatorial and approximation algorithms, including graph algorithms, scheduling, and network design.

faculty.name: Kristian Hammond
faculty.title: Bill and Cathy Osborn Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Hammond works on artificial intelligence and natural language generation, building systems that reason over data and communicate results in natural language.

faculty.name: Ken Forbus
faculty.title: Walter P. Murphy Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Forbus works on qualitative reasoning, analogical reasoning, and cognitive systems, building AI systems that model human commonsense and conceptual reasoning.

faculty.name: Han Liu
faculty.title: Orrington Lunt Professor of Computer Science and (by courtesy) Industrial Engineering & Management Sciences
faculty.summary: Liu works on statistical machine learning, including high-dimensional and nonparametric inference, optimization, and the theoretical foundations of deep learning.

faculty.name: Jason Hartline
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Hartline works on economics and computation, including auction and mechanism design, approximation in economic settings, and the theory of markets.

faculty.name: Jessica Hullman
faculty.title: Ginni Rometty Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Hullman researches data visualization and human-computer interaction, focusing on how people reason with data and uncertainty and how to design visual and statistical communication.

faculty.name: Peter Dinda
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science and (by courtesy) Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Dinda's group works on experimental computer systems, including operating systems, parallel and high-performance computing, and virtualization.

faculty.name: Fabian Bustamante
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Bustamante's group studies large-scale distributed and networked systems, with an emphasis on internet and mobile network measurement and performance.

faculty.name: Aleksandar Kuzmanovic
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Kuzmanovic researches computer networking and networked systems, including internet architecture, measurement, and the interaction of networks with applications.

faculty.name: Nikos Hardavellas
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science, Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Hardavellas researches computer architecture and systems, focusing on memory systems and energy-efficient parallel architectures for data-intensive workloads.

faculty.name: Edith Elkind
faculty.title: Ginni Rometty Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Elkind studies algorithmic game theory and computational social choice, including voting, coalition formation, and fair division in multiagent systems.

faculty.name: Konstantin Makarychev
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Makarychev works on theoretical computer science, particularly approximation algorithms, clustering, and combinatorial optimization.

faculty.name: Aravindan Vijayaraghavan
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and (by courtesy) Industrial Engineering & Management Sciences
faculty.summary: Vijayaraghavan works on theoretical computer science and the foundations of machine learning, including approximation algorithms, clustering, and provable methods for learning.

faculty.name: V.S. Subrahmanian
faculty.title: Walter P. Murphy Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Subrahmanian works on artificial intelligence and security, including machine learning and data analytics for cybersecurity, counterterrorism, and computational policy.

faculty.name: Xinyu Xing
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Xing researches systems and software security, including automated vulnerability discovery and analysis and the security of machine-learning systems.

faculty.name: Xiao Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Wang researches cryptography and security, specializing in efficient secure multiparty computation, zero-knowledge proofs, and their practical implementations.

faculty.name: Robby Findler
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Findler is a core developer of the Racket programming language and works on programming languages, software contracts, and language-based development tools.

faculty.name: Christos Dimoulas
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Dimoulas studies programming languages, including type systems, software contracts, and the design of languages that enforce correctness and security properties.

faculty.name: Matthew Kay
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, Associate Professor of Communication Studies
faculty.summary: Kay works on human-computer interaction and data visualization, including uncertainty visualization and tools that help people interpret data and statistical information.

faculty.name: Brenna Argall
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science, Professor of Mechanical Engineering, Professor of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
faculty.summary: Argall's group develops assistive and rehabilitation robotics, including shared-control and machine-learning methods that adapt robotic devices to users with motor impairments.

faculty.name: Emma Alexander
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and (by courtesy) Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Alexander works at the intersection of computer vision and optics, designing computational imaging systems and studying depth and light-based sensing inspired by biological vision.

faculty.name: Manling Li
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Li works on natural language processing and multimodal AI, including information and knowledge extraction and language-model agents that reason across text, vision, and structured knowledge.

faculty.name: Miklos Racz
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, Associate Professor of Statistics
faculty.summary: Racz works on probability, statistics, and network science, including inference on random graphs and the mathematics of large networked systems.

faculty.name: Simone Campanoni
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and (by courtesy) Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Campanoni works on compilers and computer architecture, developing program-analysis and code-optimization techniques that automatically extract parallelism and performance.

faculty.name: Bryan Pardo
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Pardo leads work on machine listening and audio, developing machine-learning and interactive tools for music and sound analysis, separation, and production.

faculty.name: Karan Ahuja
faculty.title: Lisa Wissner-Slivka and Benjamin Slivka Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Ahuja studies human-computer interaction and ubiquitous computing, developing sensing systems and machine learning methods that let devices perceive human activity and context.

faculty.name: Nivedita Arora
faculty.title: Allen K. and Johnnie Cordell Breed Junior Professor of Design, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Assistant Professor of Computer Scien
faculty.summary: Arora designs sustainable, self-powered interactive computing devices and materials, spanning human-computer interaction, embedded sensing, and low-power hardware.

faculty.name: Larry Birnbaum
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Birnbaum works on artificial intelligence, natural language processing, and intelligent information systems, including natural language generation and machine-assisted content.

faculty.name: Yan Chen
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Chen's research spans computer networking and security, including network measurement, intrusion and malware detection, and security of mobile and IoT systems.

faculty.name: Alok Choudhary
faculty.title: Harold Washington Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Computer Science
faculty.summary: Choudhary works on high-performance and parallel computing, large-scale data mining, and data-intensive scientific computing.

faculty.name: Andrew Crotty
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Crotty builds database and data-management systems, focusing on high-performance query processing and analytics engines.

faculty.name: Douglas Downey
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Downey works on natural language processing and machine learning, including information extraction, language models, and AI methods applied to scientific text.

faculty.name: Michael Horn
faculty.title: Charles Deering McCormick Professor of Teaching Excellence, Professor of Computer Science, Professor of Education and Social Policy
faculty.summary: Horn designs interactive and tangible computing technologies for learning, spanning human-computer interaction, educational technology, and the learning sciences.

faculty.name: Ian Horswill
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Horswill works on artificial intelligence for interactive systems and games, including behavior-based and cognitively inspired AI for characters and agents.

faculty.name: Maia Jacobs
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Assistant Professor of Preventive Medicine
faculty.summary: Jacobs designs human-centered computing and AI tools for health, studying how patients and clinicians interact with health technologies and decision-support systems.

faculty.name: Russell Joseph
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Joseph researches computer architecture, with an emphasis on power, thermal, and reliability management in processors and hardware systems.

faculty.name: Sam Kriegman
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering, Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering
faculty.summary: Kriegman studies embodied AI and robotics, using evolutionary and machine-learning methods to design bodies and behaviors of soft, biohybrid, and reconfigurable robots.

faculty.name: Sidhanth Mohanty
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Mohanty works in theoretical computer science on spectral and average-case algorithms, random constraint satisfaction, and the sum-of-squares hierarchy.

faculty.name: Seda Ogrenci
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Ogrenci researches reconfigurable and embedded computing, including FPGA-based systems and hardware acceleration for machine learning at the edge.

faculty.name: Eleanor O'Rourke
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, Associate Professor of Education and Social Policy
faculty.summary: O'Rourke designs learning technologies and studies human-computer interaction in education, including tools that support student motivation and growth mindset.

faculty.name: Chris Riesbeck
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Riesbeck works on artificial intelligence and cognitive science, including case-based reasoning and learning-by-doing approaches to education.

faculty.name: Jennie Rogers
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Rogers builds database and data-management systems, with work on federated databases and privacy-preserving query processing across multiple data owners.

faculty.name: Michael Rubenstein
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering
faculty.summary: Rubenstein researches swarm and multi-robot systems, developing large collectives of simple robots that coordinate to achieve self-assembly and collective behavior.

faculty.name: Kate Smith
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and (by courtesy) Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Smith works on quantum computing systems, including architectures, compilation, and system-software techniques for near-term quantum hardware.

faculty.name: Uri Wilensky
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science, Professor of Education and Social Policy, Lorraine Morton Professor
faculty.summary: Wilensky created the NetLogo modeling environment and studies agent-based modeling of complex systems and computationally rich approaches to STEM education.

faculty.name: Marcelo Worsley
faculty.title: Karr Family Associate Professor of Computer Science, Associate Professor of Learning Sciences
faculty.summary: Worsley works on multimodal learning analytics and human-computer interaction, using sensing and machine learning to understand and support hands-on and inclusive learning.

faculty.name: Haoqi Zhang
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Zhang works on human-computer interaction and social computing, designing crowdsourcing and community systems that coordinate people to accomplish complex goals.

faculty.name: Ruohan Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science (beginning September 1, 2026)
faculty.summary: Zhang, an incoming assistant professor, works on reinforcement and imitation learning for robotics and embodied AI, including learning from human attention and demonstration.

programs.program_name: Industrial Engineering and Management Sciences PhD

faculty.name: Bruce Ankenman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on developing simple but statistically rigorous tools for designing and analyzing physical and simulation-based experiments, motivated by limited access engineers have to statistical methods.

faculty.name: Daniel Apley
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on statistical modeling and analysis of engineering and industrial systems, with work on interpretable neural networks, hyperparameter optimization, and concept drift monitoring. Received the Wilcoxon Prize for best practical application paper in Technometrics.

faculty.name: Seyed Iravani
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research applies stochastic processes, queueing theory, and game theory to the design and control of manufacturing, service operations, healthcare systems, and supply chains. Director of Graduate Studies.

faculty.name: Diego Klabjan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on machine learning, deep learning, and analytics with concentrations in finance, transportation, sport, and bioinformatics. Director of the MS in Machine Learning and Data Science Program and the Center for Deep Learning.

faculty.name: Simge Küçükyavuz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on optimization theory and methodology, especially mixed-integer programming, large-scale optimization, and optimization under uncertainty, with applications to infrastructure systems and statistical learning. Chair of IEMS and David A. and Karen Richards Sachs Professor.

faculty.name: Sanjay Mehrotra
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops methods for decision optimization under uncertainty by studying geometric and algebraic properties of problems. Pioneered risk-adjusted and distributionally robust optimization, with major applications in modeling the US national transplant system. Director of the Center for Engineering and Health.

faculty.name: David Morton
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops stochastic and distributionally robust optimization methods for decision-making under uncertainty, with applied work spanning public health crisis response, energy infrastructure resilience, and security-related resource allocation. Walter P. Murphy Professor.

faculty.name: Jorge Nocedal
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on developing and analyzing optimization algorithms — including noise-tolerant and adaptive sampling methods — for large-scale applications in machine learning, engineering design, and the sciences. Walter P. Murphy Professor and Director of the Center for Optimization and Statistical Learning.

faculty.name: Karen Smilowitz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on operations research applied to transportation and logistics, with emphasis on humanitarian logistics and disaster relief operations. James N. and Margie M. Krebs Professor and Associate Provost for Undergraduate Education.

faculty.name: Dashun Wang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on the science of science, leveraging data-driven interdisciplinary methods to uncover patterns in scientific careers, collaboration, innovation, and the dynamics of success and failure. Kellogg Chair of Technology and Director of the Center for Science of Science and Innovation.

faculty.name: Noshir Contractor
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Network Science and Computational Social Science
faculty.summary: Investigates how network structures emerge and function in business, science, healthcare, and space travel, advancing computational methods to study algorithmically shaped societies and team dynamics. Jane S. and William J. White Professor of Behavioral Sciences.

faculty.name: Chang-Han Rhee
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on advanced probability theory and stochastic simulation, particularly the analysis of rare events and large deviations in random processes, also exploring mathematical foundations of AI.

faculty.name: Zhaoran Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops AI and machine learning methods for autonomous decision-making, making them theoretically principled and practically efficient for large-scale societal challenges involving multiple interacting agents.

faculty.name: Ermin Wei
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on control and operation of networked systems, particularly market analysis of smart grid and energy networks, along with large-scale distributed optimization algorithms.

faculty.name: Minshuo Chen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical and methodological underpinnings of machine learning and decision-making, with emphasis on diffusion models for generative AI and deep reinforcement learning for complex systems.

faculty.name: Julia Gaudio
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops mathematical and statistical methods for recovering hidden structures in random networks, with applications in community detection in spatial networks and random instance optimization problems.

faculty.name: Izzy Grosof
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops mathematical and algorithmic approaches to improve performance and reliability of computing systems through stochastic queueing models and scheduling theory, with emphasis on multi-server environments and tail latency reduction.

faculty.name: Yiping Lu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Machine Learning Theory and Scaling Laws
faculty.summary: Investigates theoretical foundations of scaling in machine learning — why performance improves predictably with more data, model size, and compute — spanning optimization geometry, statistical complexity, and inference-time computation.

faculty.name: Sean Sinclair
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Designs data-driven algorithms for sequential decision-making, applying reinforcement learning and operations management to societal challenges such as fair resource allocation and cloud compute optimization.

faculty.name: Naichen Shi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Advances integrative and generative AI methods for aligning heterogeneous data and knowledge across complex engineering systems, with particular application to advanced manufacturing and digital twins.

faculty.name: Zikai Xiong
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Joining Northwestern IEMS as an Assistant Professor on August 1, 2026. Research interests not yet listed on departmental profile.

funding.note: Nearly all admitted PhD students receive full support (tuition, stipend, health insurance)

programs.program_name: Engineering Sciences and Applied Mathematics PhD

funding.note: Nearly all admitted receive support; fellowship year 1, then RA/TA (min $3,080/mo, tuition, health)

faculty.name: Daniel Abrams
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Abrams develops mathematical and dynamical-systems models to understand complex phenomena ranging from synchronization and chimera states in oscillator networks to social dynamics such as opinion polarization and language competition. He is Co-Director of the Northwestern Institute on Complex Systems (NICO).

faculty.name: Luis A. Nunes Amaral
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Amaral's work applies quantitative and network-based approaches to diverse challenges, from forecasting transportation network evolution to analyzing clinical states from electronic health records and studying citation patterns in science. He has published over 180 peer-reviewed papers in journals such as Nature, Science, PNAS, and Cell.

faculty.name: Alvin Bayliss
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Bayliss develops and analyzes computational models of multi-species ecological communities, with a focus on cyclic competition dynamics and pattern formation. He serves as Director of Graduate Studies for ESAM.

faculty.name: David Chopp
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Chopp develops numerical algorithms and computational models for interface-driven phenomena. His work spans biofilm growth and signaling, phase field modeling of materials, and fracture mechanics using level set methods.

faculty.name: William Kath
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Kath's work centers on mathematical modeling of biological systems, particularly circadian rhythms and neural signaling. He has contributed to understanding how temperature drives circadian gene regulation and how sensory systems enable rapid threat assessment.

faculty.name: Diego Klabjan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Klabjan's work focuses on machine learning and deep learning with applications in finance, transportation, sports, and bioinformatics. He is Director of the Center for Deep Learning and the MS in Machine Learning and Data Science program.

faculty.name: Erik Luijten
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computational Materials Science and Soft Matter
faculty.summary: Luijten's group uses computer simulations to understand experimental phenomena from microscopic system features and to design new materials. His projects span self-assembly, charge transport in electrolytes, programmable/active matter, and dielectric materials.

faculty.name: Michael J. Miksis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Miksis's work centers on fluid dynamics at small scales and interfaces, spanning electrohydrodynamic flows around colloidal particles, vesicle and droplet shape dynamics, and capillary phenomena. He serves as Director of MS Studies for ESAM.

faculty.name: Adilson Motter
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Motter's group investigates cascading dynamics, spontaneous synchronization, network control, and symmetry phenomena with applications to quantum networks, machine learning, power grids, microfluidics, and metamaterials. He directs the Center for Network Dynamics.

faculty.name: Jorge Nocedal
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Nocedal's work spans algorithm design, software implementation, and mathematical analysis of optimization methods. His research focuses on noise-tolerant optimization, adaptive sampling, and quasi-Newton algorithms with applications in machine learning and engineering design.

faculty.name: Neelesh A. Patankar
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Patankar's lab develops computational fluid dynamics techniques for fluid-structure interaction problems and applies them to understand organ physiology in clinical contexts. The group also works on phase control using engineered surface textures for applications like anti-icing and condensation.

faculty.name: Hermann Riecke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Riecke's work centers on how plasticity restructures neuronal networks and how feedback from higher brain areas shapes information processing, with a particular focus on the olfactory system. He also studies pattern formation in spatially extended dynamical systems.

faculty.name: Petia Vlahovska
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Vlahovska leads the Complex Fluids and Soft Interfaces Lab, integrating experimental and theoretical modeling of physical and biological systems. Her group explores biomembrane electromechanics, self-organization in active matter, and interfacial instabilities.

faculty.name: Vladimir Volpert
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Volpert investigates pattern formation and traveling waves in nonlinear systems, with applications ranging from combustion and frontal polymerization to cyclic ecological population dynamics. His recent work focuses on mathematical models of multi-species ecological systems.

faculty.name: Rosemary Braun
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Braun develops computational methods that combine bioinformatic information with experimental data to characterize molecular interaction networks. Her work aims to understand how these networks drive complex phenotypes, particularly cancers.

faculty.name: James Fitzgerald
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Fitzgerald's lab combines first-principles theory, phenomenological modeling, data analysis, and experimental design to build theoretical frameworks linking brain circuit activity to behavior. They seek general principles spanning across different systems and model organisms.

faculty.name: Madhav Mani
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Mani's group develops mathematical frameworks to illuminate biological processes, pairing data-driven methods with the aesthetics and sensibilities of mathematics and theoretical physics. They collaborate with experimental biology groups across organismal development, cellular physiology, and ecological dynamics.

faculty.name: Alexander (Sasha) Tchekhovskoy
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Tchekhovskoy studies how black holes and neutron stars consume stars, launch relativistic jets, and influence galaxy evolution. His work involves large-scale numerical simulations to model accretion disks and jets, linking simulations to observational data.

faculty.name: Istvan Kovacs
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Kovacs develops novel methodologies to predict emerging structural and functional patterns across fields from systems biology to quantum physics, working closely with experimental groups. His research bridges structure and function in complex systems.

faculty.name: Daniel Lecoanet
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Lecoanet studies fluid dynamics in astrophysical and geophysical contexts, such as stellar interiors and planetary atmospheres, using theoretical approaches and numerical simulations. He is a core developer of the Dedalus spectral-method PDE solver.

faculty.name: Yiping Lu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Lu studies when, why, and how machine-learning systems improve predictably as resources such as data, model size, and compute are scaled. His work aims to build a general theory of scalable learning in which increased resources provably and reliably lead to better performance.

faculty.name: Niall Mangan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Mangan works at the intersection of mechanistic modeling and data science, connecting the speed and automation of data-driven model selection with the explanatory power of bottom-up mechanistic modeling. Her work spans biological network inference, microbial engineering, and solar cell optimization.

faculty.name: Krishna Shrinivas
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: The Shrinivas lab builds computational frameworks to predict and engineer the processes that power life at the molecular and cellular scales, blending biology, physics, machine learning, and engineering. Current work spans genome organization, physics-driven AI for biomolecule design, and computation in biological systems.

faculty.name: Pedram Khalili
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops spintronic materials and devices, including magnetic memory (MRAM) and spin-based logic.

faculty.name: Nathaniel P. Stern
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Studies light-matter interactions in 2D materials and nanophotonic systems for quantum and spin-based technologies.

faculty.name: Koray Aydin
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Designs metamaterials, metasurfaces and nanophotonic devices for manipulating light at the nanoscale.

faculty.name: Michael J. Bedzyk
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Uses x-ray scattering and synchrotron methods to determine atomic-scale structure of surfaces, interfaces and thin films.

faculty.name: Venkat Chandrasekhar
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Studies mesoscopic and nanoscale electronic transport, including superconductivity and proximity effects at low temperatures.

faculty.name: Lin X. Chen
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Uses ultrafast optical and x-ray spectroscopy to study excited-state dynamics for solar energy conversion and photochemistry.

faculty.name: Vinayak P. Dravid
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops advanced electron microscopy and characterization of nanomaterials, interfaces and functional devices.

faculty.name: Andrew Geraci
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Uses levitated optomechanical sensors and precision measurement to search for dark matter and test fundamental forces.

faculty.name: Pallab Goswami
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Develops theory for emergent quantum phases and phase transitions in strongly correlated and topological materials.

faculty.name: Matthew Grayson
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies quantum transport in semiconductor nanostructures and anisotropic thermoelectric materials and devices.

faculty.name: Sossina Haile
faculty.title: Walter P. Murphy Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops solid-state ionic materials for fuel cells, electrolysis and electrochemical energy conversion.

faculty.name: Mark Hersam
faculty.title: Walter P. Murphy Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies nanomaterials and 2D materials for nanoelectronics, energy and quantum applications using scanning probe microscopy and nanofabrication.

faculty.name: Mahdi Hosseini
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops quantum photonic systems, optical quantum memories and nanophotonic devices for quantum information.

faculty.name: Archana Kamal
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Theorist working on quantum control, superconducting qubits, nonreciprocal devices and open quantum systems.

faculty.name: John B. Ketterson
faculty.title: Fayerweather Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Experimental condensed matter physicist studying superconductivity, superfluidity, magnetism and nonlinear optical phenomena.

faculty.name: Jens Koch
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Theorist of superconducting quantum circuits and circuit QED; co-developed the transmon qubit.

faculty.name: Tim Kovachy
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Uses atom interferometry with cold atoms for precision measurement, gravitational-wave detection and dark matter searches.

faculty.name: Prem Kumar
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Works on nonlinear and quantum optics, quantum communication and photonic quantum networks.

faculty.name: Lincoln J. Lauhon
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies semiconductor nanowires and 2D materials using atom probe tomography and correlated nanoscale characterization.

faculty.name: Erik Luijten
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops simulation methods for soft matter, studying self-assembly and the behavior of colloids and charged systems.

faculty.name: Brian Odom
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Develops trapped molecular-ion techniques for precision spectroscopy and quantum control.

faculty.name: James M. Rondinelli
faculty.title: Walter Dill Scott Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Uses first-principles computation to design functional oxides and other materials with tailored electronic, optical and magnetic properties.

faculty.name: Selim Shahriar
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Works on atomic and quantum optics for precision sensors, including atomic clocks, gyroscopes and slow-light devices.

faculty.name: G. Jeffrey Snyder
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies thermoelectric materials and the fundamentals of charge and heat transport for energy conversion.

faculty.name: Chris Wolverton
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Uses first-principles calculations and machine learning for computational materials discovery, including energy-storage and structural materials.

faculty.name: Vadim Backman
faculty.title: Sachs Family Professor of Biomedical Engineering and Medicine
faculty.summary: Develops optical and biophotonics technologies for early cancer detection and for probing chromatin nanoarchitecture.

faculty.name: David Barton
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops new material platforms and integrated optical devices using scalable semiconductor nanofabrication for energy-efficient computing, communications and nonlinear optics.

faculty.name: Michelle Driscoll
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Experimental soft matter physicist studying colloidal suspensions, driven and active systems, and complex fluid flows.

faculty.name: Pulak Dutta
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Studies the structure of surfaces, interfaces, thin films and ordered molecular layers using x-ray diffraction.

faculty.name: Horacio Espinosa
faculty.title: James N. and Nancy J. Farley Professor in Manufacturing and Entrepreneurship
faculty.summary: Investigates the mechanics of nanomaterials and bioinspired materials, developing MEMS-based testing and nanomanufacturing methods.

faculty.name: Enectali Figueroa-Feliciano
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Develops cryogenic and superconducting detectors for dark matter searches and x-ray astrophysics.

faculty.name: James Fitzgerald
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Neurobiology
faculty.summary: Theoretical neuroscientist building and testing theories that link biological complexity to brain functions such as sensory processing, learning and motor control.

faculty.name: Jennifer Fowlie
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Grows transition-metal-oxide heterostructures by pulsed laser deposition and engineers their structural, electronic and magnetic properties, including superconducting nickelates.

faculty.name: Gerald Gabrielse
faculty.title: Board of Trustees Professor in Physics
faculty.summary: Performs ultra-precise measurements with trapped particles and antimatter to test fundamental physics.

faculty.name: Anupam Garg
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Theoretical physicist working on quantum tunneling, spin systems and foundational aspects of quantum mechanics.

faculty.name: James D. Gaynor
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Ultrafast spectroscopist studying how photochemical processes are governed by quantum coherence, electronic correlations and vibronic coupling on femtosecond-to-attosecond timescales.

faculty.name: Franz Geiger
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Uses nonlinear optical spectroscopy to study molecular processes at environmental and energy-relevant interfaces.

faculty.name: Anna Grassellino
faculty.title: Adjunct Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Directs Fermilab's Superconducting Quantum Materials and Systems (SQMS) Center, developing superconducting RF cavities for quantum computing and accelerators. National-lab-affiliated Applied Physics advisor.

faculty.name: William P. Halperin
faculty.title: John Evans Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Experimental low-temperature physicist studying superfluid helium-3, unconventional superconductors and NMR in quantum fluids.

faculty.name: Songi Han
faculty.title: Mark and Nancy Ratner Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Develops magnetic resonance methods including dynamic nuclear polarization and EPR to study hydration dynamics and biomolecular structure.

faculty.name: Chris Jacobsen
faculty.title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Develops x-ray microscopy and spectromicroscopy for high-resolution imaging of biological and materials systems.

faculty.name: Mercouri G. Kanatzidis
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Discovers and characterizes new solid-state materials including thermoelectrics, halide perovskites and semiconductors.

faculty.name: Ella King
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops inverse-design methods for dynamic, responsive and self-correcting materials at the intersection of soft matter, materials design and biological physics. (Incoming faculty, starting September 2026.)

faculty.name: Diego Klabjan
faculty.title: Professor of Industrial Engineering and Management Sciences
faculty.summary: Works on machine learning, deep learning and large-scale optimization and their applications to data-driven problems.

faculty.name: Istvan Kovacs
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Studies complex networks, statistical physics of disordered systems and applications to biological and materials networks.

faculty.name: Sam Kriegman
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Studies evolutionary and biological robotics and artificial life, including computationally designed living robots (xenobots).

faculty.name: Tobin Marks
faculty.title: Charles E. and Emma H. Morrison Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Works on catalysis, organometallic chemistry and electronic/optical materials including transparent conductors and organic electronics.

faculty.name: Hooman Mohseni
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops nanophotonic and optoelectronic devices, including high-sensitivity photodetectors and imaging and biosensing systems.

faculty.name: Adilson Motter
faculty.title: Charles E. and Emma H. Morrison Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Studies the dynamics and control of complex networks and nonlinear systems across physical and biological domains.

faculty.name: Elvira Mulyukova
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Models mantle convection, rock rheology and the dynamics of planetary interiors.

faculty.name: Teri W. Odom
faculty.title: Charles E. and Emma H. Morrison Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Designs plasmonic nanostructures and nanolasers and develops multiscale nanofabrication for photonic and biomedical applications.

faculty.name: Monica Olvera de la Cruz
faculty.title: Lawyer Taylor Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Theoretical soft-matter scientist studying charged polymers, self-assembly and electrostatics in complex and biological materials.

faculty.name: Ertuğrul Özbudak
faculty.title: Robert Laughlin Rea Professor of Cell and Developmental Biology
faculty.summary: Physicist-turned-biologist studying developmental pattern formation, somite segmentation and the biophysics of gene expression, using zebrafish models.

faculty.name: Charudatta Phatak
faculty.title: Adjunct Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Uses Lorentz transmission electron microscopy to study nanoscale magnetic materials and spin textures. Argonne National Laboratory scientist and affiliated Applied Physics advisor.

faculty.name: Jonathan Rivnay
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops organic electronic materials and devices, including conducting polymers, for bioelectronic and neural interfaces. (Title per the program directory; verify current rank.)

faculty.name: Alex Romanenko
faculty.title: Adjunct Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Fermilab scientist working on superconducting RF materials and cavities for quantum computing and accelerators within the SQMS Center. Affiliated Applied Physics advisor.

faculty.name: Ted Sargent
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Develops colloidal quantum dots and perovskite materials for photovoltaics, LEDs and electrochemical CO2 conversion.

faculty.name: Jim Sauls
faculty.title: Adjunct Professor of Physics and Astronomy
faculty.summary: Theorist of unconventional superconductivity and superfluidity, including superfluid helium-3 and topological superconductors. Longtime Applied Physics faculty, now adjunct.

faculty.name: George C. Schatz
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Theoretical chemist modeling nanophotonics, plasmonics, molecular dynamics and the optical properties of nanomaterials.

faculty.name: Tamar Seideman
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Theorist studying molecular electronics, coherent control, quantum dynamics and light-matter interactions in nanoscale systems.

faculty.name: Krishna Shrinivas
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies computation and self-organization in biological and physical systems, including biomolecular condensates and physics-based design of disordered proteins.

faculty.name: Dayne Swearer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Develops plasmonic photocatalysts, including antenna-reactor and dilute single-atom-alloy nanoparticles, that use light to drive chemical reactions.

faculty.name: Petia Vlahovska
faculty.title: Professor of Mechanical Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies the fluid dynamics of soft and biological matter, including membranes, drops and electrohydrodynamic and active systems.

faculty.name: Peter W. Voorhees
faculty.title: Frank C. Engelhart Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies phase transformations and microstructure evolution, including coarsening and solidification, through theory and 4D characterization.

faculty.name: Michael R. Wasielewski
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Studies photoinduced electron transfer, molecular spin dynamics and solar energy conversion, including molecular qubits for quantum information.

faculty.name: Emily Weiss
faculty.title: Adjunct Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Studies the photophysics and photochemistry of quantum dots and nanocrystals, including excitonic processes and photocatalysis. Listed as adjunct Applied Physics faculty.

faculty.name: Hao Zhang
faculty.title: Professor of Biomedical Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops optical imaging technologies including photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography for retinal and biomedical imaging.

faculty.summary: Works on dynamical systems, including celestial mechanics and Hamiltonian dynamics.

faculty.name: Sandy Zabell
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Eric Zaslow
faculty.title: Henry Sanborn Noyes Chair in Mathematics; Causeway Co-Director
faculty.summary: Works in mathematical physics, including mirror symmetry and its connections to symplectic geometry.

faculty.name: Xiumin Du
faculty.title: Associate Professor; AT&T Research Fellow
faculty.summary: Works in harmonic analysis, including the pointwise convergence of Schrodinger solutions and restriction theory.

faculty.name: John Francis
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works in topology, including factorization homology and higher category theory.

faculty.name: Reza Gheissari
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works in probability theory, including statistical mechanics and the dynamics of interacting particle systems.

faculty.name: Bao Le Hung
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works in algebraic number theory, including Galois representations and the Langlands program.

faculty.name: Yuchen Liu
faculty.title: Associate Professor; AT&T Research Fellow
faculty.summary: Works in algebraic geometry, including K-stability of Fano varieties and moduli spaces.

faculty.name: Rachel Greenfeld
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on Fourier analysis and additive combinatorics, including tiling problems.

faculty.name: Marcus Michelen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in probability and combinatorics, including random structures and the statistical mechanics of discrete systems.

faculty.name: Gus Schrader
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in representation theory, including quantum groups and cluster algebras.

faculty.name: Ananth Shankar
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in arithmetic geometry and number theory, including Shimura varieties and abelian varieties.

faculty.name: Alexander Smith
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in number theory, including arithmetic statistics and the distribution of class groups and Selmer groups.

faculty.name: Jakub Witaszek
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in algebraic geometry, including birational geometry and geometry in positive and mixed characteristic.

faculty.name: Allen Yuan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in topology and homotopy theory, including chromatic and algebraic aspects of stable homotopy.

faculty.name: Beth Andrews
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on model fitting and prediction for nonlinear, non-Gaussian processes observed over space and time, with applications in economics, finance, geosciences, and signal processing.

faculty.name: Kaize Ding
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on data mining, machine learning, and large foundation models, with emphasis on graph neural networks, data-efficient learning (few-shot, weakly-supervised, self-supervised), and reliable AI for applications in cybersecurity, healthcare, and urban computing.

faculty.name: Larry Hedges
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on developing and applying statistical methods for social, medical, and biological sciences, with major emphasis on meta-analysis for combining results across studies, design of social experiments, and the replication crisis in science.

faculty.name: Hongmei Jiang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on design and analysis of high-throughput genomic and metagenomic data, including statistical methods for microbiome data, longitudinal trajectory subgroups for precision medicine, and multiple comparisons.

faculty.name: Wenxin Jiang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans mathematical statistics, biostatistics, data mining, Bayesian statistics, and econometrics, including work on ecological regression with partial identification and asymptotic distributions for data mining lift measures.

faculty.name: Han Liu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses computation and data as a lens to explore science and intelligence, focusing on nonparametric structure learning and representation learning to advance both statistical machine learning and deep learning, with applications to scientific data.

faculty.name: Matey Neykov
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on high-dimensional statistics and machine learning, particularly high-dimensional nonparametric estimation, variable selection, inference, and graph property testing, with applications to electronic medical records and personalized medicine.

faculty.name: Miklos Z. Racz
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research sits at the intersection of probability, statistics, computer science, and information theory, focusing on statistical inference on large random discrete structures, graph matching in correlated random graphs, community detection, and applications to DNA data storage.

faculty.name: Feng Ruan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research at the intersection of statistics, optimization, and machine learning, developing rigorous understanding of how to design statistical models amenable to local algorithms and developing theory for problems under resource constraints.

faculty.name: Noelle I. Samia
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical models for nonstationary, serially correlated, heteroscedastic count and continuous time-series data with applications in infectious diseases, ecology, and biomedical research, and also works on multimodal large language models and AI-driven scientific discovery.

faculty.name: Thomas Severini
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on likelihood-based statistical methods such as maximum likelihood estimation, higher-order asymptotic approximations, and statistical methods for models with many parameters with applications in finance, econometrics, and sports data analysis.

faculty.name: Bradly C. Stadie
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on reinforcement learning, using feedback to teach machines new behaviors, with applications to robotics, biological sciences, and large language models, including combining ChatGPT with robot control.

faculty.name: Elizabeth Tipton
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for causal generalizations, improving how findings from randomized trials and meta-analyses can inform policy and practice, including methods to enhance generalizability of experiments and small-sample adjustments for meta-analysis.

faculty.name: Ji-Ping Wang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on statistical applications in bioinformatics and computational biology, developing machine learning methods and software tools for analyzing genomic data including nucleosome positioning, RNA-seq normalization, CRISPR-Cas9 efficiency prediction, and spatial transcriptomics.

faculty.name: Sandy Zabell
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on mathematical probability, particularly large deviation theory and Bayesian statistics, along with the history, philosophical foundations, and legal applications of probability and statistics, including DNA identification evidence.

faculty.name: Joshua W. Shaevitz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops precision measurement tools to study biological systems across scales, from bacterial cell mechanics and collective motility to machine-learning-based quantification of animal behavior. Serves as Director of Graduate Studies for the Biophysics program and co-Director of the Center for the Physics of Biological Function.

faculty.name: William Bialek
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses theoretical physics to uncover fundamental principles governing biological systems, from information processing in neural circuits to optimal coding strategies in embryonic development and flocking behavior.

faculty.name: Thomas Gregor
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the physical principles of multicellular life, focusing on how gene regulatory networks encode positional information and drive precision pattern formation in developing Drosophila embryos.

faculty.name: Andrew M. Leifer
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how brain-wide neural dynamics generate behavior using whole-brain calcium imaging and optogenetics in C. elegans, mapping how signals propagate across the entire nervous system.

faculty.name: Gautam Reddy
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops physics-inspired theory and computational tools to build phenomenological models of learning and decision-making in biological systems, from olfactory navigation to evolutionary dynamics.

faculty.name: Clifford P. Brangwynne
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneered the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation organizes the intracellular space, studying how biomolecular condensates regulate genome function and how condensates solidify in neurodegenerative diseases.

faculty.name: Ned S. Wingreen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses theoretical and computational approaches to model biological systems including microbial community dynamics, intracellular phase separation, bacteria-phage interactions, and B cell evolution in the immune system.

faculty.name: Andrej Kosmrlj
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the mechanics of soft and biological matter, including phase separation in multicomponent biomolecular condensates and the mechanical forces that shape developing tissues and organs.

faculty.name: Sabine Petry
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the molecular architecture and function of the microtubule cytoskeleton, discovering how cells build the mitotic spindle through branching microtubule nucleation and developing microtubule-based nanoscale transport networks.

faculty.name: Howard A. Stone
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Explores the intersection of fluid mechanics and biophysics, studying microfluidics, bacterial biofilm dynamics, the physical behavior of biomolecular condensates, and microbial motility in complex fluid environments.

faculty.name: Jared E. Toettcher
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses optogenetic tools to dissect and control cell signaling pathways with high spatial and temporal precision, studying how signaling dynamics encode cell fate decisions in development and disease.

faculty.name: Martin H. Wuhr
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Advances quantitative proteomics technology and combines it with computational and imaging approaches to understand how protein abundance, localization, and organization control cellular function across scales.

faculty.name: Haw Yang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops single-molecule spectroscopy and 3D single-particle tracking methods to study protein conformational dynamics and nanoscale transport phenomena in complex biological environments.

faculty.name: Stanislav Y. Shvartsman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Combines quantitative experiments and computational modeling to study how genomically encoded signaling networks and self-organizing processes control embryonic development, with a focus on the ERK signaling cascade.

faculty.name: Celeste M. Nelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses interdisciplinary approaches combining engineering, physics, and biology to understand the mechanical principles governing tissue morphogenesis, with a focus on how lungs form across different species.

faculty.name: Sigrid Adriaenssens
faculty.title: Ritter Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Director, Program in Mechanics, Materials and Structures
faculty.summary: Adriaenssens's research focuses on lightweight surface systems and how they can be optimized and realized to interact with extreme structural or environmental loading, spanning mechanics, materials, and structures.

faculty.name: Joshua Atkinson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the Omenn-Darling Bioengineering Institute
faculty.summary: Atkinson's lab uses synthetic biology, protein engineering, biophysics, and electrochemistry to understand and control how microbes and proteins transport electrons, engineering biotechnologies for sustainability, environmental monitoring and remediation, chemical synthesis, and resource recovery.

faculty.name: Elie Bou-Zeid
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Bou-Zeid integrates theory, numerical simulations, and experimental observations to study flow and transport in the atmospheric boundary layer, with applications to the built environment, energy efficiency in buildings, urban sensor networks, wind energy, and surface-atmosphere exchange over polar sea ice.

faculty.name: Ian Bourg
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the High Meadows Environmental Institute
faculty.summary: Bourg examines the fundamental properties of water at interfaces and their impact on environmental systems, including the effect of clay minerals on hydrology and mechanics of sedimentary media, mineral-organic interactions in contaminant fate and soil carbon storage, and hygroscopicity of natural systems.

faculty.name: Maria Garlock
faculty.title: Daniel Tsui Professor in Engineering; Co-Director, Program in Architecture and Engineering; Head of Forbes College
faculty.sub_field: Resilient structural design for extreme loads
faculty.summary: Garlock's scholarship focuses on creative and resilient structural design for extreme loads such as fires, earthquakes, and storm surges, studying these hazards both as isolated and cascading multi-hazard events while bridging academia and engineering practice.

faculty.name: Branko Glisic
faculty.title: Chair and Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Glisic works in structural health monitoring, smart structures, and heritage structures, developing advanced sensing technologies (fiber optic sensors, sensing sheets, RF-tags, GPR) and data-analysis methods for structural and material identification and prediction across bridges, buildings, pipelines, and historical monuments.

faculty.name: Jürgen Hackl
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Hackl's research lies at the interface of network science and complex infrastructure systems, focusing on spatial-temporal networks, uncertainty quantification, digital twin technologies, and intelligent risk and resilience assessment of cities under climate change.

faculty.name: Peter Jaffé
faculty.title: William L. Knapp '47 Professor of Civil Engineering; Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Jaffé's research addresses the physical, chemical, and biological processes governing transport and transformation of pollutants in the environment and their application to remediation of contaminated systems, including biogeochemical reaction-transport in soils and sediments.

faculty.name: Ryan Kingsbury
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment
faculty.summary: Kingsbury's research accelerates development of electrochemical technologies for clean water and energy by advancing understanding of ion-selective materials such as membranes and electrodes, seeking a molecular-level understanding of ion selectivity to engineer higher-performing materials for desalination, fuel cells, and flow batteries.

faculty.name: Liuchi Li
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Li's research focuses on the mechanics and physics of complex material systems involving multi-body contact, friction, and fracture, developing computational and experimental approaches to characterize macroscopic behavior of granular media and crack propagation in heterogeneous materials for resilient infrastructure.

faculty.name: Ning Lin
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Director of Graduate Studies; Director of Undergraduate Studies
faculty.summary: Lin's research areas include natural hazards and risk analysis, wind engineering, coastal engineering, and climate change impact and adaptation, with a primary focus on hurricane risk analysis integrating science, engineering, and policy to study weather extremes and mitigation.

faculty.name: Jyotirmoy Mandal
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Mandal's research involves understanding and controlling nano-to-macro scale radiative heat flows in natural environments and artificial surfaces, at the intersection of optics and materials science, designing scalable materials that radiatively thermoregulate to make human environments more sustainable and climate resilient.

faculty.name: Denise Mauzerall
faculty.title: William S. Tod Professor of Public and International Affairs and Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.sub_field: Air quality, energy and climate policy
faculty.summary: Mauzerall analyzes the impacts of energy technology choices on air quality, public health, food security, and greenhouse gas mitigation, conducting policy-relevant research using regional and global atmospheric chemistry/climate models and atmospheric, agricultural, and epidemiological data.

faculty.name: Reed Maxwell
faculty.title: William and Edna Macaleer Professor of Engineering and Applied Science; Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the High Meadows Environmental Inst
faculty.summary: Maxwell's research centers on understanding how much terrestrial freshwater exists and how fast it is being replenished or depleted, focusing on groundwater, evapotranspiration, and snow, and connections within the hydrologic cycle under anthropogenic stress using integrated hydrologic modeling, field observations, and remote sensing.

faculty.name: Reza Moini
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Moini's research focuses on bio-inspired design and development of architected materials using additive manufacturing and robotic technologies for civil infrastructure, studying the mechanics of intrinsically brittle engineering materials and developing ductile, flaw-tolerant responses through biomimetic design.

faculty.name: Glaucio H. Paulino
faculty.title: Margareta Engman Augustine Professor of Engineering; Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Professor of the Princeton Materials Institute
faculty.summary: Paulino works in applied mechanics, developing methodologies to characterize deformation and fracture of existing and emerging materials, topology optimization for large-scale multiscale and multiphysics problems, computational mechanics, variational methods, and deployable structures and origami engineering.

faculty.name: Catherine Peters
faculty.title: George J. Magee Professor of Geosciences and Geological Engineering; Director, Program in Geological Engineering
faculty.summary: Peters works in environmental chemistry and geochemistry, focusing on the environmental challenges of subsurface energy technologies such as geologic carbon dioxide sequestration, geothermal energy production, and hydraulic fracturing for shale.

faculty.name: Amilcare Porporato
faculty.title: Thomas J. Wu '94 Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the High Meadows Environmental Institute
faculty.summary: Porporato's research focuses on quantitative description and prediction of the terrestrial water cycle, with special interest in the impact of the hydrologic cycle on ecosystem processes (ecohydrology) and related energy, carbon, and nutrient cycles, studying soil moisture-microbe-plant dynamics through theory and experiment.

faculty.name: Anu Ramaswami
faculty.title: Sanjay Swani '87 Professor of India Studies; Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies, and t
faculty.summary: Ramaswami is an interdisciplinary environmental engineer and leader on sustainable urban infrastructure systems, exploring how sectors providing water, energy, food, buildings, mobility, connectivity, waste, and green spaces shape human and environmental wellbeing from local to global scales.

faculty.name: Zhiyong Jason Ren
faculty.title: Eugene Higgins Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment; Associate Director for Research, Andlin
faculty.summary: Ren's lab works on the water-energy nexus, especially water sector decarbonization and resource recovery through processes such as water and CO2 electrolysis, wastewater treatment and reuse, desalination, and carbon capture and utilization, using electrochemistry, microbiology, and AI/machine learning.

faculty.name: Gabriele Villarini
faculty.title: Theodora Shelton Pitney Professor of Environmental Studies; Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the High Meadows Environmental Institute; Vice
faculty.summary: Villarini's research interests focus broadly on flood hydrology, extreme events, hydroclimatology, and climate predictions and projections, and he serves as Editor-in-Chief for Advances in Water Resources.

faculty.name: Claire White
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and the Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment
faculty.summary: White's research focuses on understanding and optimizing engineering and environmental materials, emphasizing the chemical mechanisms responsible for formation and long-term degradation of sustainable cements, along with conventional cements and new materials for carbon dioxide capture.

faculty.name: Mark Zondlo
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Director of Graduate Studies
faculty.summary: Zondlo's research focuses on the sources, sinks, and distributions of trace gases important for air quality, the carbon and nitrogen cycles, and climate change, developing and deploying optical-based sensors for field measurements bridging in-situ and remote sensing scales.

faculty.name: Chong Xie

faculty.name: Anna-Karin Gustavsson

faculty.name: Caleb Kemere
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Bioengineering

faculty.name: Anatoly B. Kolomeisky

faculty.name: Lan Luan

faculty.name: Amanda Marciel

faculty.name: Peter J. A. Nordlander

faculty.name: Xaq Pitkow
faculty.title: Associate Professor (now Carnegie Mellon University; formerly Rice ECE / Baylor)

faculty.name: Robert M. Raphael
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering

faculty.name: Harel Shouval
faculty.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering (Rice) and Neuroscience (UTHealth)
faculty.summary: Uses theoretical and computational approaches to study the rules of synaptic plasticity and their implications for learning, memory and neural development.

faculty.name: Jerzy Szablowski
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Develops noninvasive technologies combining synthetic biology and hardware to monitor and control brain activity, including drug delivery and blood-based biomarkers of neural activity.

faculty.name: Ming Tang
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Materials Science and NanoEngineering

faculty.name: James M. Tour
faculty.title: T. T. and W. F. Chao Professor of Chemistry; Professor of Materials Science and NanoEngineering
faculty.summary: Develops methods to synthesize graphene and MXenes, extract critical metals from waste, destroy toxic chemicals such as PFAS, and build light-activated molecular machines.

faculty.name: Ashok Veeraraghavan
faculty.title: Professor and Department Chair of Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Works on computational imaging, compressive sensing and computer vision, including lensless FlatCam and FlatScope systems for neural interfaces.

faculty.name: Rafael Verduzco
faculty.title: A. J. Hartsook Professor of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
faculty.summary: Studies polymer chemistry and characterization, including polymeric membranes for water treatment, bottlebrush polymers, covalent organic frameworks and bioelectronic devices.

faculty.name: Julea Vlassakis
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Designs micro- and nanoscale single-cell and single-molecule technologies to study proteins and their interactions, with applications to pediatric cancers such as Ewing sarcoma.

faculty.name: Geoff Wehmeyer
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering
faculty.summary: Investigates nanoscale heat transfer, including thermal property measurements of nanomaterials and thermal management for microelectronics and energy conversion.

faculty.name: Peter G. Wolynes
faculty.title: Bullard-Welch Foundation Professor of Chemistry
