faculty.name: Itai Ashlagi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Game theory, market design, matching markets
faculty.summary: Focuses on design and analysis of marketplaces where matching is central. Developed kidney exchange mechanisms (Franz Edelman Laureate). NSF-CAREER recipient; PhD from Technion.

faculty.name: Nicholas Bambos
faculty.title: Richard W. Weiland Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computer systems performance, networking, cloud computing, digital health
faculty.summary: Heads the Computer Systems Performance Engineering Lab. Research in architecture and high-performance engineering of computer systems and networks, with emphasis on medical and healthcare analytics. PhD from UC Berkeley.

faculty.name: Jose H. Blanchet
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied probability, Monte Carlo methods, extreme events
faculty.summary: Amazon Scholar and IMS Fellow. Leads DoD MURI on extreme events. Editor-in-Chief of Mathematics of Operations Research. Recipient of Erlang Prize and PECASE.

faculty.name: Margaret Brandeau
faculty.title: Coleman F. Fung Professor
faculty.sub_field: Health policy modeling, operations research, mathematical modeling
faculty.summary: Develops applied mathematical and economic models to support health policy decisions. Research covers HIV prevention, opioid epidemic, and homelessness responses. INFORMS Fellow.

faculty.name: Kay Giesecke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Financial engineering, credit risk, computational finance
faculty.summary: Research in financial engineering and quantitative risk management, developing machine learning and Monte Carlo methods for credit risk, mortgage markets, and systemic risk.

faculty.name: Peter Glynn
faculty.title: Thomas W. Ford Professor
faculty.sub_field: Stochastic simulation, queueing theory, applied probability
faculty.summary: Renowned researcher in stochastic simulation and applied probability, with foundational contributions to simulation methodology, queueing networks, and Markov processes.

faculty.name: Ashish Goel
faculty.title: Stanford W. Ascherman MD Professor
faculty.sub_field: Algorithms, market design, social choice, computational advertising
faculty.summary: Research in algorithms, market design, and computational social choice, with applications to online platforms, voting systems, and computational advertising.

faculty.name: Aaron Sidford
faculty.title: Associate Professor (MS&E & CS)
faculty.sub_field: Algorithms, convex optimization, numerical linear algebra
faculty.summary: Research in algorithmic foundations of optimization and numerical linear algebra, developing faster algorithms for fundamental problems in convex optimization and machine learning.

faculty.name: Chuck Eesley
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in entrepreneurship and innovation, studying the factors that influence entrepreneurial success, technology commercialization, and university-industry collaboration.

faculty.name: Ramesh Johari
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Platform economics, online marketplaces, mechanism design
faculty.summary: Research in platform economics and online marketplaces, studying pricing, reputation systems, and mechanism design for digital platforms and sharing economy.

funding.note: Research Assistantships fund salary, tuition allowance, health subsidy

faculty.name: Charlotte Bøttcher
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies condensed matter systems at the intersection of quantum information science, focusing on quantum phase transitions in Josephson junction arrays and hybrid material platforms for quantum computing. Joining Stanford Applied Physics in 2025.

faculty.name: Philip H. Bucksbaum
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses ultrafast lasers to probe atomic and molecular structure and dynamics on femtosecond and attosecond timescales, directing the Stanford PULSE Institute and advancing strong-field laser-atom physics and time-resolved x-ray science.

faculty.name: Michel Digonnet
faculty.title: Professor (Research)
faculty.summary: Develops advanced fiber-optic sensors, gyroscopes, and radiation-balanced fiber lasers, with expertise spanning photonic-bandgap fibers, slow-light fiber Bragg gratings, and MEMS-based optical acoustic sensors.

faculty.name: Martin M. Fejer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates nonlinear optical materials and devices, guided wave optics, and microstructured ferroelectrics for applications in lasers, precision optical characterization, and quantum science.

faculty.name: Ian R. Fisher
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies quantum materials with unconventional electronic and magnetic ground states, with an emphasis on design and discovery of new materials and the use of strain as a probe of and tuning parameter for exotic electronic phases. Serves as Department Chair.

faculty.name: Surya Ganguli
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Applies statistical physics and deep learning theory to understand how neural circuits compute, spanning synaptic plasticity, population dynamics, and the theory of deep neural networks.

faculty.name: Benjamin Good
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Applies tools from statistical physics and population genetics to understand evolutionary dynamics in rapidly evolving microbial populations such as the gut microbiome, bridging non-equilibrium physics and quantitative biology.

faculty.name: Tony Heinz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates electronic properties and dynamics of nanoscale materials including graphene and transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers using advanced optical spectroscopies. Directs the Edward L. Ginzton Laboratory.

faculty.name: Harold Y. Hwang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies complex oxide materials and heterostructures, with notable contributions to superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates, freestanding oxide membranes, and emergent phenomena at oxide interfaces. Directs SIMES.

faculty.name: Aharon Kapitulnik
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates correlated and disordered electron systems in reduced dimensions, developing precision instrumentation to detect subtle physical signatures including time-reversal symmetry breaking in unconventional superconductors.

faculty.name: Mark A. Kasevich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops atom interferometry and quantum metrology techniques for precision inertial sensing, entanglement-enhanced measurements, gravitational wave detection, and tests of fundamental physics including the equivalence principle.

faculty.name: Young Lee
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies novel electronic and magnetic materials in single crystalline form, focusing on quantum spin liquids, exotic superconductivity, and topological phases in quantum magnets using neutron and x-ray scattering.

faculty.name: Benjamin L. Lev
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Explores nonequilibrium quantum many-body physics using confocal cavity QED with ultracold quantum gases of dysprosium and twisted 2D materials, investigating quantum neural networks, spin glasses, and novel phases of quantum matter.

faculty.name: Hideo Mabuchi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of quantum optics, cavity QED, and quantum information science, developing coherent Ising machines for combinatorial optimization and advancing nonlinear photonic systems.

faculty.name: Kathryn A. Moler
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops and applies scanning SQUID microscopy to image magnetic fields and supercurrents in quantum materials with micron-scale resolution, studying vortex dynamics, topological insulators, and oxide heterointerfaces.

faculty.name: David A. Reis
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses femtosecond x-ray scattering and laser-based techniques at LCLS to study ultrafast dynamics in solids, including nonequilibrium lattice dynamics, high-harmonic generation in solids, and photo-induced phase transitions.

faculty.name: Amir Safavi-Naeini
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops chip-scale quantum photonic and acoustic devices on thin-film lithium niobate, including quantum acoustic processors, squeezed light sources, and microwave-to-optical transducers for quantum networks.

faculty.name: David Schuster
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Advances superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics for quantum computing, focusing on quantum error correction, high-coherence qubits, and microwave-to-optical quantum transduction using Rydberg atoms.

faculty.name: Zhi-Xun Shen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops photon-based instrumentation including ARPES to study quantum materials, best known for discovering the momentum-resolved d-wave pairing gap and pseudogap in high-temperature superconductors.

faculty.name: Jonathan Simon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Creates synthetic quantum matter using strongly interacting photons confined in metamaterial structures, exploring phenomena from Weyl semimetals to fractional quantum Hall states of light and developing mm-wave-to-optical transducers.

faculty.name: Yuri Suzuki
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Explores emergent interfacial phenomena and functional properties in complex oxide thin films and heterostructures, focusing on low-dimensional electron gases, spin current generation, and multifunctional materials.

faculty.name: Alfred Zong
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies light-induced nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum materials using ultrafast electron diffraction, attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, and coherent diffraction imaging with in-situ strain and gating capabilities.

faculty.name: Emmanuel Candes
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics and Statistics
faculty.summary: Compressed sensing, high-dimensional statistics, matrix completion, multiple testing. Winner of 2026 Shaw Prize in Mathematical Sciences.

faculty.name: Ravi Vakil
faculty.title: Robert Grimmett Professor in Mathematics
faculty.summary: Algebraic geometry, moduli spaces, enumerative geometry, Grothendieck ring, tropical geometry.

faculty.name: Yakov Eliashberg
faculty.title: Herald L. and Caroline L. Ritch Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Symplectic and contact topology, h-principle, complex geometry, Stein manifolds.

faculty.name: Brian Conrad
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics, Director of Undergraduate Studies
faculty.sub_field: Number Theory, Arithmetic Geometry, Algebraic Groups
faculty.summary: Arithmetic geometry, algebraic groups, p-adic geometry, number theory.

faculty.name: Rafe Mazzeo
faculty.title: Cassius Lamb Kirk Professor of Natural Sciences
faculty.summary: Geometric analysis, PDE on manifolds, moduli spaces with singularities, index theory on singular spaces.

faculty.name: Jonathan Luk
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Hyperbolic PDE, general relativity, black holes, stability problems. Winner of 2026 AMS Bocher Memorial Prize.

faculty.name: Mohammed Abouzaid
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Symplectic topology, Floer homology, Lagrangian submanifolds, mirror symmetry.

faculty.name: Andras Vasy
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Microlocal analysis, scattering theory, PDE on manifolds, general relativity.

faculty.name: Kannan Soundararajan
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Analytic number theory, L-functions, multiplicative number theory, random matrix models.

faculty.name: Eleny Ionel
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Symplectic geometry, Gromov-Witten theory, moduli spaces, enumerative invariants.

faculty.name: Jacob Fox
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Extremal and probabilistic combinatorics, Ramsey theory, graph limits, discrete geometry.

faculty.name: Maryam Mirzakhani
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: RIP. Teichmuller theory, hyperbolic geometry, ergodic theory on moduli spaces. Fields Medalist (2014).

faculty.name: Sarah Peluse
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Additive Combinatorics, Number Theory, Harmonic Analysis
faculty.summary: Additive combinatorics, higher-order Fourier analysis, arithmetic combinatorics. Winner of 2026 AWM Microsoft Research Prize.

faculty.name: Daniel Altman
faculty.title: Szego Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Higher-order Fourier analysis, additive combinatorics, ergodic theory.

faculty.name: Jae Hee Lee
faculty.title: Szego Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Symplectic topology, mirror symmetry, Floer theory, Fukaya categories.

faculty.name: Steven Kerckhoff
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Teichmuller theory, hyperbolic geometry, 3-manifolds, Kleinian groups.

faculty.name: Akshay Venkatesh
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.sub_field: Number Theory, Automorphic Forms, Algebraic Topology
faculty.summary: Automorphic forms, analytic number theory, representation theory, algebraic topology. Fields Medalist (2018).

faculty.name: Tadashi Tokieda
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Mathematical physics, dynamical systems, experimental mathematics, geometry, topology.

faculty.name: Soren Galatius
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Algebraic topology of moduli spaces, cobordism categories, homological stability.

faculty.name: Lexing Ying
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.sub_field: Applied Math, Scientific Computing, Machine Learning
faculty.summary: Fast numerical algorithms, multiscale methods, scientific machine learning, quantum chemistry computation.

faculty.name: George Papanicolaou
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.sub_field: Applied Math, Stochastic Processes, Wave Propagation
faculty.summary: Stochastic processes, random media, wave propagation, homogenization, financial mathematics.

faculty.name: Gunnar Carlsson
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics
faculty.summary: Algebraic topology, topological data analysis, computational topology, applied topology.

faculty.name: Persi Diaconis
faculty.title: Professor of Mathematics and Statistics
faculty.summary: Probability, mixing times, random walks on groups, magic tricks and mathematics, Bayesian statistics.

faculty.name: David Goldhaber-Gordon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how electrons organize and interact when confined to nanoscale structures, using cryogenic precision measurements and scanning probe techniques to explore exotic quantum states, moire superlattices, and topological insulators.

faculty.name: Kathryn Moler
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses scanning SQUID microscopy to image and characterize superconducting and magnetic phenomena in quantum materials, including vortex dynamics, topological insulators, and oxide heterostructures.

faculty.name: Aharon Kapitulnik
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates emergent phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems, including superconductivity and quantum phase transitions, using home-built scanning probe microscopes and precision magneto-optical tools.

faculty.name: Steven Kivelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theories for strongly correlated electronic systems, explaining how electron interactions produce emergent macroscopic phenomena including high-temperature superconductivity, quantum liquid crystals, and spin liquids.

faculty.name: Srinivas Raghu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies emergent behavior in quantum condensed matter systems, including non-Fermi liquids, quantum criticality, topological photonics, and Chern-Simons matter dualities in strongly interacting disordered systems.

faculty.name: Vedika Khemani
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies non-equilibrium quantum phases of matter, including time crystals and many-body quantum dynamics, exploring fundamental questions about thermalization and emergent phenomena in driven quantum systems.

faculty.name: Benjamin Feldman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Explores quantum systems in two-dimensional materials and moire heterostructures, investigating how electron interactions produce symmetry breaking, topological excitations, and new correlated phases.

faculty.name: Mark Kasevich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneers atom interferometry and quantum sensing technologies for precision measurement, including tests of general relativity, gravitational wave detection with atomic sensors, and matter-wave interferometry at macroscopic scales.

faculty.name: Benjamin Lev
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Explores quantum many-body physics at the intersection of ultracold atomic physics, quantum optics, and condensed matter, using confocal cavity QED to engineer out-of-equilibrium quantum gases and control twisted 2D materials.

faculty.name: Monika Schleier-Smith
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Advances optical control of interactions among laser-cooled atoms for quantum simulation, metrology, and computation, developing entanglement-enhanced sensing protocols and engineering novel quantum many-body states.

faculty.name: Jason Hogan
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops atom interferometry techniques for precision tests of fundamental physics, including gravitational wave detection with the MAGIS-100 atomic sensor, tests of general relativity, and searches for dark matter.

faculty.name: Savas Dimopoulos
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates fundamental physics beyond the Standard Model, co-proposing the Supersymmetric Standard Model and large extra dimensions; currently uses atom interferometry to test general relativity at unprecedented precision.

faculty.name: Peter Graham
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theories beyond the Standard Model spanning cosmology, dark matter, and gravitational wave detection, inventing novel experiments such as CASPEr and DM Radio to search for axion dark matter.

faculty.name: Eva Silverstein
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops testable mechanisms for cosmic inflation and addresses fundamental questions in quantum gravity and string theory, including singularity resolution and holographic models of de Sitter expansion.

faculty.name: Stephen Shenker
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Contributes foundational results in string theory and M-theory, including the first nonperturbative formulations of string theory and the matrix theory proposal, with recent work on quantum chaos and black holes.

faculty.name: Douglas Stanford
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on quantum gravity, black hole physics in holographic models, and connections between quantum information theory and spacetime geometry, including the dynamics of wormholes and chaotic quantum systems.

faculty.name: Xiaoliang Qi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the interplay of quantum entanglement, quantum gravity, and topological states of matter, using tensor networks and solvable models to understand emergent spacetime geometry from quantum dynamics.

faculty.name: Giorgio Gratta
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads experiments on fundamental particles and their interactions, including landmark neutrino oscillation measurements with KamLAND, searches for neutrinoless double beta decay with liquid xenon detectors, and tests of gravity at sub-millimeter distances.

faculty.name: Patricia Burchat
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies dark matter and dark energy using gravitational lensing with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (LSST), with a deep background in accelerator-based particle physics including CP violation and charm mixing measurements.

faculty.name: Risa Wechsler
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates galaxy formation, large-scale structure, and the nature of dark matter and dark energy using large numerical simulations combined with observational data from DES, DESI, and Rubin Observatory's LSST.

faculty.name: Chao-Lin Kuo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Searches for primordial gravitational waves in the cosmic microwave background through experiments at the South Pole (BICEP), Atacama (Simons Observatory), and in space (LiteBIRD), while developing superconducting detector systems for cosmology.

faculty.name: Peter Michelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) collaboration as Principal Investigator, studying gamma-ray bursts, pulsars, active galactic nuclei, and searching for dark matter signatures in diffuse gamma-ray emission.

faculty.name: Tom Abel
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses ab initio supercomputer simulations to study cosmic history, from the formation of the first stars and galaxies to cosmological reionization, pioneering adaptive-mesh-refinement algorithms and machine learning applications in astrophysics.

funding.note: Generally full financial support for first five years

faculty.name: Kevin Arrigo
faculty.title: Donald and Donald M. Steel Professor of Earth Sciences
faculty.summary: Professor of Earth System Science studying the ecology and biogeochemistry of polar marine ecosystems, phytoplankton dynamics, and sea ice. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment.

faculty.name: Jen Burney
faculty.title: Professor of Environmental Social Sciences and of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor working at the intersection of agriculture, energy, and climate in developing regions. Senior Fellow at the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies.

faculty.name: Karen Casciotti
faculty.title: Professor of Oceans and of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying the marine nitrogen cycle using stable isotope tracers and microbial biogeochemistry. Serves as Associate Dean for Facilities and Shared Labs.

faculty.name: Steven J. Davis
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying energy and carbon emissions systems and pathways to deep decarbonization. Senior Fellow at the Precourt Institute for Energy.

faculty.name: Giulio De Leo
faculty.title: Professor of Oceans and of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor working on the ecology of infectious disease and the management of marine and freshwater ecosystems. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment.

faculty.name: Anne Dekas
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Associate Professor studying environmental microbial activity and biogeochemistry, including nitrogen fixation, using single-cell and isotope techniques.

faculty.name: Noah Diffenbaugh
faculty.title: William Wrigley Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying climate dynamics, extreme weather events, and the impacts of climate change. Kimmelman Family Senior Fellow.

faculty.name: Rodolfo Dirzo
faculty.title: Bing Professor in Environmental Science and Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying biodiversity loss, defaunation, and plant-animal interactions. Associate Dean for Integrative Initiatives in Environmental Justice and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Scott Fendorf
faculty.title: Terry Huffington Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying the biogeochemistry of soils and sediments, including contaminant cycling such as arsenic. Senior Associate Dean for Research and Professor of Photon Science.

faculty.name: Chris Field
faculty.title: Melvin and Joan Lane Professor of Interdisciplinary Environmental Studies
faculty.summary: Professor of Earth System Science and Biology and Director of the Woods Institute for the Environment, studying global ecology, the carbon cycle, and climate change.

faculty.name: Christopher Francis
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science and of Oceans
faculty.summary: Professor studying the diversity and activity of microorganisms driving the nitrogen cycle in marine and estuarine environments. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Steven Gorelick
faculty.title: Cyrus Fisher Tolman Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying water resources, groundwater, and coupled human-natural water systems. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment.

faculty.name: Sebastian Heilpern
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying the links between biodiversity, freshwater ecosystems, and human food and nutrition systems.

faculty.name: Alison Hoyt
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying soil carbon cycling and greenhouse gas dynamics, including peatland and tropical systems. Center Fellow, by courtesy, at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Rob Jackson
faculty.title: Michelle and Kevin Douglas Provostial Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying the global carbon and methane cycles, greenhouse gas emissions, and ecosystem-climate interactions. Senior Fellow at the Woods and Precourt Institutes.

faculty.name: Alexandra Konings
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Associate Professor using satellite remote sensing to study vegetation water dynamics and land-atmosphere carbon and water exchange. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Eric Lambin
faculty.title: George and Setsuko Ishiyama Provostial Professor
faculty.sub_field: Land system science / land use change
faculty.summary: Professor studying land use and land cover change, deforestation, and human-environment interactions. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment.

faculty.name: David Lobell
faculty.title: Benjamin M. Page Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying agricultural systems, food security, and crop responses to climate using satellite data. William Wrigley Senior Fellow at multiple Stanford institutes.

faculty.name: Katharine (Kate) Maher
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying water-rock interactions, chemical weathering, and geochemical approaches to carbon removal. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Adam Pellegrini
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying how fire and disturbance shape ecosystem biogeochemistry, carbon, and nutrient cycling.

faculty.name: Aditi Sheshadri
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying atmospheric circulation and dynamics, including stratosphere-troposphere coupling and atmospheric waves. Center Fellow, by courtesy, at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Leif Thomas
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying ocean dynamics, including fronts, submesoscale processes, and turbulent mixing. By courtesy, of Oceans.

faculty.name: Yuan Wang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying aerosols, clouds, and their effects on climate and air quality. Center Fellow, by courtesy, at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Paula V. Welander
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying microbial lipid biosynthesis and geobiological biomarkers linking microbes to the geologic record. Associate Dean for Research.

faculty.name: Elliott White Jr.
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying coastal wetland ecosystems, blue carbon, and land-water dynamics using remote sensing. Center Fellow, by courtesy, at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Earle Wilson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor studying ocean mixing and circulation, including polar and high-latitude ocean processes. By courtesy, of Geophysics and Oceans.

faculty.name: Gabrielle Wong-Parodi
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Associate Professor studying environmental decision-making, risk perception, and behavioral responses to climate and environmental hazards. Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Page Chamberlain
faculty.title: Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences and of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor whose research uses geochemistry and stable isotopes to study paleoclimate, tectonics, and landscape evolution.

faculty.name: Tadashi Fukami
faculty.title: Professor of Biology and of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying community assembly, priority effects, and microbial ecology in systems such as nectar and soil.

faculty.name: Kabir Peay
faculty.title: Professor of Biology and of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Professor studying the ecology and biogeography of fungi and mycorrhizal symbioses. Senior Associate Dean for Education and Director of the Earth Systems Program.

faculty.name: Greg Beroza
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Analyzes seismograms using machine learning and data mining to understand earthquake source processes, image shallow crustal structure with ambient seismic fields, and quantify seismic hazards.

faculty.name: Biondo Biondi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops algorithms for 3-D seismic imaging of Earth's subsurface, including wave-equation migration, migration velocity analysis, and distributed fiber-optic sensing for reflection seismology.

faculty.name: Ettore Biondi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Advances distributed fiber-optic sensing technologies to monitor dynamic Earth system processes, using existing telecom fiber cables as dense seismic arrays for earthquake, volcanic, and environmental applications.

faculty.name: Jef Caers
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops decision-making methods under uncertainty for Earth resource exploration, applying AI and geostatistics to critical mineral supply, geothermal energy, and subsurface risk quantification.

faculty.name: Eric Dunham
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses physics-based computational simulations to characterize earthquake rupture dynamics, tsunami generation and propagation, volcanic processes, and ice shelf mechanics.

faculty.name: Anton Ermakov
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the internal structure and evolution of Solar System bodies using spacecraft gravity, topography, and radiometry data combined with geophysical and orbital dynamics modeling.

faculty.name: Simon Klemperer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the structure, tectonics, and composition of the continental lithosphere using active and passive seismology, with major field programs across the Himalaya-Tibet orogen, Basin and Range, and Ethiopian Rift.

faculty.name: Rosemary Knight
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneered the field of hydrogeophysics, using near-surface geophysical methods including airborne electromagnetics and nuclear magnetic resonance to image groundwater systems and inform water resource management.

faculty.name: Alexandra Konings
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies interactions between the global carbon and water cycles using satellite remote sensing, particularly microwave sensing of vegetation water content and plant hydraulic processes.

faculty.name: Ching-Yao Lai
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Integrates mathematical and machine-learned models with observational data to study ice dynamics in Antarctica and Greenland, advancing fundamental understanding of ice sheet flow under climate change.

faculty.name: Mathieu Lapôtre
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the physics of sedimentary and geomorphic processes that shape planetary surfaces, with applications to paleoenvironmental reconstructions on Earth and Mars using rover and orbital data.

faculty.name: Dustin Schroeder
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Advances ice-penetrating radar methods to observe and understand the interaction of ice and water across the solar system, from rapidly changing ice sheets to subsurface exploration of Europa and other icy moons.

faculty.name: Paul Segall
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies earthquake and volcano deformation using GPS, InSAR, and strainmeter data combined with physics-based models to understand fault mechanics, slow slip events, and induced seismicity.

faculty.name: Jenny Suckale
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops customized mathematical models of natural hazards — including volcanic eruptions, ice-sheet instability, and induced seismicity — tested against observational data for disaster risk reduction.

faculty.name: Sonia Tikoo-Schantz
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses paleomagnetism and rock magnetism to investigate dynamo magnetic fields and thermal evolution of planetary bodies, and to understand impact cratering processes on the Earth, Moon, and asteroids.

faculty.name: Laura Schaefer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Models atmosphere-interior exchange on rocky planets, studying the evolution of planetary atmospheres from magma ocean outgassing through long-term volatile cycles, and assessing conditions for habitability on exoplanets.

faculty.name: Da Yang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies atmospheric convection, cloud organization, and climate dynamics using theory, observations, numerical models, and machine learning to understand extreme weather and climate processes.

faculty.name: Howard Zebker
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneered spaceborne radar interferometry (InSAR) for measuring millimeter-scale surface deformation over wide areas, with applications to earthquake strain, volcanic inflation, ice sheet mass balance, and groundwater subsidence.

faculty.name: Halleh Balch
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Oceans and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering, and HHMI Hanna Gray Faculty Fellow
faculty.summary: Balch is an experimental physicist whose research focuses on advancing water sustainability and ocean exploration through new technologies based on nanoscale control over light-matter interactions and engineered materials.

faculty.name: Barbara Block
faculty.title: Charles and Elizabeth Prothro Professor of Marine Sciences, Professor of Oceans and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Block, based at Hopkins Marine Station, studies the physiology and ecology of large pelagic marine predators such as tunas and sharks, using electronic tagging and physiological research to inform ocean conservation.

faculty.name: Alexandria Boehm
faculty.title: Richard and Rhoda Goldman Professor of Environmental Studies, Professor of Oceans and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Boehm studies pathogens in natural and engineered environments and their transmission to humans through water, and works broadly on coastal water quality including the sources, transport, and ecology of fecal indicator organisms, pathogens, and nitrogen.

faculty.name: Karen Casciotti
faculty.title: Associate Dean for Facilities and Shared Labs, Professor of Oceans, of Earth System Science and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Casciotti studies the marine nitrogen cycle using stable isotope geochemistry, geochemical modeling, and molecular biology to understand how nitrate, nitrite, and nitrous oxide are produced and consumed in ocean waters, particularly in oxygen-deficient zones.

faculty.name: Larry Crowder
faculty.title: Edward Ricketts Provostial Professor, Professor of Oceans, Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and Professor, by courtesy, of Environmental
faculty.summary: Crowder's research centers on predation and food web interactions, recruitment variation in fishes, population and food web modeling in conservation biology, and interdisciplinary approaches to marine conservation.

faculty.name: Kristen Davis
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Oceans and, by courtesy, of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Davis is an engineer and oceanographer studying how physical processes shape coastal waters, combining principles of fluid mechanics, oceanography, and ecology using field observations and numerical tools to examine ocean circulation and its influence on marine ecosystems.

faculty.name: Giulio De Leo
faculty.title: Professor of Oceans, of Earth System Science and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: De Leo is a theoretical ecologist investigating processes driving population dynamics, focusing on resilience of ecosystems to natural and anthropogenic stressors, including parasitic and infectious diseases and sustainable management of marine populations.

faculty.name: Rob Dunbar
faculty.title: W.M. Keck Professor in the School of Earth Sciences, Professor of Oceans, Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and Professor, by courtesy, o
faculty.summary: Dunbar's research studies global environmental change with a focus on air-sea interactions, tropical marine ecosystems, polar climate, and biogeochemistry, and he is interested in environmental policy directed toward problem-solving.

faculty.name: Christopher Francis
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science, of Oceans and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Francis studies the molecular, biogeochemical, and ecological aspects of microbially-mediated cycling of nitrogen and metals, examining microorganisms involved in nitrification, denitrification, and manganese cycling in coastal and estuarine systems.

faculty.name: Oliver Fringer
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering and of Oceans
faculty.summary: Fringer develops and applies numerical models and high-performance computational techniques to study fundamental processes influencing the dynamics of the coastal ocean, rivers, lakes, and estuaries.

faculty.name: William Gilly
faculty.title: Professor of Oceans
faculty.summary: Gilly, based at Hopkins Marine Station, studies the neurobiology and physiology of marine organisms, including the behavior and biology of Humboldt squid and other cephalopods.

faculty.name: Jeremy Goldbogen
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Oceans
faculty.summary: Goldbogen, based at Hopkins Marine Station, is a comparative physiologist studying the integrative biology of marine organisms, with a particular focus on the feeding biomechanics, energetics, and foraging ecology of baleen whales.

faculty.name: Fiorenza Micheli
faculty.title: David and Lucile Packard Professor of Marine Science, Professor of Oceans and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Micheli, chair of the Oceans Department and co-director of the Center for Ocean Solutions, studies the processes shaping marine communities and coastal social-ecological systems, including climatic impacts, marine predator ecology, small-scale fisheries sustainability, and marine protected areas.

faculty.name: Stephen Monismith
faculty.title: Obayashi Professor in the School of Engineering and Professor of Oceans
faculty.summary: Monismith applies fluid mechanics principles to flow processes in rivers, lakes, estuaries, and oceans with particular interest in ecological impacts, studying estuarine hydrodynamics and mixing, flows over coral reefs, and stratified turbulence.

faculty.name: Stephen Palumbi
faculty.title: Jane and Marshall Steel Jr. Professor of Marine Sciences, Professor of Oceans and of Biology
faculty.summary: Palumbi studies the genomics of marine organisms to address basic evolutionary questions and practical conservation, including human-induced evolutionary change and developing genomic methods to identify ocean species and corals resistant to climate change.

faculty.name: Brooke Weigel
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Oceans
faculty.summary: Weigel is a marine ecologist whose research focuses on the ecology, physiology, and genomics of marine algae and microbial communities, particularly the feedbacks between climate change, kelp forests, microbes, and carbon cycling in the ocean; her lab is based at Hopkins Marine Station.

faculty.name: Gretchen C. Daily
faculty.title: Bing Professor of Environmental Science and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and, by courtesy, at the Freeman Spogli Institute for Inter
faculty.summary: Daily is co-founder and Faculty Director of the Stanford Natural Capital Project; her research quantifies the production and value of ecosystem services, harmonizes biodiversity conservation with agriculture, and develops policies for integrating nature into societal decisions.

faculty.name: Eric Lambin
faculty.title: George and Setsuko Ishiyama Provostial Professor and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.sub_field: Land use change and environmental geography
faculty.summary: Lambin, a geographer and environmental scientist, studies the causes and impacts of land use changes worldwide; he chaired the international Land Use and Land Cover Change project and has received the Volvo Environment Prize and Blue Planet Prize.

faculty.name: Chris Field
faculty.title: Melvin and Joan Lane Professor of Interdisciplinary Environmental Studies, Director of the Woods Institute for the Environment, Professor of Earth System Scienc
faculty.summary: Field's research focuses on climate change, especially solutions that improve lives now, decrease future warming, and support vibrant economies, with recent projects emphasizing reduced risks from coastal flooding and wildfires; he co-chaired IPCC Working Group II.

faculty.name: Rob Jackson
faculty.title: Michelle and Kevin Douglas Provostial Professor and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and at the Precourt Institute for Energy
faculty.sub_field: Global change biology and carbon cycle
faculty.summary: Jackson and his lab examine the many ways people affect the Earth, producing scientific knowledge to shape policies and reduce environmental footprints; he chairs the Global Carbon Project and works to measure and reduce methane emissions and air pollution.

faculty.name: David Lobell
faculty.title: Benjamin M. Page Professor, William Wrigley Senior Fellow at the Freeman Spogli Institute, at the Woods Institute for the Environment and at the Stanford Instit
faculty.summary: Lobell directs the Center on Food Security and the Environment; his research focuses on agriculture and food security, generating and using unique datasets to study rural areas and climate change risks and adaptations in cropping systems.

faculty.name: Noah Diffenbaugh
faculty.title: William Wrigley Professor and Kimmelman Family Senior Fellow
faculty.summary: Diffenbaugh's research focuses on understanding what aspects of the climate system most directly and acutely impact people and ecosystems; he has served as a Lead Author for the IPCC and studies climate variability, change, and extremes.

faculty.name: Katharine (Kate) Maher
faculty.title: Professor of Earth System Science, Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and Professor, by courtesy, of Earth and Planetary Sciences
faculty.summary: Maher's research examines the carbon cycle through multiple lenses, combining computer models with field and laboratory measurements to link hydrologic, chemical, and biological processes; current projects include soil carbon cycling, water quality, and carbon dioxide removal.

faculty.name: Steven Gorelick
faculty.title: Cyrus Fisher Tolman Professor and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Gorelick directs the Global Freshwater Initiative and has published extensively on groundwater management, water security, water resources vulnerability in developing regions, remediation design, and ecohydrology.

faculty.name: Jenna Davis
faculty.title: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering, of Environmental Social Sciences and Higgins-Magid Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute
faculty.summary: Davis heads the Stanford Program on Water, Health & Development, with research and teaching focused at the nexus of water, economic development, and public health, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, with field research in more than 20 countries.

faculty.name: Meagan Mauter
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Civil & Environmental Engineering, of Photon Science, Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and at the Precourt Instit
faculty.summary: Mauter directs the Water and Energy Efficiency for the Environment Lab (WE3Lab), aiming to provide sustainable water supply in a carbon-constrained world through innovation in water treatment technology, optimization of water management, and redesign of water policy.

faculty.name: William Abraham Tarpeh
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Chemical Engineering and, by courtesy, of Civil and Environmental Engineering
faculty.summary: Tarpeh's lab reimagines liquid waste streams as resources, developing and evaluating novel approaches to resource recovery from wastewaters at molecular, unit-process, and systems scales using electrochemistry, separations, and reactor design.

faculty.name: Sally Benson
faculty.title: Precourt Family Professor, Professor of Energy Science Engineering and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment and the Precourt Institute for E
faculty.summary: Benson studies technologies and pathways to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, including geologic storage of CO2 in deep underground formations and energy systems analysis for a low-carbon future; she co-founded the Stanford Center for Carbon Storage.

faculty.name: Adam Brandt
faculty.title: Professor of Energy Science Engineering and Senior Fellow at the Precourt Institute for Energy
faculty.sub_field: Energy systems and life cycle assessment
faculty.summary: Brandt is interested in reducing the environmental impacts of energy systems, focusing on understanding, measuring, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions from fossil energy sources using life cycle assessment and process optimization.

faculty.name: Ines M. L. Azevedo
faculty.title: Professor of Energy Science Engineering, Senior Fellow at the Precourt Institute for Energy and Professor, by courtesy, of Civil and Environmental Engineering a
faculty.summary: Azevedo works on problems that combine environmental, technical, economic, and policy issues, assessing how energy systems are likely to evolve, the technologies that can address future energy needs, and the decision-making of agents in the economy.

faculty.name: Marshall Burke
faculty.title: Professor of Environmental Social Sciences, Senior Fellow at the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies, at the Woods Institute for the Environment,
faculty.summary: Burke uses tools from the social and natural sciences to measure environmental change and its impacts on society, spanning climate change, air pollution, food security, and poverty measurement, combining economics, statistics, remote sensing, and machine learning.

faculty.name: Jen Burney
faculty.title: Professor of Environmental Social Sciences, of Earth System Science and Senior Fellow at the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies
faculty.sub_field: Climate, air pollution and food security
faculty.summary: Burney's research focuses on the coupled relationships between climate and food security, measuring air pollutant emissions, quantifying climate and pollution effects on food systems, and designing and evaluating adaptation and mitigation strategies for farmers.

faculty.name: Nicole Ardoin
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Environmental Social Sciences and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Ardoin and her Social Ecology Lab research motivations for and barriers to environmental behavior at individual and collective scales, using mixed methods to study place-based connections, environmental learning, and social-ecological interactions in sustainability decision-making.

faculty.name: Barton Thompson
faculty.title: Robert E. Paradise Professor of Natural Resources Law, Professor of Environmental Social Sciences and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Thompson, a global expert on water and natural resources, focuses on how to improve resource management through legal, institutional, and technological innovation, and directs the Water in the West program at the Woods Institute.

faculty.name: Erin Mordecai
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Biology and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Mordecai's research focuses on the ecology of infectious disease, studying how climate, species interactions, and global change drive infectious disease dynamics in humans and natural ecosystems, combining mathematical modeling and empirical work.

faculty.name: Jenny Suckale
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Geophysics and, Senior Fellow, by courtesy, at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Suckale's group studies disasters to reduce the risk they pose, developing customized mathematical models tested against observational data and informed by community needs, spanning volcanic eruptions, ice-sheet instability, permafrost, induced seismicity, and flood-risk mitigation.

faculty.name: Jane Kathryn Willenbring
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences and, by courtesy, of Earth System Science
faculty.summary: Willenbring is a geologist who studies the evolution of the Earth's surface, especially how landscapes are affected by tectonics, climate change, and life, using geochemical techniques including cosmogenic nuclides, high-resolution topography, and landscape evolution models.

faculty.name: Sylvia K. Plevritis
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Russ B. Altman
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Barbara Engelhardt
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Chiara Sabatti

faculty.name: Lu Tian
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Dennis Wall
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Stephen B. Montgomery
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Teri Klein

faculty.name: Emily Alsentzer

faculty.name: Roxana Daneshjou
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of DBDS and Dermatology, working on AI and machine learning applications in dermatology with focus on algorithmic fairness and health equity.

faculty.name: Jason Fries
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of DBDS and Medicine (Computational Medicine), developing natural language processing and machine learning methods for extracting insights from clinical and biomedical text data.

faculty.name: Olivier Gevaert
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and DBDS, developing machine learning methods for multi-omics data integration and biomedical data fusion, particularly in cancer research.

faculty.name: Manuel Rivas
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of DBDS, focusing on statistical genetics methods for large-scale biobank data analysis to understand the genetic basis of complex human diseases.

faculty.name: Julia Salzman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on statistical computational biology with emphasis on RNA splicing analysis, single-cell methods, cancer biology, and computational approaches to study microbes.

faculty.name: Nigam H. Shah
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and DBDS, Chief Data Scientist for Stanford Health Care, working on clinical informatics and machine learning for healthcare delivery improvement.

faculty.name: Wing Hung Wong
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Stephen R. Pierce Family Goldman Sachs Professor, applying statistics, computation, and engineering approaches to biology and medicine, with focus on gene regulation and precision medicine.

faculty.name: Serena Yeung
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of DBDS, developing computer vision and deep learning methods for medical applications including surgical video analysis and clinical decision support.

faculty.name: James Zou
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor of DBDS, working on machine learning methods for biomedical data analysis, genomics, AI safety and fairness in healthcare applications.

faculty.name: Aaron Newman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor of DBDS, developing computational methods for studying tumor heterogeneity, cancer stem cells, and tumor immunology using single-cell and bulk genomic data.

faculty.name: Mark Musen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and DBDS, working on biomedical ontology, knowledge representation, and clinical informatics standards for intelligent data analysis.

faculty.name: Joseph (Jody) Puglisi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the role of RNA in cellular processes and disease, focusing on the mechanism of translation and RNA structure/dynamics using biophysical tools such as NMR and cryo-EM.

faculty.name: K. Christopher Garcia
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structural and functional basis of receptor/ligand interactions relevant to human health, focusing on immune system receptors, host-pathogen interactions, and protein engineering for therapeutic development.

faculty.name: Soichi Wakatsuki
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the structural biology of ubiquitin signaling, protein self-assembly, and vesicle transport using X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, and integrative multi-scale bioimaging approaches.

faculty.name: William Greenleaf
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops high-throughput sequencing and microscopy tools to understand how the physical state of the genome governs gene regulation and cellular identity, working at the intersection of genomics, epigenomics, and biophysics.

faculty.name: Rhiju Das
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops computational methods to predict and design RNA structure and function, combining high-throughput experiments with the crowdsourced Eterna platform to solve RNA folding and design problems.

faculty.name: Daniel Fisher
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Applies theoretical physics approaches to understand evolutionary and ecological dynamics, including microbial diversity, cancer evolution, and the physical principles governing population-level biological phenomena.

faculty.name: Kerwyn Casey (KC) Huang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses analytical, computational, and experimental approaches to understand how physical principles govern bacterial cell shape, division, and organization, with a focus on membrane tension and cell-wall synthesis.

faculty.name: Judith Frydman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how proteins fold in living cells, focusing on molecular chaperones and protein quality control networks, and how their dysfunction contributes to cancer and neurodegenerative diseases.

faculty.name: Daniel Herschlag
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the fundamental behavior of RNA and proteins, focusing on enzyme catalysis, RNA folding, and RNA-protein interactions to understand the physical and chemical principles underlying biological function.

faculty.name: Axel Brunger
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the molecular mechanisms of synaptic neurotransmission using structural biology and biophysics, focusing on the synaptic proteins that mediate membrane fusion and nerve cell communication.

faculty.name: Lynette Cegelski
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops interdisciplinary chemical biology and solid-state NMR approaches to study bacterial biofilms and cell-wall architecture, with the goal of discovering new antibiotics and understanding microbial community structure.

faculty.name: Polly Fordyce
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops microfluidic platforms for high-throughput quantitative biophysics and single-cell genomics, enabling large-scale measurement of kinetic and thermodynamic constants governing molecular interactions and cellular function.

faculty.name: Zev Bryant
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the mechanochemistry of molecular motors using single-molecule biophysics techniques, investigating how nanoscale biological machines convert chemical energy into mechanical work with a focus on torque generation and unconventional myosins.

faculty.name: Alice Ting
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops and disseminates molecular technologies such as proximity labeling (APEX, TurboID) for mapping protein interactions and signaling networks in living cells and neurons.

faculty.name: Benjamin Good
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Applies statistical physics and population genetics to understand microbial evolutionary dynamics, developing theoretical principles to forecast and control evolution in microbial communities including the gut microbiome.

faculty.name: Patrick Bassal
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Civil, Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Combines nonlinear dynamic geotechnical modeling with subsurface characterization, geostatistics, and remote sensing (InSAR, LiDAR) to understand ground failures from natural hazards. Conducted post-earthquake reconnaissance including the 2023 Turkiye-Syria earthquakes.

faculty.name: Min Liew
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Specializes in permafrost and cold regions geotechnics, climate change-related geohazards, and climate-resilient sustainable civil infrastructure. Uses numerical modeling of coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical physics validated with laboratory, field, and sensing methods.

faculty.name: Halil Sezen
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Researches structural analysis, design, and performance assessment of structures under extreme loading conditions, including dynamic behavior and collapse of buildings and rehabilitation of concrete buildings and bridges. Has published over 150 peer-reviewed articles with funding from NSF, FHWA, and DOE.

faculty.name: Abdollah Shafieezadeh
faculty.title: Professor, Civil, Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Abba G. Lichtenstein Professorship in Civil Engineering
faculty.summary: Leads the RAMSIS Lab advancing uncertainty quantification, reliability, resilience, and life-cycle performance assessment methods for structural and infrastructure systems ranging from buildings and bridges to power grids and flood defenses, addressing both acute hazards and chronic deterioration.

faculty.name: Lisa Burris
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Focuses on increasing the sustainability of concrete construction through novel supplementary and alternative cementitious materials for traffic infrastructure, characterizing material properties and linking hydration to concrete strength and durability.

faculty.name: Ethan Kubatko
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops and applies computational models of fluid flow and transport processes, with applications from hurricane storm surge simulation to sea-level rise impacts on estuarine systems and tidal turbine performance. Directs the Computational Hydrodynamics and Informatics Laboratory.

faculty.name: Benjamin Coifman
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Works on intelligent transportation systems, developing new approaches to traffic surveillance that lead to better traffic control, spanning traffic flow theory and driver dynamics while bridging academic research with practical implementation.

faculty.name: Rabi Mishalani
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Applies probabilistic modeling, statistical inference, experimental design, and optimization to public transportation planning and operations, real-time network monitoring, and infrastructure resilience decision-making, using OSU's campus transit system as a living laboratory.

faculty.name: Andre Carrel
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Associate Professor, Knowlton School of Architecture
faculty.summary: Directs the Travel Behavior Research Group, studying the dynamics of travel behavior, travelers' adaptation to experienced service quality, and the impact of emerging mobility technologies (autonomous, shared, alternative-fuel) on travel demand to inform sustainable transportation policy.

faculty.name: Kelsea Best
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Assistant Professor, Knowlton School of Architecture
faculty.summary: Investigates how climate change interacts with human societies and infrastructure, and how adaptation strategies can be implemented equitably, using computational methods such as machine learning and agent-based modeling of coupled human-natural systems.

faculty.name: Jim Stagge
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Directs the Hydrologic Extremes Research Laboratory, investigating the frequency and severity of droughts and floods, climate change impacts on water resources, and management strategies to protect society and the environment.

faculty.name: Linda Weavers
faculty.title: Professor, Civil, Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; John C. Geupel Chair, College of Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops water and hazardous waste treatment technologies, investigating ultrasound for treatment of emerging contaminants such as PFAS, harmful algal bloom control, and membrane defouling. Has secured over $35 million in sponsored research funding.

faculty.name: John Lenhart
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Associate Chair
faculty.summary: Studies reactions and processes at important natural and engineered interfaces to understand contaminant fate, combining experiments with mathematical modeling on topics including cyanotoxins, microplastics, arsenic in Ohio groundwater, and rare earth element recovery from acid mine drainage.

faculty.name: Karen Dannemiller
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Directs the Indoor Environmental Quality research group, studying chemical and microbial processes in indoor environments that impact human health, with funding from NSF, NIH, HUD, and NASA.

faculty.name: Rongjun Qin
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering
faculty.summary: Develops computational methods for accurately measuring static and moving objects in urban contexts using aerial/UAV imagery, LiDAR, and satellite multispectral/hyperspectral images. Author of the RSP and MSP software tools for reconstructing 3D information from 2D images.

faculty.name: Alper Yilmaz
faculty.title: Professor, Civil Environmental and Geodetic Engineering; Professor, Computer Science and Engineering (courtesy)
faculty.summary: Leads the Photogrammetric Computer Vision Lab, focusing on biomimetic navigation systems for unmanned systems, anomaly mining in multi-physics data, and learning geospatial information for scene understanding, with over $13M in extramural funding and 190+ publications.

faculty.name: Lei Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Civil, Environmental and Geodetic Engineering
faculty.summary: Specializes in acquiring, analyzing, and interpreting geodetic data, developing high-precision GNSS positioning algorithms with applications to tectonic and geodynamic deformations and interactions between environmental changes and the solid Earth.

faculty.name: Raef Bassily
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Computer Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Associate Professor working on the theoretical foundations of machine learning, with emphasis on differential privacy, private optimization, and statistical learning theory.

faculty.name: Tanya Berger-Wolf
faculty.title: Professor, Computer Science and Engineering (joint with EEOB and ECE); Director, Translational Data Analytics Institute
faculty.summary: Professor and director of the Translational Data Analytics Institute whose work applies data science, computer vision, and network analysis to ecology, wildlife conservation, and imageomics.

faculty.name: Spyros Blanas
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Computer Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Associate Professor researching database systems and high-performance data management, including query processing on modern hardware and large scientific datasets.

faculty.name: Michael Bond
faculty.title: Professor, Computer Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Professor researching programming languages and systems, with emphasis on concurrency, memory models, and improving the reliability and performance of software.

faculty.name: Eric Fosler-Lussier

faculty.summary: Professor researching automatic speech recognition, spoken-language processing, and natural language processing, with applications including clinical and biomedical language.

faculty.name: Zeyu Guo

faculty.name: Pooya Hatami

faculty.name: Mahdi Khalili
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Computer Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor working on trustworthy machine learning, including fairness, privacy, and the societal impacts of learning algorithms.

faculty.name: Zhiqiang Lin

faculty.summary: Distinguished Professor and director of the Institute for Cybersecurity and Digital Trust whose research covers systems and software security, binary analysis, and IoT/mobile security.

faculty.name: Xia Ning

faculty.summary: Professor whose research applies data mining and machine learning to biomedical problems including drug discovery, molecular design, and health informatics.

faculty.title: Professor, Computer Science and Engineering

faculty.name: Andrew Perrault

faculty.name: Mi Zhang

faculty.name: Xueru Zhang

faculty.name: Kannan Athreya

faculty.name: Shaileshh Bojja Venkatakrishnan

faculty.summary: Assistant Professor working on networked and distributed systems with a focus on blockchain and decentralized peer-to-peer network design.
