faculty.name: Mina Aganagic
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Aganagic's work sits at the intersection of mathematics and theoretical physics, using techniques from string theory and mirror symmetry to address problems in geometry and topology. Her research explores knot categorization, quantum Langlands correspondences, and topological vertex theory.

faculty.name: Suncica Canic
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Canic's research focuses on mathematical modeling and analysis of partial differential equations arising in fluid dynamics, particularly fluid-structure interaction problems with applications to cardiovascular mechanics, hemodynamics, and medical device design.

faculty.name: Jennifer Chayes
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Chayes's research applies tools from probability and graph theory to problems in machine learning and complex networks, with a focus on mathematical structures like graphons for modeling large-scale systems. She holds joint appointments in EECS, Information, and Statistics.

faculty.name: Steven N. Evans
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Evans' research spans stochastic processes and their applications to mathematical biology, including phylogenetics, population genetics, and evolutionary dynamics. His work develops probabilistic models for biological systems with rigorous mathematical foundations.

faculty.name: Ming Gu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Gu develops fast and stable algorithms for large-scale linear algebra problems, including matrix factorizations, eigenvalue computations, and structured linear systems, spanning both theoretical foundations and practical applications in scientific computing and data analysis.

faculty.name: Venkatesan Guruswami
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Guruswami's research lies at the intersection of computer science and mathematics, focusing on error-correcting codes, algebraic methods for computation, and approximate optimization. He also serves as Director of the Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing.

faculty.name: Olga Holtz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Holtz's work lies at the intersection of numerical linear algebra, matrix theory, and combinatorics, focusing on communication costs and computational complexity of algorithms. She investigates structured matrices, root localization of polynomials, and communication-efficient matrix multiplication.

faculty.name: Michael J. Lindsey
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Lindsey's research develops numerical methods and mathematical theory for computational physics problems, with emphasis on electronic structure calculations, quantum many-body systems, and tensor network methods bridging applied mathematics and computational quantum science.

faculty.name: Lin Lin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Lin develops mathematical and computational methods for quantum mechanical systems, spanning numerical algorithms for quantum chemistry (Kohn-Sham DFT) and quantum computing algorithms including Hamiltonian simulation, phase estimation, and ground-state preparation.

faculty.name: Per-Olof Persson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Persson's research focuses on computational mathematics and scientific computing, particularly unstructured mesh generation, high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods, and their applications to computational fluid dynamics, fluid-structure interaction, and wave propagation problems.

faculty.name: Fraydoun Rezakhanlou
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Rezakhanlou's work sits at the intersection of probability theory and PDEs, focusing on stochastic models and conservation laws. His research spans scalar conservation laws with random initial conditions, stochastic Navier-Stokes, particle systems, and multi-agent reinforcement learning.

faculty.name: James A. Sethian
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Sethian pioneered level set and fast marching methods for solving PDEs on irregular domains with moving interfaces, with applications spanning semiconductor manufacturing, seismic imaging, fluid dynamics, and tumor growth simulation.

faculty.name: Chris Shannon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Shannon applies rigorous mathematical tools including transversality theory, Lipschitz functions, and equilibrium analysis to foundational questions in economic theory, examining subjective beliefs, market stability, preference evolution, and strategic behavior.

faculty.name: Nikhil Srivastava
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Srivastava's work lies at the intersection of mathematics and theoretical computer science, focusing on random matrix theory and the geometry of polynomials. He co-resolved the Kadison-Singer problem and developed the theory of interlacing families, constructing bipartite Ramanujan graphs of all degrees.

faculty.name: Franziska Weber
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Weber's research centers on the theoretical and computational study of nonlinear partial differential equations, combining techniques from numerical analysis and applied mathematics. She is also affiliated with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

faculty.name: Jon Wilkening
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Wilkening develops numerical methods and computational algorithms to solve PDEs, with applications ranging from fluid dynamics (water waves, swimming sheets) to materials science and micromagnetics, combining mathematical analysis with high-performance computing.

faculty.name: Mariusz Wodzicki
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Wodzicki's research spans noncommutative geometry, cyclic homology, and algebraic K-theory, developing algebraic tools that bridge pure and applied mathematics, including work on determinants in infinite dimensions and zeta-regularized products.

faculty.name: Maciej Zworski
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Zworski's research centers on semiclassical analysis and its applications to mathematical physics, particularly scattering theory and quantum chaos. He investigates resonances, quantum decay rates, and spectral properties of operators using microlocal analysis techniques.

faculty.name: Carlos Bustamante
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Carlos Bustamante is a biophysicist who uses single-molecule approaches to study the mechanics of DNA, RNA, and proteins. He is best know for pioneering optical tweezers experiments that measure the forces driving molecular motors as well as the forces required the study of unfolding and refolding of individual proteins and RNAs.

faculty.name: Ahmet Yildiz
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Research Interests

faculty.name: Jennifer Doudna
faculty.title: Nobel Laureate in Chemistry; Professor; Li Ka Shing Chancellor’s Chair in Biomedical and Health Sciences, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Jennifer Doudna is a Nobel Laureate in Chemistry, and a Professor of Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology. Her research focuses on RNA as it forms a variety of complex globular structures, some of which function like enzymes or form functional complexes with proteins.

faculty.name: Eva Nogales
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Our lab is dedicated to gaining mechanistic insight into crucial molecular processes in the life of the eukaryotic cell.

faculty.name: Susan Marqusee
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: The long-term goal of our research is to understand the structural and dynamic information encoded in the linear sequence of amino acids. Proteins undergo an incredible transformation from one-dimensional sequence information into complex three-dimensional shapes that carry out intricate cellular functions.

faculty.name: James Hurley
faculty.title: Professor; Kirsch Springer Chair in Biological Sciences, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: The interplay between proteins and membrane lipids is central to almost every aspect of cell biology.

faculty.name: Jay Groves
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Living cells are not at all well-mixed reaction chambers. Rather, the molecular processes of life occur in dynamic spatial patterns and often operate far from equilibrium.

faculty.name: Daniel Fletcher
faculty.title: Professor; Purnendu Chatterjee Chair in Engineering Biological Systems, Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Daniel Fletcher joined the bioengineering faculty in 2002 and advanced from Associate Professor to Professor in mid 2010. He is also currently serving as Vice Chair for Bioengineering. His research interests include optical and force microscopy, microfabrication, mechanical properties of cells.

faculty.name: Ehud Isacoff
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Ehud (Udi) Isacoff is a neuroscientist and biophysicist whose research probes the molecular and cellular basis of brain function, with a particular focus on synaptic signaling, sensory perception, and circuit dynamics.

faculty.name: Teresa Head-Gordon
faculty.title: University Endowed Chair in Computational Science, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Teresa Head-Gordon is a theoretical and computational chemist and biophysicist whose research develops and applies molecular modeling techniques to understand water structure, protein dynamics, and biomolecular interactions.

faculty.name: Ke Xu
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Professor Xu and his research group develop advanced microscopy and spectroscopy tools to interrogate biological, chemical, and materials systems at the nanoscale with extraordinary resolution, sensitivity, and functionality.

faculty.name: Jamie Cate
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: The Cate Lab explores how genes are put into action by translation. Translation is the universal process of protein synthesis, in which the ribosome translates the four-letter genetic code in messenger RNA into the twenty-letter code of proteins.

faculty.name: Sanjay Kumar
faculty.title: E. H. and Mary E. Pardee Professor; Director, California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences at UC Berkeley, Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Sanjay Kumar, M.D., Ph.D., is a leading figure in bioengineering whose research focuses on interactions between cells and biomaterials.

faculty.name: Stephen Brohawn
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Sensation of environmental stimuli, thought, learning, memory, and other aspects of neuronal communication, hormone secretion and movement all rely on cellular electrical signals. The Brohawn Lab studies life’s electrical system from a molecular and biophysical perspective.

faculty.name: Hernan Garcia
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Hernan Garcia is an associate professor in the the Department of Molecular & Cell Biology, and the Department of Physics.

faculty.name: Aaron Streets
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Lester John and Lynne Dewar Lloyd Distinguished Professor in the College of Engineering, Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: The Streets lab develops hardware, software, and molecular tools to study how cells interpret their genome.

faculty.name: Markita Landry
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering
faculty.summary: Markita del Carpio Landry is a physicist, neuroscientist, and plant biotechnologist whose research combines nanotechnology, imaging, and neurobiology. She is best known for developing nanosensors that monitor neurotransmitter dynamics in the brain, providing new tools to study dopamine and serotonin in real time.

faculty.name: Nicholas Ingolia
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Nicholas Ingolia is a Professor in the Department of Molecular & Cell Biology.

faculty.name: Xavier Darzacq
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Genetics, Genomics and Development, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Life is motion and biological processes are inherently dynamic. When viewed under a microscope, living cells move, change shape, grow and divide.

faculty.name: Eunyong Park
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Eunyong Park is an associate professor in the Department of Molecular & Cell Biology. His research group studies the biogenesis and homeostasis of intracellular organelles, such as endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria.

faculty.name: Evan Miller
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Research in the Miller lab operates at the interface of molecular and cell biology, synthetic chemistry, and neuroscience. They seek to exploit expertise in synthetic chemistry, probe design, imaging, molecular biology, and electrophysiology to create and deploy molecular tools for mapping brain activity.

faculty.name: Karthik Shekhar
faculty.title: John F. Heil Junior Assistant Professor, Dept of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering
faculty.summary: Karthik Shekhar is a chemical engineer and computational biologist whose research is at the interface of neuroscience and biophysics. He is best known for developing single-cell transcriptomic methods to map cellular heterogeneity in complex tissues, including the brain and retina. Current projects are focused on two broad themes.

faculty.name: Bronwyn Lucas
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Bronwyn Lucas is an assistant professor of biochemistry, biophysics and structural biology in the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology.

faculty.name: Margaux Pinney
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Margaux Pinney is a biochemist whose research harnesses and refines high-throughput enzymology technologies to probe fundamental questions about protein function.

faculty.name: Robert Saxton
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Robert Saxton is an Assistant Professor of Molecular and Cell Biology and Chemistry studying molecular mechanisms of immune cell signaling in the context of tissue inflammation and repair.

faculty.name: Ahmad Omar
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Materials Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: Ahmad Omar is an assistant professor in the Department of Material Science and Engineering. The Omar Group's research aims to advance our theoretical understanding of both natural and synthetic soft condensed matter systems.

faculty.name: Ting Xu
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Researches in Xu's group take advantage of the recent developments in de novo protein design and peptidomimetics, polymer science and nanoparticles synthesis and manipulation, and use designed peptides and proteins in concert with the self-assembly of block copolymers, conjugated molecule and nanoparticles as platforms to generate...

faculty.name: Yvette Fisher
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Yvette Fisher is an assistant professor of Neurobiology. The goal of her research is to use navigational circuitry to understand how neural circuits perform different computations under different conditions. Her research group explores this question in the fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster.

faculty.name: Jun-Chau Chien
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Division of Electrical Engineering (EECS)
faculty.summary: Jun-Chau Chien is an Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. His research focuses on analog/mixed-signal integrated circuits, bioelectronics, and RF/mmWave high-speed ICs.

faculty.name: Charles Whittaker
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, School of Public Health
faculty.summary: Charles Whittaker is an Assistant Professor of Infectious Diseases and Vaccinology at UC Berkeley who uses advanced analytical approaches to study the transmission dynamics and control of pathogens with pandemic potential.

faculty.name: Max Staller
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: The Staller Lab combines experiments, computation and theory to study gene regulation. The group is initially focused on how transcription factors activate gene expression in yeast and human cells. They use high throughput methods and machine learning to study the relationship between protein sequence and function.

faculty.name: Ashley Wolf
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, School of Public Health
faculty.summary: Ashley Wolf is an Assistant Professor of Infectious Diseases and Vaccinology at the School of Public Health with a joint appointment in the Center for Computational Biology.

faculty.name: Greg Tikhomirov
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Division of Computer Science (EECS)
faculty.summary: Greg Tikhomirov is an assistant professor in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences, with a background in chemistry, bioengineering, medicine, and nanotechnology.

faculty.name: Holger Müller
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Physics
faculty.summary: Precision measurements using lasers and cold atoms, as well as using ultra-intense continuous-wave lasers to develop new molecular traps and contrast enhancement in transmission electron microscopy.

faculty.name: David Limmer
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: David Limmer is a Professor in the Department of Chemistry at University of California Berkeley, a Research Scientist in the Materials and Chemical Sciences Divisions of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and a Fellow of the Kavli Energy NanoSciences Institute. From 2016-2018 he held the Chevron Chair in Chemistry at UC Berkeley.

faculty.name: Gary Karpen
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Gary Karpen is a professor of Cell and Developmental Physiology in the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology, and a Senior Scientist at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

faculty.name: Rachel Brem
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Plant and Microbial Biology
faculty.summary: Over the four billion years that life has evolved on this planet, organisms have acquired amazing phenotypes. Some, like the spots on a butterfly wing, might capture our attention by their sheer beauty. Others get us excited in a very different way—by their translational relevance.

faculty.name: Derfogail Delcassian
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Derfogail Delcassian is an assistant professor in the Department of Bioengineering. She brings a new research area to the Bioengineering Department– precisely designed chemical tools in combination with 3D printing and materials– to controllably deliver signals which direct immune cell behavior.

faculty.name: Michael Yartsev
faculty.title: Associate Professor , Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Michael Yartsev is a Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) investigator and associate professor in the Departments of Bioengineering and Neuroscience. His lab seeks to understand the neural basis of natural spatial, social and acoustic behaviors in mammals.

faculty.name: Frederic Theunissen
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Integrative Biology
faculty.summary: The long-term goal of our research is to understand the neural mechanisms underlying the recognition of complex sounds such as speech or animal communications.

faculty.name: Ian Swinburne
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: The Swinburne Lab studies how tissues, cells, and subcellular dynamics coordinate to generate organs and initiate physiologies. The lab’s current goal is to understand the mechanisms of hydraulic control within vertebrate organs.

faculty.name: Peter Sudmant
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Integrative Biology
faculty.summary: The Sudmant Lab uses computational, statistical, and experimental methods to interrogate genetic and molecular phenotypic diversity at both the organismal and cellular level. Our lab studies the evolution of aging, and the evolution of genome structure.

faculty.name: Kranthi Mandadapu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering
faculty.summary: Kranthi K. Mandadapu is an associate professor and a theorist in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (College of Chemistry) at UC Berkeley. His lab is broadly interested in understanding the physical behaviors of systems at multiple length and time scales.

faculty.name: Richard Kramer
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Neuroscience

faculty.name: Na Ji
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Na Ji develops next-generation optical microscopy methods for understanding the brain at higher resolution, greater depth, and faster time scales.

faculty.name: Jack Gallant
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Jack Gallant is a cognitive neuroscientist whose research investigates how the brain represents and processes naturalistic information. He is best known for developing computational models that decode brain activity to reveal how sensory and cognitive information is encoded in the cerbral cortex.

faculty.name: Marla Feller
faculty.title: Paul Licht Distinguished Professor in Biological Sciences, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology

faculty.name: Daniel Feldman
faculty.title: Professor; Coates Family Endowed Chair in Neuroscience, Dept of Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Dan Feldman is a neuroscientist whose research focuses on sensory processing, synaptic plasticity, and neural circuit function in cerebral cortex.

faculty.name: Michael DeWeese
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Michael DeWeese is a professor in the Department of Physics and the Department of Neuroscience. His group’s research spans three broad areas: nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, machine learning theory, and systems neuroscience.

faculty.name: Eric Betzig
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Eric Betzig is a Professor of Molecular and Cell biology, a Senior Fellow at the Janelia Research Campus, and an Investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute at the University of California, Berkeley. His Ph.D.

faculty.name: Hillel Adesnik
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Hillel Adesnik is a neuroscientist whose research focuses on sensory processing, cortical circuits, and neural computation. He investigates how ensembles of neurons in the brain’s cortex encode perception and integrate sensory information.

faculty.name: Roberto Zoncu
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Roberto Zoncu is a Professor in the Molecular Therapeutics Division of the Department of Molecular & Cell Biology. His research focuses on the following questions.

faculty.name: Denis Titov
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: The Denis Titov lab uses computational and experimental approaches to work on quantitative understanding of human metabolic pathway regulation and deciphering the molecular basis of again.

faculty.name: David Savage
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Dave is a Professor in the Department of Molecular & Cell Biology at the University of California, Berkeley and an Investigator in the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. Dave was born and raised in rural Iowa. He continues to help manage his family’s farm, which was recognized in 2010 as an Iowa Heritage Farm.

faculty.name: Dan Rokhsar
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: My research is focused on understanding the origin, evolution, and diversity of animals (and, more generally, other groups of eukaryotes) by combining computational genome analysis with comparative developmental biology

faculty.name: Richard Mathies
faculty.title: Professor of the Graduate School, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Richard Mathies has developed a variety of modern laser-based spectroscopic techniques to study excited-state reaction dynamics in photoactive proteins and to develop novel microfabricated chemical and biochemical analysis devices for terrestrial and extra-terrestrial applications.

faculty.name: Priya Moorjani
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Priya Moorjani is an assistant professor in the Department of Molecular & Cell Biology. Her lab focuses on using statistical and computational approaches to study questions in human genetics and evolutionary biology.

faculty.name: Barbara Meyer
faculty.title: Professor; HHMI Investigator, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Barbara Meyer is a professor in the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology.

faculty.name: Evan Williams
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Professor Williams' research group is developing and applying novel instrumental and computational techniques in mass spectrometry, tandem mass spectrometry, separations, and laser spectroscopy to solve problems of fundamental interest in chemistry and biochemistry.

faculty.name: Andreas Martin
faculty.title: Professor; HHMI Investigator, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology
faculty.summary: Andy Martin is a Howard Hughes Medical Institute Investigator and Professor of Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology. His research interests:

faculty.name: Steven Brenner
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: The Brenner research lab has four key research interests involving computational and experimental genomics. Gene regulation by alternative splicing and nonsense-mediated mRNA decay.

faculty.name: Oskar Hallatschek
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Dept of Physics
faculty.summary: The complexity of the biological world demonstrates that chance can produce powerful results since evolution is ultimately driven by random mutational events.

faculty.name: Michael Eisen
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology

faculty.name: Mohammad Mofrad
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Prof. Mohammad Reza Kaazempur Mofrad is a Professor of Bioengineering and Mechanical Engineering at UC Berkeley, where he leads a multidisciplinary research program at the interface of biomechanics, mechanobiology, artificial intelligence, and computational biology.

faculty.name: David Drubin
faculty.title: Professor; Ernette Comby Chair in Microbiology, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology

faculty.name: Abby Dernburg
faculty.title: Professor, Dept of Molecular & Cell Biology

faculty.name: Sandrine Dudoit
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Alan Hubbard
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Xiudi Li

faculty.name: Mark van der Laan
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: Jingshen Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Laura Balzer

faculty.name: Alejandro Schuler

faculty.name: Evan A. Variano

faculty.title: Professor and Chair, Environmental Health Sciences Division
faculty.summary: Uses statistical and mathematical modeling to study how infectious diseases such as West Nile virus, TB, and schistosomiasis spread in response to urbanization, climate change, and shifting water resources.

faculty.name: Joshua Apte
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Investigates human exposure to air pollution from neighborhood to global scales, including how historical policies such as redlining drive disparities in air quality exposure.

faculty.name: Rachel Morello-Frosch
faculty.title: Professor, Environmental Health Sciences; Community Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Examines the social determinants of environmental health disparities and how inequality and psychosocial stress interact with chemical exposures, often using community-based participatory research.

faculty.name: Ellen Eisen
faculty.title: Professor in Residence, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Applies biostatistical and epidemiological methods to occupational and environmental health, addressing healthy worker survivor bias and workplace contributions to chronic disease.

faculty.name: Jay Graham
faculty.title: Associate Professor in Residence, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Applies epidemiologic methods and DNA sequencing to understand antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic infectious disease transmission across global regions.

faculty.name: Laura Kwong
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Studies environmental contamination and infectious disease exposure affecting child and maternal health in low-income countries, developing and evaluating engineering interventions through randomized controlled trials.

faculty.name: Ajay Pillarisetti
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Investigates how household energy consumption affects air pollution exposure, human health, and climate change, with a focus on low- and middle-income countries.

faculty.name: David J.X. González
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Studies how pollution from extractive industries and climate-driven disasters affects public health, using population-level data and community-engaged methods to address health disparities.

faculty.name: Misbath Daouda
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Examines the distribution of health benefits from energy transitions in the context of climate change in the US and West Africa using environmental epidemiology and exposure modeling.

faculty.name: Rosemarie de la Rosa
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Studies how social and environmental factors in childhood become biologically embedded and affect susceptibility to pollutant exposures, including combined effects of psychosocial stress and air pollution.

faculty.name: Bambarendage Pinithi Upekka Perera
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Studies how environmental toxicants alter the epigenome during critical developmental stages, integrating molecular biology and toxicology to examine maternal-fetal interactions and sex-specific epigenetic regulation.

faculty.name: Carly Hyland
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Cooperative Extension, Environmental Health Sciences
faculty.summary: Investigates how climate change affects agricultural and food systems workers through interconnected exposures like heat, wildfire smoke, and pesticides, using community-engaged and mixed methods.

faculty.name: David Ackerly
faculty.title: Dean of Rausser College of Natural Resources and Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates climate change effects on California biodiversity, including distribution modeling, long-term vegetation dynamics, drought tolerance of native trees, and post-fire forest dynamics.

faculty.name: Justin Brashares
faculty.title: Professor and G.R. & W.M. Goertz Chair
faculty.summary: Studies how wildlife consumption and habitat conversion affect animal communities and population persistence, integrating ecology with economic, political, and cultural factors for conservation.

faculty.name: Carl Boettiger
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on ecological forecasting and decision-making under uncertainty for conservation and natural resource management, especially in systems prone to sudden regime shifts.

faculty.name: Timothy Bowles
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates soil health, climate resilience, and sustainable farming systems, examining how biodiversity-based agroecological approaches affect soil and climate adaptation.

faculty.name: Benjamin Blonder
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies plant responses to climate change through forest ecophysiological and genetic analyses, community assembly theory, and responses to heatwaves across temporal scales.

faculty.name: Stephanie Carlson
faculty.title: Professor and A.S. Leopold Chair in Wildlife Biology
faculty.summary: Studies the evolutionary ecology and conservation of freshwater fishes, focusing on the dynamics of California's inland fishes and factors shaping their persistence.

faculty.name: Todd Dawson
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how plants interact with their environments using physiological plant ecology, stable isotope biogeochemistry, and ecohydrology, emphasizing woody plants and forest systems.

faculty.name: Iryna Dronova
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses remote sensing and spatial analysis to study ecosystem and landscape ecology, with emphasis on wetland biodiversity, phenological patterns, and urban green spaces.

faculty.name: Alejandra Echeverri
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Conservation Science
faculty.summary: Investigates how human behaviors such as habitat conversion affect wildlife, combining ornithological fieldwork with social science to advance biocultural conservation in the Neotropics.

faculty.name: Trevor Keenan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how terrestrial ecosystems respond to climate change and variability, focusing on carbon cycling, water use, and atmosphere feedbacks using large datasets, models, and field studies.

faculty.name: Céline Pallud
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Examines the transport and fate of chemical species in soils and sediments, emphasizing microbial processes affecting contaminant mobility using field, laboratory, and modeling approaches.

faculty.name: Albert Ruhi
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates how freshwater ecosystems respond to global change, particularly hydrologic alteration and drought, studying community dynamics, biodiversity, and regime shifts in river food webs.

faculty.name: Christopher Schell
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how urban carnivores such as coyotes and foxes adapt to city life, integrating behavioral and physiological approaches with research on how systemic racism shapes urban ecosystems.

faculty.name: Whendee Silver
faculty.title: Professor of Ecosystem Ecology and Biogeochemistry
faculty.summary: Studies how climate change and human activities affect biogeochemical cycling, focusing on carbon sequestration in grasslands, peatlands, and tropical forests, including the Marin Carbon Project.

faculty.name: Scott Stephens
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies wildland fire's interactions with ecosystems, including prehistoric fire regimes, current impacts, fire policy, and Indigenous-led ecosystem stewardship under climate change.

faculty.name: Lucas Vargas Zeppetello
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates land-atmosphere interactions, climate variability, and ecosystem responses to climate change.

faculty.name: Ian Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how environmental variation drives genetic, phenotypic, and ecological diversity across space and time through landscape genomics and evolutionary biology.

faculty.name: Manuela Girotto
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies hydrologic response and human-natural process interactions using land surface remote sensing and data assimilation, including snow hydrology and hydrology's contribution to sea-level change.

faculty.sub_field: Agricultural Water Management / Land, Air and Water Resources
faculty.summary: Cooperative Extension Associate Professor in Land, Air and Water Resources; Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group faculty member working in agricultural water management.

faculty.name: Laura Foglia
faculty.title: Associate Adjunct Professor
faculty.sub_field: Groundwater Modeling / Land, Air and Water Resources
faculty.summary: Associate Adjunct Professor in Land, Air and Water Resources; Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group faculty member working in groundwater modeling and water resources management.

faculty.name: Cristina Lazcano
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Soil Ecology
faculty.sub_field: Soil Ecology / Land, Air and Water Resources
faculty.summary: Associate Professor in Land, Air and Water Resources; Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group faculty member working in soil ecology.

faculty.name: Troy Magney
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor in Plant Sciences; Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group faculty member working in remote sensing of vegetation and carbon flux.

faculty.name: Brett A. Poulin
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Environmental Chemistry / Land, Air and Water Resources
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor in Land, Air and Water Resources; Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group faculty member working in aquatic environmental chemistry.

faculty.name: Sarah Yarnell
faculty.title: Associate Professional Researcher
faculty.sub_field: Watershed Hydrology and Ecology / Land, Air and Water Resources
faculty.summary: Associate Professional Researcher at the Center for Watershed Sciences; Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group faculty member working in watershed hydrology and river ecology.

faculty.name: Nael El-Farra
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Process control, systems engineering, biomedical systems
faculty.summary: Research in process systems engineering and control, with applications to biomedical systems, energy systems, and manufacturing. Focuses on distributed and networked control of complex systems.

faculty.name: Heather Bischel
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on environmental health engineering and water sustainability. Studies water and wastewater treatment for emerging contaminants, PFAS bioaccumulation, rapid virus detection, and resource-oriented sanitation. Led UC Davis wastewater-based SARS-CoV-2 epidemiology monitoring during COVID-19.

faculty.name: Christopher Cappa
faculty.title: Professor and Vice Chair
faculty.summary: Research on atmospheric aerosols and air quality, investigating the physical, chemical, and optical properties of particulate matter. Studies how aerosols influence climate and develops improved representations of aerosol processes in climate models.

faculty.name: Anthony S. Wexler
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Leading researcher on air pollution aerosols and atmospheric chemistry. Studies the formation and evolution of particulate matter in urban environments, the chemical mechanisms of smog formation, and the human health effects of airborne particles.

faculty.name: Michael J. Kleeman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on urban and regional air quality, focusing on the characterization, modeling, and source apportionment of atmospheric aerosols. Studies how emissions from different sources contribute to particulate matter pollution and associated health impacts.

faculty.name: Frank J. Loge
faculty.title: Professor; Director, Center for Water-Energy Efficiency
faculty.summary: Research on water-energy efficiency and sustainable systems, studying water reuse technologies, urban and agricultural water demand management, and data-driven optimization of water distribution systems. NSF CAREER Award recipient.

faculty.name: Thomas M. Young
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on environmental chemistry applied to water quality and contaminated site remediation. Studies the fate and transport of organic pollutants in environmental systems, with focus on sorption processes and the development of remediation technologies.

faculty.name: Jeannie L. Darby
faculty.title: Professor and Vice Chair
faculty.summary: Research on water and wastewater treatment processes, focusing on disinfection technologies and the removal of inorganic contaminants including arsenic and chromium from drinking water supplies.

faculty.name: Maureen Kinyua
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on biological wastewater treatment and resource recovery, with emphasis on anaerobic digestion and waste-to-energy technologies. Applies engineering approaches to improve sanitation and energy access in developing communities.

faculty.name: Fabian Bombardelli
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on environmental fluid mechanics and multiphase flow, developing computational models for turbulent flows, sediment transport, and bubble plumes. Applications include reservoir oxygenation, river restoration, and coastal engineering.

faculty.name: Jonathan Herman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on water resources planning and management under uncertainty. Develops multi-objective optimization and decision support frameworks to help water agencies adapt to climate change, manage reservoir operations, and balance competing water demands.

faculty.name: Holly Oldroyd
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on environmental fluid dynamics at the land-water-atmosphere interface. Studies turbulent transport processes in lakes, reservoirs, and coastal waters, and their interactions with atmospheric boundary layer dynamics.

faculty.name: Jason T. DeJong
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneer in biogeotechnical engineering, developing biologically-mediated soil improvement methods such as microbial-induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) for ground improvement, liquefaction mitigation, and erosion control. Also advances in-situ site characterization methods.

faculty.name: Ross W. Boulanger
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Internationally recognized expert in geotechnical earthquake engineering. Research focuses on liquefaction assessment, seismic soil-structure interaction, and ground improvement methods. His work has significantly influenced professional practice codes worldwide.

faculty.name: Katerina Ziotopoulou
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on geotechnical earthquake engineering, developing advanced constitutive models and numerical methods for simulating soil behavior during seismic loading, with focus on liquefaction and cyclic soil response.

faculty.name: Amit Kanvinde
faculty.title: Professor and Department Chair
faculty.summary: Research on the seismic performance and design of steel structures, focusing on fracture and fatigue at extreme limit states. His work on column base connections and steel brace behavior has been incorporated into national design specifications (AISC). Recipient of the ASCE Norman Medal.

faculty.name: Michele Barbato
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on nonlinear structural analysis and dynamics, structural reliability under multiple natural hazards, climate adaptation of infrastructure, and sustainable construction materials including earth-block and bio-based building materials.

faculty.name: John E. Bolander
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on high-performance cement-based materials for civil infrastructure, including fiber-reinforced cement composites, durability assessment, structural health monitoring, and computational modeling of material behavior.

faculty.name: Alejandro Martinez
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on geotechnical engineering including bio-inspired approaches to soil-structure interface design, deep foundation systems, and innovative site characterization methods. Studies geomaterial behavior at multiple scales.

faculty.name: Alissa Kendall
faculty.title: Professor; Director, Institute of Transportation Studies
faculty.summary: Research on life cycle assessment and industrial ecology applied to transportation, energy, and infrastructure systems. Studies the environmental impacts of electric vehicles, bioenergy pathways, and sustainable materials for infrastructure.

faculty.name: Miguel A. Jaller
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on sustainable urban freight systems, city logistics, and humanitarian logistics. Studies the impacts of e-commerce on transportation systems and develops strategies for reducing freight-related emissions and congestion in urban areas.

faculty.name: Kari Edison Watkins
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on sustainable transportation systems, focusing on public transit, bicycling, and pedestrian infrastructure. Studies how technology and information can improve transit accessibility and promote active transportation modes.

faculty.name: Sabbie Miller
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on sustainable infrastructure materials and the built environment. Assesses the environmental impacts of construction materials using life cycle methods, and develops low-carbon alternatives including bio-derived and polymeric materials for infrastructure.

faculty.name: Yueyue Fan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on network optimization and stochastic modeling applied to transportation and infrastructure systems. Develops methods for planning and managing networks under uncertainty, with focus on resilience to disruptions and natural hazards.

faculty.name: Sashi K. Kunnath
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research on structural engineering and earthquake engineering, focusing on nonlinear modeling of reinforced concrete and steel structures under extreme loading, progressive collapse analysis, and performance-based seismic design.

faculty.name: Vladimir Yarov-Yarovoy
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computational Structural Biology / Ion Channel Biophysics
faculty.summary: Develops computational methods (Rosetta-Membrane) for membrane protein structure prediction and design, focusing on voltage-gated ion channels (Nav, Cav, Kv). Designs subtype-specific ion channel modulators for chronic pain and epilepsy treatment.

faculty.name: Eleonora Grandi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops biophysically detailed computational models of cardiac electrophysiology, ion transport, and signaling to understand mechanisms of heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and hypertension. Chair of the Biophysics Graduate Group.

faculty.name: Jon Sack
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates voltage-gated potassium (Kv) and sodium (Nav) channels, developing novel fluorescent probes and toxin-based tools to visualize and manipulate ion channel activity. Studies Kv2/KvS heteromers and their roles in neuronal signaling.

faculty.name: John Voss
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to study protein misfolding and aggregation in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's. Develops spin-labeled compounds that disrupt amyloid-beta aggregation and novel metal-free MRI contrast agents.

faculty.name: Sanjeevi Sivasankar
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies cell-cell adhesion at the single-molecule level using atomic force microscopy (AFM), focusing on cadherin proteins critical for tissue integrity. Investigates how mechanical forces regulate cadherin adhesion, with implications for cancer metastasis.

faculty.name: Tonya Kuhl
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Colloidal and Interface Science / Membrane Biophysics
faculty.summary: Studies biological membrane interactions, colloidal self-assembly, and complex fluids using high-resolution surface force measurements. Investigates lipid raft stability, membrane phase behavior, and targeted drug delivery systems. Chair of Chemical Engineering.

faculty.name: Atul N. Parikh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates membrane biophysics and bioengineering, studying lipid phase separation, membrane remodeling under osmotic stress, and synthetic cell construction using giant vesicles. Develops phospholipid-based materials for biosensing and drug delivery.

faculty.name: Justin Siegel
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Combines computational tools (Rosetta Molecular Modeling Suite) with experimental validation to design novel enzymes, including those catalyzing reactions not found in nature. Develops therapeutic enzymes for celiac disease and applies AI-driven protein engineering for industrial applications.

faculty.name: Cheemeng Tan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Engineers artificial cellular systems and synthetic cells for biosensors, drug delivery, and understanding biological principles. Develops platforms like VESSEL for engineering extracellular vesicle surface proteins and cyborg cells that are non-replicating but metabolically active.

faculty.name: R. Holland Cheng
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses cryo-electron microscopy and tomography to study macromolecular structure and function, with focus on virus assembly and infection mechanisms. Develops protein-based capsids for precision nanomedicine and mucosal delivery of CRISPR gene-editing tools.

faculty.name: Alexei A. Stuchebrukhov
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical and computational methods for biological electron and proton transfer, including the foundational Tunneling Currents method. Studies the electron transport chain, redox-driven proton pumps in Complex I and cytochrome c oxidase, and proton migration along membranes.

faculty.name: Patrice Koehl
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops computational methods at the interface of computer science, biophysics, and structural biology, including algorithms for protein shape analysis, solvation thermodynamics, and conformational transition path computation (MinActionPath). Models biomolecular electrostatics and solvation for drug design.

faculty.name: Enoch P. Baldwin
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies protein-nucleic acid interactions using X-ray crystallography and biochemistry. Investigates CTP synthetase filament formation as a novel regulatory mechanism relevant to anti-cancer drug development, and engineers TALE DNA-binding proteins for programmable DNA recognition.

faculty.name: Jawdat Al-Bassam
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies microtubule cytoskeleton structure and dynamics using cryo-electron microscopy. Mapped the structure and mechanism of tubulin cofactor complexes linked to rare childhood brain disorders (chaperone tubulinopathies), and investigates augmin-mediated microtubule branching and kinesin motor regulation.

faculty.name: Richard J. McKenney
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies molecular motor proteins (kinesins and dyneins) that transport cargo along microtubules, using single-molecule TIRF microscopy and biochemistry. Investigates how motor dysfunction leads to neurodegeneration and cancer, with focus on KIF1A-linked pediatric disorders.

faculty.name: Igor Vorobyov
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods to study drug interactions with ion channels and membrane proteins. Leads multi-scale modeling efforts linking atomistic simulations to cardiac cell/tissue models for predicting drug-induced arrhythmia risk.

faculty.name: Stefano Morotti
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops biophysically detailed mathematical models of cardiac and vascular myocyte electrophysiology and calcium signaling. Investigates mechanisms of heart failure and atrial fibrillation, with focus on sex-specific arrhythmia mechanisms and cross-species translational models.

faculty.name: Daisuke Sato
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies mechanisms of cardiac arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death using multiscale modeling and nonlinear dynamics. Investigates calcium cycling in cardiac myocytes, ryanodine receptor dynamics, and mechano-chemo-transduction coupling leading to arrhythmia.

faculty.name: Alla F. Fomina
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates calcium signaling and membrane trafficking in immune cells and neuroendocrine cells. Studies CRAC channels and store-operated calcium entry in T lymphocyte activation, and mechanisms of exocytosis and endocytosis in chromaffin cells.

faculty.name: Jill L. Silverman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses rodent model systems for translational research on neurodevelopmental disorders including Angelman syndrome, autism, and pediatric epilepsy. Pioneered stem cell gene therapy approaches to reverse Angelman syndrome phenotypes, integrating behavioral phenotyping with in vivo electrophysiology.

faculty.name: Leonor Saiz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Integrates computational biophysics, systems biology, and machine learning to study gene regulation and signal transduction networks. Models protein-DNA interactions, DNA looping, and stochastic dynamics of macromolecular assemblies using multiscale approaches from atomistic MD to cellular behavior.

faculty.name: Surl-Hee (Shirley) Ahn
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops and applies enhanced sampling molecular dynamics methods (weighted ensemble) as a computational microscope to study protein dynamics at atomic resolution. Investigates drug-target interactions for pain therapy and proteins implicated in Parkinson's disease.

faculty.name: Jennifer Cash
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structural biology and regulation of Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factors (RhoGEFs) such as P-Rex1/2, which are implicated in cancer metastasis. Uses cryo-EM, X-ray crystallography, and HDX-MS to understand RhoGEF activation and identify small-molecule inhibitors.

faculty.name: R. Jayakrishnan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying transportation systems, traffic network modeling, and intelligent transportation systems.

faculty.name: Wenlong Jin
faculty.title: Professor

faculty.title: Associate Professor

faculty.name: Christopher Olivares Martinez

faculty.name: Diego Rosso
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying wastewater treatment processes, aeration, and the water-energy nexus in water resource recovery.

faculty.name: Brett Sanders

faculty.summary: Chancellor's Professor studying flood inundation modeling, hydraulics, and coastal and urban flood hazards.

faculty.name: Jean-Daniel Saphores
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying transportation and environmental economics, policy, and sustainable urban systems.

faculty.name: Soroosh Sorooshian
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor and Samueli Endowed Chair
faculty.summary: Distinguished Professor studying hydrology, hydrometeorology, and satellite-based precipitation estimation and hydrologic modeling.

faculty.name: Lizhi Sun
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying mechanics of materials, composites, and structural sensing and damage detection.

faculty.name: Jasper Vrugt
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying hydrologic modeling, uncertainty quantification, and computational optimization methods.

faculty.name: Farzin Zareian
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor studying earthquake engineering, performance-based seismic design, and structural risk assessment.

faculty.name: Syed Jafar
faculty.title: Chancellor's Professor
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in network information theory. Known for seminal contributions to interference alignment and degrees of freedom in wireless networks. IEEE Information Theory Society Paper Award recipient.

faculty.name: Hamid Jafarkhani
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneer in space-time coding for multi-antenna wireless communications. Known for super-orthogonal space-time trellis codes and contributions to MIMO communication theory.

faculty.name: A. Lee Swindlehurst
faculty.title: Professor (Nicolaos G. and Sue Curtis Alexopoulos Presidential Chair, Department Chair)
faculty.summary: Department Chair. Research in signal processing for wireless communications, array processing, and MIMO radar systems. Known for contributions to signal processing for multiple-antenna systems.

faculty.name: Payam Heydari
faculty.title: Chancellor's Professor (Henry Samueli Faculty Excellence Professor)
faculty.summary: Research in high-frequency integrated circuit design for communication and sensing applications. Focus on silicon-based mm-wave and terahertz circuits and systems.

faculty.name: Jean-Luc Gaudiot
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research in computer architecture and parallel processing. Contributions to multithreaded processors, dataflow architectures, and instruction-level parallelism. IEEE Fellow and former Computer Society president.

faculty.name: Fadi Kurdahi
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research in VLSI system design and design automation. Focus on system-on-chip architectures, embedded and cyber-physical systems, and reconfigurable computing. IEEE Fellow.

faculty.name: Nader Bagherzadeh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in computer architecture, parallel processing, and 3D integrated circuit design. Focus on GPU architectures, networks-on-chip, and efficient parallel computing platforms.

faculty.name: Pramod Khargonekar
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in control systems theory. Known for foundational work in robust control and H-infinity control. Recent focus on control and optimization of power grids and renewable energy systems.

faculty.name: Ozdal Boyraz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in integrated photonics and optical communications. Focus on silicon photonic devices, optical interconnects, and nonlinear optical signal processing for communications and sensing.

faculty.name: Peter Burke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in nanoelectronic devices and their biomedical applications. Focus on carbon nanotube and graphene electronics for sensing and biomedical diagnostics.

faculty.name: Mohammad Al Faruque
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Director of the Center for Resilient Autonomous Systems. Research in cyber-physical systems and IoT with applications to smart grid, autonomous vehicles, and Industry 4.0.

faculty.name: Filippo Capolino
faculty.title: Dean's Professor
faculty.summary: Research in electromagnetics and photonics, including metamaterials, plasmonics, and antenna design. Focus on engineered electromagnetic structures for communications, sensing, and energy.

faculty.name: Aparna Chandramowlishwaran
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in high-performance computing and parallel algorithms for scientific computing applications. Focus on optimizing computational workflows for modern heterogeneous architectures.

faculty.name: Hung Cao
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) for biomedical applications. Focus on implantable sensors, wearable health monitoring devices, and wireless biomedical systems.

faculty.name: Yanning Shen
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Network Science
faculty.summary: Research in machine learning and statistical signal processing for network data. Focus on graph-based learning, high-dimensional statistics, and applications to neuroscience and social networks.

faculty.name: Yasser Shoukry
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in security and resilience of cyber-physical and autonomous systems. Focus on formal methods for detection and mitigation of attacks on autonomous vehicles and industrial control systems.

faculty.name: Marco Levorato
faculty.title: Professor (Joint CS and EECS)
faculty.summary: Research in wireless communications, edge computing, and machine learning for networked systems. Focus on AI-driven optimization of distributed IoT and edge systems.

faculty.name: Boris Vaisband
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research in VLSI circuits and systems. Focus on power delivery and clock distribution in 3D integrated systems and heterogeneous integration for high-performance computing.

faculty.name: Zhiying Wang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in coding theory and information theory. Contributions to coding for distributed storage systems, flash memories, and emerging storage technologies including DNA data storage.

faculty.name: Athina Markopoulou
faculty.title: Professor (EECS, CS)
faculty.summary: Director of the ProperData Center for data transparency and privacy. Research in network measurement, online privacy, and applying data science to understand network behavior.
