faculty.name: Neville Bethel
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on the de novo design of protein motion, engineering proteins with defined conformational dynamics.

faculty.name: Itay Budin
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the biochemistry and synthetic biology of cell membranes.

faculty.name: Michael Burkart
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans natural product synthesis and biosynthesis, biological chemistry and enzymology, and metabolic engineering.

faculty.name: Galia Debelouchina
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses NMR spectroscopy and chemical biology to study structural biology problems in aging and gene regulation.

faculty.name: Lalit Deshmukh
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Applies solution NMR spectroscopy to study amyloids, neurodegenerative diseases, post-translational modifications, and viruses.

faculty.name: Neal Devaraj
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Presidential Chair in Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics; research in biomimetic chemistry, artificial cells, and chemical biology.

faculty.name: Gourisankar Ghosh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Biochemistry and biophysics of transcription, signaling, pre-mRNA splicing, and mRNA transport.

faculty.name: Partho Ghosh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies mechanisms of bacterial and protozoan pathogenesis and the host response against infectious microbes.

faculty.name: Kamil Godula
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Co-Director of the UCSD Glycobiology Research and Training Center; develops nanotechnologies for analyzing glycan function and glycomaterials for stem cell-based tissue regeneration.

faculty.name: Mark Herzik
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Elucidates the mechanisms of macromolecular transport into and within mitochondria using cryo-EM.

faculty.name: Patricia Jennings
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Biophysical chemistry of protein structure, dynamics, and folding using NMR spectroscopy.

faculty.name: Lisa Jones
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses oxidative labeling and mass spectrometry for the structural characterization of proteins in their native cellular environment.

faculty.name: Simpson Joseph
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the molecular mechanism of protein synthesis.

faculty.name: Judy Kim
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Biophysical chemistry using spectroscopic studies of membrane protein folding and dynamics.

faculty.name: Elizabeth Komives
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure, function, dynamics, and thermodynamics of protein-protein interactions using NMR, mass spectrometry, and kinetics.

faculty.name: Alexis Komor
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Deputy Director of the Sanford Stem Cell Innovation Center; research in genome editing, DNA damage and repair, and functional genomics.

faculty.name: Colleen McHugh
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies RNA-protein interactions, assembly of RNPs, and the structural biology of multimeric complexes.

faculty.name: Tatiana Mishanina
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies transcription and its regulation, including RNA polymerase structure and function in bacteria and human mitochondria.

faculty.name: Ulrich Muller
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the evolution of catalytic RNAs and the origin of life.

faculty.name: Christopher Obara
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research in cellular biochemistry, biophysics, and macromolecular structure; joint appointment in Pharmacology.

faculty.name: Johannes Schoeneberg
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Roger Tsien Chancellor's Faculty Fellow; develops 4D adaptive optics lattice light-sheet imaging, petabyte-scale image processing, and machine learning to study mitochondrial dynamics and organoids.

faculty.name: Susan Taylor
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure, function, dynamics, and localization of PKA as a prototype for the protein kinase superfamily; also Distinguished Professor of Pharmacology.

faculty.name: F. Akif Tezcan
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry
faculty.summary: Works on bioinorganic and biophysical chemistry, protein structure/function/evolution, and biomaterials.

faculty.name: Navtej Toor
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure and function of introns and retroelements.

faculty.name: Brian Zid
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies gene expression control during stress and mRNA localization to membrane-less compartments.

faculty.name: Daniel Donoghue
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies receptor tyrosine kinases in human cancer.

faculty.name: Fleur Ferguson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor jointly appointed in Chemistry and Biochemistry and the Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences; specific research details not stated on the program faculty page.

faculty.name: Alex Guseman
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry; specific research details not stated on the program faculty page.

faculty.name: Christine Hrycyna
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry and Dean of the School of Physical Sciences (joined UCSD in 2023); a biochemist whose work has focused on membrane transport proteins and multidrug resistance.

faculty.name: Adrian Jinich
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Runs a mixed computational and experimental group developing machine-learning methods to predict enzyme function from sequence and uncover uncharacterized enzymes.

faculty.name: Julia Stauber
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research in inorganic synthesis, organometallic synthesis, and bioinorganic chemistry.

faculty.name: Akif Tezcan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in bioinorganic and biophysical chemistry, materials and biomaterials chemistry, and protein structure, function, and evolution.

faculty.name: Wei Wang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in epigenomics, cellular reprogramming, protein recognition, computational biology, and systems biology; also Professor of Cellular and Molecular Medicine.

faculty.name: Jerry Yang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in bioorganic chemistry, molecular self-assembly, molecular synthesis, materials chemistry, and bionanotechnology; joint appointment in Materials Science and Engineering.

faculty.name: Hongbo Zhao
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research in computational soft and living matter and biomolecular condensates; joint appointment in the Department of Physics.

faculty.name: Pavel Pevzner
faculty.title: Professor (Ronald R. Taylor Chair, Program Co-Director)
faculty.summary: Co-Director of the BISB program. Pioneer in computational molecular biology. Foundational work on de novo peptide sequencing, genome assembly algorithms, and computational mass spectrometry.

faculty.name: Terry Gaasterland
faculty.title: Professor (Program Director)
faculty.summary: Program Director of BISB. Research in computational genome analysis, including comparative genomics, transcriptome analysis, and methods for identifying causal genetic variants.

faculty.name: Vineet Bafna
faculty.title: Professor (CSE)
faculty.summary: Research in bioinformatics algorithms with focus on structural variation detection in cancer genomes, circulating tumor DNA analysis, and algorithmic problems in protein mass spectrometry.

faculty.name: Trey Ideker
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneer in biological network analysis. Research on integrating multi-omics data with protein interaction networks to understand disease mechanisms, particularly cancer. Creator of Cytoscape network analysis tools.

faculty.name: Hannah Carter
faculty.title: Professor (Program Associate Director)
faculty.summary: Associate Director of BISB. Research in cancer genomics, developing computational methods for interpreting genetic variants in tumors and understanding their functional impact through network-based approaches.

faculty.name: Jill Mesirov
faculty.title: Professor (Associate Vice Chancellor, Computational Health Sciences)
faculty.summary: Research in computational biology and cancer genomics. Known for developing Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) and influential bioinformatics tools. Focus on integrative analysis of cancer genomic data.

faculty.name: Rob Knight
faculty.title: Professor (Pediatrics, CSE, BioE)
faculty.summary: Leading microbiome researcher. Pioneer in developing computational methods for analyzing microbial communities. Co-founder of the American Gut Project and QIIME bioinformatics platform for microbiome analysis.

faculty.name: Shankar Subramaniam
faculty.title: Professor (Bioengineering, CSE)
faculty.summary: Founder of the Bioinformatics and Systems Biology graduate program. Research in systems biology linking genomics to metabolic and signaling networks, with applications to understanding disease mechanisms.

faculty.name: Bernhard Palsson
faculty.title: Professor (Y.C. Fung Endowed Chair in Bioengineering)
faculty.summary: Pioneer of genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction and constraint-based modeling. Research on computational methods for predicting cellular phenotypes from genome sequences.

faculty.name: Siavash Mirarab
faculty.title: Associate Professor (ECE)
faculty.summary: Research in computational phylogenetics, developing methods for scalable species tree estimation from genomic data. Known for ASTRAL species tree inference method.

faculty.name: Melissa Gymrek
faculty.title: Associate Professor (CS, Medicine)
faculty.summary: Research in computational genomics focusing on the role of short tandem repeats in human phenotypes and disease. Developing algorithms for genotyping and analyzing repetitive genetic variation.

faculty.name: Yatish Turakhia
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (ECE)
faculty.summary: Research on algorithms and hardware accelerators for genome analysis. Known for developing efficient algorithms for large-scale sequence analysis and phylogenomic inference.

faculty.name: Kun Zhang
faculty.title: Professor (Bioengineering)
faculty.summary: Pioneer in single-cell multi-omics technologies. Research on developing methods for analyzing single-cell genome, epigenome, and transcriptome data, with applications to cancer and developmental biology.

faculty.name: Nathan E. Lewis
faculty.title: Professor (Pediatrics)
faculty.summary: Research in systems biology using genome-scale metabolic models integrated with multi-omics data. Focus on understanding cellular metabolism, glycosylation networks, and biomanufacturing optimization.

faculty.name: Nuno Bandeira
faculty.title: Professor (Pharmacy, CSE)
faculty.summary: Research in computational mass spectrometry, developing algorithms and software tools for identifying proteins and their modifications from tandem mass spectrometry data.

faculty.name: Gene Yeo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in RNA biology and genomics, developing computational and experimental methods to study RNA processing and RNA-binding proteins in neurodegeneration and autism.

faculty.name: Ludmil Alexandrov
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on mutational processes in cancer. Known for discovering cancer mutational signatures and developing computational methods to characterize the processes that generate somatic mutations.

faculty.name: Vikas Bansal
faculty.title: Associate Professor (Pediatrics, CSE)
faculty.summary: Research in computational genomics, developing algorithms for haplotype phasing, variant calling, and analyzing structural variation in genomes. Focus on applications in rare disease diagnosis.

faculty.name: Tiffany Amariuta
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (HDSI, BMI)
faculty.summary: Research in statistical genetics, developing methods for fine-mapping disease-associated genetic variants and understanding the genetic architecture of complex traits across diverse populations.

faculty.name: Kit Curtius
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (Biomedical Informatics)
faculty.summary: Research in mathematical modeling of cancer evolution. Focus on developing computational approaches to optimize cancer screening strategies and understand progression dynamics using genomic data.

faculty.name: Florin Vaida
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in survival analysis, clinical trials methods, longitudinal data analysis, and mixed-effects models. Serves as Graduate Programs Director and Doctoral Program Director for Biostatistics.

faculty.name: Lin Liu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistics methods including clinical trials design, survival analysis, and prognostic modeling. Serves as MS Program Director.

faculty.name: Karen Messer
faculty.title: Professor and Division Chief
faculty.summary: Research in cancer biostatistics including clinical trials methodology, survival analysis, and statistical methods for smoking cessation and tobacco control research as Division Chief.

faculty.name: Sonia Jain
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistical methods for clinical trials, Bayesian adaptive designs, and statistical methodology for clinical research in neurodegenerative diseases and critical care.

faculty.name: Loki Natarajan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in cancer biostatistics, developing methods for evaluating lifestyle interventions on cancer outcomes, including physical activity and dietary trials with survival endpoints.

faculty.name: Steve Edland
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistical methods for Alzheimer's disease and neurodegenerative research, including clinical trial design and analysis of cognitive and biomarker outcomes.

faculty.name: Armin Schwartzman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in statistical methods for neuroimaging data analysis, multiple testing procedures, spatial statistics, and false discovery rate control for high-dimensional brain imaging data.

faculty.name: Ronghui (Lily) Xu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in survival analysis methodology, random effects models, and clinical trial design with applications in cancer and biomedical research.

faculty.name: Charles Berry
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in statistical genetics and computational biology, developing methods for analyzing genomic data and integrating genetic information in biomedical studies.

faculty.name: Hyunkeun Ryan Cho
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistical methods for longitudinal data analysis, semiparametric modeling, and applications in clinical and public health research.

faculty.name: Wesley Thompson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in statistical methods for psychiatric and behavioral research, developing approaches for integrating diverse data types and longitudinal mental health outcome analysis.

faculty.name: Xin Tu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistical methods with applications in mental health and behavioral research, including longitudinal modeling, causal mediation analysis, and health services outcomes.

faculty.name: Chito Hernandez
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistical methods applied to infectious disease research, clinical trials, and global health studies.

faculty.name: Ronald G. (Ryy) Thomas
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in clinical trial design and analysis for Alzheimer's disease and aging studies, including large-scale multicenter trials in neurodegenerative disease research.

faculty.name: Xinlian Zhang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in high-dimensional biostatistics, developing variable selection and regularization methods for genomic and biomedical data analysis.

faculty.name: Jingjing Zou
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in biostatistical methodology with applications in clinical and public health research, developing novel approaches for complex health data challenges.

faculty.name: Matthew Alford
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies ocean dynamics including internal waves, the mixed layer, abyssal overflows, and turbulence, with an emphasis on ocean instrumentation and observations. Co-leads the Multiscale Ocean Dynamics group at Scripps.

faculty.name: Paola Cessi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops models of the oceanic general circulation and of climate dynamics, focusing on how ocean circulation and ocean-atmosphere interactions shape Earth's climate.

faculty.name: Ian Eisenman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates ocean and climate dynamics with particular emphasis on sea ice, climate feedbacks, and large-scale atmospheric and oceanic circulation.

faculty.name: Falk Feddersen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies nearshore (surfzone and inner-shelf) physical oceanography, including coastal wave dynamics, mixing, and numerical modeling of coastal processes.

faculty.name: Sarah Giddings
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies estuarine and coastal ocean dynamics and their interactions, including bio-physical interactions and exchange between estuaries, the surfzone, and the coastal ocean.

faculty.name: Sarah Gille
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Southern Ocean dynamics and remote sensing
faculty.summary: Studies Southern Ocean climate and dynamics, including wind forcing of the Southern Ocean and heat transport by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, along with satellite oceanography and air-sea exchange.

faculty.name: Jennifer MacKinnon
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates small-scale dynamical processes in the ocean, primarily internal waves, submesoscale instabilities, and associated turbulence, combining field observations with modeling to improve climate model representations.

faculty.name: Matthew Mazloff
faculty.title: Researcher
faculty.summary: Investigates ocean circulation and dynamics, specializing in ocean modeling and state estimation with particular focus on the Southern Ocean, including the Southern Ocean State Estimate.

faculty.name: Mark Merrifield
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies coastal oceanography, including surface and internal waves and sea level variability. Directs the Center for Climate Change Impacts and Adaptation at Scripps.

faculty.name: Sarah Purkey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Abyssal circulation and ocean heat content
faculty.summary: Investigates abyssal ocean circulation and variability and ocean heat and sea level rise budgets through large-scale ocean observations to understand climate impacts.

faculty.name: Daniel Rudnick
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the physical and biological dynamics of the upper ocean, with particular focus on fronts and eddies and air-sea interactions, using sustained observations including underwater gliders.

faculty.name: Lia Siegelman
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies geophysical fluid dynamics using satellite data, field observations, and computational models, focusing on mesoscale and submesoscale turbulence and air-sea and sea-ice interactions.

faculty.name: Janet Sprintall
faculty.title: Research Oceanographer
faculty.summary: Studies tropical interocean exchanges including the Indonesian Throughflow, Southern Ocean dynamics, and sustained monitoring of large-scale ocean circulation.

faculty.name: Shang-Ping Xie
faculty.title: Professor and Roger Revelle Chair in Environmental Science
faculty.summary: Investigates ocean-atmosphere interactions and their role in climate formation, variability, and change, through diagnostic and modeling studies across the Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian Oceans.

faculty.name: Nicholas Lutsko
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies atmospheric dynamics, climate sensitivity, and climate impacts and adaptation, using modeling of the atmosphere and climate system.

faculty.name: Amato Evan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies dust storms and mineral dust aerosols, including their dynamics, climate impacts, and radiative forcing, using field measurements, satellite data, and numerical modeling.

faculty.name: Duncan Watson-Parris
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the climate impact of anthropogenic aerosol through interactions with clouds and radiation, and applies machine learning techniques to improve climate modeling across scales.

faculty.name: Amy Waterhouse
faculty.title: Research Scientist
faculty.summary: Investigates internal waves and mixing, including how global patterns of diapycnal mixing relate to internal wave energy sources and how submarine canyons modify internal wave energy fluxes and coastal processes.

faculty.name: Gunnar Voet
faculty.title: Associate Research Scientist
faculty.summary: Investigates dense overflows, internal waves, and turbulent mixing using shipboard and moored observations, examining how these processes impact the large-scale ocean circulation.

faculty.name: Ivana Cerovecki
faculty.title: Researcher
faculty.sub_field: Southern Ocean and water mass formation
faculty.summary: Investigates Southern Ocean circulation and mode water formation, with particular focus on air-sea heat and freshwater fluxes and eddy dynamics.

funding.note: ~5 yrs support (RA/TA/fellowships) incl. tuition, fees, stipend

faculty.name: Octavio Aburto
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Aburto studies marine reserves and commercially exploited species and their fisheries, coordinating the Gulf of California Marine Program with work across Mexico and Latin America. He is also a conservation photographer documenting coastal ecosystems.

faculty.name: Andrew D. Barton
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Barton is a biological oceanographer studying the physiology, ecology, macroecology, and biodiversity of marine microbes. His group maps phytoplankton distributions by integrating ocean models with large observational datasets to understand climate impacts on marine ecosystems.

faculty.name: Simone Baumann-Pickering
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Baumann-Pickering specializes in acoustic ecology, using passive acoustic monitoring to study behavioral patterns, geographic distribution, habitat preference, and predator-prey interactions of marine animals such as beaked whales. Her work advances understanding of adaptations to anthropogenic impacts.

faculty.name: Jeff S. Bowman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Bowman studies the diversity and function of marine microbial communities, including bacteria and single-celled phytoplankton. His lab explores marine, terrestrial, and host microbial ecology with interests spanning polar ecology, astrobiology, and bioinformatics.

faculty.name: Anela Choy
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Pelagic and deep-sea food web ecology
faculty.summary: Choy is a sea-going biological oceanographer studying open-ocean water-column and deep-sea food web structure and function, focusing on how organic matter flows through and connects species. Her work examines impacts of global environmental change and commercial fishing on pelagic ecosystems.

faculty.name: Moira Decima
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Decima studies plankton food webs and zooplankton communities and curates the Pelagic Invertebrate Collection. Her lab investigates how these communities respond to environmental perturbations including El Nino, global warming, and ocean acidification.

faculty.name: Julia Diaz
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Diaz lab explores the biogeochemistry of ocean health and marine ecosystem functioning, focusing on how interactions between ocean geochemistry and microbiology, especially phytoplankton, shape climate and natural resources.

faculty.name: Amro Hamdoun
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Marine cell biology and environmental toxicology
faculty.summary: The Hamdoun lab studies cellular mechanisms of small-molecule transport of drugs, signaling molecules, and environmental toxicants, pioneering study of toxicant interactions with ABCB1/P-glycoprotein and discovery of Transporter Interfering Chemicals.

faculty.name: Ryan Hechinger
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Hechinger works to understand the ecology and evolution of parasites and parasitism, using them to advance broader ecological and evolutionary science.

faculty.name: James Leichter
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Coastal biological oceanography and marine ecology
faculty.summary: Leichter's research focuses on coastal biological oceanography and marine ecology, including work in cold-water kelp forests, coral reefs, and Antarctic research diving.

faculty.name: Deirdre Lyons
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Evolutionary developmental biology of marine invertebrates
faculty.summary: Lyons studies gene regulatory networks, evolutionary developmental biology, and the development of marine invertebrates, especially molluscs, annelids, and echinoderms.

faculty.name: Paul Ponganis
faculty.title: Research Scientist (Research Marine Biologist)
faculty.sub_field: Diving physiology of marine mammals and birds
faculty.summary: Ponganis studies diving physiology and behavior in marine mammals and birds, including oxygen management and physiological adaptations to breath-hold diving.

faculty.name: Greg Rouse
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Marine invertebrate biodiversity and deep-sea biology
faculty.summary: Rouse specializes in animal biodiversity and deep-sea habitats such as whale falls, hydrothermal vents, and methane seeps, with research on Osedax bone-eating worms, seadragons, and Xenoturbella. He also curates the Scripps Benthic Invertebrate Collection.

faculty.name: Stuart Sandin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Sandin studies the biology and ecology of coral reef ecosystems, including large-scale efforts to characterize reef health across islands worldwide.

faculty.name: Brice Semmens
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Semmens' research spans coastal, conservation, and coral reef ecology with a focus on fisheries biology and management and population and community ecology.

faculty.name: Jennifer Smith
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Marine benthic and coral reef ecology
faculty.summary: Smith investigates the factors that structure marine benthic communities, focusing on how human impacts affect coral reef and kelp forest ecosystems, including seaweed ecology and ocean acidification.

faculty.name: George Sugihara
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor of Natural Science (McQuown Chair)
faculty.summary: Sugihara integrates mathematical modeling with ecological theory to study ecosystem dynamics and food-web interactions, with applications to climate change and coastal systems.

faculty.name: Martin Tresguerres
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Tresguerres studies the physiology of aquatic organisms with emphasis on pH and CO2 sensing, cellular signaling, ion transport, and acid-base regulation in marine systems.

faculty.name: Jennifer Taylor
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Taylor studies the biomechanics and physiology of marine invertebrates, especially crustacean exoskeletons and molting, integrating functional morphology with behavior, ecology, and evolution.

faculty.name: Daniel Wangpraseurt
faculty.title: Associate Researcher
faculty.sub_field: Coral ecophysiology and reef restoration engineering
faculty.summary: Wangpraseurt studies the ecophysiology of corals and uses that knowledge to develop tools for reef restoration and engineering, including biomaterials and bioprinting.

funding.note: ~5 yrs support (RA/TA/fellowships) incl. tuition, fees, stipend

faculty.name: Sarah Aarons
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses isotope compositions of natural materials such as mineral dust and sediment to reconstruct paleo-environmental conditions and understand Earth's geochemical evolution. Her group studies the evolution of Earth's surface through time as a function of a changing climate.

faculty.name: Tomas Capaldi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Geologist studying mountain belt development and erosion through sedimentary records, combining field work, geochronology and geochemistry, and forward modeling. His research addresses tectonic-climate interactions and sediment transport systems.

faculty.name: Emily Chin
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates igneous and metamorphic petrology, high-temperature and isotopic geochemistry, and tectonics, with projects on volcanism-plate interactions, the evolution of continental lithosphere, and the geology of Western North America.

faculty.name: Catherine Constable
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on geomagnetism, paleomagnetism, electromagnetism, and mathematical and theoretical geophysics, using numerical modeling to understand the behavior and evolution of Earth's magnetic field.

faculty.name: James Day
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Specializes in high-temperature geochemical and volcanological research, including time-series studies of volcanic systems, evolution of the mantle lithosphere, and planetary formation processes traced through meteoritic materials.

faculty.name: Margo Odlum
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops and applies techniques to document thermal, chemical, and mechanical signatures of deformation and fluid-rock interactions in the lithosphere. Her group integrates field geology, microscale observations, geochronology, and geochemistry to study active and ancient fault zones, including strike-slip faults in Alaska and Yukon.

faculty.name: Vashan Wright
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans granular physics, rock physics, reflection seismology, and planetary geophysics, including studies of slope failure, assessment of water on Mars, and the evolution of fault systems.

faculty.name: Ross Parnell-Turner
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies geodynamics, marine geology and geophysics, and tectonics, including mantle plumes, volcanic eruption cycles, and how plate spreading is accommodated at the seafloor.

faculty.name: Yehuda Bock
faculty.title: Research Geodesist, Senior Lecturer, and Director of the Scripps Orbit and Permanent Array Center
faculty.summary: Applies precise GNSS positioning and observational networks to lithospheric deformation, earthquake physics, and natural hazards, including tsunami early warning, machine learning for crustal processes, and integration of radar and GPS observations.

faculty.name: Steven Constable
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the electrical conductivity of Earth's crust and mantle using marine electromagnetic methods and seafloor instrumentation, with applications to offshore groundwater, gas hydrate, and tectonic plate boundaries.

faculty.name: Wenyuan Fan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Observational seismologist investigating earthquake source kinematic and dynamic processes, slow earthquakes, and subduction zone processes, as well as ocean-solid earth interactions using array seismology and marine geophysics.

faculty.name: Yuri Fialko
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies crustal deformation and the physics of earthquakes and volcanoes using space geodesy techniques such as InSAR and GPS, combined with mechanical modeling of active tectonics and rock mechanics.

faculty.name: Helen Amanda Fricker
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates the cryosphere and polar regions using satellite remote sensing, focusing on ice sheet processes and the role of ice in the climate system and environmental change.

faculty.name: Alice Gabriel
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works in computational and theoretical seismology and earthquake physics, using high-performance computing to model subduction zone earthquakes, tsunami genesis, and ground motion.

faculty.name: Gabi Laske
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Observational seismologist focusing on structural seismology and surface wave modeling of Earth's interior, including the collection and analysis of ocean-bottom seismic data.

faculty.name: Dave May
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate professor at the Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics working on computational geodynamics and numerical methods for simulating solid-earth processes.

faculty.name: Matthias Morzfeld
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops mathematical and computational methods for data assimilation and inverse problems, studying how sampling techniques perform in high-dimensional spaces and applying them to merge models with data across Earth science applications.

faculty.name: David Sandwell
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on geodynamics, space geodesy, and global seafloor mapping, improving the resolution of the marine gravity field from satellite altimetry and measuring deformation along the San Andreas Fault system.

faculty.name: Peter Shearer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Seismologist at the Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics whose research focuses on earthquake physics and using seismic waves to study the deep structure of the Earth.

faculty.name: Adrian Borsa
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Specializes in geodesy and remote sensing, applying satellite and ground-based measurements to lithospheric deformation, polar science, and land surface hydrology.

faculty.name: Lihini Aluwihare
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies organic matter composition and cycling in the ocean, using analytical and isotopic techniques to trace the origins of marine organic matter and the metabolic diversity of aquatic microbial communities.

faculty.name: Ralph Keeling
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the Scripps CO2 and O2 programs and studies atmospheric composition and the global carbon cycle, using long-term atmospheric measurements to understand climate change and Earth's biogeochemical cycles.

faculty.name: Jeff Severinghaus
faculty.title: Professor of Geosciences
faculty.summary: Studies trapped bubbles of gases contained in ice cores to track changes in ancient climate, with broader interests in biogeochemistry, greenhouse gases, and past climate change.

faculty.name: Amina Schartup
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates environmental biogeochemistry and toxicology, focusing on how contaminants such as mercury cycle through and interact with marine and aquatic systems.

requirements.admission_model: Direct PhD entry allowed without MS

funding.note: PhD students typically funded via fellowships/GSR/TA; first-year NRST covered for nonresidents

faculty.name: Divyakant Agrawal
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor (Chair)
faculty.summary: Department Chair. Research in database systems and distributed data management. Focus on scalable data processing in cloud environments and big data analytics. ACM Distinguished Scientist.

faculty.name: Amr El Abbadi
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research in data management for distributed and cloud systems. Focus on fault-tolerant distributed databases, scalable data processing, and recently blockchain data management. ACM Fellow.

faculty.name: Timothy Sherwood
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research in computer architecture, particularly architectural support for security. Known for work on timing channel analysis, hardware security, and designing novel microarchitectures for emerging workloads.

faculty.name: Linda Petzold
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor (Mehrabian Engineering Chair)
faculty.summary: Pioneer in numerical methods for differential-algebraic equations and scientific computing. Research in computational methods for systems biology, particularly stochastic simulation of cellular processes. NAS member, NAE member.

faculty.name: Giovanni Vigna
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Leading researcher in computer security. Known for work on malware analysis, web security, and vulnerability detection. Director of the UCSB SecLab and co-founder of the Shellphish hacking team. ACM Fellow.

faculty.name: Ambuj K. Singh
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.sub_field: Data Mining, Network Science, Machine Learning
faculty.summary: Research in data mining, network science, and graph-based machine learning. Focus on analyzing complex networks in biology, social media, and neuroscience. Leads the Dynamo lab.

faculty.name: Subhash Suri
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research in algorithms with contributions to computational geometry, network algorithms, and data structures. Recent work on privacy-preserving algorithms and algorithmic game theory.

faculty.name: Tobias Hollerer
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Pioneer in augmented reality research. Focus on AR/VR systems, spatial computing, and 3D user interfaces. Known for creating the Four Eyes Lab pushing the boundaries of mixed reality.

faculty.name: William Wang
faculty.title: Professor (Mellichamp Endowed Chair in Mind and Machine Intelligence)
faculty.summary: Research in natural language processing and machine learning. Focus on language understanding, knowledge-grounded dialogue, and integrating structured knowledge with neural language models. Leads the NLP Group.

faculty.name: Chandra Krintz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in distributed systems, cloud computing, and IoT solutions for societal challenges. Leads the UCSB SmartFarm project applying computing to sustainable agriculture. ACM Distinguished Scientist.

faculty.name: Rich Wolski
faculty.title: Professor (Duval Family Presidential Chair in Energy Efficiency)
faculty.summary: Research in high-performance cloud computing and energy-efficient distributed systems. Known for foundational work on cloud resource management and the Eucalyptus open-source cloud platform.

faculty.name: Tevfik Bultan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in software analysis and verification. Known for work on string analysis for web applications and comprehensive formal verification frameworks. Leads the VLab.

faculty.name: Xifeng Yan
faculty.title: Professor (Venkatesh Narayanamurti Endowed Chair in CS)
faculty.summary: Research in data mining and machine learning. Focus on graph mining, network analysis, and knowledge discovery from large-scale structured and textual data. Known for contributions to graph pattern mining.

faculty.name: Christopher Kruegel
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in computer security, particularly malware analysis and detection. Known for influential work on botnet analysis and web application security. Co-founder of Lastline (acquired by VMWare).

faculty.name: Elizabeth Belding
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in wireless networking and Information and Communication Technologies for Development (ICTD). Focus on bringing Internet connectivity to rural and underserved communities worldwide. ACM Fellow.

faculty.name: Daniel Lokshtanov
faculty.title: Professor (Vice Chair)
faculty.summary: Vice Chair. Research in theoretical computer science, particularly parameterized complexity and graph algorithms. Known for foundational contributions to kernelization theory and fixed-parameter tractability.

faculty.name: Eric Vigoda
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in theoretical computer science with focus on randomized algorithms, Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, and approximate counting. Known for analyzing phase transitions in combinatorial structures.

faculty.name: Ben Hardekopf
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in programming languages and compilers with focus on program analysis for security and optimization. Known for work on pointer analysis, information flow, and compiler-based security.

faculty.name: Yu Feng
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in programming languages with focus on automated program analysis and verification. Developing tools for automatically finding bugs and verifying properties of real-world software systems.

faculty.name: Arpit Gupta
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in computer networking with focus on network management, cloud infrastructure networking, and Internet measurement. Building practical systems for network operations.

requirements.admission_model: PhD applicants must already hold a Master's degree (else apply MS/PhD)

funding.note: Merit-based GSR/TA/fellowships covering stipend, fees, health insurance, NRST

faculty.name: Leon Balents
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates quantum magnetism, correlated electron systems, and complex materials. Known for predicting topological insulators and Weyl semimetals, and for advancing the understanding of quantum spin liquids — exotic states of matter with macroscopic quantum entanglement of electronic spin.

faculty.name: Matthew Fisher
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of many-body theory and quantum information theory, with current focus on the non-equilibrium quantum dynamics of open and monitored quantum systems. Previously held positions at IBM, the Kavli Institute, Microsoft Station Q, and Caltech.

faculty.name: Andrea Young
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on quantum electronics in two-dimensional systems, exploring emergent electronic phenomena in van der Waals heterostructures and moiré materials.

faculty.name: Cenke Xu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies quantum many-body systems where the interplay between quantum fluctuation and correlation effects produces diverse phenomena such as quantum criticality, non-Fermi liquids, quantum spin liquids, and topological matter, with applications to transition metal oxides, moiré heterostructures, and cold atom systems.

faculty.name: Sagar Vijay
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of quantum condensed matter physics and quantum information science, focusing on far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics, universal traits of highly entangled quantum matter, and quantum error correction. Recipient of the Sloan Research Fellowship and the 2023 William L. McMillan Award.

faculty.name: Chenhao Jin
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Builds optical spectroscopy and imaging tools to watch quantum phenomena across space and time, exploring 2D materials, moiré superlattices, spin systems, strongly correlated materials, and topological systems, with a focus on the interplay between dimensionality, many-body interaction, fluctuations, and competing orders.

faculty.name: Ania Bleszynski Jayich
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Builds quantum technologies centered on solid-state spins, photons, and phonons to investigate foundational questions in quantum science and condensed matter physics.

faculty.name: Michel Devoret
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates quantum non-equilibrium phenomena in superconducting circuits with applications to quantum information processing, including quantum computation and quantum sensing. Pioneered the field of quantronics, where collective degrees of freedom like currents and voltages display quantum behavior.

faculty.name: John Martinis
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates superconducting devices, focusing on minimizing noise and enhancing sensitivity. His main effort involves building a quantum computer based on Josephson junction quantum bits, and he led the Google quantum supremacy experiment.

faculty.name: David Weld
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Employs ultracold quantum degenerate gases to investigate a broad spectrum of quantum dynamical phenomena, with current interests spanning quantum simulation, quantum thermodynamics, kicked quantum matter, Floquet engineering, quasicrystals, atom interferometry, and anyon synthesis.

faculty.name: David Patterson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Extends the tools of atomic, molecular, and optical physics to prepare polyatomic molecules in single quantum states for the first time. Develops novel spectroscopy methods for ultraprecise chemical analysis, with interests spanning quantum information systems, parity violation in molecular spectra, and single-molecule chiral analysis.

faculty.name: David Berenstein
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works primarily on quantum field theories and their equivalence to quantum gravity in higher dimensions via the AdS/CFT correspondence, exploring deep connections between gauge theories and gravitational physics.

faculty.name: Nathaniel Craig
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of high energy physics, particle phenomenology, and cosmology, exploring physics beyond the Standard Model through effective field theory methods and collider signatures.

faculty.name: Xi Dong
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Explores the connection between quantum entanglement and emergent spacetime through the holographic duality between string theory and quantum field theories. Also investigates foundational questions in quantum gravity and phenomenological aspects of particle physics and cosmology.

faculty.name: Steven Giddings
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on quantum gravity, quantum field theory, black holes, quantum cosmology, and elementary particles, with a focus on fundamental questions at the intersection of general relativity and quantum mechanics.

faculty.name: David Gross
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Nobel laureate (2004) recognized for the discovery of asymptotic freedom in quantum chromodynamics. His research spans high energy physics, quantum field theory, and string theory. Permanent member of the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

faculty.name: Gary Horowitz
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on classical and quantum gravity, with particular emphasis on black holes and spacetime singularities. Member of the National Academy of Sciences and former President of the International Society on General Relativity and Gravitation.

faculty.name: Donald Marolf
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Explores black holes, gravitational aspects of string theory, and how gravity, entropy, and entanglement intersect. Investigates how bulk physics is encoded in gauge theory quantum states and studies thermal transport, quantum observables in gravity, and the firewall paradox.

faculty.name: Claudio Campagnari
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Conducts direct searches for new physics processes with the CMS experiment at the LHC, with a shift toward searches for exotic signatures such as long-lived new particles and milli-charged particles. Also performs precision Standard Model tests including measurements of rare top quark decays and Higgs boson properties.

faculty.name: Joe Incandela
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Searches for new fundamental particles at high-energy colliders. Involved in the discovery of the top quark in 1995 and the first observation of the Higgs boson in 2012. His group currently works on high-granularity silicon-based calorimeters for the CMS experiment and the LDMX light dark matter experiment.

faculty.name: David Caratelli
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist studying neutrinos to understand the fundamental laws of nature and the evolution of the universe, with work centered on the MicroBooNE and DUNE experiments investigating sterile neutrino oscillations and developing liquid argon time projection chamber technology.

faculty.name: Brendan Bowler
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates planet formation, growth, migration, and atmospheric evolution using observatories like Keck, HST, and JWST. His ultimate objective is to directly characterize terrestrial worlds in the habitable zones of their host stars in search of signs of life.

faculty.name: Benjamin Mazin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops optical/UV/X-ray Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) and astronomical instrumentation, with a current focus on building and using MKID-based instruments for detecting and characterizing nearby exoplanets.

faculty.name: S. Peng Oh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies galaxy formation and evolution along with the physics of diffuse plasmas, cosmic rays, turbulence, and the gaseous environments around galaxies and within galaxy clusters.

faculty.name: Crystal Martin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how galaxies assemble and how the universe transitioned from a neutral to an ionized intergalactic medium, using spectroscopy and imaging to measure properties of stars and gas in and around galaxies, applying concepts from hydrodynamics, radiative transfer, cosmology, and stellar evolution.

faculty.name: Maxwell Millar-Blanchaer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on the direct imaging of exoplanets, brown dwarfs, and debris disks using polarimetry to detect faint objects near bright stars, combining instrument-building, large-telescope observations, and novel data analysis techniques.

faculty.name: Prateek Agrawal
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of particle physics and cosmology, investigating dark matter, early universe physics, and astrophysical probes of new fundamental physics.

faculty.name: Philip Lubin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the early universe through millimeter-wavelength observations and develops applications of directed energy for planetary defense and relativistic propulsion. Co-investigator on the Planck cosmology mission and co-recipient of the 2006 and 2018 Gruber Prizes in Cosmology.

faculty.name: Lars Bildsten
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor and Director of the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics (KITP), conducting research in theoretical astrophysics and cosmology.

faculty.name: Dirk Bouwmeester
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates quantum information science and quantum decoherence using optomechanical systems such as phononic crystal membranes made of silicon nitride and diamond, and on-chip optical waveguides coupled to superfluid helium.

faculty.name: Mark Bowick
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Deputy Director of the KITP who investigates symmetry, symmetry-breaking, geometry, and topology across fields ranging from quantum field theory to soft and living matter, with recent focus on the statistical mechanics of thermalized 2D metamaterials such as graphene and elastic membranes.

faculty.name: Frank Brown
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Theoretical Biophysics
faculty.summary: Works in the physics of soft and living matter, developing theoretical and computational approaches to biophysical and biochemical systems.

faculty.name: Jean Carlson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies complex systems spanning condensed matter theory and the physics of soft and living matter, applying physics-based modeling to complex and biological systems.

faculty.name: Caitlin Casey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the assembly of the most massive galaxies in the universe using observations from telescopes such as JWST and ALMA to understand how galaxies formed and evolved in the earliest cosmic times, and leads the COSMOS survey that identifies rare, extreme galaxies and examines their large-scale environments.

faculty.name: Zvonimir Dogic
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Condensed Matter Experimental / Soft and Living Matter
faculty.summary: Experimental soft matter physicist who reproduces diverse dynamical phenomena of living systems in simplified systems built from a minimal set of building blocks, studying out-of-equilibrium active matter with applications spanning robotics and microfluidics.

faculty.name: Clifford Johnson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Concentrates on quantum gravity, superstring theory, quantum field theory, and particle physics, with particular focus on strongly coupled phenomena.

faculty.name: Joseph Hennawi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works in astrophysics and cosmology, studying quasars, the intergalactic medium, and the large-scale structure of the universe through observation and data analysis.

faculty.name: Andreas Ludwig
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on condensed matter theory, studying quantum many-body systems including topological phases of matter, disordered systems, and quantum entanglement.

faculty.name: M. Cristina Marchetti
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Condensed Matter Theory / Soft and Living Matter
faculty.summary: Theoretical physicist studying active matter and living systems, investigating how assemblies of energy-consuming entities develop organized behaviors at scales much larger than their individual components, with applications ranging from crowd dynamics to epithelial cell migration in wound healing.

faculty.name: David Morrison
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works in mathematical physics and string theory, studying the geometry of string compactifications and connections between algebraic geometry and quantum field theory.

faculty.name: Chetan Nayak
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Condensed matter theorist and Director of Microsoft Station Q, working on topological phases of matter and their application to topological quantum computing.

faculty.name: Harry Nelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: High Energy Experimental Physics / Dark Matter
faculty.summary: Designs and builds novel particle detectors to search for new physics, focusing for the past two decades on the direct detection of dark matter through underground experiments including CDMS, LUX, and LZ.

faculty.name: Jeffrey Richman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist working in high energy physics on collider-based searches and precision measurements that test the Standard Model and probe for new phenomena.

faculty.name: Cyrus Safinya
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Biomolecular Materials
faculty.summary: Distinguished Professor studying the physics and materials science of biological systems, using soft matter physics and molecular engineering approaches to investigate biomolecular materials.

faculty.name: Joan-Emma Shea
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Theoretical Biophysics
faculty.summary: Works in the physics of soft and living matter, using theoretical and computational methods to study protein folding, biomolecular self-assembly, and related biophysical systems.

faculty.name: Mark Sherwin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental condensed matter physicist and Director of the Institute for Terahertz Science and Technology, using the UCSB Free-Electron Lasers to study quantum condensed matter driven by strong periodic fields, including photo-excited quasiparticles and quantum coherence in spin systems.

faculty.name: Boris Shraiman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Biophysics Theory
faculty.summary: Permanent Member of the KITP working in theoretical biophysics, applying physics-based approaches to problems in the physics of soft and living matter, including quantitative biology and developmental dynamics.

faculty.name: David Stuart
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist and Department Chair, working in high energy physics with the CMS experiment at the LHC to search for new particles and test the Standard Model.

faculty.name: Anthony Zee
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Applies field-theoretical methods to strongly correlated quantum systems across particle physics and condensed matter, using concepts such as gauge theory and topological actions to study superconductivity, quantum Hall fluids, and disordered systems, seeking insights that bridge particle and condensed matter physics.

faculty.name: Deborah Fygenson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Biophysics
faculty.summary: Experimental biophysicist and Director of the Graduate Program working in the physics of soft and living matter, studying biomolecular self-assembly and DNA nanotechnology.

faculty.name: Omar A. Saleh
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Single-Molecule Biophysics
faculty.summary: Conducts experimental research on biopolymer elasticity using single-molecule stretching techniques and studies biomimetic organelles built from reconstituted assemblies of nucleic acids and proteins to understand fundamental principles of biomolecular behavior.

faculty.name: Andrew Jayich
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental AMO physicist working with trapped ions to perform precision measurements and searches for new physics through quantum control of atomic and molecular ions.

faculty.name: Xiao Luo
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: High Energy Experimental Physics / Neutrino Physics
faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist working in high energy physics with a focus on neutrino physics and accelerator-based neutrino experiments.

faculty.name: Everett Lipman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Single-Molecule Biophysics
faculty.summary: Experimental biophysicist working in the physics of soft and living matter, developing single-molecule techniques and instrumentation to study biomolecular dynamics.

faculty.name: Matthieu Louis
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Biophysics and Neuroscience
faculty.summary: Investigates how odor tracking (chemotaxis) emerges through neural-circuit computations in Drosophila larvae, combining computational and experimental methods to map and functionally characterize the neural circuits that convert olfactory information into navigational decisions.

faculty.name: Sebastian Streichan
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Physics of Soft and Living Matter / Developmental Biophysics
faculty.summary: Biophysicist working in the physics of soft and living matter, studying the physics of morphogenesis and tissue dynamics during animal development using quantitative imaging.

faculty.name: Hugh Lippincott
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: High Energy Experimental Physics / Dark Matter
faculty.summary: Experimental physicist and Vice Chair for Research working on the direct detection of dark matter, developing and operating underground noble-liquid detector experiments to search for dark matter particles.

faculty.name: Tejaswi Venumadhav Nerella
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works in astrophysics and cosmology with a focus on gravitational-wave astrophysics, developing methods to detect and analyze gravitational-wave signals from compact binary mergers.

funding.note: All students in good standing fully supported; ~$37,000 annual salary plus tuition, fees, health insurance
Meeting deadline required for departmental/campus financial support consideration

faculty.name: Amalendu Krishna

faculty.title: Professor

faculty.summary: Assistant Professor working on optimal transport, calculus of variations, and numerical methods for PDE.

faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor working in differential geometry, with emphasis on curvature operators and geometric analysis.

faculty.name: Paul Atzberger

faculty.name: Peter Garfield

faculty.summary: Research interests in differential geometry and mathematics education.

faculty.summary: Associate Professor (joint with Statistics and Applied Probability) working on financial mathematics, machine learning, and stochastic control.

faculty.name: Stephen Bigelow
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor working in topology, braid groups, and quantum topology.

faculty.name: Sui Tang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Associate Professor working in applied mathematics, machine learning, and data-driven modeling; NSF CAREER awardee.

faculty.name: Xianzhe Dai
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor working in differential geometry, global analysis, and index theory of elliptic operators.

faculty.summary: Associate Professor in number theory, working on automorphic forms, p-adic L-values, and Iwasawa theory.

faculty.title: Professor

faculty.name: John Hsu

faculty.name: Tomoyuki Ichiba

faculty.name: Michael Ludkovski

faculty.name: Wendy Meiring

faculty.summary: Research in applied statistics focusing on statistics of space-time processes and environmental statistics, studying spatial and temporal patterns in environmental data.

faculty.name: Gareth Peters
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in actuarial mathematics, quantitative risk management, insurance statistics, statistical machine learning in insurance, and green finance and cryptocurrency analytics.

faculty.name: Yuedong Wang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in applied statistics and biostatistics, developing statistical methods including smoothing splines and nonparametric regression with biomedical applications.

faculty.name: Andrew Carter
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in mathematical statistics, focusing on theoretical foundations of statistical methods and nonparametric inference. Serves as Graduate Vice Chair.

faculty.name: Nils-Christian Detering
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in applied probability and stochastic processes, including random graph models and their applications in financial mathematics and network analysis.

faculty.name: Raisa Feldman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in probability theory and stochastic processes with emphasis on time series analysis, heavy-tailed distributions, and applications in finance and engineering.

faculty.name: Alex Franks
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in multivariate statistics, causal inference methodology, biostatistics, and sports analytics, developing methods for analyzing complex correlated data structures.

faculty.name: Sang-Yun Oh
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research in graphical models, covariance estimation, applied statistics, computational statistics, and statistical computing with emphasis on scalable machine learning methods.

faculty.name: Michael Gu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research in Bayesian statistics, spatio-temporal processes, functional data analysis, and uncertainty quantification with environmental and scientific applications.

faculty.name: Chao Gao

faculty.name: Veronika Rockova
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Bridges statistics and machine learning for large-scale data analysis, specializing in Bayesian methods. Created methods including EMVS, Spike-and-Slab LASSO, and Factor Rotations to Sparsity. Recent work incorporates GANs into posterior sampling algorithms, with applications in public health and biomedicine.

faculty.name: Rebecca Willett
faculty.title: Professor

Research spans compressed sensing, inverse problems in imaging, learning theory, and statistical signal processing with interdisciplinary applications in astronomy, neuroscience, EHR analysis, and atmospheric science. Faculty Director of AI at the Data Science Institute.

faculty.name: Dan Nicolae
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on understanding the role of genetic, genomic and environmental factors in complex human diseases, from theoretical statistics to data analysis. Research includes functional genomics, microbiome research, multi-omics data integration, and network biology.

faculty.name: Wei-Biao Wu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Establishes a systematic theory for high-dimensional inference under dependence, developing tools for model selection, covariance matrix estimation, and multiple testing for dependent data. Studies deep Gaussian approximation and concentration inequalities for dependent variables.

faculty.name: Mengjie Chen
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Computational biologist and statistician bridging statistical methodological advances and biomedical applications. Develops methods for single-cell genomics, epitranscriptomics profiling, and characterizing intra-tumor heterogeneity from cancer genomics data.

faculty.name: Lek-Heng Lim
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works in computational mathematics and data science foundations. Recipient of the Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship and Guggenheim Fellowship. Co-leads an NSF Institute on Foundations of Data Science.

faculty.name: Dacheng Xiu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methodologies for financial data and their economic implications. Earlier work on risk measurement and portfolio management with high-frequency data; current research focuses on machine learning solutions for big-data problems in empirical asset pricing.

faculty.name: Frederic Koehler
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research centers on computational learning theory and related topics including probability theory, high-dimensional statistics, and optimization, with particular focus on learning and inference in graphical models. PhD from MIT; previously a Motwani Postdoctoral Fellow at Stanford.

faculty.name: Per A. Mykland

faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research develops Bayesian machine learning methods for high-dimensional structured data, including tensor decomposition, network models, and applications to political science and international relations.

faculty.name: Victor Veitch
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on integrating causal reasoning with machine learning, including representation learning and deep learning theory, with applications to natural language processing and social science.

faculty.name: Cong Ma
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on high-dimensional statistics, matrix and tensor estimation problems, and statistical foundations of reinforcement learning and machine learning.

faculty.name: Mary Sara McPeek
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on statistical methods for genetic analysis, including pedigree-based linkage analysis, association mapping, and methods for complex trait genetics.

faculty.name: Yuehaw Khoo
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans optimization, tensor methods, machine learning, and scientific computing with applications to data science and physical sciences.

faculty.name: Daniel Sanz-Alonso
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on uncertainty quantification, Bayesian inverse problems, data assimilation methods, and their applications in geophysical sciences and engineering.

faculty.name: Tobin R. Sosnick
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Sosnick lab integrates experimental (HX, NMR, SAXS, mass spectrometry) and computational (molecular dynamics, coarse-grain simulations) approaches to study protein and RNA folding, function, and design. Recent work explores transcriptome-wide mRNP condensation in stress granule formation, temperature-dependent fold-switching in the circadian clock protein KaiB, and the design of light-sensitive allosteric proteins for optogenetics.

faculty.name: Erin J. Adams
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Adams lab investigates the molecular signals the immune system uses to distinguish healthy from unhealthy tissue, focusing on unconventional T cell recognition involving γδ T cells, NKT cells, and MAIT cells alongside antigen presentation by nonclassical MHC-like proteins. The group integrates biochemistry, structural biology, protein engineering, and cellular assays to uncover how immune effector cells regulate human disease.

faculty.name: Eduardo Perozo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Perozo lab studies the structure, function, and gating mechanisms of ion channels, including potassium channels (Shaker, HERG, BK), mechanosensitive channels (MscS), and voltage-sensing domains. The group uses structural biology, electrophysiology, and biophysical approaches to understand how lipid bilayer deformations drive channel gating and how conformation-specific tools can discriminate functional states.

faculty.name: Robert J. Keenan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Keenan lab investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying membrane protein biogenesis and quality control using biochemical reconstitution, structural biology (cryo-EM), and cell biology approaches. Recent work focuses on the ribosome-translocon complex, regulated N-glycosylation at the secretory translocon, and unifying models for how multi-pass membrane proteins are built and folded at the ER.

faculty.name: Benoit Roux
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Roux lab bridges theoretical/computational chemistry and experimental biochemistry to understand molecular mechanisms of membrane proteins, especially ion channels. The group develops and applies molecular simulation tools (notably the CHARMM software package) to study channel gating, ion permeation, and inactivation processes at atomic resolution, while also working on antibody polyreactivity characterization and biosensor design.

faculty.name: Joseph A. Piccirilli
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Piccirilli lab investigates RNA structure, function, and enzymology, with a focus on ribozyme mechanisms, tRNA modifications and their roles in mitochondrial pathology, and RNA-small molecule interactions. The group employs chemical biology, biochemistry, and structural approaches to understand RNA conformational dynamics in disease contexts and the fundamental chemistry of RNA catalysis.

faculty.name: Phoebe A. Rice
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Rice lab investigates how mobile genetic elements move using biochemical, structural, and microbiological approaches. Current work focuses on the SCCmec element of MRSA, the paradigmatic Mu transposase, large serine integrases and their directionality control, and transpososome structures, with implications for understanding horizontal gene transfer and microbial pathogenesis.

faculty.name: Anthony A. Kossiakoff
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Kossiakoff Group investigates how molecular recognition drives biological function, combining structural methods (crystallography, cryo-EM) with protein engineering tools. A major focus is developing synthetic antibodies and chaperone-assisted crystallography to tackle protein systems recalcitrant to conventional approaches, with applications spanning mycobacterial cell wall biosynthesis, mTOR signaling, chemokine receptor-arrestin interactions, and apoptosis.

faculty.name: Rama Ranganathan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Ranganathan lab studies the design principles underlying structure, function, and adaptation in biological systems from atomic to cellular scales. The group uses coevolutionary analysis, deep learning-guided protein design, time-resolved crystallography, and systems biology approaches to understand how complex biological functions — from protein folding to allosteric regulation to signaling networks — arise through evolutionary processes.

faculty.name: Tao Pan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Pan lab studies tRNA biology and epitranscriptomics, focusing on how tRNA dynamics and mRNA modifications like m6A regulate gene expression. The group developed high-throughput sequencing methods to measure tRNA abundance, charging, and modifications, discovered the m6A switch mechanism, and investigates how the gut microbiome reprograms host m6A modifications in a tissue-dependent manner.

faculty.name: Marcos Sotomayor
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Sotomayor lab integrates computational structural biology, simulations, and biochemistry to study how mechanical forces are detected and transduced at the molecular level. A central focus is the auditory hair-cell mechanotransduction complex, including TMC1/2 channels and cadherin-based tip-link proteins, with additional work on TMEM63 mechanosensitive channels and the biophysics of lipid scrambling.

faculty.name: Marvin W. Makinen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Makinen lab focuses on vanadium-based compounds for cancer imaging and therapy, developing vanadium-48-labeled vanadyl acetylacetonate as a novel PET imaging agent. Research also investigates vanadyl chelates as inhibitors of protein tyrosine phosphatase-1B, an enzyme regulating insulin and leptin signaling linked to breast, colorectal, and ovarian cancer.

faculty.name: Chuan He
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The He lab investigates how reversible RNA and DNA methylation regulate gene expression and cellular processes. Discovered the first RNA demethylase (FTO), launching the field of epitranscriptomics, and characterized the m6A methyltransferase complex and reader proteins. Recent work explores RNA modification systems as therapeutic targets in leukemia, microbiome-derived cell-free RNA modifications for colorectal cancer detection, and m6A readers in antitumor immunity.

faculty.name: Joseph W. Thornton
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Thornton lab investigates how protein functions evolve over deep time using phylogenetic reconstruction of ancestral proteins followed by synthesis and experimental characterization. The group tackles questions such as how complex molecular systems evolve, the role of epistasis, whether evolution is reversible, and how protein architecture itself evolves, combining evolutionary biology, biochemistry, biophysics, and computational biology.

faculty.name: D. Allan Drummond
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Drummond lab investigates how cells cope with stress at the molecular level, focusing on the formation and dissolution of large assemblies of proteins and RNA during events like heat shock. The group integrates in vivo imaging, in vitro reconstitution, mechanistic biochemistry, quantitative proteomics, and molecular evolutionary analyses, primarily using budding yeast as a model organism to study stress-triggered biomolecular condensation as an adaptive, evolutionarily tuned response.

faculty.name: Jingyi Fei
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Fei lab investigates how RNAs govern gene expression across bacterial and eukaryotic systems using advanced single-molecule and super-resolution imaging. Recent work has explored transcriptome-wide mRNA condensation preceding stress granule formation, RNA localization dynamics at nuclear speckles linked to splicing efficiency, translational T-box riboswitch mechanisms, and KARR-seq for mapping cellular higher-order RNA structures.

faculty.name: Engin Ozkan
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Ozkan lab investigates the biochemistry and interaction networks of proteins essential for nervous system development, focusing on deciphering protein-protein interaction networks of the extracellular space required for axon guidance, pruning, and synapse formation. The group employs a multidisciplinary approach combining crystallography, cellular signaling assays, and protein engineering with genetic modifications in model organisms.

faculty.name: Minglei Zhao
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Zhao lab studies the mechanisms of molecular machines and their roles in human disease, focusing on two primary systems: the p97/ubiquitination system (a central hub in cellular protein homeostasis linked to neurodegenerative diseases and cancer) and the vault RNP particle (the largest ribonucleoprotein in eukaryotes whose function remains elusive). The group uses structural, proteomic, and imaging approaches to elucidate molecular mechanisms.

faculty.name: Demet Arac-Ozkan
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Arac lab investigates how cell-surface receptors mediate intercellular adhesion and communication, focusing on their roles in brain development, synapse formation, and neural wiring. Using structural biology and biochemical approaches, the group studies adhesion GPCRs (ADGRG6/GPR126, ADGRL3/Latrophilin3, CELSR1-3) with direct relevance to neurological disorders, developmental impairments, glioblastoma, and congenital anosmia.

faculty.name: Ronald S. Rock
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: The Rock lab investigates how myosin motor proteins navigate the cytoskeleton and dynamically organize cells, studying biological motion from single-molecule to cellular scales. The group uses advanced fluorescence microscopy, optical tweezers, and structural biology to observe myosin movement in vitro and in living cells, and has developed optogenetic tools like LILAC for enhanced actin imaging.

faculty.name: Cassandra Hayne
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: The Hayne lab investigates how tRNAs are processed and regulated, focusing on the making and breaking of tRNAs by ribonucleases, with implications for neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders. Using cryo-electron microscopy, the group has elucidated the structural basis of pre-tRNA recognition and cleavage by the human TSEN (tRNA splicing endonuclease) complex.

faculty.name: Axel Concepcion
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: The Concepcion lab identifies and characterizes novel membrane proteins and ion channels in immune cells, combining functional genomics, systems immunology, electrophysiology, and cell biology to understand how ion channels regulate immune responses. Research has implications for viral infection, autoimmunity, and cancer, with recent work funded by the NIH and Cancer Research Foundation.
