faculty.name: Manuel Franco Sevilla
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental high energy flavor physics at collider experiments.

faculty.name: Will Fox
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental plasma physics in the Energy Research Facility.

faculty.name: Brian Clark
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Experimental Astroparticle Physics / High-Energy Neutrino Astronomy
faculty.summary: Detects and studies ultra-high-energy neutrinos using radio-detection techniques across the Askaryan Radio Array, the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, and the Radio Neutrino Observatory-Greenland, spanning data analysis, simulation, and detector development.

faculty.name: Phoebe Hamilton
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental particle physicist on the LHCb experiment at the LHC, studying semileptonic b-hadron decays, lepton-flavor-universality tests, and CP violation, and developing detector electronics for the Upstream Tracker sub-detector.

faculty.name: Xiangdong Ji
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Theorist studying the quark and gluon structure of the nucleon within Quantum Chromodynamics, known for a gauge-invariant decomposition of nucleon spin into quark and gluon spin and orbital angular momentum contributions; also participates in liquid-xenon dark-matter searches.

faculty.name: Ki-Yong Kim
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads the Ultrafast Optical Science group, using ultrashort laser pulses spanning terahertz to X-ray wavelengths to probe laser interactions with atoms, molecules, solids, and plasmas, with a focus on intense-laser generation of strong THz radiation via two-color gas plasmas.

faculty.name: Alicia Kollár
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Chesapeake Associate Professor whose group builds superconducting circuit-QED systems as artificial photonic materials, engineering coplanar-waveguide resonator lattices (including hyperbolic-space lattices and flat bands) to realize quantum simulators of lattice and spin models.

faculty.name: Daniel Lathrop
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Nonlinear Dynamics / Experimental Geophysical & Fluid Physics
faculty.summary: The Nonlinear Dynamics Lab studies turbulent fluid flows, geomagnetism, and superfluid helium, using rotating liquid-sodium experiments (including a 3-meter geodynamo) as laboratory models of Earth's core to understand dynamo generation of planetary magnetic fields.

faculty.name: Norbert Linke
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental group working with trapped atomic ions on quantum information processing, including implementation of quantum algorithms, machine learning for quantum computers, hybrid quantum simulation, and ion-photon quantum networking; directs UMD's National Quantum Laboratory (QLab).

faculty.name: Wolfgang Losert
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the nonlinear dynamics of complex living systems at the convergence of physics, biology, and AI, examining how cell motion and collective behavior respond to physical cues such as surface topography, adhesivity, and cell-cell adhesion, with a focus on cancer biology.

faculty.name: Ryo Mori
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Alford L. Ward Assistant Professor whose group investigates emergent phenomena in quantum materials using advanced multidimensional photoemission spectroscopy, exploring intrinsic states as well as states created through external driving or artificial design.

faculty.name: Maria Mukhina
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops intracellular force nanoprobes with quantitative optical readout and super-resolution imaging to study how cells manage mechanical energy across subcellular structures and orchestrate transitions between functional architectures of the genome.

faculty.name: Min Ouyang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans nanoscale condensed matter physics, materials chemistry, and instrumentation development, focusing on light-matter-spin interactions at the nanoscale using nanomaterials advancement, ultrafast spectroscopy, and new local-probe techniques.

faculty.name: Johnpierre Paglione
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Director of the Maryland Quantum Materials Center, blending materials exploration with the study of quantum phenomena in unconventional superconductors, topological materials, and strongly correlated electron systems.

faculty.name: Christopher Palmer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on the CMS experiment at the LHC, investigating the Higgs boson through di-Higgs searches and contributing to detector development including the CMS MIP Timing Detector, following earlier work on the Higgs discovery and HL-LHC tracker upgrades.

faculty.name: Sasha Philippov
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: First-principles theory and modeling of plasmas around black holes and neutron stars, studying coherent radio emission mechanisms (including Fast Radio Bursts), flares from accreting black holes and merging neutron stars, and particle acceleration in black-hole-powered jets.

faculty.name: Douglas Roberts
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental high-energy physicist whose research centers on the BaBar experiment; has also served as the department's Associate Chair for Graduate Studies.

faculty.name: Steven Rolston
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: AMO physicist and JQI Fellow leading the Rolston ultracold matter group, creating controlled interactions between photons using atoms as intermediaries and developing techniques to manipulate individual and paired photons for light-based quantum technologies.

faculty.name: Jay Sau
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical condensed matter physicist applying topological principles to protected solid-state and cold-atomic systems for quantum information processing, working on topological superconductivity, Majorana fermions, and non-abelian phases for quantum computation.

faculty.name: Nathan Schine
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: AMO physicist whose lab studies the intersection of controlled coherent dynamics and engineered dissipation by interfacing a neutral-atom (ytterbium) array with an optical cavity to simulate hard-to-probe quantum phenomena.

faculty.name: Eun-Suk Seo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads UMD's Cosmic Ray Physics Group, studying the origin, acceleration, and propagation of highly relativistic galactic cosmic rays using balloon- and space-borne detectors through projects such as CREAM/ISS-CREAM, ATIC, AMS, and BESS.

faculty.name: Peter Shawhan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Gravitational-wave physicist working on LIGO who searches for signals from merging black holes and neutron stars, and who helped establish rapid sharing of gravitational-wave event candidates to enable multi-messenger electromagnetic follow-up.

faculty.name: Aaron Sternbach
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental condensed matter physicist whose lab investigates and manipulates quantum materials using nano-optical methods including ultrafast, near-field, and broadband spectroscopy, achieving roughly 10-nanometer spatial resolution across the far- to near-infrared.

faculty.name: Gregory Sullivan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on neutrino detection and cosmic-ray physics through the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole, where he served as spokesperson (2011-2013); his group contributed to the first observations of cosmic neutrinos.

faculty.name: Raman Sundrum
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Theoretical research on extra spacetime dimensions, supersymmetry, and strongly coupled dynamics in particle physics and cosmology; best known for the Randall-Sundrum warped extra-dimension models. Director of the Maryland Center for Fundamental Physics.

faculty.name: Arpita Upadhyaya
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The Upadhyaya lab uses quantitative imaging, biophysical measurements, and computational analysis to study cellular mechanics and the physical forces that let cells sense and respond to their environment, focusing on immune cells and cancer cells.

faculty.name: Edo Waks
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Herbert Rabin Distinguished Professor leading the Quantum Photonics Laboratory, developing quantum technology based on nanoscale photonic and semiconductor devices for quantum computation, communication, and sensing, spanning photonic quantum walks, semiconductor quantum emitters, and solid-state quantum nonlinear optics.

faculty.name: Ronald Walsworth
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Minta Martin Professor leading an interdisciplinary group developing precision-measurement and quantum-sensing tools centered on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, including quantum diamond microscopy, NV-NMR spectroscopy, and dark-matter searches; founding director of the UMD Quantum Technology Center.

faculty.name: Victor Yakovenko
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Condensed matter theorist studying the electronic properties of materials and a pioneer of econophysics, applying statistical-physics methods to economic and financial problems such as income and wealth inequality.

faculty.name: William Phillips
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Works on laser cooling and trapping of neutral atoms, quantum information with single-atom qubits, Bose-Einstein condensates, atoms in optical lattices, and coherent matter-wave optics. Shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics for developing methods to cool and trap atoms with laser light.

funding.note: Admitted with TA or RA; university and Chemical Physics fellowships available

faculty.name: John T. Fourkas
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the dynamics of liquids and interfaces with ultrafast nonlinear optical spectroscopy and develops multiphoton nanolithography for nanofabrication.

faculty.name: Amy S. Mullin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses high-resolution laser spectroscopy to study molecular collisional energy transfer and employs an optical centrifuge to spin molecules into extreme rotational states.

faculty.name: Christopher Jarzynski
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Develops the theory of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics, including the Jarzynski equality and thermodynamics of small systems.

faculty.name: Pratyush Tiwary
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Combines machine learning with statistical mechanics to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations and understand rare events such as conformational changes and crystallization.

faculty.name: Wolfgang Losert
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies collective and dynamic behavior in living cells and in nonlinear physical systems such as granular materials.

faculty.name: Daniel P. Lathrop
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Runs experiments on turbulence, nonlinear dynamics, and magnetohydrodynamics, including a rotating liquid-sodium model of the Earth's geodynamo.

faculty.name: Howard M. Milchberg
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Investigates intense laser-matter interactions, nonlinear optics, and laser-plasma phenomena such as optical filamentation.

faculty.name: William D. Phillips
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Nobel laureate whose research develops laser cooling and trapping of atoms and studies ultracold quantum gases.

faculty.name: Steve Rolston
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies ultracold atoms, ultracold plasmas, and quantum information science using atomic physics techniques.

faculty.name: Edward Ott
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: A leading figure in chaos and nonlinear dynamics, studying complex systems and machine-learning approaches to predicting dynamics.

faculty.name: Ronald L. Walsworth
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops quantum sensing tools based on nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond for precision measurement and imaging across the sciences.

faculty.name: Arpita Upadhyaya
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the physics of cell mechanics and force generation, including how immune cells sense and respond to mechanical cues.

faculty.name: Janice E. Reutt-Robey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses scanning tunneling microscopy and surface science methods to study molecular self-assembly and reactions at interfaces.

faculty.name: Yu-Huang Wang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the chemistry and spectroscopy of carbon nanotubes and DNA-nanotube hybrid materials.

faculty.name: Efrain Rodriguez
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Synthesizes and characterizes solid-state materials such as superconductors and magnetic compounds, using neutron and X-ray scattering.

faculty.name: Johnpierre Paglione
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Experimental condensed matter physicist studying unconventional superconductivity and quantum materials.

faculty.name: Min Ouyang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies nanoscale materials and their optical and quantum properties for nanophotonics applications.

faculty.name: Sang Bok Lee
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops nanostructured materials for electrochemical energy storage and related applications.

faculty.name: Srinivasa R. Raghavan
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the self-assembly of soft materials such as gels, vesicles, and complex fluids.

faculty.name: Leah Dodson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses spectroscopy of gas-phase radicals and clusters to study chemical species relevant to atmospheric and astrochemical environments.

faculty.name: Avik Dutt
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops photonic systems including synthetic dimensions in optical resonators for quantum information and simulation.

faculty.name: Silvina Matysiak
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops multiscale molecular simulations to study the structure and dynamics of proteins, peptides, and membranes.

faculty.name: Thomas E. Murphy
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on photonics, nonlinear optics, and optoelectronic devices, including photonic approaches to computing.

faculty.name: Yanne Chembo
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies nonlinear optical phenomena in microresonators, optical frequency combs, and microwave photonics.

faculty.name: Hong-Zhou Ye
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops electronic structure and quantum chemistry methods to model the properties of molecules and materials.

faculty.name: Daniel Falvey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies photochemical reactions and reactive intermediates using physical organic chemistry approaches.

faculty.name: Lawrence Sita
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops organometallic catalysts for precision polymerization and materials synthesis.

faculty.name: Robert M. Briber
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structure of polymers and soft/biological materials using neutron and X-ray scattering.

faculty.name: Wendell T. Hill III
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Director of the Chemical Physics Program; studies strong-field and ultrafast laser-matter interactions, atomic and molecular dynamics, and quantum optics.

faculty.name: David Fushman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses NMR spectroscopy and computation to study protein structure and dynamics, focusing on ubiquitin signaling and the recognition of polyubiquitin chains.

faculty.name: Andrei Vedernikov
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops organometallic complexes and catalysts for selective C-H functionalization and oxidation reactions.

faculty.name: Alice C. Mignerey
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies nuclear reaction dynamics and heavy-ion collisions to probe the properties and transport of nuclear matter.

faculty.name: Eun-Suk Seo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads balloon- and space-borne experiments such as CREAM/ISS-CREAM to measure high-energy cosmic rays and probe their origin and propagation.

faculty.name: Zhiwei Li
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Leads a group using structural chemistry to synthesize and programmably assemble nanoparticles, studying photon-electron and photon-phonon dynamics for photonics, quantum engineering, and energy applications.

faculty.name: Yanxin Liu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Combines cryo-electron microscopy, cryo-electron tomography, and molecular dynamics simulation to study molecular chaperones such as HSP90 and disease-related protein complexes.

faculty.name: Yu Liu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses laser cooling and optical/ion trapping to prepare ultracold molecules in defined quantum states for studies of quantum chemistry, coherent control, and quantum computation.

faculty.name: Maria Mukhina
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Combines nanobiotechnology, materials science, and new microscopy techniques to study the mechanics of the genome and how cells generate, transduce, and respond to mechanical forces.

faculty.name: Timothy Koeth
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on nuclear engineering, particle accelerators, and reactor physics, including radiation detection and nuclear materials.

faculty.name: Peter Kofinas
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Chair of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering who develops functional polymer materials for energy storage, batteries, membranes, and biomedical applications.

faculty.name: Mohamad Al-Sheikhly
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies radiation-induced chemistry and its use in synthesizing and modifying polymers and biomaterials, including free-radical mechanisms and radiation dosimetry.

faculty.name: John Cumings
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses in situ electron microscopy to study nanoscale transport of charge and heat and the mechanical and magnetic behavior of nanomaterials.

faculty.name: Luz J. Martinez-Miranda
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses X-ray scattering to study the structure and ordering of liquid crystals and their interfaces with nanoparticles and biological systems.

faculty.name: Yifei Mo
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses first-principles computation and machine learning to design materials for energy storage, including solid-state battery electrolytes.

faculty.name: Oded Rabin
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops nanostructured materials for plasmonic sensing, thermoelectrics, and nanoscale energy conversion.

faculty.name: Lourdes Salamanca-Riba
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses transmission electron microscopy to characterize the structure of thin films, nanostructures, and covetic metal-carbon materials.

faculty.name: Mario Dagenais
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops integrated photonic and optoelectronic devices, including semiconductor lasers, waveguides, and solar cells.

faculty.name: Ashwani Gupta
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Studies combustion, high-temperature reacting flows, and energy conversion, including distributed/colorless combustion and waste-to-energy processes.

faculty.name: Panagiotis Dimitrakopoulos
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Uses computational modeling to study the dynamics of cells, capsules, and droplets in flow and other soft-matter and interfacial phenomena.

faculty.name: Ian White
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops optical and paper-based biosensors, including SERS and optofluidic devices, for rapid chemical and biological diagnostics.

faculty.name: James A. Carton
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies ocean circulation, ocean reanalysis, and the role of the oceans in climate variability.

faculty.name: Russell Dickerson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Measures trace gases and aerosols to study air pollution, atmospheric chemistry, and their effects on climate and air quality.

faculty.name: Sumant Nigam
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies large-scale climate dynamics, including ocean-atmosphere interactions, droughts, and decadal climate variability.

faculty.name: Ramalingam Chellappa
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Works on computer vision, pattern recognition, and machine learning methods for image and video analysis.

faculty.name: James Carton
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Physical oceanographer studying ocean dynamics and the ocean's role in climate variability. Developed the widely used SODA ocean reanalysis. Research spans tropical climate (ENSO), global ocean heat content, Arctic climate and sea ice loss, and Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Fellow of the American Meteorological Society.

faculty.name: Russell Dickerson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on atmospheric chemistry and air pollution, including trace gas measurements, satellite remote sensing of atmospheric composition, and the impact of emissions on air quality and climate. Leads field campaigns studying urban and regional air pollution.

faculty.name: Zhanqing Li
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor
faculty.summary: Research on aerosols, clouds, radiation budget, and climate forcing. Uses satellite remote sensing and ground-based measurements to study aerosol-cloud-radiation interactions and their impacts on climate, with extensive work on East Asian and global aerosol systems.

faculty.name: Xin-Zhong Liang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops regional climate models with a focus on land-atmosphere interactions, climate downscaling, and hydrometeorology. Research addresses regional climate predictability, extreme weather events, and climate impacts on water resources and agriculture.

faculty.name: Sumant Nigam
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor and Department Chair
faculty.summary: Studies climate dynamics and atmospheric circulation, focusing on climate variability from seasonal to decadal timescales. Research includes monsoon systems, teleconnections, and the mechanisms driving regional hydroclimate variability and change.

faculty.name: Lars Peter Riishojgaard
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on data assimilation methods, numerical weather prediction, and the design and impact assessment of Earth observing systems. Previously served as Director of the WMO Integrated Global Observing System.

faculty.name: Ross Salawitch
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on stratospheric ozone depletion and recovery, atmospheric chemistry affecting air quality, and the global carbon cycle. Investigates the intersection of atmospheric composition, climate change, and environmental policy.

faculty.name: Ning Zeng
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies climate modeling and the global carbon cycle, including land-atmosphere interactions and biogeochemical feedbacks. Research extends to climate intervention strategies and the role of terrestrial ecosystems in climate regulation.

faculty.name: Da-Lin Zhang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leading expert in mesoscale meteorology and numerical weather prediction. Research focuses on the dynamics and prediction of tropical cyclones, severe convective storms, and heavy precipitation events through high-resolution modeling.

faculty.name: Timothy Canty
faculty.title: Associate Professor, MEES Director
faculty.summary: Research on atmospheric chemistry, including stratospheric and tropospheric ozone, photochemical modeling, and the use of satellite observations to understand atmospheric composition and air quality trends.

faculty.name: Sinead Farrell
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on the cryosphere, using satellite remote sensing (particularly altimetry) to study sea ice thickness, snow on sea ice, and Arctic climate change. Works on satellite mission development for polar observations.

faculty.name: Kayo Ide
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research on data assimilation theory and methods, including Lagrangian data assimilation and observing system design. Applies techniques across geophysical disciplines including atmosphere, ocean, and solid Earth.

faculty.name: Jonathan Poterjoy
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Graduate Program Director
faculty.summary: Develops advanced data assimilation methods for ensemble forecasting and numerical weather prediction, with applications to hurricane prediction and high-impact weather. Research bridges theory and operational forecasting.

faculty.name: Jacob Wenegrat
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies physical oceanography and ocean dynamics, focusing on submesoscale processes, air-sea interaction, and the role of ocean turbulence in climate. Combines theory, numerical modeling, and observational analysis.

faculty.name: Christopher Kenseth
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on atmospheric chemistry focusing on aerosol formation and transformation, particularly secondary organic aerosols. Uses advanced mass spectrometry techniques to characterize aerosol chemical composition and reactions.

faculty.name: Maria Molina
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on climate variability and extremes using machine learning and climate modeling approaches. Investigates predictability of extreme weather and climate events, with a focus on improving understanding of atmospheric processes.

faculty.name: Madeleine Youngs
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Physical oceanographer studying ocean circulation and its role in climate, with emphasis on the Southern Ocean. Uses numerical models and observational tracers to understand ocean ventilation and transport pathways.

faculty.name: Arpita Upadhyaya
faculty.title: Professor of Physics (Biophysics Program Co-Director)
faculty.summary: Upadhyaya's lab studies how cellular mechanics and cytoskeletal forces let cells sense and respond to their physical environment, focusing on the mechanical regulation of biochemical signaling during immune response, cancer, and development. The group uses advanced and single-molecule microscopy, computational image analysis, and biophysical force measurements.

faculty.name: Jeffery Klauda
faculty.title: Professor of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering (Biophysics Program Co-Director)
faculty.summary: Klauda's group uses molecular simulations and thermodynamic modeling to describe the function, dynamics, and physical properties of cellular membranes, developing models of lipid-lipid interactions and membranes ranging from yeast and bacteria to human ocular-lens and neuronal membranes. The lab also studies membrane-associated proteins involved in transport, cell death, and signaling.

faculty.name: Wolfgang Losert
faculty.title: Professor of Physics
faculty.summary: Losert's lab investigates the dynamical properties of complex living systems at the convergence of physics and biology, with a focus on cancer, studying how physical cues such as electric fields and nanotopography guide the motion of individual and collective cells. The group discovered that cell migration can be guided by nanotopography through control of actin-wave dynamics.

faculty.name: Christopher Jarzynski
faculty.title: Distinguished University Professor, Chemistry & Biochemistry / Physics / IPST
faculty.summary: Jarzynski develops theoretical and computational tools for understanding nonequilibrium behavior and estimating thermodynamic properties at the molecular scale, including applications to biophysical problems, artificial molecular machines, and the relationship between thermodynamics and information. He is known for the 1997 Jarzynski equality relating nonequilibrium work to equilibrium free-energy differences.

faculty.name: Pratyush Tiwary
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry / IPST
faculty.summary: Tiwary's group combines equilibrium and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with deep learning to model the thermodynamics and dynamics of complex molecular systems, including the statistical dynamics of rare events and the dynamics of drug unbinding and protein-kinase plasticity for computational drug design. His RAVE method was among the first to use AI to enhance molecular-dynamics sampling.

faculty.name: Silvina Matysiak
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Matysiak's lab uses statistical thermodynamics and coarse-grained molecular modeling to understand how molecular behavior dictates macroscopic properties of biological systems, studying the self-assembly of soft materials such as surfactants, proteins, lipids, and polysaccharides. A particular focus is on molecular mechanisms relevant to neurodegenerative diseases and certain cancers.

faculty.name: Sergei Sukharev
faculty.title: Professor of Biology / IPST
faculty.summary: Sukharev studies the molecules and principles cells use to detect mechanical force, focusing on mechanosensitive ion channels that convert membrane tension into cellular signals. His lab cloned the bacterial large-conductance mechanosensitive channel MscL and continues to dissect the gating mechanisms of MscL and the smaller MscS using electrophysiology, biochemistry, and biophysics.

faculty.name: David Fushman
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry
faculty.summary: Fushman studies proteins as dynamic molecular machines at atomic resolution, focusing on structure, dynamics, and recognition in multi-domain proteins and complexes and on ubiquitin-mediated intracellular signaling. His lab combines NMR and relaxation, small-angle X-ray/neutron scattering, and molecular dynamics, and has developed methods to build and determine 3D structures of defined-length ubiquitin chains.

faculty.name: Theodore Kwaku Dayie
faculty.title: Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry
faculty.summary: Dayie studies RNAs as dynamic signaling molecules and drug targets, probing the structural and dynamic basis of molecular recognition in RNA complexes using isotope (13C/15N/2H) labeling, high-resolution multidimensional solution NMR, and SAXS. His group developed chemoenzymatic labeling technologies that yield sharp NMR signals for large viral RNAs of 20-78 kDa.

faculty.name: Jason Kahn
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry
faculty.summary: Kahn's lab studies the analysis, structure, function, and design of protein-DNA complexes on the 50-1000 bp length scale, best known for work on DNA looping, bending, twisting, and cyclization. Projects use bulk and single-molecule FRET to characterize Lac-repressor-anchored DNA loops and the role of DNA structure in transcription and gene regulation.

faculty.name: Yanxin Liu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry / IBBR
faculty.summary: Liu's lab focuses on the molecular and structural understanding of protein complexes related to human disease, with an emphasis on chaperone-mediated protein folding and translocation into membrane-bound organelles. The group integrates high-resolution single-particle cryo-EM, cryo-electron tomography, and large-scale atomistic molecular dynamics simulation.

faculty.name: Giuliano Scarcelli
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Scarcelli directs the Optics Biotech Lab, where he developed confocal Brillouin scattering microscopy, a label-free, non-contact technique that maps the mechanical properties (stiffness, viscosity) of cells and tissues at the nanoscale without disturbing function. He applies it to how mechanical properties change during aging, wound healing, disease, and tumor metastasis.

faculty.name: Kimberly Stroka
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Stroka's lab explores the role of mechanical forces in physiological and pathological processes, focusing on mechanobiology of the vascular endothelium, cell-cell interactions at the blood-brain barrier during tumor metastasis, and engineered cellular microenvironments for cell adhesion, migration, and division. The group builds in vitro models using microfabricated devices, cell-mechanics tools, and quantitative image analysis.

faculty.name: Gregg Duncan
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Duncan leads the Respiratory Nano Bioengineering Lab, using nanotechnology and bioengineering to understand the lung airway microenvironment and mucus barrier in health and disease and to develop therapies for asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis. His group studies nanoparticle mobility in mucus (including machine-learning-informed prediction) and engineers synthetic mucus biomaterials.

faculty.name: Helim Aranda-Espinoza
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Aranda-Espinoza leads the Cell Biophysics Laboratory, studying how cells respond to external mechanical stresses in healthy and pathological conditions, along with soft matter and the biophysics of membranes and the cytoskeleton. His long-term aim is a fundamental, quantitative understanding of how motile cells adhere, spread, and crawl, focusing on neurons and cells involved in cardiovascular disease.

faculty.name: Peter Nemes
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry
faculty.summary: Nemes develops ultrahigh-resolution, ultrasensitive quantitative mass spectrometry at single-cell and micro-region scales to study the biomolecular mechanisms of development, brain function, aging, and addiction. His lab built single-cell MS instrumentation capable of identifying and quantifying roughly 1,000-2,000 proteins between single embryonic cells and performs subcellular proteomics and metabolomics in vivo.

faculty.name: Brian Pierce
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Cell Biology & Molecular Genetics / IBBR
faculty.summary: Pierce's lab performs computational structural biology focused on modeling and design of immune recognition, including antibodies, T cell receptors, and structure-based vaccine design, using docking and design algorithms such as Rosetta, ZDOCK, and ZAFFI. The group has produced tools including the TCR3D and CoV3D structure databases and the TCRmodel/TCRmodel2 servers for modeling TCR complexes.

faculty.name: Michelle Girvan
faculty.title: Professor of Physics / IPST
faculty.summary: Girvan's research on complex networks sits at the intersection of statistical physics, nonlinear dynamics, and computer science, with biological applications including epidemiology and genetic regulatory networks and recent work at the interface of network science and machine learning. She is a co-namesake of the Girvan-Newman community-detection algorithm.

faculty.name: Joshua Weitz
faculty.title: Professor of Biology (Clark Leadership Chair in Data Analytics)
faculty.summary: Weitz leads the Quantitative Viral Dynamics group, exploring how viruses transform human and environmental health by synthesizing theory, computational simulation, and model-data integration. Research spans quantitative viral ecology, marine viral impacts on the carbon cycle, bacteriophage therapy, microbial ecology and evolution, and infectious disease dynamics.

faculty.name: Catherine K. Kuo
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Kuo directs the Developmental and Regenerative Engineering Laboratory, developing tissue-engineering and therapeutic solutions for tendon injuries, disease, and tendon-related birth defects, informed by mechanisms of embryonic tendon development and scarless healing. Her team studies the mechanobiology of embryonic tendon development to identify regulators of tendon formation for regenerative therapies.

faculty.name: Katharina Maisel
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering
faculty.summary: Maisel leads the MAISEL Lab (Mucosal Associated Immune System Engineering and Lymphatics), integrating materials science, immunology, and mucosal-barrier physiology to design nanoparticles that probe and cross biological barriers such as the lymphatics, interstitial tissue, and mucosal surfaces. The group studies how tissue material properties govern nanoparticle transport to improve vaccines and immunotherapies.

faculty.name: Robert M. Briber
faculty.title: Professor of Materials Science & Engineering
faculty.summary: Briber is an internationally recognized researcher in polymer physics and directs the High Resolution Neutron Scattering Research Program at Maryland. His interests include polymer phase transitions, morphology and structure, the chain conformation of synthetic and biological polymers, and neutron and X-ray scattering characterization of materials.

faculty.name: Jeremy M. Testa
faculty.title: Professor, Chesapeake Biological Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Investigates how biological, chemical, and physical processes interact in coastal ecosystems, focusing on eutrophication, nutrient and oxygen cycling, and ocean acidification through experiments, data analysis, and computational modeling.

faculty.name: Ming Li
faculty.title: Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Uses numerical modeling to study physical oceanography and estuarine and coastal dynamics, including how physical processes drive hypoxia and harmful algal blooms and how climate change and extreme weather affect coastal systems.

faculty.name: Jeffrey C. Cornwell
faculty.title: Research Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies biogeochemistry and nutrient, metal, and sulfur cycling in estuaries and coastal wetlands, including microbial nitrogen removal, oyster-associated nutrient dynamics, and tidal wetland nutrient balances.

faculty.name: Sairah Malkin
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Works to quantify and predict rates and pathways of geochemical cycling in aquatic systems, emphasizing benthic carbon and nutrient processing and sulfur-oxidizing bacteria in sediments.

faculty.name: Greg Silsbe
faculty.title: Assistant Research Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies phytoplankton physiology and photosynthetic processes in marine environments using bio-optical instrumentation and remote sensing, along with tropical limnology.

faculty.name: William Nardin
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Researches the impact of storms and sea level rise on wetland eco-geomorphology and the coupling between river/estuarine hydrodynamics and coastal processes.

faculty.name: Andrea Pain
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies carbon and nutrient processes across the land-sea interface, including coastal groundwater and Arctic processes, and their implications for coastal ecosystems under climate change.

faculty.name: Cindy Palinkas
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Focuses on geological oceanography and sediment transport and deposition in intertidal, fluvial, and estuarine environments, including how tidal marshes respond to environmental change.

faculty.name: Jacob Cram
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies marine microbial communities and how organisms both shape and are shaped by their environment, with emphasis on marine snow particles and ocean biogeochemistry.

faculty.name: Hongsheng Bi
faculty.title: Professor, Chesapeake Biological Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies fine-scale spatial distributions of pelagic organisms and their trophic interactions, developing underwater plankton imaging systems and deep learning techniques for zooplankton assessment.

faculty.name: Carys Mitchelmore
faculty.title: Professor, Chesapeake Biological Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Focuses on the detection of chemical contaminants and understanding their toxicity and implications for ecosystem health.

faculty.name: Mario Tamburri
faculty.title: Professor, Chesapeake Biological Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies the chemical ecology of aquatic organisms, invasive species, and biofouling, and develops coastal sensor and marine monitoring technologies.

faculty.name: Matthew Gray
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Horn Point Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies the physiological response of marine invertebrates to current and future environmental conditions and the ecological benefits these organisms provide.

faculty.name: Xin Zhang
faculty.title: Professor, Appalachian Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Evaluates how socioeconomic and biogeochemical processes affect the global nutrient cycle, addressing agricultural sustainability and nutrient pollution mitigation.

faculty.name: Zach Zbinden
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Appalachian Laboratory (UMCES)
faculty.summary: Studies biodiversity distribution and dynamics from a 'genes to ecosystems' perspective, emphasizing population genomics of freshwater fish and species resilience to climate change.

faculty.name: Andrew H. Baldwin
faculty.title: Professor and Extension Specialist
faculty.summary: Studies plant and ecosystem dynamics in natural and restored tidal and inland wetlands, including plant regeneration, carbon and nitrogen cycling, invasive species, and climate change impacts. Applies ecological knowledge to improve wetland restoration outcomes.

faculty.name: William Bowerman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies avian predators, particularly bald eagles, as biological indicators of environmental health. Examines how contaminants, human activities, and habitat degradation affect wildlife populations using long-term Great Lakes eagle datasets.

faculty.name: Frank J. Coale
faculty.title: Professor & Acting Assistant Dean
faculty.summary: Researches soil phosphorus dynamics and the relationships among agronomic production practices and phosphorus over-enrichment of surface waters. Applies nutrient management science to protect Chesapeake Bay water quality while maintaining agricultural productivity.

faculty.name: Robert L. Hill
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how soil management practices affect water movement through soil and the transport of agricultural chemicals. Develops computational tools for nutrient management planning and environmental risk assessment.

faculty.name: Stephanie Lansing
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads the Bioenergy and Biotechnology Lab, focusing on renewable energy, water quality, and waste treatment. Converts food and agricultural waste into biofuels and bioplastics through anaerobic digestion and thermochemical processes.

faculty.name: Paul T. Leisnham
faculty.title: Professor and Department Chair
faculty.summary: Studies invasion and control of medically important mosquitoes and watershed health using population and community ecology, global change biology, and public health perspectives. Research funded by NSF, USDA-NIFA, EPA-STAR, and NOAA.

faculty.name: Adel Shirmohammadi
faculty.title: Professor, Associate Dean for Research
faculty.summary: Researches watershed-scale environmental modeling and water quality management, including stormwater management in urban and suburban ecosystems and sustainable management of agro-ecosystems. Also studies links between drinking water quality and human cancer incidence via GIS analysis.

faculty.name: Gurpal Toor
faculty.title: Professor and Extension Specialist
faculty.summary: Develops solutions to manage nutrients in the plant root-zone and protect water quality, addressing nitrogen and phosphorus pollution in the Chesapeake Bay by studying release and transport mechanisms in soil-plant-water systems.

faculty.name: Ray Weil
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: International expert in soil management and soil health, especially sustainable agricultural systems in industrial and developing countries. Developed soil microbial biomass and active carbon tests adopted by USDA/NRCS and researchers worldwide.

faculty.name: Stephanie Yarwood
faculty.title: Professor and Graduate Director
faculty.summary: Investigates the microbial ecology of soils across agricultural, wetland, forest, and urban ecosystems, examining how disturbances such as wetland restoration and agricultural management affect microbial communities, nitrogen cycling, greenhouse gas emissions, and carbon storage.

faculty.name: Martin C. Rabenhorst
faculty.title: Ray Weil E-Nnovate Endowed Professor in Soil Science
faculty.summary: Studies the genesis, morphology, and classification of hydromorphic soils in water-saturated environments including non-tidal wetlands and coastal marshes, and develops technology for documenting reducing soil conditions.

faculty.name: Jennifer M. Mullinax
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies threats to wildlife populations and how environmental change affects species, including common tern declines in Maryland, urbanization impacts on bat activity, and habitat modeling for black bears under land-use change.

faculty.name: Brian A. Needelman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Applies pedological concepts to environmental and social problem-solving, including digital soil mapping for precision sustainable agriculture and coastal wetland soil processes related to blue carbon sequestration and methane emissions.

faculty.name: Masoud Negahban-Azar
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Leads the Water Security and Sustainability Lab, focusing on environmental modeling, innovative water reuse solutions, and diagnostic decision support systems for water resource management, including alternative water sources and best management practices in the Atlantic coastal plain.

faculty.name: Mitchell A. Pavao-Zuckerman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Directs the Urban and Built Environment Sustainability Lab, linking ecology, design, policy, and technology to study green infrastructure ecosystem services, tree transpiration effects on urban stormwater, and agrivoltaics that co-locate solar power with agriculture.

faculty.name: Wendy Peer
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Runs the Physiology and Genetics Lab applying biochemistry, genetics, and live cell imaging to study how plants regulate growth and respond to environmental conditions, with focus on specialized compounds such as flavonoids, hormone function, and auxin homeostasis.

faculty.name: David R. Tilley
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Integrates ecological engineering, systems ecology, and innovation to develop solutions for the built and managed environment, including vegetated systems for thermal and water performance, environmental accounting, and use of generative AI for ecological analysis and design.

faculty.name: Lance Yonkos
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Conducts laboratory and field studies on contaminant abundance, transport, fate, and toxicological effects in fresh and estuarine waters and sediments, with focus on microplastics and endocrine-disrupting compounds in the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

faculty.name: Candice M. Duncan
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies transport and characterization of organic and inorganic contaminants in the vadose zone and uses phytoremediation to remove pollutants such as chlorinated VOCs, PFAS, and metals from soil, water, and air.

faculty.name: Travis Gallo
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how urban environments shape species distributions, populations, communities, and behaviors, providing evidence-based solutions that conserve biodiversity while improving urban residents' lives; work spans urban bat conservation and mammal metacommunity dynamics.

faculty.name: Akash Koppa
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Hydrologist and civil engineer working on large-scale, high-resolution atmosphere and land surface modeling; his lab investigates how land-atmosphere feedbacks modulate the formation and expansion of drylands.

faculty.name: Jared Wilmoth
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Leads the Soil Chemical Interfaces (W-SCI) Lab investigating mechanistic connections between soil systems, biogeochemical cycles, and climate, examining how soil chemistry and redox transformations affect global carbon cycling.

faculty.name: Drew S. Coleman
faculty.title: Professor of Earth, Marine and Environmental Sciences; Chair of E3P
faculty.summary: Applies radiogenic isotope geochemistry and geochronology to environmental problems, including understanding contaminant transport, watershed processes, and geological controls on environmental systems. Also researches magma generation and crustal evolution.

faculty.name: Angel Hsu
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Public Policy and E3P
faculty.summary: Director of the Data-Driven EnviroLab. Research uses data science and AI to analyze climate policy and environmental governance, tracking subnational and non-state climate actions globally and examining their effectiveness and accountability.

faculty.name: Andrew J. Yates
faculty.title: Professor of Economics; Director of Graduate Studies, E3P
faculty.summary: Research on environmental and resource economics, studying the design and evaluation of environmental policies, environmental markets, and economic incentives for pollution control and natural resource management.

faculty.name: John Bruno
faculty.title: Professor of Biology
faculty.summary: Research on marine ecology and conservation, focusing on the impacts of climate change on marine biodiversity, particularly coral reef ecosystems. Studies species interactions, community dynamics, and ecosystem resilience.

faculty.name: Todd BenDor
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor of Sustainable Community Design, City and Regional Planning
faculty.summary: Research on sustainable community design and environmental planning, focusing on green infrastructure, ecosystem service markets, and the intersection of urban development and environmental protection.

faculty.name: Clark Gray
faculty.title: Professor of Geography and Environment
faculty.summary: Research on population-environment interactions, studying how environmental change affects human migration and livelihoods, and how demographic change influences environmental outcomes, particularly in developing regions.

faculty.name: Miyuki Hino
faculty.title: Associate Professor of City and Regional Planning
faculty.summary: Research on climate risk, impacts, and adaptation, examining how households and communities respond to flooding and other climate hazards. Studies the effectiveness of policy interventions in reducing climate vulnerability.

faculty.name: Donald T. Hornstein
faculty.title: Thomas F. Taft Distinguished Professor of Law; Director, Center on Risk, Resilience, Energy, and the Environment
faculty.summary: Research spans environmental and energy law, administrative law, and insurance law as applied to climate risk and disaster resilience. Examines legal frameworks for managing environmental risks and promoting clean energy transitions.

faculty.name: Noah Kittner
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Environmental Sciences and Engineering & City and Regional Planning
faculty.summary: Research on energy systems and sustainability, including renewable energy integration, energy storage technology deployment, and the nexus of energy policy, public health, and environmental quality.

faculty.name: Charles Mitchell
faculty.title: Professor of Biology
faculty.summary: Research at the intersection of disease ecology, community ecology, and microbial ecology. Studies how pathogen dynamics are shaped by species interactions and environmental change in plant and natural systems.

faculty.name: Conghe Song
faculty.title: Professor and Chair of Geography and Environment
faculty.summary: Uses remote sensing and ecosystem modeling to study forest dynamics, land use/land cover change, and human-environment interactions. Research spans from local to global scales examining ecosystem responses to environmental change.

faculty.name: Paige Weber
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Economics
faculty.summary: Research on environmental and energy economics, examining the distributional impacts of environmental policies, energy market design, and the relationship between pollution exposure and socioeconomic outcomes.

faculty.name: Jill Stewart
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
faculty.summary: Research on water quality microbiology, studying the ecology and fate of microbial contaminants in water systems. Investigates pathogen transport, detection methods, and the links between environmental quality and public health.

faculty.name: Jason West
faculty.title: Professor of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
faculty.summary: Research on the intersection of air pollution, climate change, and human health using global atmospheric models. Investigates the health impacts of air quality under future climate scenarios and the co-benefits of climate mitigation.

faculty.name: Michael Emch
faculty.title: W.R. Kenan Jr. Distinguished Professor of Geography and Environment; Professor of Epidemiology
faculty.summary: Research on spatial epidemiology and environmental health, using geographic information systems and spatial analysis to understand disease patterns, environmental exposures, and health disparities.

faculty.name: Amanda DelVecchia
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Geography and Environment
faculty.summary: Research on aquatic ecosystem ecology and biogeochemistry, examining carbon and nutrient cycling in streams, rivers, and wetlands. Investigates how disturbance and environmental change alter ecosystem function.

faculty.name: Caela O'Connell
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Anthropology
faculty.summary: Research on environmental anthropology examining human-environment relationships, water governance, and agricultural livelihoods. Studies how communities navigate environmental change and resource management challenges.

faculty.name: Diego Riveros-Iregui
faculty.title: Bowman and Gordon Gray Distinguished Professor of Geography and Environment
faculty.summary: Research on ecohydrology and carbon cycling, studying the coupling between water and carbon cycles in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on tropical highland and montane environments.

faculty.name: Erika Wise
faculty.title: Professor of Geography and Environment
faculty.summary: Research on climatology and dendrochronology using tree rings to reconstruct past climate variability, understand hydroclimate dynamics, and assess water resource vulnerabilities under climate change.

faculty.name: Lindsay L. Dubbs
faculty.title: Research Associate Professor, Institute for the Environment; Director, Outer Banks Field Site
faculty.summary: Research on ecosystem ecology and biogeochemistry of coastal systems, and the environmental effects of marine renewable energy development. Integrates field research with sustainability assessment of ocean energy technologies.

faculty.name: Greg Gangi
faculty.title: Teaching Professor, Associate Director for Clean Technology and Innovation, E3P
faculty.summary: Leads the clean technology and innovation curriculum within E3P, focusing on the business, technology, and policy dimensions of clean energy and sustainability transitions. Bridges academic knowledge with entrepreneurial practice.

faculty.name: Paul Taillie
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Geography and Environment
faculty.summary: Research on landscape and wildlife ecology, studying how land use and environmental change affect wildlife populations and communities, with focus on coastal ecosystems and conservation planning.

programs.university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

faculty.name: Rebecca Fry
faculty.title: Department Chair and Carol Remmer Angle Distinguished Professor in Children's Environmental Health
faculty.summary: Research uses toxicogenomic and systems biology approaches to understand the molecular mechanisms of metal-induced disease and the factors contributing to inter-individual susceptibility to environmental exposures, with emphasis on children's environmental health.

faculty.name: Barbara J. Turpin
faculty.title: Professor, Director of Graduate Studies
faculty.summary: Leading atmospheric chemist studying air pollution formation and human exposure. Research focuses on atmospheric multiphase chemistry, including aqueous-phase formation of secondary organic aerosol in clouds and fog, and the implications for indoor and outdoor air quality.

faculty.name: Gregory Characklis
faculty.title: W. R. Kenan Jr. Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Director of the Center on Financial Risk in Environmental Systems. Research addresses water resource management through economic and financial analysis, developing strategies to manage financial risk in water supply systems under growing demand and climate uncertainty.

faculty.name: Orlando Coronell
faculty.title: Philip C. Singer Distinguished Professor and Associate Chair for Academics
faculty.summary: Research on physical and chemical processes for water and wastewater treatment, with focus on membrane-based separations, advanced sorbent materials, and the removal of emerging contaminants including PFAS from water systems.

faculty.name: Jason D. Surratt
faculty.title: Cary C. Boshamer Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research on atmospheric chemistry focusing on the formation and evolution of secondary organic aerosols. Investigates the chemical mechanisms by which volatile organic compounds are transformed into particulate matter in the atmosphere.

faculty.name: William Vizuete
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses computational models to study atmospheric chemistry and air pollution. Research focuses on understanding ozone and particulate matter formation in urban atmospheres through the integration of chemical mechanisms and atmospheric models.

faculty.name: Jason West
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research at the nexus of air pollution, climate change, and human health. Uses global atmospheric models to quantify the health impacts of air pollution and assess the co-benefits of climate change mitigation for air quality and public health.

faculty.name: Dale Whittington
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on water and sanitation economics with extensive experience in developing countries. Studies household water demand, the economic valuation of water and sanitation improvements, and the planning and financing of water infrastructure.

faculty.name: Joe Brown
faculty.title: Professor, Water Institute Director
faculty.summary: Research on water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) in low-income settings, studying environmental health microbiology and the effectiveness of interventions to reduce enteric infectious disease transmission.

faculty.name: Kun Lu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research uses metabolomics and exposomics approaches to understand how environmental exposures affect human health at the molecular level, developing biomarkers of exposure and effect using advanced mass spectrometry techniques.

faculty.name: Cass T. Miller
faculty.title: Okun Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research on the fate and transport of contaminants in subsurface and porous media systems, developing advanced computational methods to simulate multiphase flow and reactive transport in groundwater environments.

faculty.name: Glenn Morrison
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research on indoor air quality and the chemistry of indoor surfaces, studying how buildings influence human exposure to pollutants through interactions between air, surfaces, and occupants. Focus on semi-volatile organic compounds and exposure science.

faculty.name: Aaron Salzberg
faculty.title: Jennifer and Don Holzworth Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Research and practice at the intersection of water, sanitation, and international policy. Previously served as the first Special Coordinator for Water Resources at the U.S. Department of State, directing U.S. foreign policy on drinking water and water resources.

faculty.name: Noah Kittner
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies energy systems planning and policy with a focus on renewable energy integration, battery storage deployment, and the environmental and equity dimensions of energy transitions. Also holds appointment in City and Regional Planning.

faculty.name: Amanda Northcross
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Director of Undergraduate Studies
faculty.summary: Research on air pollution exposure assessment with focus on household air pollution in low- and middle-income countries. Develops and evaluates low-cost monitoring technologies to characterize personal exposures and inform interventions.

faculty.name: Julia Rager
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Associate Chair for Strategic Initiatives
faculty.summary: Integrates computational toxicology, bioinformatics, and exposure science to understand the health effects of environmental chemical mixtures. Develops data-driven approaches for chemical risk assessment and high-throughput screening.

faculty.name: Marc Serre
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Develops geostatistical and spatial analysis methods for environmental exposure assessment. Research focuses on mapping environmental contaminants in water and air to inform epidemiological studies and risk assessment.

faculty.name: Courtney G. Woods
faculty.title: Associate Professor, MPH Program Director
faculty.summary: Research on environmental justice and health disparities, using community-based participatory research approaches to address environmental health inequities and build community capacity for environmental decision-making.

faculty.name: Musa Manga
faculty.title: Joan Heckler Gillings Endowed Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on sustainable water and sanitation systems for low-resource settings, focusing on non-sewered sanitation, resource recovery from waste, and the intersection of sanitation, public health, and environmental quality.

faculty.name: Ryan Cronk
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on global water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems, focusing on the sustainability of WASH interventions, monitoring and evaluation methods, and the development of resilient environmental health infrastructure.

faculty.name: Michael B. Fisher
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research on global drinking water quality and access, developing and evaluating appropriate technologies for water quality monitoring and treatment in low-resource settings, and studying implementation approaches for lasting WASH improvements.

faculty.name: Paul Watkins
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leading expert in mechanistic toxicology and drug-induced liver injury. Research bridges preclinical toxicology and clinical translation, developing novel biomarkers and approaches for predicting and understanding hepatotoxicity.

faculty.name: David Adalsteinsson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Conducts research spanning biology, interface problems, spatial modeling, algorithm development, and scientific computing visualization tools, developing mathematical and computational methods for spatial modeling in biology with practical applications through his company Visual Data Tools.

faculty.name: Jaime Arguello
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research in aggregated search (integrating results from multiple sources) and search assistance (helping users with complex search tasks), along with information retrieval, data mining, and machine learning. Recipient of an NSF CAREER Award and directs the Interactive Information Systems Lab.

faculty.name: Amina Abdu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Examines AI governance, focusing on how quantification, law, institutions, and values shape the algorithmic implementation of public policy. Collaborates with policy organizations such as the Federation of American Scientists to translate academic findings into policy recommendations.

faculty.name: Iain Carmichael
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical and machine learning algorithms for complex data such as networks, multi-modal data integration, and high-resolution medical imaging, with a focus on computational pathology.

faculty.name: Can Chen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research includes control theory, network science, machine learning, deep learning, tensor algebra, numerical analysis, and computational biology, with a specific focus on using hypergraph learning to interpret biological networks.

faculty.name: Anita Crescenzi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies time constraints and time pressure in exploratory information-seeking, information search for decision-making, metacognitive regulation, and search system design for learning and problem-solving, along with FAIR data practices.

faculty.name: Snehalkumar 'Neil' Gaikwad
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Specializes in responsible AI and policy, examining ethical issues surrounding equity, access, and discrimination in algorithmic system design. Founding Director of the Society-Centered AI Lab with appointments in Data Science and Computer Science.

faculty.name: Hsun-Ta Hsu
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Analyzes the use of artificial intelligence to address societal disparities and improve systems, with research at the intersection of AI and social welfare.

faculty.name: Harlin Lee
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Focuses on learning from high-dimensional data on graphs, networks, or low-dimensional subspaces, with applications in health care and social science. Holds affiliations in Math, Computer Science, and Computational Medicine.

faculty.name: Youzuo Lin
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research areas include physics-informed machine learning, deep learning, and computational methods applied to computational imaging, signal/image analysis, subsurface imaging, medical imaging, cancer detection, and earthquake detection.

faculty.name: Yifei Lou
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of computational mathematics and data sciences, focusing on signal/image recovery from limited measurements constrained by technical or economic limits.

faculty.name: Alex McAvoy
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: An applied mathematician working in evolutionary dynamics, game theory, multi-agent learning, and networks, studying how behaviors spread in populations via heterogeneous social networks.

faculty.name: Santiago Olivella
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Bayesian Methods and Political Data Science
faculty.summary: Develops Bayesian probabilistic models and machine learning techniques to study electoral and legislative politics, bridging political science with data science methodology.

faculty.name: Huaxiu Yao
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Researches building reliable and responsible foundation models from both theoretical and applied perspectives, working on making large-scale AI systems more trustworthy.

faculty.name: Jack Snoeyink
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Professor with joint appointment in Computer Science and SDSS, with expertise in computational geometry and algorithms applied to data science problems.

faculty.name: Justin Sola
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor with joint appointment in Sociology and SDSS, working at the intersection of computational methods and social science research.

faculty.name: Ran Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor joining SDSS in July 2025 from a postdoctoral position at University of Washington. Further research details available via SDSS directory.

faculty.name: Weitong Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Assistant Professor in SDSS who earned a PhD from UCLA. Further research details available via the SDSS directory.

faculty.name: Tarek Zikry
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Faculty joining SDSS in July 2025 from a postdoctoral position at Columbia University's Zuckerman Institute, with membership in the Medical School's Bioinformatics and Computational Biology T32 training program.

faculty.name: Keriayn Smith
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Academic scientist focused on RNA structure and molecular interactions; also founded a nonprofit supporting underrepresented STEM students. Research bridges molecular biology with data science approaches.

faculty.name: David Gotz
faculty.title: Professor, Director of CHIP
faculty.summary: Directs the Carolina Health Informatics Program; researches health informatics with focus on data visualization and visual analytics for clinical data.

faculty.name: Saif Khairat
faculty.title: Professor, Associate Director of CHIP
faculty.summary: Serves as Associate Director of CHIP; researches health and nursing informatics with focus on clinical decision support and system usability.

faculty.name: Melissa Haendel
faculty.title: Sarah Graham Kenan Distinguished Professor, Director of Precision Health
faculty.summary: Researches translational informatics and precision health with focus on ontology development and rare disease diagnostics.

faculty.name: Christopher Shea
faculty.title: Professor, PhD Program Director
faculty.summary: Directs the CHIP PhD program; researches health policy and organizational informatics with focus on patient safety and health services.

faculty.name: Emily Pfaff
faculty.title: Associate Professor, School of Medicine
faculty.summary: Researches clinical informatics with focus on electronic health record data for real-world evidence and chronic disease management.

faculty.name: Danny T.Y. Wu
faculty.title: Associate Professor, School of Information & Library Science
faculty.summary: Researches user-centered design for clinical informatics with focus on data visualization and clinical workflow analysis.

faculty.name: Shahriar Nirjon
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Computer Science
faculty.summary: Researches mobile health and wearable computing with focus on embedded sensor systems and wireless health monitoring.

faculty.name: Rebecca Kitzmiller
faculty.title: Associate Professor, School of Nursing
faculty.summary: Researches nursing informatics and clinical decision support with focus on implementation science and healthcare workflow.

faculty.name: Lukasz Mazur
faculty.title: Professor, School of Information & Library Science / School of Medicine
faculty.summary: Researches clinical informatics and human factors engineering with focus on patient safety and cognitive workload in healthcare.

faculty.name: Kathryn Morbitzer
faculty.title: Associate Professor, School of Pharmacy
faculty.summary: Researches pharmacy informatics and digital health with focus on medication safety and health information technology.

faculty.name: Alexander Tropsha
faculty.title: K.H. Lee Distinguished Professor, School of Pharmacy
faculty.summary: Researches computational chemistry and drug discovery with focus on QSAR modeling and chemical informatics for drug design.

faculty.name: Iain Carmichael
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Pathology & School of Data Science
faculty.summary: Researches biomedical data science and machine learning with focus on pathology informatics and causal inference methods.

faculty.name: Neil Gaikwad
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, School of Data Science / Computer Science
faculty.summary: Researches society-centered AI with focus on health equity, human-centered AI, and social impact of AI in healthcare.

faculty.name: Jingping Nie
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, School of Data Science
faculty.summary: Researches health data science and AI with focus on machine learning and natural language processing for clinical applications.

faculty.name: Di Wu
faculty.title: Core CHIP Faculty
faculty.summary: Researches biostatistics and health data science with focus on statistical methods for clinical and translational research.

faculty.name: Yue (Ray) Wang
faculty.title: Core CHIP Faculty
faculty.summary: Researches medical imaging informatics and AI with focus on computer vision and radiomics for diagnostic imaging.

faculty.name: Alison M. Stuebe
faculty.title: Professor, School of Medicine, Distinguished Professor of Infant & Young Child Feeding
faculty.summary: Researches clinical informatics with focus on maternal and infant health, including breastfeeding and women's health informatics.

faculty.name: Rick Baker
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies structural biology, membrane trafficking, and cancer biology with cryo-EM methods development.

faculty.name: Wolfgang Bergmeier
faculty.title: Professor; Director of Graduate Studies
faculty.summary: Studies the adhesion mechanisms of platelets and neutrophils.

faculty.name: Rebecca Berlow
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies intrinsically disordered proteins, protein-protein interactions, dynamics, and allostery using NMR spectroscopy.

faculty.name: Joshua Boyer
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the molecular basis of RNA function.

faculty.name: Brian M. Button
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies mucus biophysical properties and the mechanisms of mucociliary clearance in the airways.

faculty.name: Sharon Campbell
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the structural biology of regulatory molecules controlling cell growth and cell adhesion.

faculty.name: Charles W. Carter, Jr.
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies protein crystallography, structural polymorphism and function, including aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases.

faculty.name: Xian Chen
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies systems cancer biology and immunology, including protein-protein interaction networks by mass spectrometry.

faculty.name: Venkata Chirasani
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Models biomolecular complexes using molecular dynamics simulations and computational drug design.

faculty.name: Jean Cook
faculty.title: Chair & Professor
faculty.summary: Studies cell cycle control in human cells and genome stability using quantitative single-cell analysis.

faculty.name: Jill Dowen
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies three-dimensional genome organization and gene expression in stem and cancer cells.

faculty.name: Justin Jenson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the biochemistry and structural biology of anti-phage immunity.

faculty.name: Hengming Ke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies X-ray protein crystallography and biochemistry.

faculty.name: Krzysztof Krajewski
faculty.title: Professor; Director of Peptide Synthesis Core
faculty.summary: Works on peptide chemistry and synthesis, histone post-translational modifications, and peptide-based assays.

faculty.name: Brian Kuhlman
faculty.title: Professor; Co-Director, Molecular & Cellular Biophysics Program
faculty.summary: Works on computational protein design, protein therapeutics, and molecular modeling.

faculty.name: Karin Leiderman Gregg
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Uses mathematical modeling of biochemical systems, especially blood coagulation, and computational biofluid dynamics.

faculty.name: William Marzluff
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies histone mRNA processing and histone locus body formation using biochemical and genetic analysis.

faculty.name: Saskia Neher
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies lipoprotein lipase and lipid metabolism using cryo-EM, enzymology, and structural biology.

faculty.name: Dale A. Ramsden
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies chromosome breaks and enzymes that repair DNA, targeting DNA repair for cancer therapy.

faculty.name: Aziz Sancar
faculty.title: Distinguished Professor
faculty.summary: Studies DNA repair enzymology and genomics and the mammalian circadian clock (Nobel laureate).

faculty.name: Chrystal Starbird
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies receptor signaling and protein-protein interactions using crystallography and cryo-EM.

faculty.name: Brian D. Strahl
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies histone modifications and epigenetics using yeast genetics and peptide arrays.

faculty.name: Joshua D. Strauss
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Director of cryo-EM Core
faculty.summary: Studies cellular and structural biology using cryo-electron microscopy.

faculty.name: Qi Zhang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the molecular basis of RNA function and dynamics.
