faculty.name: Fan Zhang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Develops cryptographic and systems solutions for securing blockchains and decentralized systems through trusted hardware and novel consensus mechanisms.

faculty.name: Kazuki Irie
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science

faculty.name: Smita Krishnaswamy
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science (additional appointment in Genetics)

faculty.name: Rex (Zhitao) Ying
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science

faculty.name: Abraham Silberschatz
faculty.title: Sidney J. Weinberg Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Works on database systems, operating systems, bioscience database systems, storage systems, network management, and distributed systems.

faculty.name: Ben Fisch
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Develops cryptographic techniques and proofs for secure, verifiable computation in distributed systems and blockchain applications.

faculty.summary: Studies the physics of climate, geophysical fluid dynamics, phase transitions, and nonequilibrium phenomena in complex materials.

funding.note: Fully funded 5+ yrs (~$52k stipend + full tuition)

faculty.name: P. M. Aronow
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Develops statistical methods for causal inference using experimental and observational data, focusing on design-based approaches, interference in networks, variance estimation, and regression discontinuity designs, with applications in political science, biostatistics, and public health.

faculty.name: Andrew Barron
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of information theory, probability, and statistics, with foundational contributions to universal approximation bounds for neural networks (4,200+ citations), the minimum description length principle, capacity-achieving sparse superposition codes, and high-dimensional function estimation. Recipient of the 2024 Shannon Award.

faculty.name: Joseph Chang
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans stochastic processes, Bayesian inference, Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, evolutionary tree reconstruction, and statistical genetics. Develops Bayesian and MCMC-based approaches for problems in probability and statistics, including change-point problems and applications in autism research.

faculty.name: Yuejie Chi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on theoretical and algorithmic foundations of data science, generative AI, reinforcement learning, and signal processing. Current emphasis on improving the performance, efficiency and reliability of generative AI and decision making in data-intensive but resource-limited settings, including chain-of-thought reasoning, RLHF, and diffusion models.

faculty.name: Mark Gerstein
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Leads a biomedical data science lab bridging vast data generation in biomedical sciences with analytic approaches from statistics and computer science. Works on genome annotation (ENCODE), disease genomics (cancer, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder), macromolecular dynamics, interpretable machine learning, and genomic data privacy including homomorphic encryption.

faculty.name: Anna Gilbert
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research lies at the intersection of analysis, probability, discrete mathematics, and algorithms, focusing on randomized algorithms for signal and image processing, sparse approximation, and compressed sensing. Known for foundational work on Orthogonal Matching Pursuit for signal recovery from random measurements (8,600+ citations).

faculty.name: John Lafferty
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Pursues broad machine learning research from statistical theory to applications, best known for co-inventing Conditional Random Fields (CRFs). Current work focuses on understanding how intelligence and cognition emerge in the brain and in computational systems, spanning NeuroAI, reinforcement learning, abstract reasoning, and neural computation. Director of Yale's Center for Neurocomputation and Machine Intelligence.

faculty.name: Zongming Ma
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Multimodal Data Integration and Spatial Statistics
faculty.summary: Builds statistical foundations and scalable algorithms for joint analysis of weakly linked multimodal data, bridging spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, and digital pathology to turn fragmented, heterogeneous measurements into calibrated inference and actionable biomedical discovery.

faculty.name: Dan Spielman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on spectral and algebraic graph theory, solving Laplacian linear equations, graph sparsification, smoothed analysis of algorithms, and the Kadison-Singer problem. Also develops methods for balancing covariates in randomized experiments via Gram-Schmidt walk design. Director of Yale's Institute for Foundations of Data Science. Recipient of the Godel Prize (2008, 2015) and Nevanlinna Prize.

faculty.name: Yihong Wu
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of high-dimensional statistics, information theory, and optimization, focusing on information-theoretic and computational limits of statistical problems, planted structures in networks and matrices (community detection, graph matching), empirical Bayes, and functional estimation. Co-authoring the forthcoming book 'Information Theory: From Coding to Learning.' IMS Fellow and Sloan Fellow.

faculty.name: Huibin (Harry) Zhou
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans decision theory, high-dimensional statistical inference, covariance and precision matrix estimation, Gaussian mixture models, and spectral clustering. Contributed optimality results for sparse covariance estimation, high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures, and community detection. Former department chair (2012-2021). NSF CAREER Award recipient.

faculty.name: Xiang Zhou
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Statistical Genetics and Genomic Data Science
faculty.summary: Develops statistical and machine learning methods including deep learning and AI for large-scale genetic and genomic data analysis. Works on GWAS, molecular QTL mapping, single-cell and spatial omics to understand how genomic variation influences biological functions and contributes to phenotypic variation in human diseases and complex traits.

faculty.name: Zhou Fan
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Random Matrix Theory and High-Dimensional Statistics
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of mathematical statistics, probability theory, and computational algorithms. Research focuses on random matrix theory, high-dimensional statistics, methods inspired by statistical physics (AMP, replica method), and applications in statistical genetics and cryo-electron microscopy. NSF CAREER Award and Arthur Greer Memorial Prize recipient.

faculty.name: Sekhar Tatikonda
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research spans information theory, communications, networking, and statistical inference. Contributed to feedback channel coding theory using directed information and Markov decision processes, sparse regression codes, network tomography via phylogenetic inference methods, and convergence analysis of belief propagation on graphs with cycles. NSF CAREER Award recipient.

faculty.name: Johan Ugander
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computational Social Science and Network Science
faculty.summary: Uses statistical and computational methods to study social networks, human behavior, and their interplay. Research spans causal inference under network interference, discrete choice theory and preference learning, information diffusion mechanisms, voting systems, and algorithmic social systems including peer review and ranking models. NSF CAREER Award recipient.

faculty.name: Sinho Chewi
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Sampling, Optimal Transport, and Diffusion Models
faculty.summary: Broadly interested in the mathematics of machine learning and statistics, focusing on the complexity of log-concave sampling (writing a book on this topic), optimal transport with applications to variational inference, and theory for score-based diffusion generative models. Works span Langevin algorithms, mean-field variational inference, and information-theoretic lower bounds.

faculty.name: Roy Lederman
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Mathematics of Data Science and Cryo-EM
faculty.summary: Works on mathematics of data science combining inverse problems and unsupervised learning, with key applications in structural biology (cryo-EM heterogeneity analysis and hyper-molecules), Bayesian inference (Riemannian Hamiltonian Monte Carlo), manifold learning (Alternating Diffusion for multi-sensor data), and computational biology (randomized DNA/RNA search algorithms).

faculty.name: Shuangping Li
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Research interests include probability theory, high-dimensional statistics, theoretical machine learning, and the theory of algorithms, with work spanning spectral clustering, Gaussian mixture models, binary perceptron models, and random graph analysis.

faculty.name: Lu Lu
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Scientific Machine Learning and AI for Science
faculty.summary: Leads a group focused on scientific machine learning (SciML) and AI for science (AI4Science), developing theory, algorithms, and software for modeling and simulating physical and biological systems. Research spans physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), neural operators for PDEs, diffusion models for inverse problems, and scientific foundation models.

faculty.name: Theo McKenzie
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Spectral Geometry, Random Graphs, and Random Matrices
faculty.summary: Researches spectral geometry of discrete systems, studying random matrices and random graphs using analytic and probabilistic methods. Key results include the Ramanujan property and edge universality of random regular graphs, optimal eigenvalue rigidity, quantum ergodicity for periodic graphs, and constructions of high-girth near-Ramanujan expanders.

faculty.name: Theodor Misiakiewicz
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Develops theoretical foundations for modern machine learning paradigms, with particular focus on deep learning theory. Research spans kernel and random feature methods in high dimensions, non-convex optimization and landscape analysis, computational learning theory, and random matrix theory. Authored lecture notes on mathematics of deep learning and computational complexity of deep learning.

faculty.name: Omar Montasser
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.sub_field: Theory of Machine Learning and Robustness
faculty.summary: Explores theory and foundations of machine learning with focus on robustness to adversarial examples and distribution shifts. Research spans adversarial robustness, distribution learning and score matching, LLM hallucination detection via chain-of-thought supervision, multi-distribution learning, and transformation-invariant learning.

faculty.name: Zhuoran Yang
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the intersection of machine learning, statistics, game theory, and optimization. Primary focus areas are foundations of reinforcement learning in multi-agent systems where agents interact strategically, and understanding emergent behaviors of large language models during pre-training and post-training and their relationship to model architecture.

faculty.name: Ilias Zadik
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works at the interface of high-dimensional statistics, theory of machine learning, theory of computation, and probability theory. Builds mathematical tools to understand computational and statistical challenges in modern ML, focusing on computational-statistical tradeoffs, phase transition phenomena (All-or-Nothing), connections between statistics and cryptography, and the cost of differential privacy in statistics.

requirements.deadline_display: Dec 1, 2026 (for Fall 2027 entry; ATOC: "Your application must be submitted by the deadline, December 1, for admission in the fall semester.")
requirements.english: Required for international applicants: TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo, with a test date within 2 years of the intended admission term. CU Boulder Graduate School minimums for most programs: TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 115. ATOC does not publish a program-specific minimum. Exemptions exist for citizens of qualifying countries or 1+ year of full-time academic study in the US/a qualifying country.
requirements.admission_model_note: Not explicitly stated as committee vs. advisor-match. ATOC asks applicants to describe "ATOC-specific research interests, including faculty members or scientists with whom you would like to work" in the personal statement. The Academic FAQ notes students may work with advisors outside ATOC (other departments, CIRES/INSTAAR/LASP, NCAR/NOAA) but must then have a co-advisor who is an ATOC core or research faculty member.

funding.note: ATOC states: "Almost all admitted doctoral students are offered financial support from the department in the form of a Teaching Assistant (TA) position or from an advisor's research grant as a Research Assistant (RA) position." Positions include tuition remission of 9+ credit hours per semester, ~90% of health insurance costs, most student fees, and a monthly stipend. Incoming PhD students are supported at 50% (20 hours/week) during the first fall and spring semesters and typically work 100% as an RA for 3 months in the summer. 2026-2027 annual salary is no less than $48,870 (pre-comps) to $51,450 (post-comps). No explicit multi-year guarantee is published, so status is Unknown/Verify.

requirements.contact_note: No official page explicitly tells applicants to contact faculty before applying. The application instructions do ask applicants to name faculty members or scientists they would like to work with in the personal statement.
requirements.duration: Unknown/Verify (ATOC publishes 36 credit hours of coursework plus 30 dissertation hours, a written Part I comprehensive exam normally taken in the second year and an oral Part II normally in the third year, but does not state a typical time-to-degree)

requirements.fee_display: $85 non-refundable (OSU catalog). A domestic/international split was not stated on an official page.

TOEFL institution code 4586; scores valid 2 years; requirement waived for degree-holders from OSU's listed English-speaking countries.
requirements.admission_model_note: CEOAS states that a faculty member's agreement to serve as research mentor is required before admission, and instructs applicants to identify and contact potential mentors before applying.

funding.note: CEOAS states: "Graduate teaching or research assistantships provide a monthly stipend, tuition remission and subsidized health insurance." Applicants are advised to indicate interest in both GTA and GRA positions to maximize their chances. All materials must be submitted by the Dec 15 deadline to be considered for support (domestic and international alike). Response deadline for funded offers is April 15. No explicit multi-year guarantee is published, so status is Unknown/Verify.

requirements.contact_note: Strongly encouraged and effectively required: "Start researching possible faculty mentors early and be persistent... Then contact them via email or telephone to let them know you are applying and you are interested in their research." A faculty member's agreement to serve as research mentor is required before admission. Note that every CEOAS faculty profile carries an official "Graduate students: Accepting for advising / Not accepting at this time" flag — the recruitment status on each advisor card below comes from that flag, as fetched 2026-07-15.

faculty.name: Dawn Barlow
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (Senior Research), Marine Mammal Institute
faculty.summary: Studies the ecology and conservation of pelagic predators such as whales, dolphins, porpoises and seabirds, asking what drives when and where they are found and how their distributions overlap with human activities. Uses species distribution modeling, spatial statistics, bioacoustics and oceanographic data at the intersection of biological oceanography, ecology and applied conservation management.

faculty.name: Andrew Barnard
faculty.title: Associate Professor (Senior Research)
faculty.summary: His official CEOAS profile lists no research description beyond his title and Oceanography unit affiliation.

faculty.name: Jack Barth
faculty.title: University Distinguished Professor of Oceanography
faculty.summary: Works on coastal ocean dynamics, coastal marine ecosystems, hypoxia, inner continental shelf dynamics, flow-topography interactions and eastern boundary currents and their associated jets and eddies. Uses high-resolution observations from the inner continental shelf to the adjacent deep ocean in an eastern boundary current upwelling system, and develops ocean observing systems.

faculty.name: Kim Bernard
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Seeks to understand how natural and anthropogenic forces influence plankton community structure and trophic interactions in marine pelagic ecosystems, with a research focus on polar zooplankton ecology. Leads the Zooplankton Ecology Lab studying how climate change and other anthropogenic disturbances alter zooplankton ecology at individual, population and community levels.

faculty.name: Kristen (Caison) Buck
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research focuses on the interface between marine chemistry and ocean ecosystems, with particular emphasis on the role of metal-binding organic ligands in the cycling and bioavailability of trace metals including iron, copper and nickel. Iron is an essential micronutrient whose scarcity limits primary productivity across large regions of the global ocean, while copper is a common anthropogenic contaminant to estuaries and the coastal ocean.

faculty.name: Lorenzo Ciannelli
faculty.title: Professor, Associate Dean for Graduate Programs
faculty.summary: Primary research focus is fisheries oceanography and marine ecology, studying the causes of temporal and spatial variation of marine populations as well as the management implications of the factors involved. A substantial fraction of the work revolves around early life stages of fish, alongside adult stage ecology and predator-prey trophic interactions in marine ecosystems.

faculty.name: Byron Crump
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies aquatic microbial ecology in marine, estuarine and freshwater ecosystems, including bacterial and archaeal biogeography, organic matter and nutrient cycling, microbial food web structure, and the composition and development of microbial communities. Also examines the influence of hydrodynamics and particle cycling on microbial activity.

faculty.name: Jesse Cusack
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies small to mesoscale ocean processes such as turbulence, flows over topography, internal waves and eddies.

faculty.name: Edward Dever
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research interests include cross-shelf exchange processes, the analysis and prediction of Lagrangian transport, and air-sea interaction, using analysis of physical oceanographic and meteorological data (primarily moored time series and surface drifters) and analytical models. Has played a leadership role in the design, construction and operation of the NSF Ocean Observatories Initiative.

faculty.name: Emily Eidam
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the transfer of sediment through riverine and coastal environments, as well as short-timescale depositional histories from fortnightly to centennial timescales. Much of this work is centered in the Arctic and sub-Arctic, where rapidly changing environmental conditions drive changes in how sediments are dispersed through fluvial systems and deposited and reworked on continental shelves.

faculty.name: Jennifer Fehrenbacher
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Interim Program Director for Ocean, Earth, and Atmospheric Sciences Graduate Program
faculty.summary: Combines trace element and stable isotope geochemistry, biomineralization and marine biology, developing and using proxies (primarily trace elements in marine calcifiers) to reconstruct ocean circulation, temperature and chemistry in the past. Asks how marine calcifiers make their shells and how they control trace element/Ca ratios relative to seawater, which underpins the use of those ratios as paleo-proxies.

faculty.name: Melanie Fewings
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on observational coastal physical oceanography and meteorology.

faculty.name: Jonathan Fram
faculty.title: Associate Professor (Senior Research), OOI Endurance Array Project Manager
faculty.summary: Co-PI and Project Manager for the Endurance Array portion of the Ocean Observatories Initiative; his field of research is environmental fluid mechanics. Previously delineated physical processes that affected nutrient dynamics in biogeochemical hotspots including kelp beds, coral reefs, Arctic lakes and vegetated tidal marshes.

faculty.name: Amrapalli Garanaik
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (Senior Research)
faculty.summary: Works on geophysical and environmental fluid dynamics, with a focus on turbulent mixing and transport in oceanic flows and their critical impact on Earth's climate and ecosystems.

faculty.name: Jessica Garwood
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies small-scale physical-biological interactions in the ocean, especially their implications for transport of plankton or sediment.

faculty.name: Miguel Goñi
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Seeks to better understand the cycling of natural organic matter in the earth's surface, mainly in aquatic environments such as oceans, estuaries, rivers, groundwater and lakes, and to elucidate the role that organic matter plays in the global biogeochemical cycles of major elements such as carbon, oxygen and nitrogen. Ongoing research includes organic matter cycling in river-dominated ocean margins including deltas and estuaries, and factors controlling the generation and export of organic matt

faculty.name: Burke Hales
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on biogeochemical oceanography, including ocean-margin carbon cycling and the processes impacting the state of aqueous carbonate chemistry in estuarine and coastal waters and their effects on ocean acidification and hypoxia. Also analyzes the physics, biology and chemistry of the coastal and surface ocean using high-speed sampling and analysis systems, and develops sensors for robust measurement of ocean chemistry.

faculty.name: Michael Harte
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: A marine geographer who studies sustainable management of marine resources. Academic research addresses fisheries policy and the wider subject of sustainable management of marine resources, with interdisciplinary interests in rights-based fishery management systems, capacity building, co-management of coastal marine resources, marine ecosystem services and marine spatial planning.

faculty.name: Samara Haver
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (Senior Research), CIMERS
faculty.summary: Uses passive acoustic monitoring to understand underwater environments and marine species, with a special focus on soundscapes and ocean noise.

faculty.name: Lauren (Laurie) Juranek
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on dissolved gases, isotope biogeochemistry, the marine biological pump and the marine carbon cycle. Projects include late-season productivity, carbon and nutrients in a changing Arctic, model-driven investigations of oceanic transition zones (SCOPE-Gradients), and Southern Ocean Carbon and Climate Modeling (SOCCOM).

faculty.name: Maria Kavanaugh
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works on seascape ecology, remote sensing and global change.

faculty.name: P. Michael (Mike) Kosro
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies coastal oceanography, shelf/deep-sea exchange processes, eastern boundary currents (including the California and Peru/Chile systems), remote sensing, ocean acoustics and ocean circulation.

faculty.name: Andone Lavery
faculty.title: Executive Director of the Gaulke Center for Marine Innovation and Technology
faculty.summary: Her official CEOAS profile lists no research description beyond her title and Oceanography unit affiliation.

faculty.name: Astrid Leitner
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the impacts of abrupt and complex bathymetry across scales on the ecology and behavior of marine animals, with a special focus on the deep sea.

faculty.name: Jim Lerczak
faculty.title: Professor and Associate Dean for Research
faculty.summary: Works on coastal physical oceanography including the study of internal tides, high-frequency internal waves and circulation in the vicinity of fronts; estuarine oceanography including the dynamics that drive three-dimensional circulation and the mechanisms that transport and disperse materials within estuaries; and physical/biological interactions which influence larval dispersal.

faculty.name: Ricardo Letelier
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the scales of response of marine pelagic microorganisms, populations and communities to environmental perturbations, and the role of these responses on biogeochemical cycles, primary productivity, nitrogen fixation, photosynthesis and chlorophyll passive (solar-induced) fluorescence, along with the physical and chemical factors controlling these processes.

faculty.name: Ricardo Matano
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on large-scale ocean circulation, the dynamics of western boundary currents, ocean modeling, geophysical fluid dynamics and the circulation in the Southern Ocean. Specific interests include the low-frequency variability of the South Atlantic and South Indian Ocean circulation, interocean exchanges, and the shelf circulation in the southwestern Atlantic.

faculty.name: Erin McParland
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses metabolomics and other techniques to understand the cycling of carbon by marine microbes.

faculty.name: David Mellinger
faculty.title: Professor (Senior Research)
faculty.summary: His official CEOAS profile lists no research description beyond his title and Oceanography unit affiliation.

faculty.name: Tuba Ozkan-Haller
faculty.title: Dean and Professor
faculty.summary: Works on near-shore circulation modeling, data assimilation in the near-shore region, time-series analysis techniques, water-wave propagation, sediment suspension and transport, and evolution of the near-shore morphology. Projects include prediction of low-frequency motions in the near-shore zone and shear instabilities of the surf-zone long-shore current.

faculty.name: Brodie Pearson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies the physics of mixing processes (i.e. turbulence) in the ocean, develops new ways to add this mixing to computer models of the ocean, and assesses the impacts of this mixing on the Earth system and its climate.

faculty.name: Kipp Shearman
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Studies physical processes in the coastal ocean, and is most interested in understanding the dynamics of the evolving structure of the density field over the shelf, how it is affected by external forcing and how it in turn affects the circulation within the coastal ocean. The approach is observational, using innovative sampling techniques such as Autonomous Underwater Vehicles coupled with modeling and analysis.

faculty.name: Yvette Spitz
faculty.title: Professor,  Program Director for Oceanography, Oceanography Unit Chair
faculty.summary: Investigates the main pathways in marine ecosystems and develops coupled physical-biological models. Uses data-assimilative models in conjunction with observations from long-term time series and ocean color data to modify model pathways and estimate model parameters and errors for the North Pacific carbon cycle, and models ecosystem response to upwelling off the Oregon coast.

faculty.name: George Waldbusser
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on benthic ecology and sediment biogeochemistry: the role of organisms in modifying physical and biogeochemical processes in sediments, species interactions in sediments, coastal and estuarine acidification effects on bivalves, the importance of benthic habitats in biogeochemical cycling, and tidal flat ecology.

faculty.name: Greg Wilson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Research involves the physics of the nearshore coastal ocean including waves, currents and sediment transport, using new observational and modeling tools and often a probabilistic approach. Work includes measuring statistics of fluid-sediment interaction at the seabed using acoustics, instrumenting beaches to measure shoaling and breaking waves, and using beach cameras with model-data assimilation to improve forecasts of nearshore currents such as rip currents.

faculty.name: Edward (Ed) Zaron
faculty.title: Associate Professor (Senior Research)
faculty.summary: Works on ocean modeling and data assimilation, satellite altimetry, and geophysical fluid dynamics.

faculty.name: Tamara Baumberger
faculty.title: Assistant Professor (Senior Research)
faculty.summary: Studies the gas chemistry of hydrothermal vents and methane seeps with a special interest in the carbon cycle and noble gas chemistry.

faculty.name: Jeffrey Beeson
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Uses seafloor and subseafloor imaging to explore the dynamics of plate boundary tectonics, methane seepage and submarine volcanism.

faculty.name: Jessica (JC) Creveling
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Examines sea-level change throughout Earth's ice ages and the attendant paleoceanographic, paleoclimatological and paleoecological shifts. Current work integrates field observation of the sedimentary record with global geophysical numerical models to refine estimates of past sea level heights for both warmer and colder intervals in Earth's history.

faculty.name: Kevin Konrad
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Works on noble gas geochronology, marine geology, mantle geodynamics and volcanism.

faculty.name: Mitchell Lyle
faculty.title: Professor (Senior Research)
faculty.summary: Reconstructs Cenozoic-Holocene Earth systems from sediment composition and deposition patterns. Current research includes Miocene equatorial Pacific paleoproductivity from XRF scanning, ocean carbon cycling, geochemical tracers of sediment flux, redistribution and sorting, Neogene evolution of Arabian Sea sedimentation (IODP Expedition 355), and seismic stratigraphy and pelagic sedimentation.

faculty.name: Peter Ruggiero
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on coastal geomorphology (nearshore morphodynamics, modeling coastal evolution, large-scale coastal behavior), coastal hazards (impact of climate change and variability on coastal change and flood hazards, modeling the coupled human-natural system) and nearshore processes (swash processes, dynamics of high-energy dissipative beaches).

faculty.name: Joseph Stoner
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on sediment magnetism including paleomagnetism, environmental magnetism, geomagnetism, sedimentology, stratigraphy and paleoclimatology. Current research reconstructs space/time patterns of the Holocene geomagnetic field in the Arctic, the Gulf of Alaska, Iceland, East Greenland and the North Atlantic, and the late Pleistocene paleomagnetic record from the Chilean Margin.

faculty.name: Simon de Szoeke
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Interested in atmosphere-ocean interaction and its influence on the climate, with much of the research focused on the tropics, where the most sunlight results in warm sea surface temperature and strong fluxes of heat from the ocean to the atmosphere, mostly in the form of evaporation.

faculty.name: Jennifer (Jenny) Hutchings
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Research interests revolve around sea ice dynamics and mechanics, with active field work supporting validation and development of rheological models of sea ice deformation for climate investigations and ice drift and dispersion forecasting. Interests include ocean-atmosphere interactions as modified by an evolving ice cover, and understanding how changing mechanical properties of the ice pack relate to feedbacks in the arctic climate system.

faculty.name: Jonathan Nash
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Explores the physics of turbulence and mixing as key to understanding ocean dynamics, using innovative instrumentation, detailed analysis and simple dynamical models to understand the generation and evolution of turbulence and quantify irreversible fluxes of heat, salt, biology, chemicals and momentum. Applications include buoyant ice-melt plumes that bring heat toward glaciers, heat and carbon fluxes controlling air-sea exchange, turbulent diffusion of nutrients and plankton, and sediment trans

faculty.name: Larry O'Neill
faculty.title: Associate Professor and Director of the Oregon Climate Service
faculty.summary: Studies the influence of air-sea interactions on climate variability of the North Pacific and North America, the variability of surface winds over the ocean and their consequences for ocean circulation and air-sea heat and momentum exchange, the influences of ocean currents and temperature on air-sea interactions, and the relationship between surface winds, sea surface height and surface ocean currents.

faculty.name: Erin Pettit
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on glacier and ice sheet dynamics including ice-shelf stability, ice/ocean interactions, ice rheology and deformation, ice-core climate history, water percolation in firn, englacial and subglacial water movement, and applied geophysical methods in ice such as seismics, acoustics, borehole logging and radar.

faculty.name: Roger Samelson
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on the fluid dynamics and thermodynamics of the ocean and atmosphere, coastal and arctic meteorology, and nonlinear dynamics of geophysical fluids.

faculty.name: Andreas Schmittner
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on climate change, ocean biogeochemical cycles, interactions in the climate system, paleoclimate and ocean circulation. Projects include mixing and the meridional overturning circulation in the modern and glacial ocean, Antarctic ice sheet-ocean-carbon cycle interactions during the last deglaciation, modeling the ocean distribution of neodymium isotopes, and quantifying the modern and glacial ocean's carbon cycle including isotopes.

faculty.name: Eric Skyllingstad
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: Works on upper ocean turbulence, mesoscale coastal internal waves and ocean-atmosphere coupling, including simulation of coastal circulations, modeling of turbulence under sea ice and leads, and resonant interaction between surface winds and upper ocean turbulence.

faculty.name: Seth Zippel
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Studies how the ocean and the atmosphere interact using field measurements from a diverse set of regions including estuaries, the open ocean and the Arctic, spanning waves, wave breaking, wave/current and wave/ice interaction, turbulence and boundary layers.

faculty.name: James Watson
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Works on complex adaptive systems, environmental science, social-ecological systems and quantitative analyses, including seascape ecology, marine spatial planning and coastal vulnerability.

requirements.deadline_display: Dec 1, 2026 (for Fall 2027 entry; APPM: "The application deadline for domestic AND international applicants is December 1st every year, for admissions in the following fall semester." The PhD program has no spring admissions.)
requirements.english: Required for international applicants: TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo exam scores. APPM department minimum TOEFL: internet-based (iBT) 100, computer-based 250, paper-based 600. The department publishes no IELTS or Duolingo minimum (Unknown/Verify). The TOEFL/IELTS requirement is waived if the applicant's native language is English, or if the applicant has completed at least one year of full-time study at a US institution (or an institution in a country where English is the native language) at the time of submission or within two years from the desired admission term.
requirements.admission_model_note: Reviewed by the department's graduate/admissions committee; applicants are generally notified of the graduate committee's decision by April 1. No advisor pre-match is required: the catalog states "A PhD student can be advised by core faculty or co-advised by an affiliate involved in applied mathematics." The department reports 20 core faculty and 25 affiliated faculty from other academic departments and colleges. Applicants not accepted to the PhD program are considered for the MS program.

funding.note: APPM Graduate FAQ: "Do all incoming graduate students automatically receive financial support from the department? No, but most graduate students enter the program with either a teaching assistantship or a research assistantship." It also states that doctoral candidates do not need to request support in the personal statement because "All doctoral candidates are considered for funding and sent offers of support once admitted." No guaranteed multi-year funding package, stipend figure or tuition-remission detail is published on the department pages, so status is Unknown/Verify.

requirements.contact_note: No official APPM page tells applicants to contact faculty before applying, and the personal-statement guidance does not ask applicants to name faculty; it asks how you became interested in applied mathematics, how your background prepared you for graduate study, and your educational and professional goals. The "Applying to Graduate School" page advises applicants to "do your homework with regard to understanding our graduate program" and, in the personal statement, to "be sure to address why you want to join our department" - but it does not mention contacting faculty.

faculty.name: Adrianna Gillman
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: Her stated research interests are fast algorithms such as the Fast Multipole Method and fast direct solvers; integral equation formulations for the mathematical modeling of physics and other real world applications; wave scattering, acoustics and variable media; and techniques for handling challenging geometries such as corners, edges and periodic domains.

faculty.name: Andrew Grace
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: He joined the Department of Applied Mathematics in 2025, after concurrent NSERC and ND-ECI postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Notre Dame and graduate work at the University of Waterloo. His research interests lie broadly in computational fluid mechanics, motivated by applications of turbulent and quasi-turbulent fluid flows, specifically relating to the transport of heat and other materials in natural systems.

faculty.name: David Bortz
faculty.title: Professor in Applied Mathematics / Professor in Computer Science / IQ Biology Graduate Faculty / RASEI Affiliate / Colorado COVID-19 Modeling Team
faculty.summary: His group develops and analyzes computational methods for weak-form scientific machine learning, a class of methods robust to substantial noise and highly computationally efficient. Modeling applications include system identification, governing equation discovery, coarse-graining and reduced-order modeling, frequently applied to biological systems including collective and individual motion in wound healing, structured population dynamics, and disease ecology and epidemiology. More recently the group has expanded applications to atmospheric fluid models and computational plasma physics in the context of fusion.

faculty.name: Eduardo Corona
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: His stated research interests are fast algorithmic frameworks for large-scale physics simulation, fast direct solvers and hierarchical decomposition methods, scientific data compression methods, integral equation formulations for numerical PDE in fluids, active soft matter, wave scattering and elasticity, and singular and near-singular integration methods for integral kernels.

faculty.name: Eric Vance
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: No research description is published on his official APPM profile, which lists only his title, contact details and links to his CV, Google Scholar page and teaching. The department tags him under the Statistics and Data Science research area. Specific research topics: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: François G. Meyer
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computational Mathematics / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: No research description is published on his official APPM profile, which lists only his title and contact details. The department tags him under the research areas Computational Mathematics and Statistics and Data Science. Specific research topics: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Gregory Beylkin
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: His APPM profile lists his research interests as numerical analysis, signal processing, wave propagation, inverse problems and quantum chemistry.

faculty.name: Ian Grooms
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.summary: His research interests encompass ocean model development, the development of new data assimilation methods, and the theory of geophysical fluid dynamics and turbulence. He received his PhD in Applied Mathematics from CU Boulder in 2011, was a postdoc at the Courant Institute at NYU from 2011 to 2015, joined the APPM faculty in fall 2015 and has been tenured since 2022. He co-chairs the CESM Ocean Model Working Group and is president-elect (2025-2026) of the Nonlinear Geophysics section of AGU.

faculty.name: James Curry
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.summary: The department tags him under the Physical Applied Mathematics research area. His APPM profile is a biography (PhD in Mathematics from UC Berkeley with Oscar Lanford; professor at CU Boulder since 1989; President's Teaching Scholar since 1993; Chair of Applied Mathematics 2003-2012; NSF Division of Mathematical Sciences Program Director 2012-2014) and does not state current research topics. Specific research topics: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: James Meiss
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics / Physical Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: His APPM profile lists his research interests as nonlinear phenomena and physical applied mathematics. The department tags him under the research areas Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics and Physical Applied Mathematics. No further research detail is given on the official profile.

faculty.name: Juan G. Restrepo
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics / Mathematical Biology
faculty.summary: His APPM profile lists his research interests as dynamics on and structure of complex networks, synchronization, nonlinear dynamics and chaos, spread of information and disease in complex social networks, and criticality in functional brain networks.

faculty.name: Manuel E. Lladser
faculty.title: Professor / Associate Director of the Master of Science in Applied Mathematics (MSAM) Program
faculty.sub_field: Stochastic Processes and Applications / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: His APPM profile lists his research interests as probability (theory and applications), computational biology, mathematical machine learning, and statistics.

faculty.name: Mark Hoefer
faculty.title: Department Chair / Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics / Physical Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: His research is in physical applied mathematics motivated by real world problems, generally in the field of nonlinear waves, with a focus on two areas: the fluid dynamics of dispersive media with accompanying wave excitations including dispersive shock waves (DSWs) and solitary waves, and the dynamics of ferromagnetic media in nanomagnetism. Methods employed include mathematical modeling, analysis, asymptotics, Whitham modulation theory, numerical analysis, and in-house experiment in the Dispersive Hydrodynamics Lab.

faculty.name: Mark J. Ablowitz
faculty.title: CU Distinguished Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics / Physical Applied Mathematics
faculty.summary: His APPM profile lists his research interests as nonlinear phenomena and physical applied mathematics. The department tags him under the research areas Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics and Physical Applied Mathematics. No further research detail is given on the official profile.

faculty.name: Nancy Rodriguez
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Applied Nonlinear PDEs and Dynamics / Mathematical Biology
faculty.summary: Her research concentrates on nonlinear partial differential equations, specifically those pertinent to urban crime, segregation, biological aggregation, chemotaxis and ecology, using mathematical modeling, numerical analysis and mathematical analysis to study the intricacies of social, biological and ecological systems. Her contributions have expanded the theoretical understanding of non-local PDEs and have yielded insights into crime dynamics and prevention, social segregation and pest control. She obtained her doctoral degree from UCLA, mentored by Andrea Bertozzi.

faculty.name: Stephen Becker
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Computational Mathematics / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: His group works on information extraction from datasets, in a hybrid field combining applied math with computer science and signal processing techniques. Specific topics include optimization (first-order methods, quasi-Newton methods, primal-dual algorithms, convex analysis), problems from computational imaging and semi-definite programs, and mathematical applications such as compressed sensing, matrix completion and variants including robust PCA, and non-negative matrix factorization.

faculty.name: Vanja Dukic
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Statistics and Data Science / Mathematical Biology
faculty.summary: Her APPM profile lists her research interests as statistics, mathematical biology, ecology and environmental statistics, and risk modeling and insurance.

faculty.name: William Kleiber
faculty.title: Professor / Director of the Master of Science in Applied Mathematics (MSAM) Program
faculty.sub_field: Statistics and Data Science / Mathematical Geosciences
faculty.summary: He is an applied statistician with general research interests in spatial statistics and mathematical geosciences. Recent work involves multivariate spatial processes, extreme weather risk analysis, stochastic weather generators, statistics for energy science, and emulation and uncertainty quantification for geophysical models. He received his PhD in Statistics from the University of Washington in 2010 and spent two years as a postdoctoral researcher at NCAR's Institute for Mathematics Applied to Geosciences.

faculty.name: Ye He
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Her official APPM profile states only that Ye He will begin with the Department of Applied Mathematics in Academic Year 2026-2027. No research description and no departmental research-area tag are published on the official page, so her research area is Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Yu-Jui Huang
faculty.title: Associate Professor
faculty.sub_field: Stochastic Processes and Applications / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: His research is focused on mathematical finance and applied probability. It involves stochastic analysis, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and the theory of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear PDEs.

faculty.name: Zachary Kilpatrick
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.sub_field: Mathematical Biology / Stochastic Processes and Applications
faculty.summary: His research group works to identify neural mechanisms underlying cognition by developing and validating mathematical models, linking observed individual and collective behaviors to a diversity of constrained cognitive strategies and developing new mathematical and computational tools for solving, fitting and identifying nonlinear and stochastic models of biological inference and its underlying neural activity representations. Research interests include decision making and Bayesian inference, dynamics of collective behavior (especially foraging), spatiotemporal dynamics of neural circuit models, and stochastic processes and first passage time methods.

faculty.name: Aaron Clauset
faculty.title: Professor, Department of Computer Science (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.sub_field: Computational Science / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: His CU Computer Science profile describes him as an internationally recognized expert on network science, data science and complex systems, and recipient of the 2016 Erdos-Renyi Prize in Network Science. His group's page describes broad, multidisciplinary research on networks, dynamics and data in complex systems. He is also affiliated with the BioFrontiers Institute and is External Faculty at the Santa Fe Institute.

faculty.name: Alireza Doostan
faculty.title: Professor, Ann and H.J. Smead Department of Aerospace Engineering Sciences (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.sub_field: Computational Mathematics / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: His UQ and Data-Driven Modeling Group page (within the Aerospace Mechanics Research Center, Department of Aerospace Engineering Sciences) states the lab is led by Professor Alireza Doostan and that the group actively develops novel uncertainty quantification and data-driven methods and applies them to engineering problems.

faculty.name: Ankur Gupta
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Chemical and Biological Engineering profile lists his education (PhD, Chemical Engineering, MIT, 2017) and awards including the 2025 Soft Matter Lectureship, C&EN Talented 12 (2025) and an AFOSR Young Investigator Award (2025). A research-interest statement was not published on the official profile: specific research topics Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Bri-Mathias Hodge
faculty.title: Professor, Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His official page states he is a Professor and Associate Chair for Research and Graduate Education in the Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering, and an Associate Director and Fellow of the Renewable and Sustainable Energy Institute (RASEI), and that he was formerly a Chief Scientist at NREL. His group page is titled Power & Energy Systems. Further research detail: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Carlos Brunet Martins-Filho
faculty.title: Professor of Economics (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His official CU-hosted page lists him as Professor of Economics and Professor of Applied Mathematics (affiliate) at the University of Colorado at Boulder. The page does not publish a research statement, so his specific research topics are Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Daniel Larremore
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.sub_field: Statistics and Data Science / Mathematical Biology
faculty.summary: His CU Computer Science profile summarizes his work as networks, malaria parasites, computational social science and complex systems, and states that his research develops statistical and inferential methods for analyzing large-scale network data and uses those methods to solve applied problems in diverse domains including public health and academic labor markets. He is also core faculty in the BioFrontiers Institute.

faculty.name: David Albers
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Biomedical Informatics, University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Anschutz School of Medicine profile lists him as Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics and describes interdisciplinary development and application of computational methods in informatics. Further research detail was not verified on an official page: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Emily Jensen
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: Her CU Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering profile lists her area as Systems & Controls but publishes no research-interest statement, so her specific research topics are Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Franck Vernerey
faculty.title: Professor, Paul M. Rady Department of Mechanical Engineering (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Mechanical Engineering profile lists his research interests as mechanics of soft matter, computational multiscale modeling, cell/colloid mechanics, and tissue growth and morphogenesis. A major focus of his Soft Matter Mechanics group is to uncover the fundamental rules that govern the physical and mechanical behavior of dynamic networks in nature and apply these to the development of active and smart matter.

faculty.name: Jed Brown
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His official page states: "Our research is in fast algorithms and robust community software for physically-based modeling, prediction, inference, and design." He leads the PhyPID research group and is an associate editor for the Journal of Open Source Software.

faculty.name: Jeffrey B Weiss
faculty.title: Professor, Department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU ATOC profile and personal page list his research interests as geophysical turbulence, coherent structures, fluid transport, predictability and stochastic models.

faculty.name: John Evans
faculty.title: Department Chair and Associate Professor, Ann and H.J. Smead Department of Aerospace Engineering Sciences (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Aerospace profile lists his focus area as Fluid Dynamics and his degrees as PhD and MS in Computational and Applied Mathematics (UT Austin). He leads the Computational Mechanics and Geometry Laboratory (CMGLab), which its page says pioneers new approaches to the modeling, simulation and optimization of aerospace, naval, energy and other systems.

faculty.name: Liz Bradley
faculty.title: Professor, Department of Computer Science (listed as Elizabeth Bradley on the CU Computer Science directory) (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: She leads the Complex Systems Group in the Department of Computer Science and holds a joint appointment with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, with other affiliations including the Department of Applied Mathematics and the Santa Fe Institute (external faculty). Her CU Computer Science profile is biographical (SB, SM and PhD from MIT; at CU Boulder since January 1993) and her personal page lists teaching in Chaotic Dynamics and nonlinear dynamics; specific current research topics: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Marco M. Nicotra
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His official page states he is an Associate Professor in the Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering at CU Boulder and leads the ROCC research group. The CU ECEE directory additionally lists him as Associate Chair for Undergraduate Education. Further research detail was not published on the official profile: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Melike Sirlanci
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Biomedical Informatics, University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: Her official page states she is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Biomedical Informatics at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. Further research detail was not verified on an official page: Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Meredith Betterton
faculty.title: Professor, Department of Physics (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: Her CU Physics profile states she is interested in the physics of cell division and related biophysics. Current projects address motor protein dynamics and microtubule length regulation, cytoskeletal active matter, mitotic spindle assembly and regulation, chromosome segregation in cell division, and disordered proteins in the nuclear pore complex.

faculty.name: Natalie Vriend
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Paul M. Rady Department of Mechanical Engineering (listed as Nathalie M. Vriend on the CU Mechanical Engineering directory) (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: Her CU Mechanical Engineering profile describes her research as imaging, measuring and modelling granular flows in the environment. She leads the Granular Flow Laboratory and is an expert in performing detailed laboratory experiments and targeted field work involving particulate flows such as sand and snow, also employing numerical simulations and theoretical modelling to complement observations.

faculty.name: Nicholas Dwork
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Biomedical Informatics, University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Anschutz School of Medicine profile states his research focuses on medical imaging and radiation therapy, that he is interested in developing faster MRI for young pediatric subjects and fetuses, and that he is also interested in quantitative Optical Coherence Tomography. He received his PhD from Stanford University in 2019.

faculty.name: Orit Peleg
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science and BioFrontiers Institute (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: Her CU profile states she seeks to understand the behavior of disordered living systems by merging tools from physics, biology, engineering and computer science. Her lab page states its goal is to formulate and test phenomenological theories about natural signal design principles and their emergent spatiotemporal patterns.

faculty.name: Peter Hamlington
faculty.title: Department Chair and Professor, Paul M. Rady Department of Mechanical Engineering (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Mechanical Engineering profile lists his research interests as computational fluid dynamics. He leads the Turbulence and Energy Systems Laboratory (TESLa), whose research areas are listed as fire dynamics, high-speed combustion, industrial systems, ocean biogeochemistry, turbulent flows and wind energy.

faculty.name: Rafael Frongillo
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Computer Science profile states his research lies at the interface between theoretical machine learning and economics, primarily focusing on domains such as information elicitation and crowdsourcing which involve the exchange of information for money, drawing techniques from convex analysis, game theory, optimization and statistics. His personal page adds that he also works in dynamical systems.

faculty.name: Scott Parker
faculty.title: Professor, Department of Physics (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Physics profile states his research is in the area of kinetic theory and simulation of plasmas, with most current work on direct numerical simulation of tokamak plasma turbulence on large massively parallel computers, done in a five-dimensional phase space using newly developed particle-based methods. His group page adds that he is a Fellow of RASEI and of the Center for Integrated Plasma Studies.

faculty.name: Sean O'Rourke
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of Mathematics (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Mathematics profile lists his research as probability and random matrix theory, and his personal page states his research interests include probability, random matrix theory and random polynomials. He received his PhD at the University of California, Davis under the direction of Alexander Soshnikov.

faculty.name: Sriram Sankaranarayan
faculty.title: Professor and Department Chair, Department of Computer Science (listed as Sriram Sankaranarayanan on the CU Computer Science directory) (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Computer Science profile states his research interests include automatic techniques for reasoning about the behavior of computer and cyber-physical systems, working on fundamental problems involving modeling and analysis using hybrid dynamical systems and formal methods, with applications to artificial pancreas systems for treating type-1 diabetes. His personal page describes studying the mathematical foundations of autonomous systems.

faculty.name: Stephen Kissler
faculty.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: His CU Computer Science profile states he studies epidemiology, pathogen evolution and complex social systems. He received BS and MS degrees in Applied Mathematics at CU Boulder, earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge as a Gates Scholar, and was a postdoctoral fellow at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.

faculty.name: Tahra Eissa
faculty.title: Affiliated Faculty, Department of Applied Mathematics; home appointment at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (academic rank Unknown/Verify - no rank published on the APPM affiliate listing or on her lab page) (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.summary: Her lab page (Eissa Lab, University of Colorado Anschutz) states the lab studies how the brain makes decisions in a changing world, building decision-making games with hidden features and then using mathematical modeling and human brain recordings to uncover the strategies people use and how the brain computes them.

faculty.name: Tomoko Matsuo
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Ann and H.J. Smead Department of Aerospace Engineering Sciences (APPM Affiliated Faculty)
faculty.sub_field: Mathematical Geosciences / Statistics and Data Science
faculty.summary: Her Geospace Data Science Lab page lists her as Associate Professor and Smead Endowed Faculty Fellow in the Ann and H.J. Smead Department of Aerospace Engineering Sciences, and as Affiliate Faculty in the Department of Applied Mathematics. The lab's stated mission is advancing the science and engineering of the near-Earth space environment.

requirements.fee_display: $125 (nonrefundable). ICME does not publish its own fee and directs applicants to Stanford Graduate Admissions, which states: "The application fee is $125 and is nonrefundable." University and School of Engineering fee waivers are available; ICME is not authorized to grant waivers.
requirements.english: TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic required for applicants who are not exempt. ICME/Stanford exemption criteria (no test needed if you meet one or more): U.S. citizen or permanent resident; first language is English; a U.S. bachelor's/master's/doctoral degree (or international equivalent from a university where all instruction was in English); or two or more consecutive years of full-time professional or educational experience in English in the past 10 years. University minimum scores are set on Stanford's central Graduate Admissions TOEFL/IELTS page - specific minimum figures Unknown/Verify.
requirements.admission_model_note: The ICME Admission Committee reviews all applications online ("The Admission Committee reviews all graduate applications online"). The PhD application's Faculty Interest section asks applicants to "Select up to three faculty members whose research interests best align with yours and who could serve as potential research advisors" and states: "Your selections are non-binding and will help us route your application to relevant faculty during the review process." Admission is not contingent on pre-arranging an advisor; ICME PhD students complete first-year research rotations and align with a permanent advisor (bulletin: "Advisors assume responsibility for funding upon alignment").

funding.note: ICME Graduate Funding page: "All ICME PhD students who are in good standing relative to ICME's program requirements will be funded to the department's standard for the duration of their program. PhD students will be funded through a combination of fellowships and research or teaching assistantships during the course of their program and will receive specific information about their funding package upon admission." The Admissions FAQ repeats this. No fixed number of guaranteed years is published (funding is "for the duration of their program"), so years = null. The Stanford Graduate Fellowship (auto-considered for admitted PhDs) provides stipend + tuition for up to 12 quarters. Note: ICME does NOT guarantee funding for MS students.

requirements.contact_note: No ICME page requires or recommends contacting faculty before applying. The Admissions FAQ ("Before applying") states: "Please review our affiliated faculty members' publications for further insight into their research. If you feel that your academic background and research interests are a good match for our program, we encourage you to apply!" Instead of pre-application contact, the PhD application collects a non-binding Faculty Interest selection (up to three potential advisors) used to route the application during committee review. (Separately, the Graduate Funding page notes that RA appointments are typically "secured...by contacting a faculty member directly," but that concerns research-assistant funding, not admission.)
requirements.duration: Unknown/Verify (ICME bulletin states PhD candidacy must be achieved by the end of the sixth quarter in residence, excluding summers, and that "Candidacy expires five years from the date of submission"; no official "typical years to degree" figure is published.)

faculty.name: Ron Dror
faculty.title: Cheriton Family Professor and Professor, by courtesy, of Structural Biology and of Molecular & Cellular Physiology (ICME Faculty with Joint Appointment)
faculty.summary: Leads a research group that uses molecular simulation and machine learning to elucidate biomolecular structure, dynamics and function and to guide development of more effective medicines, combining bottom-up physics-based simulation with top-down machine learning to predict molecular structures and properties.

faculty.name: Alison Marsden
faculty.title: Douglass M. and Nola Leishman Professor of Cardiovascular Diseases; Professor of Pediatrics (Cardiology); Professor of Bioengineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Mechanical Engineering (ICME Faculty with Joint Appointment)
faculty.summary: Develops numerical methods for cardiovascular blood flow simulation and medical device design, applies optimization to large-scale fluid mechanics simulations, and applies engineering tools to patient care in cardiovascular surgery and congenital heart disease.

faculty.name: Madeleine Udell
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering (ICME Faculty with Joint Appointment)
faculty.summary: Builds the mathematical and computational foundations for scalable, accessible and responsible data-driven decision-making in high-stakes domains including healthcare, finance, marketing, operations and engineering; work spans optimization algorithms, machine learning and large-scale data analysis.

faculty.name: Mykel Kochenderfer
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics; Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI; Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Directs the Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory (SISL), researching advanced algorithms and analytical methods for robust decision-making systems, with a focus on air traffic control, unmanned aircraft and aerospace applications where decisions must be made in uncertain, dynamic environments while maintaining safety and efficiency.

faculty.name: Marco Pavone
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics; Senior Fellow at the Precourt Institute for Energy; Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering and of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Directs the Autonomous Systems Laboratory and the Center for Automotive Research at Stanford, developing methodologies for the analysis, design and control of autonomous systems, emphasizing self-driving cars, autonomous aerospace vehicles and future mobility systems.

faculty.name: Surya Ganguli
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Applied Physics; Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI; Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Neurobiology and of Electrical Engineering
faculty.summary: His Stanford profile lists his research interest as theoretical and computational neuroscience; the profile does not include an additional overview paragraph, so further specifics are Unknown/Verify.

faculty.name: Markus Covert
faculty.title: Shriram Chair of the Department of Bioengineering, Professor of Bioengineering and, by courtesy, of Chemical and Systems Biology
faculty.summary: Builds computational models of complex biological processes and uses them to guide experimental work, enabling rapid identification and validation of unknown components and interactions; systems of interest include metabolic, regulatory and signaling networks and cell-cell interactions, with current work on the dynamic behavior of NF-kappaB.

faculty.name: Noah Rosenberg
faculty.title: Stanford Professor of Population Genetics and Society; Professor of Biology
faculty.summary: His lab addresses problems in evolutionary biology and genetics through mathematical modeling, computer simulations and statistical methods, covering the combinatorics of evolutionary trees, inference of human evolutionary history, population genetics in the search for disease-susceptibility genes, gene trees and species trees, and mathematical properties of statistics for genetic variability.

faculty.name: Grant Rotskoff
faculty.title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
faculty.summary: Studies the nonequilibrium dynamics of living matter with a focus on self-organization from the molecular to the cellular scale, developing theoretical and computational tools to probe and predict properties of physical systems driven away from equilibrium, including machine learning for sampling and coarse-graining.

faculty.title: Canon Professor in the School of Engineering (Professor of Computer Science)
faculty.summary: His research focuses on the design of new computational algorithms for a variety of applications including computational fluid dynamics, computer graphics and biomechanics.

faculty.name: Anshul Kundaje
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Genetics and of Computer Science
faculty.summary: Develops machine learning models of gene regulation to decipher the genetic and molecular basis of disease; has pioneered deep learning models and interpretation frameworks to decode the functional language encoded in DNA, RNA and proteins.

faculty.name: Christopher Ré
faculty.title: Professor of Computer Science

faculty.name: Daniel Yamins
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Psychology and of Computer Science
faculty.summary: His lab investigates neuroscience, AI, psychology and large-scale data analysis, guided by the hypotheses that studying how the brain solves computational challenges can improve AI and that better AI can reveal better brain models; methods include computational modeling, high-throughput neurophysiology, functional brain imaging and behavioral psychophysics.

faculty.name: Mert Pilanci

faculty.name: Benjamin Van Roy

faculty.name: Daniel Tartakovsky
faculty.title: Professor of Energy Science and Engineering
faculty.summary: His research spans environmental fluid mechanics (subsurface flow and contaminant transport, multiphase flow, groundwater hydrology), applied and computational mathematics (uncertainty quantification, stochastic PDEs, hybrid numerical algorithms) and biomedical modeling (blood flow, microcirculation, computational cell biology).

faculty.name: Hamdi Tchelepi
faculty.title: Max Steineke Professor and Senior Fellow at the Precourt Institute for Energy; Professor and Chair of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering

faculty.name: Biondo Biondi
faculty.title: Barney and Estelle Morris Professor, Department of Geophysics
faculty.summary: His research centers on seismic data imaging and processing, including algorithms for active and passive seismic data imaging, high-performance computing for wavefield processing, fiber-optic / distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and urban seismic monitoring using telecom infrastructure.

faculty.name: Eric Dunham
faculty.title: Professor of Geophysics
faculty.summary: His research develops and uses physics-based computational simulations to characterize and understand earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanoes, including earthquake rupture dynamics, tsunami generation, volcano seismology and infrasound, and numerical methods for wave propagation.

faculty.name: Jenny Suckale
faculty.title: Associate Professor of Geophysics; Senior Fellow, by courtesy, at the Woods Institute for the Environment
faculty.summary: Her research group studies disasters to reduce the risk they pose by developing customized mathematical models tested against observational data and informed by community needs; current priorities include volcanic eruptions, ice-sheet instability, permafrost disintegration, induced seismicity and flood-risk mitigation.

faculty.title: Associate Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Chambers Faculty Scholar in the School of Engineering

requirements.admission_model: School admission by research; two intakes a year (August and January)
requirements.admission_model_note: The admission guide gives recurring dates rather than cycle-specific ones: the August intake opens 1 October and closes 31 January, with individual schools closing earlier, between 15 November and 31 December. GRE/GMAT/GATE are optional, though some programmes still ask.

funding.note: NTU Research Scholarship covers tuition and a monthly stipend (amount not published on the pages read). International research students are still eligible for the MOE subsidy with its 3-year Singapore service obligation — that route closed to coursework students.
